body.text:
Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtram
dharma-cakra-pravartano nāma prathamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra</s> (The Lotus of Compassion Sūtra). The first <s>parivarta</s> (chapter), named "<s>Dharma-cakra-pravartana</s>" (The Turning of the Wheel of the Dharma).

body.text:
om namaḥ
śrīsarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to all the glorious <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. //

children.text: buddhaṃ praṇamya sarvajñaṃ dharmaṃ saṅghaṃ guṇākaraṃ /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the <s>Buddha</s>, the omniscient one, to the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), and to the <s>Saṅgha</s> (community), the treasury of virtues,
I shall proclaim the <s>Bodhi-sūtra</s> (scripture of awakening) called <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s> (The Lotus of Compassion). //

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniḥkleśairvaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairājāneyairmahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyairapahṛtabhārairanuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptairabhijñānābhijñātairmahāśrāvakaiḥ / (

children.translated_text: KpSū 2

children.text: ) tadyathā, āyuṣmatā cājñātakauṇḍinyena āyuṣmatā cāsvajitā āyuṣmatā ca bāṣpeṇa āyuṣmatā ca mahāsthāmnā āyuṣmatā ca bhadrikeṇa āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena āyuṣmatā coruvilvākāśyapena āyuṣmatā ca gayākāśyepena āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena āyuṣmatā ca mahākātyāyanena āyuṣmatā cāniruddhena āyuṣmatā ca revatena āyuṣmatā ca kaṃphillena āyuṣmatā ca gavāṃpatinā āyuṣmatā ca pilindavatsena āyuṣmatā ca bakulena āyuṣmatā ca mahākauṣṭhilena āyuṣmatā ca bharadvājena āyuṣmatā ca mahānandena āyuṣmatā copanandena āyuṣmatā ca sundaranandena āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇena āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā āyuṣmatā ca rāhulena / evaṃ pramukhaiścānekairmahāśrākairāyuṣmatā cānandena śaikṣeṇa, anyābhyāṃ bhikṣusahasrābhyāṃ śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ / mahāprajāpatīpramukhaiśca ṣaḍbhikṣuṇīsahasraiḥ, yaśodharayā ca bhikṣuṇyā rāhulamātrā saparivārayā / aśītibhiśca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sarvairavaivartikairekajātipratibaddhairyadutānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃboddhau dhāraṇīpratilabdhairmahāpratibhānapratiṣṭhitairavaivartyadharmacakrapravartakairbahubuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitair (
children.translated_text: ) That is to say: the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, the venerable <s>Bāṣpa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāsthāman</s>, the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Uruvilvākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Kaṃphilla</s>, the venerable <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, the venerable <s>Pilindavatsa</s>, the venerable <s>Bakula</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, the venerable <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānanda</s>, the venerable <s>Upananda</s>, the venerable <s>Sundarananda</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> — headed by these and other great <s>śrāvakas</s>, and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, a learner, together with two other thousands of <s>bhikṣus</s>, both learners and those beyond learning; and six thousand <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) headed by <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>, and the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Yaśodharā</s>, mother of <s>Rāhula</s>, together with her retinue; and eighty thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> (beings of awakening), all of them <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing), bound by a single birth, that is to say, to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), who had obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention), established in great eloquence, turners of the irreversible wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, who had attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, (
KpSū 3

children.text:
) bahubuddhaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlairbahubuddhaśatasahasrasaṃstutairmaitrīparibhāvitakāyacittaistathāgatajñānāvatāraṇakuśalairmahāprajñaiḥ prajñāpāramitāgatiṃgatairbahulokadhātuśatasahasraviśrutairbahuprāṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃpālakaiḥ / tadyathā, mañjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena avalokiteśvareṇa ca mahāsthāmaprāptena ca sarvārthanāmnā ca nityodyuktena ca anikṣiptadhureṇa ca ratnapāṇinā ca bhaiṣajyarājena ca bhaiṣajyasamudgatena ca vyūharājena ca pradānaśūreṇa ca ratnacandreṇa ca pūrṇacandreṇa ca mahāvikramiṇā ca anantavikramiṇā ca trailokyavikramiṇā ca mahāpratibhānena ca satatasamitābhiyuktena
ca dharaṇiṃdhareṇa ca akṣayamatinā ca mahāmatinā ca śāntamatinā ca nakṣatrarājena ca ratnavairocanena ca maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena siṃhena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / bhadrapālapūrvaṃgamaiśca ṣoḍaśabhiḥ satpuruṣaiḥ sārdhaṃ / tadyathā, bhadrapālena ca ratnākareṇa ca susārthavāhena ca naradattena ca guhaguptena ca varuṇadattena ca indradattena ca uttaramatinā ca viśeṣamatinā ca vardhamānamatinā ca amoghadarśinā ca susaṃprasthitena ca suvikrāntavikramiṇā (
children.translated_text:
) who had planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, praised by many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, whose bodies and minds were pervaded by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), skilled in entering into the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), possessed of great wisdom, who had gone to the furthest shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), renowned across many hundreds of thousands of world-realms, protectors of many <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of hundreds of thousands of living beings. That is to say: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, <s>Sarvārthanāman</s>, <s>Nityodyukta</s>, <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>, <s>Ratnapāṇi</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasamudgata</s>, <s>Vyūharāja</s>, <s>Pradānaśūra</s>, <s>Ratnacandra</s>, <s>Pūrṇacandra</s>, <s>Mahāvikramin</s>, <s>Anantavikramin</s>, <s>Trailokyavikramin</s>, <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s>,
<s>Dharaṇiṃdhara</s>, <s>Akṣayamati</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Śāntamati</s>, <s>Nakṣatrarāja</s>, <s>Ratnavairocana</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Siṃha</s>; together with sixteen good men headed by <s>Bhadrapāla</s>. That is to say: <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, <s>Ratnākara</s>, <s>Susārthavāha</s>, <s>Naradatta</s>, <s>Guhagupta</s>, <s>Varuṇadatta</s>, <s>Indradatta</s>, <s>Uttaramati</s>, <s>Viśeṣamati</s>, <s>Vardhamānamati</s>, <s>Amoghadarśin</s>, <s>Susaṃprasthita</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikramin</s>, (
KpSū 4

children.text: ) ca anupamamatinā ca sūryagarbheṇa ca dharaṇiṃdhareṇa ca / evaṃ pramukhairaśītibhirbodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ / śakreṇa ca devānāmindreṇa viṃśatidevaputrasahasraparivāreṇa / tadyathā, candreṇa ca devaputreṇa sūryeṇa ca samantagandhena ca ratnaprabheṇa ca avabhāsaprabheṇa ca / evaṃ pramukhaiścānyairdevaputraiḥ / caturbhiśca mahārājaiḥ sārdhaṃ saparivāraiḥ / brahmaṇā ca sahāpatinā sārdhaṃ dvādaśabrahmakāyikāsahasreṇa śikhinā ca brahmaṇā jyotiḥprabheṇa ca brahmanā / evaṃ pramukhairdvādaśabhiśca brahmakāyikadevaputrasahasraiḥ / aṣṭābhiśca nāgarājaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahunāgakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ / caturbhiśca kinnararājaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahukinnarakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ / caturbhiśca gandharvakāyikairdevaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahugandharvaśatasahasraparivāraiḥ / caturbhiścāsurendraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahvasurakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ / caturbhiśca garuḍendraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahugaruḍakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāraiḥ / rājñā cājātaśatruṇā māgadhena vaidehīputreṇa sārdhaṃ bahumanuṣyarājasāmātyapaurajānapadaparivāraiḥ //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Anupamamati</s>, <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, and <s>Dharaṇiṃdhara</s>. Together with these and eighty thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s> (gods), with a retinue of twenty thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods). That is to say: <s>Candra</s> the <s>devaputra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Samantagandha</s>, <s>Ratnaprabha</s>, and <s>Avabhāsaprabha</s>. Headed by these and other <s>devaputras</s>. And with the four great kings, together with their retinues. And <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with twelve thousand <s>Brahmakāyika</s> (Brahmā-world) gods, and <s>Śikhin</s> the <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Jyotiḥprabha</s> the <s>Brahmā</s>. Headed by these and twelve thousand <s>Brahmakāyika devaputras</s>. And eight <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) kings, together with retinues of many <s>koṭīs</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>nāgas</s>. And four <s>Kinnara</s> kings, together with retinues of many <s>koṭīs</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kinnaras</s>. And four <s>Gandharva</s> (celestial musician) <s>devaputras</s>, together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>gandharvas</s>. And four <s>Asura</s> (demon) lords, together with retinues of many <s>koṭīs</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>asuras</s>. And four <s>Garuḍa</s> (eagle) lords, together with retinues of many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>garuḍas</s>. And King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, together with a retinue of many human kings, ministers, city-dwellers, and country-folk. //

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), twelve hundred in number, all of them <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) who had destroyed the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements), free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), self-mastered, with well-liberated minds, with well-liberated wisdom, noble ones, great <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), who had done what was to be done, accomplished what was to be accomplished, cast off the burden, attained their own goal, completely exhausted the fetters of existence, with minds well-liberated through right knowledge, who had reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states, endowed with the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) — great <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers). (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavāṃścatasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ (

children.translated_text: KpSū 5

children.text: ) pūjito 'rcito 'pacāyitaḥ, tadā bodhisattvaviṣayasaṃdarśanapraṇidhānavyūhasamādhiviṣayadhāraṇīmukhavyūhaṃ samādhānamukhanirdeśaṃ caryāvaiśāradyaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvānugataṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ bhāṣitumārabdhavān, tadā nānāvarṇaraśmayo niścaritā yatprabhābhirayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturmahatāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt / tena cāvabhāsena lokāntarikā aghā aghasphuṭā andhakāratamisrāḥ, yatremau candrasūryau eva maharddhikau mahānubhāvau maheśākhyau nābhipatato na virocatastatra ye sattvā upapannāste svakasvakamapi bāhuprasāritaṃ na paśyanti sma, tatrāpi tenāvabhāsena parisphuṭāḥ samānā anyonyaṃ paśyanti smānyonyaṃ saṃjānante sma / sarvāṇi buddhakṣetrāṇi ca parisphuṭāni saṃdṛśyante sma yāvad avīcirmahānirayo yāvadbrahmalokaṃ parisphuṭaṃ dṛśyate sma / ye ca teṣu sarveṣu kṣetreṣu ṣaṭsu gatiṣu sattvāste sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanto dhriyanto yāpayanto yaṃ dharmaṃ bhāṣante sma sa ca sarvo nikhilena śrūyate sma / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā yogino yogācārāḥ prāptaphalāścāprāptaphalāśca te 'pi (
children.translated_text: ) worshipped, venerated, and respected, then began to expound a great <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive) <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourse), a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (teaching cycle) called "The Display of Confidence in Practice" — a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) gateway display of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) realm of the <s>samādhi</s> of the vow to manifest the domain of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, followed by <s>bodhisattvas</s>, embraced by all <s>Buddhas</s>. At that time, rays of various colors issued forth, and by their radiance this entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world universe) was flooded with a great brilliance. And by that radiance, the dark, murky, lightless spaces between worlds — where even these two, the moon and sun, so mighty in power, so great in majesty, so great in sovereignty, cannot shine or illuminate, where beings who are reborn there cannot even see their own outstretched arms — even those were pervaded by that radiance, and those beings could see one another and recognize one another. And all the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) were seen pervaded with light, from the <s>Avīci</s> great hell up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (Brahmā-world), all pervaded and visible. And all beings in all those fields, in the six <s>gatis</s> (destinies of rebirth), were all seen. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> dwelling in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were teaching — all of it was heard in its entirety. And the <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers), yogins, practitioners of yoga, and those who had attained the fruits and those who had not yet attained the fruits in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too (
KpSū 6

children.text: ) sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anekavividhāśravaṇārambaṇādhimuktihetukāraṇopāyakauśalyairbodhicaryācāriṇaste 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvṛtāste 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / ye ca teṣu parinirvṛtānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ ratnamayadhātustūpāste 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma / antarīkṣācca puṣpavarṣam abhiprāvarṣat, manojñaśabdā amāradundubhyaḥ prasasvanuḥ ; sarvaścāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāram aṣṭādaśamahānimittam akampat prākampat saṃprākampat, avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat, acalat prācalat saṃprācalat, akṣubhyat prākṣubhyat saṃprākṣubhyat, araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat, agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat / tasmin kṣaṇe sarvato lokeṣu harṣaṇīyāstoṣaṇīyāḥ prasādanīyā avalokanīyāḥ prahlādanīyā manojñāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante sma / na ca kasyacit sattvasya viheṭhā vā trāso vā bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vā / na cānyadevalokānāṃ prabhāḥ prajñāyante / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokopapannāḥ sattvā vigataduḥkhāḥ sarvasukhasamarpitāścābhuvān / na ca kasyacit sattvasya rāgo vā dveṣo vā moho vā mātsaryo (
children.translated_text: ) were all seen. And the <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> who were practicing the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) through manifold and various means of skillful methods, causes, conditions, inclinations, and commitments — they too were all seen. And the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation) in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too were all seen. And the jewel-made <s>dhātu-stūpas</s> (reliquary shrines) of those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — they too were all seen. And from the sky a rain of flowers showered down, and wondrous sounds of celestial drums resounded that were not of <s>Māra</s>; and this entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world universe) trembled in six ways with eighteen great signs — it quaked, quaked greatly, quaked exceedingly; it shuddered, shuddered greatly, shuddered exceedingly; it shook, shook greatly, shook exceedingly; it trembled, trembled greatly, trembled exceedingly; it rumbled, rumbled greatly, rumbled exceedingly; it thundered, thundered greatly, thundered exceedingly. At that moment, from all worlds were heard sounds that were delightful, gratifying, faith-inspiring, beautiful, refreshing, and pleasing. And no being experienced annoyance, fear, terror, or paralysis. Nor were the lights of other heavenly realms perceived. All beings reborn in the hells, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s> (lord of death) became free from suffering and were endowed with every happiness. And no being was afflicted by desire, hatred, delusion, jealousy, (
KpSū 7

children.text: ) vā īrṣyā vā māno vā mrakṣo vā mado vā krodho vā vyāpādo vā paridāho vā bādhate / sarvasattvāśca parasparamitracittā hitacittā mātṛpitṛsaṃjñino 'bhūvan //
children.translated_text: ) envy, pride, hypocrisy, intoxication, anger, malice, or burning torment. And all beings became of a mind of mutual friendship and benevolence toward one another, regarding each other as mother and father. //

body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded and attended by the four assemblies, honored, revered, esteemed, (

body.text: atha ratnavairocano nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ mahānimittaprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāyaikāṃśamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat / "paramāścaryādbhutaprāpto 'haṃ bhagavan, kuta ime raśmaya āgatāḥ?, kasyaiṣa prabhāvaḥ?, ko nvatra bhagavan hetuḥ?, kaḥ pratyayo bhaviṣyati?"
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnavairocana</s>, having seen that great display of miraculous signs, quickly rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: "I have witnessed something supremely marvelous and wondrous, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! From where have these rays come? Whose is this magnificent power? What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause herein? What will be the condition?"

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān ratnavairocanaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - "śṛṇu kulaputra sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te" / "sādhu sādhu bhagavan" niti ratnavairocano bhagavataḥ pratyaśroṣīt / bhagavān ratnavairocanaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat /

children.translated_text: ) filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, pervaded with the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>; and that ground of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> is soft like <s>kācalindika</s> cotton, pleasant to the touch — when one sets down one's foot, it sinks four finger-breadths, and when one lifts one's foot, it rises back four finger-breadths — and it is strewn with various lotuses. There the trees are made of the seven precious substances, seven <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in height; from those trees hang divine saffron-colored garments, and divine musical instruments play pleasing melodies; in those trees, various birds utter delightful sounds of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), and <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening); the leaves of those trees, touching one another, produce a sound of five-fold music surpassing even the divine; and from each tree, a divine and sublime fragrance pervades for a thousand <s>yojanas</s>; and from those trees, divine ornaments hang down. And between those trees are mansions made of the seven precious substances, five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height and one hundred and fifty <s>yojanas</s> in breadth. In those mansions, gateways open in all four directions. And outside those mansions, beyond the gateways, there are lotus ponds, eighty <s>yojanas</s> in length and fifty <s>yojanas</s> in breadth. From those ponds, stairways made of the seven precious substances lead in all four directions. And from those flower filaments, <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> are born; they are reborn in those lotus filaments during the first watch of the night, and they pass that night in cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of the joy of liberation. And there, at the time of daybreak, cool, fragrant, gentle, pleasantly touching breezes blow, and they cause the closed flowers to bloom. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having risen from <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) and having relaxed the bliss of the joy of liberation, descend into the lotus filaments, and entering those pavilions, they sit cross-legged on seats made of the seven precious substances and listen to the <s>Dharma</s>. And between those trees and pavilions, in the four directions, there are mountains made of <s>jāmbūnada</s> (finest gold), twenty <s>yojanas</s> in height and three <s>yojanas</s> in breadth; and on those mountains, many hundreds of thousands of <s>sūryakānta</s> (sun-stone), <s>candrakānta</s> (moon-stone), <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire), and <s>jyotīrasa</s> gems are seen at intervals. The radiance of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, falling upon those gems on the mountains, and by that <s>Buddha</s>-radiance together with the gem-radiance, that entire <s>Padmā</s> world-realm is suffused with a perpetually magnificent brilliance. And the radiance of the moon and sun is not perceived there; only when the lotuses close and the birds become quiet, then there is the notion of 'night,' and the opposite [indicates] daytime. Thus spoken, the Blessed One said this to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnavairocana</s>: "In the last watch of that night, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, attained supreme perfect awakening. At the time of daybreak, he performed such a miraculous transformation of supernatural power that, having manifested himself up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world, from the crown of his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) he emitted sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of rays, and with those rays illuminated world-realms in the upward direction equal in number to the atoms of a <s>Buddha</s>-field. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who at that time were situated in the upward direction and looked downward — for them neither <s>Sumeru</s> came into view, nor <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, nor the dark mountains. body.translated_text: Then indeed, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having withdrawn the transformation of supernatural power, in the midst of the entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, set in motion the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> called <s>Avaivartikacakra</s> (the Wheel of Non-Retrogression), a wheel of <s>Dharma</s> that accords with the teaching, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans, for the purpose of fulfilling the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle)."

body.text: atha khalu ratnavairocano bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - "kathaṃ bhadanta bhagavan padmāyāṃ lokadhātau rātriṃdivaṃ prajñāyate?, kiyadrūpāśca tatra śabdāḥ śrūyante?, kiyadrūpeṇa te bodhisattvāścāśayena samanvāgatāḥ?, katamena vā vihareṇa viharanti?" bhagavān āha - "nityāvabhāsitā kulaputra padmā lokadhāturbuddhābhayā / tatra yadā puṣpāḥ saṃkucanti, pakṣiṇaścālpaśabdā bhavanti, bhagavāṃśca te ca bodhisattvā dhyānaiḥ krīḍanti vimuktiprītisukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayanti, tadā rātrīti prajñāyate / yadā punaste puṣpā vāteneritā bhavanti, śakunāśca manojñāni kūjanti, puṣpavṛṣṭiścābhipravarṣati, caturdiśaṃ paramasugandhā manojñā mṛdukāḥ sukhasaṃsparśā vāyavaḥ pravāyanti, bhagavāṃśca samādhervyutthāya padmottaro bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmatikramya śrāvakapratyekabuddhakathāṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, tena ca tatra divasaḥ prajñāyate / avirahitāśca tatra kulaputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā buddhaśabdena dharmaśabdena (

children.text: ) saṅghaśabdena, vaiśāradyaśabdenānabhisaṃskāraśabdenānutpādaśabdenānirodhaśabdena śāntaśabdenopaśāntaśabdena praśāntaśabdena mahāmaitrīśabdena mahākaruṇāśabdenānutpattikadharmaśabdenābhiṣekabhūmipratilābhaśabdena buddhabodhisattvaśabdenāvirahitā, nityaṃ te bodhisattvā evaṃrūpaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti sma / punaraparaṃ kulaputra ye bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ padmāyāṃ lokadhātau pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyiṣyanti vā sarve te dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatā yojanaprabhā hyavinipātadharmāṇo yāvadbodhiparyantāt / sarve te bodhisattvā maitracittāḥ snigdhacittā akaluṣacittā dāntacittāḥ kṣamācittāḥ samāhitacittāḥ prasannacittā apratihatacittāḥ śuddhacittāḥ kalyāṇacittā dharmaprīticittāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kleśapraśamanacittāḥ pṛthivīsamacittā laukikāyāṃ kathāyām anabhiratacittā lokottarāyāṃ kathāyāṃ sābhiratacittāḥ sarvakuśaladharmaparyeṣṭicittā nirupadhau (
children.translated_text: ) the word '<s>Saṅgha</s>,' the word 'fearlessness,' the word 'non-fabrication,' the word 'non-arising,' the word 'non-cessation,' the word 'peace,' the word 'tranquility,' the word 'complete peace,' the word 'great loving-kindness,' the word 'great compassion,' the word 'unarisen <s>dharmas</s>,' the word 'attainment of the stage of consecration,' the word '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>bodhisattva</s>' — they are never separated [from these]; those <s>bodhisattvas</s> constantly hear such sounds. Furthermore, O son of good family, all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who have been reborn or will be reborn in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm are endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, possess a radiance of one <s>yojana</s>, and are of the nature of non-retrogression until the end of awakening. All those <s>bodhisattvas</s> are of loving mind, affectionate mind, unpolluted mind, tamed mind, patient mind, concentrated mind, serene mind, unobstructed mind, pure mind, virtuous mind, mind delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>, mind intent on pacifying the afflictions of all beings, mind equal to the earth, mind not delighting in worldly discourse, mind delighting in supramundane discourse, mind seeking all wholesome qualities, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 16.

children.text:
) sadāprayuktacittā vyādhijarāmaraṇebhyaḥ praśāntacittāḥ sarvakleśadahanacittāḥ sarvasaṃyojanapraśamanacittāḥ sarvadharmāmanyanacittāḥ, āśayabalinaḥ prayogabalinaḥ pratyayabalinaḥ praṇidhānabalino 'sārabhinnāccālanabalino
nidhyaptibalinaḥ kuśalamūlabalinaḥ samādhānabalinaḥ śrutabalinaḥ śīlabalinaḥ tyāgabalinaḥ kṣāntibalino vīryabalino dhyānabalinaḥ prajñābalinaḥ śamathabalino vipaśyanābalino 'bhijñābalinaḥ smṛtibalino bodhibalinaḥ sarvamāravidhvaṃsanabalinaḥ sarvamārabalapramardanabalinaḥ sarvaparapravādināṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahabalinaḥ sarvakleśapramardanabalinaḥ / te ca bodhisattvā ye padmāyāṃ lokadhātau pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyiṣyanti vā bahubuddhaśatasahasrakṛtādhikārā hi avaruptakuśalamūlā; ye ca tatra padmāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetre bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyiṣyanti vā dhyānāhārāste bodhisattvā dharmāhārā gandhāhārāstadyathāpi nāma devā (
children.translated_text: ) mind ever engaged in the realm without remainder, mind at peace with regard to disease, old age, and death, mind burning all afflictions, mind pacifying all fetters, mind not disrespecting any <s>dharmas</s>; they are strong in disposition, strong in application, strong in conditions, strong in aspiration, strong in unshakeable resolve, strong in reflection, strong in roots of merit, strong in concentration, strong in learning, strong in moral conduct, strong in generosity, strong in patience, strong in vigor, strong in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), strong in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), strong in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), strong in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), strong in <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledges), strong in mindfulness, strong in awakening, strong in destroying all <s>Māras</s>, strong in crushing the power of all <s>Māras</s>, strong in defeating all rival debaters through the <s>Dharma</s>, strong in crushing all afflictions. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been reborn or will be reborn in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm have accumulated merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> and have planted roots of merit. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been or will be reborn in that <s>Padmā</s> world-realm, that <s>Buddha</s>-field, are nourished by <s>dhyāna</s>, nourished by the <s>Dharma</s>, nourished by fragrance, just as the gods (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 17.

children.text: ) brahmakāyikā, na ca tatra kavaḍikāhārāḥ prajñāyante / sarvaśaśca tatrākuśalasya nāmāpi nāsti; sarvaśaśca tatra mātṛgrāmasya nāmāpi nāsti, prajñaptirapi nāsti; sarvaśaśca tatra duḥkhaśabdo nāsti; sarvathā priyāpriyaśabdo nāsti, peyālaṃ na kleśaśabdo na parigraho na cātrāndhakāraṃ na durgandhaṃ na cittaklamatā na kāyaklamatā na narakatiryagyoniyamalokaśabdaḥ, apāyaprajñaptirapi nāsti, na kaṇṭakagahanapāṣāṇaśarkarā na cāgnirna candrasūryā na tārakārūpā na mahāsamudrā na sumerucakravāḍā na lokāntarikā na kālaparvatā na mīḍhapāṣāṇā na pāṃśuparvatāḥ, na meghavarṣaśabdo na kaluṣavāyuśabdaḥ, sarvathāpāyaśabdo nāsti, sarvathākṣaṇaśabdo nāsti / atha ca punaḥ padmā lokadhāturnityaṃ buddhābhayā bodhisattvābhayā puṇyābhayā ratnābhayā udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā / saphalāścātra nāma pakṣiṇomanojñāḥ snigdhāḥ svakasvakena svareṇa indriyabalabodhyaṅgāni pravyāharanti sma"
children.translated_text: ) of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [heaven]; and no solid food is perceived there. And there, there is not even the name of the unwholesome in any way; and there, there is not even the name of womankind in any way, nor even the designation; and there is no sound of suffering in any way; there is no sound of the pleasant and unpleasant in any way; abbreviated — no sound of affliction, no possessiveness, and there is no darkness, no foul smell, no mental fatigue, no bodily fatigue, no sound of the hells, animal realms, or <s>Yama</s>'s world; there is not even the designation of the lower realms; there are no thorns, dense thickets, rocks, or gravel; there is no fire, no moon or sun, no forms of stars, no great oceans, no <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, no inter-world darkness, no dark mountains, no excrement-rocks, no dust-mountains; there is no sound of rain-clouds, no sound of turbid winds; there is no sound of the lower realms in any way; there is no sound of inopportune births in any way. Moreover, the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm is perpetually suffused with magnificent radiance from the <s>Buddha</s>-radiance, <s>bodhisattva</s>-radiance, merit-radiance, and jewel-radiance. And there, fruitful birds with delightful and gentle voices, each in their own voice, proclaim the faculties, powers, and factors of awakening."

body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Ratnavairocana</s> said this to the Blessed One: "How, Venerable Blessed One, are night and day distinguished in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm? And what kinds of sounds are heard there? And with what kind of disposition are those <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed? And in what kind of abiding do they dwell?" The Blessed One said: "The <s>Padmā</s> world-realm, O son of good family, is perpetually illuminated by the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>. There, when the flowers close and the birds become quiet, and the Blessed One and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> sport in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and experience the bliss of the joy of liberation, then it is known as night. But when those flowers are stirred by the breeze, and the birds sing delightfully, and a rain of flowers showers down, and in the four directions supremely fragrant, delightful, gentle, pleasantly touching breezes blow, and the Blessed One, having risen from <s>samādhi</s>, <s>Padmottara</s>, surpassing the discourse of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), teaches the <s>Dharma</s> as the <s>bodhisattva</s>-collection to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> — by that, daytime is known there. And there, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> are never separated from the word '<s>Buddha</s>,' the word '<s>Dharma</s>,' (

body.text: atha khalu ratnavairocano bodhisattvo bhagavantametadavocat - "kiyanmahatī bhagavan sā padmā lokadhātuḥ?, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 18.

children.text: ) kiyacciramasau padmottarastathāgatastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati yenādyarātrāvanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiracirābhisaṃbuddhā?, kiyacciraṃ ca parinirvṛtasya saddharmaḥ sthāsyati?, kiyaccirasthāyinaste bodhisattvā ye padmāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetre pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyiṣyanti vā?, kin te bodhisattvā virahitā buddhadarśanena dharmaśravaṇena saṅghopasthānena utāhosvinneti?, kiṃ nāma cāsītpūrve sā padmā lokadhātuḥ?, kiyaccireṇa vā tatra jinasūryāstaṃgataḥ yasyānantareṇa padmottarena tathāgatenānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā?, kiṃ pratyayamapyekatyā buddhavikurvāṇān buddhaprātihāryān paśyanti ye daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ prātihāryān kurvanti, ekatyā na paśyanti?" /
children.translated_text: ) How long does this <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s> abide, endure, and sustain [himself], teaching the <s>Dharma</s>—he who has recently attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening) in this very night? And how long will the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) endure after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? How long-lived are those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been reborn or will be reborn in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field)? Are those <s>bodhisattvas</s> deprived of seeing <s>Buddhas</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and attending the <s>Saṅgha</s>, or not? And what was the former name of that <s>Padmā</s> world-realm? And after how long did the <s>Jina</s>-sun set there, immediately after which <s>Padmottara</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>? And for what reason do some see the miraculous transformations and supernatural displays of <s>Buddhas</s>—those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who perform supernatural displays in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions—while some do not see [them]?"

body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnavairocana</s> said this to the Blessed One: "How great, O Blessed One, is that <s>Padmā</s> world-realm? (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra sumeruḥ parvatarājā, aṣṭaṣaṣṭhiyojanasahasrāṇyudvedhena caturaśītiyojanasahasrāṇi vistāreṇa / kaścid eva puruṣa āgacchet vīryavān balavān, samādhibalena vā taṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarṣapamātrapramāṇaṃ bhindyāt; gaṇanātikrāntāste sarṣapā bhavanti, na śakyaṃ te sarṣapāḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 19

children.text: ) kenacid gaṇayituṃ sthāpya sarvajñajñānena; yāvantaste sarṣapaphalā bhavanti tāvantaścāturdvīpikā pramāṇā / padmā buddhakṣetramevākīrṇā bodhisattvaiḥ tadyathā sukhāvatī lokadhāturbodhisattvairākīrṇā / padmottarasya kulaputra tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya triṃśadantarakalpānyāyuḥpramāṇaṃ tiṣṭhato dhriyato yāpayato dharmaṃ ca deśayataḥ / padmottarasya kulaputra tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya daśāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati / teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ye padmāyāṃ lokadhātau pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyiṣyanti vā teṣāṃ catvāriṃśadantarakalpāyuḥpramāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) be counted by anyone except through omniscient knowledge. As many as those mustard-seed-sized fragments would be, so many four-continent world-systems [would be in the Padmā field]. The <s>Padmā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is entirely filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, just as the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> is filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The lifespan of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, while he abides, endures, and sustains [himself] teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, is thirty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. The true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And the lifespan of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who have been reborn or will be reborn in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm is forty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Just as, for example, son of good family, <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, is sixty-eight thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth. Suppose some man were to come, powerful and strong, and by the force of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) were to grind that <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, into particles the size of mustard seeds; those mustard seeds would be beyond counting—those mustard seeds could not (

body.text: pūrvaṃ ca kulaputra sā padmā lokadhātuścandanā nāma babhūva, na tvevaṃ pariśuddhābhūnna tvevam ākīrṇā śuddhasattvairbabhūva yathaitarhi padmā lokadhātuḥ / candanāyāṃ kulaputra lokadhātau candrottamo nāmābhūt tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān, sa cāpi viṃśatyantarakalpān dharmaṃ deśitavān / parinirvāṇakālasamaye (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 20

children.text: ) cāpyekatyā bodhisattvāḥ praṇidhānavaśitayānyadbuddhakṣetraṃ saṃkrāntāḥ / ye cāvaśiṣṭā bodhisattvāsteṣām etadavocan - "adyarātrau madhyame yāme candrottamastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ parinirvāsyati, parinirvṛtasya bhagavato daśāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati / kaḥ saddharmāntardhānasyānantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate?"
children.translated_text: ) some <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by the power of their former aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), transferred to other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. To those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who remained, they said: 'Tonight, in the middle watch of the night, <s>Candrottama</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The true <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Who will attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> immediately after the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.translated_text: And formerly, son of good family, that <s>Padmā</s> world-realm was called <s>Candanā</s> (Sandalwood). But it was not as purified as it is now, nor was it as filled with pure beings as the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm is now. In the <s>Candanā</s> world-realm, son of good family, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candrottama</s> (Supreme Moon), the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. He too taught the <s>Dharma</s> for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. At the time of his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena gaganamudro nāma bodhisattvaḥ, sa pūrvapraṇidhānena candrottamena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena vyākṛtaḥ / "bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputra mama parinirvṛtasya daśābhyantarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati / rātryāḥ prathame yāme mama saddharmo 'ntarahāsyati, tatraiva rātryāḥ paścime yāme tvamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, padmottaro nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampanno yāvadbuddho bhagavāṃs" / tatkālaṃ te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā yena candrottamastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhagavāṃstenopajagmuḥ, upetya candrottamasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarve te bodhisattvāḥ samādhānabalena nānāprakārairbodhisattvavikurvaiścandrottamasya (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 21

children.text: ) tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā triskṛtvaśca pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā bhagavantametadavocan - "icchāmo vayam bhadanta bhagavan nime daśābhyantarakalpā nirodhamavahitena cittenātināmayituṃ" /
children.translated_text: ) with various kinds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformations. Having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, they said this to the Blessed One: 'We wish, venerable Blessed One, to pass these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> with minds absorbed in cessation (<s>nirodha</s>).'

body.translated_text: Now at that time there was a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Gaganamudra</s> (Sky-Seal). He had been given a prophecy by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, through his former aspiration: 'After my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, son of good family, the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. In the first watch of the night, my true <s>Dharma</s> will disappear; in the last watch of that very night, you will attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. You will become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One.' At that time, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached, all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by the power of <s>samādhi</s>, performed worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s> (

body.text: tatra khalu kulaputra candrottamastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho gaganamudraṃ bodhisattvam mahāsattvamāmantryaitadavocat - "udgṛhṇa tvaṃ kulaputremaṃ sarvajñātākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ sarvātītānāgataistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairyauvarājyābhiṣiktānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ deśitaṃ, ye caitarhi daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti te 'pi buddho bhagavanto yauvarājyābhiṣiktānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ deśayanti, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani buddhā bhagavantaste 'pi yauvarājyābhiṣiktānāṃ bodhisattvānāmimaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ deśayiṣyanti / tadyathā;
body.translated_text: Thereupon, son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> and said: 'Take up, son of good family, this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s> (Entry into the Gate of the <s>Dhāraṇī</s> of the Aspect of Omniscience)—taught by all past and future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been anointed as crown-princes; and those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who presently abide, endure, and sustain [themselves] in all world-realms of the ten directions—they too teach it to <s>bodhisattvas</s> anointed as crown-princes; and those who will become <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in the future—they too will teach this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s> to <s>bodhisattvas</s> anointed as crown-princes. Namely:"

body.text: jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke sammade mahāsammade devāṃ aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭhakke amimakasi (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 22

children.text: ) hilicilitili ruruke mahāruruke jaye durjaye jayamati śānte śāntanirghoṣaṇi amūle ale amūlaparichinne mārasainya vitrāsane mukte muktapariśuddhe abhīte bhayamocane bhāradroharaṇā dānta vidyāvidyā varuttame, nigrahaṃ paravādināṃ dharmavādināmanugrahaṃ ārakṣā dharmavādināṃ caturṇāṃ smṛtyupasthānānām adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>hilicilitili ruruke mahāruruke jaye durjaye jayamati śānte śāntanirghoṣaṇi amūle ale amūlaparichinne mārasainya vitrāsane mukte muktapariśuddhe abhīte bhayamocane bhāradroharaṇā dānta vidyāvidyā varuttame</s> — [this brings about] the restraint of opponents and the assistance of <s>Dharma</s>-speakers, the protection of <s>Dharma</s>-speakers — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> (resolution) illuminating the path of the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness).

body.translated_text: <s>jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke sammade mahāsammade devāṃ aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭhakke amimakasi</s> (

body.text: buddhakāśaye amama nimama avevi arthe arthani stīraṇe lokādhimukte sandadha paribhāvane, caturṇāmāryavaṃśānāṃ adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadā /
body.translated_text: <s>buddhakāśaye amama nimama avevi arthe arthani stīraṇe lokādhimukte sandadha paribhāvane</s> — [this is] the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the four <s>āryavaṃśas</s> (noble lineages).

body.text: bhāṣīthe bhāṣaṇe dhāre dhārayati gupte śubhe śubhaprade tatphale agraphale 'niṣphale nilaha samukta amukta nirmukte atravita vimuktavati vilaphala ayukta iviti diviti ratitula tulamaṃ ahiṃsāma ititāva atvānatvāna sarvaloka anaka livindha abhūsare hatamatte veśāgravate aphala kaphala, trayāṇām ārakṣitānāṃ adhimuktipadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>bhāṣīthe bhāṣaṇe dhāre dhārayati gupte śubhe śubhaprade tatphale agraphale 'niṣphale nilaha samukta amukta nirmukte atravita vimuktavati vilaphala ayukta iviti diviti ratitula tulamaṃ ahiṃsāma ititāva atvānatvāna sarvaloka anaka livindha abhūsare hatamatte veśāgravate aphala kaphala</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> path of the three [moral trainings] that are guarded.

body.text: jaḍataḥ aniharavavatavyo idaṃ phalaṃ niyomaphalaṃ samudānāya vibhuṣa paśya sāmantra anumanto akumanto chedāvane mantrastā daśabala vigrahasthā isusthita sunikhama tīkṣṇamati āloko atitṛṣṇā adimati, pratyutpannabuddhapūrvaprahāre caturṇāṃ samyakprahāṇānāṃ adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>jaḍataḥ aniharavavatavyo idaṃ phalaṃ niyomaphalaṃ samudānāya vibhuṣa paśya sāmantra anumanto akumanto chedāvane mantrastā daśabala vigrahasthā isusthita sunikhama tīkṣṇamati āloko atitṛṣṇā adimati</s> — [directed toward] the assault on the <s>Buddhas</s> of the present and past — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts).

body.text: anye manye mane mamane vire virate śame śamitā viśānte mukte nirakṣame same samasame kṣaye akṣaye ajiti śānte samiṣṭhe dhāraṇī ālokāvabhāse ratnavrate raśmyavate jñānavate meruvate kṣayanidarśane lokapradīpanidarśane, caturṇāṃ pratisaṃvidāmadhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>anye manye mane mamane vire virate śame śamitā viśānte mukte nirakṣame same samasame kṣaye akṣaye ajiti śānte samiṣṭhe dhāraṇī ālokāvabhāse ratnavrate raśmyavate jñānavate meruvate kṣayanidarśane lokapradīpanidarśane</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges).

body.text: cakṣa ābhāsanidarśane jñānālokanidarśanaṃ ca prabhāsane sarvendriya bhūmātikrante sarvasarve vamāṃ sarve prāthavā kṣayaṃ kare gokāha vadane lokānudarśana vibhū, caturṇāṃ ṛddhipādānām adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidam /
body.translated_text: <s>cakṣa ābhāsanidarśane jñānālokanidarśanaṃ ca prabhāsane sarvendriya bhūmātikrante sarvasarve vamāṃ sarve prāthavā kṣayaṃ kare gokāha vadane lokānudarśana vibhū</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power).

body.text: acale buddhe dṛdhapracale sattve gṛhna siddhi kaṃpati nisiddha smahiddhe parekasire some caṇḍe datve acale acale apare vicivale nipare pracacale prasare anayan prabhyāse kaṃkame prabhāvini same nijase grakrame nayute, indriyāṇāṃ balānām adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>acale buddhe dṛdhapracale sattve gṛhna siddhi kaṃpati nisiddha smahiddhe parekasire some caṇḍe datve acale acale apare vicivale nipare pracacale prasare anayan prabhyāse kaṃkame prabhāvini same nijase grakrame nayute</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) and <s>balas</s> (powers).

body.text: puṣpe supuṣpe drumaparihāre abhayarucire cekaratke akṣayamastu ninile mamale pañcaśiśire lokasya vijñāne nayasaṃgṛhīte ca yukte succendena, saptānāṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>puṣpe supuṣpe drumaparihāre abhayarucire cekaratke akṣayamastu ninile mamale pañcaśiśire lokasya vijñāne nayasaṃgṛhīte ca yukte succendena</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening).

body.text: cakravajre maitra samāpade krānte kete karuṇa rudīkṣayi prītirūpe kṣamasaṃpanne arake varate kharo khare amūle mūle sādhane, caturṇāṃ vaiśāradyānām adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>cakravajre maitra samāpade krānte kete karuṇa rudīkṣayi prītirūpe kṣamasaṃpanne arake varate kharo khare amūle mūle sādhane</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses).

body.text: vartte cakre cakradhare varacakre vare prare hile hile dhare ārūpāvate huhure yathā jibhaṃga niṃbare yathāgne yathāparaṃ cariniśe yathā bhayaririśi (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 25

children.text: ) satyanirhāra jaracavila vīryanirhāra cure mārganirhāra samādhinirhāra prajñānirhāra vimuktinirhāra vimuktijñānadarśananirhāra nakṣatranirhāra candranirhāra sūryanirhāra padāścaturuttaratathāgatena adbhutaṃ niradbhutaṃ saṃbuddhaṃ abuddha ihabuddhaṃ tatrabuddhaṃ nihaṃgamapare alaha dalaha paṇḍare paṇḍare tatrāntalu māṃgagharaṇi pūṭani saṃpūṭani gatapraṃgamanuniruva nāśani nāśabandhani cicchini cicchidra mayova hidiṃgamā vare mare hanane bharaṃ bhare bhinde bhire bhire ruṣare śaraṇe darane pravartte varaṇāḍaye vidranvumā varakhumā brahmacāriṇa indravani dhidhirāyani maheśvaralalani mamasume alamini ekākṣaraci vaṃcani carasti ābhicaṇḍāla sūre sarvasurā āvarasurā punakanitāṃ paṇḍitāṃ āyinakaṇḍi jabhāme gandhare atra runimakare bhirohiṇī siddhamatte vilokamate, buddhādhiṣṭhite dhāraṇīmukhe daśānāṃ balānām adhimuktiprakāśanapadamidaṃ" //
children.translated_text: ) <s>satyanirhāra jaracavila vīryanirhāra cure mārganirhāra samādhinirhāra prajñānirhāra vimuktinirhāra vimuktijñānadarśananirhāra nakṣatranirhāra candranirhāra sūryanirhāra padāścaturuttaratathāgatena adbhutaṃ niradbhutaṃ saṃbuddhaṃ abuddha ihabuddhaṃ tatrabuddhaṃ nihaṃgamapare alaha dalaha paṇḍare paṇḍare tatrāntalu māṃgagharaṇi pūṭani saṃpūṭani gatapraṃgamanuniruva nāśani nāśabandhani cicchini cicchidra mayova hidiṃgamā vare mare hanane bharaṃ bhare bhinde bhire bhire ruṣare śaraṇe darane pravartte varaṇāḍaye vidranvumā varakhumā brahmacāriṇa indravani dhidhirāyani maheśvaralalani mamasume alamini ekākṣaraci vaṃcani carasti ābhicaṇḍāla sūre sarvasurā āvarasurā punakanitāṃ paṇḍit��ṃ āyinakaṇḍi jabhāme gandhare atra runimakare bhirohiṇī siddhamatte vilokamate</s> — established by the <s>Buddha</s>, this is the gate of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — this is the <s>adhimukti</s> illuminating the path of the ten <s>balas</s> (powers [of a <s>Tathāgata</s>])."

body.translated_text: <s>vartte cakre cakradhare varacakre vare prare hile hile dhare ārūpāvate huhure yathā jibhaṃga niṃbare yathāgne yathāparaṃ cariniśe yathā bhayaririśi</s> (

body.text: samanantarārabdhe khalu punarbhagavatā asmin sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśe atha tāvadiyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ kaṃpitā prakaṃpitā saṃprakaṃpitā calitā pracalitā saṃpracalitā kṣubhitā prakṣubhitā saṃprakṣubhitā garjitā pragarjitā saṃpragarjitā, unnamati praṇamati saṃpraṇamati / tathārūpaścāvabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ yaddaśasu dikṣu gaṇanāsamatikrāntā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavaḥ udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā babhūva / naiva tasmin samaye sumerucakravāḍamahācakravāḍaḥ cakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti / daśasu dikṣu gaṇanāsamātikrāntā lokadhātavaḥ samāpāṇitalajātā saṃdṛśyante / ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā daśasu dikṣu gaṇanāsamatikrāntāsu lokadhātuṣu prativasanti, ye samādhidhāraṇīkṣāntipratilabdhāḥ, te tathāgatabalena svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣvantarhitā imāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātumāgatvā gṛdhrakūṭe parvate bhagavataḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntā, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā nānāprakārairvividhairbodhisattvavikurvitairbhagavataḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tatraiva niṣeduḥ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaśravaṇārthaṃ / gaṇanāsamatikrāntāśca devanāgayakṣāsurakumbhāṇḍapiśācā (

children.translated_text: <s>KpSū</s> 27

children.text: ) yena gṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvato yena ca bhagavāṃstenopajagmuḥ, upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirabhivandya, ekānte niṣedurimaṃ ca sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ śravaṇārthāṃ / ye cātra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sannipatitāste sarve padmāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paśyanti sma, padmottaraṃ ca tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ mahatā bodhisattvagaṇena parivṛtaṃ / samanantarodāhṛtasya cāsya bhagavatā sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśasya dvāsaptabhirgaṅgānadīvālikāsamairbodhisattvairmahāsattvairiyaṃ dhāraṇī pratilabdhā, dhāraṇīpratilabdhāśca te bodhisattvā daśasu dikṣu gaṇanāsamatikrāntān lokadhātusthān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyanti sma, sarvāṃśca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyanti sma / āścaryaprāptāste samādhibalena bodhisattvavikurvitena ca buddhapūjāṃ kṛtvā tasthuḥ /
children.translated_text: ) they went toward <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain and toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), and having approached and bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with their heads, they sat down apart for the purpose of hearing this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> (Entry into the Gateway of the Dhāraṇī of the Aspect of Omniscience). And all the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who had assembled there beheld the <s>Padmā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, surrounded by a great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And immediately after this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> was proclaimed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was attained by <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> equal in number to seventy-two Gaṅgā river-sands, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> beheld in the ten directions the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> dwelling in world-realms beyond calculation, and beheld all the arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities. Filled with wonder, by the power of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) and by the miraculous transformations of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, they performed worship of the <s>Buddha</s> and remained standing.

body.translated_text: Immediately upon the Blessed One's beginning to speak this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s>, this great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) shook in six ways: it trembled, trembled greatly, trembled very greatly; it shook, shook greatly, shook very greatly; it quaked, quaked greatly, quaked very greatly; it thundered, thundered greatly, thundered very greatly; it rose up, bowed down, bowed down greatly. And such a radiance appeared that in the ten directions, world-realms beyond counting, equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, became clearly visible with a magnificent radiance. At that time, neither <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, nor <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> came within the range of sight. World-realms beyond counting in the ten directions appeared as if upon the palm of one's hand. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who dwelt in world-realms beyond counting in the ten directions—those who had attained <s>samādhi</s>, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience)—by the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having disappeared from their respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, arrived in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, approached the Blessed One on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, performed worship of the Blessed One with various kinds of <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformations, and sat down there for the purpose of hearing the <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s>. And <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s> beyond counting (

body.text:
bhagavāṃstān evam āha - "imaṃ kulaputra sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ bodhisattvo
mahāsattvo bhāvayamānaścaturaśītidhāraṇīmukhaśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhate, dvāsaptatiśca dhāraṇīmukhasahasrāṇi pratilabhate, ṣaṣṭiṃ ca samādhimukhasahasrāṇi pratilabhate / imāṃ ca dhāraṇīṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 28.

children.text: ) pratilabdho bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāmaitrīṃ pratilabhate mahākaruṇāṃ pratilabhate / kevalamasya samādheḥ pratilābhāya bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣān dharmān avabudhyate sarvajñajñānaṃ ca pratilabhate / iha ca sakalabuddhadharmāṇāṃ parigrahaḥ / imāṃ ca dhāraṇīṃ svabhāvena buddhvā buddhā bhagavantaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmāṃ deśayanti, na cātikṣipraṃ parinirvāyanti /
children.translated_text: ) — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has attained it attains great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and attains great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). Solely through the attainment of this <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> comprehends the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening) and attains the knowledge of omniscience. And herein is the encompassing of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. And having realized this <s>dhāraṇī</s> by its own nature, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings and do not too quickly enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation).

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to them thus: "A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, O son of good family, who cultivates this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>, attains eighty-four hundred-thousand <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, and attains seventy-two thousand <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, and attains sixty thousand <s>samādhi</s>-gateways. And this <s>dhāraṇī</s> (

body.text: paśyata kulaputrāsyāḥ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśāyā dhāraṇyā anubhāvenāyaṃ mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya prādurbhūtaḥ, mahāṃścābhāso yenāvabhāsenānantāparyantā buddhakṣetrā udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā, yenāvabhāsenānantāparyantebhyo buddhakṣetrebhya ime 'nantāparyantā bodhisattvā abhyāgatāḥ, imaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ śravaṇārthaṃ / ye ceha sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanantāparyantā devāḥ kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā nāgā yakṣāsuramanuṣyāmanuṣyā vā imāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ śroṣyanti, te sahaśravaṇena sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśasyāvaivartino bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / likhamānaścāvirahito bhavati buddhadarśanena dharmaśravaṇena saṅghopasthānena yāvadanuttareṇa parinirvāṇena; (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 29.

children.text: ) svādhyāyamānaśca bodhisattva imaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ sarvāṇi gāḍhakarmāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ kṣapayati, janmaparivartena ca prathamāṃ bhūmimākrāmati; bhāvayamānaśca bodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ, yadi tasya bodhisattvasya pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāṇi syurupacitāṇi tānyapyasya parikṣayaṃ gacchanti, yena janmaparivartena ca prathamāṃ bhūmimavakrāmati; yasya nāstyanantaryāṇi tasya tena janmanā sarvāṇyanyāni karmāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ gacchanti, janmaparivartena ca prathamāṃ bhūmimavakrāmati / yo 'pi na bhāvayati na svādhyāyati śṛṇvanaśca dharmabhāṇakasya paṭṭaṃ bandhati, tasya gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanto dhriyanto yāpayantaḥ anyalokadhātusthāḥ sādhukāramanupradāsyanti, te 'pi buddhā bhagavanto vyākariṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, na cireṇa cāsau bodhisattvaḥ paṭṭaparityāgena yauvarājye 'bhiṣicyate, ekajātipratibaddhaśca bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / evameva yaḥ kaścid gandhena pūjāṃ karoti so 'pi na cireṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhigandhasya lābhī bhavati, puṣpeṇa pūjāṃ kṛtvā (
children.translated_text: ) and the <s>bodhisattva</s> who recites this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> completely exhausts all heavy <s>karmas</s> (actions) without remainder, and within one lifetime-cycle enters upon the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). And the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who cultivates this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> — even if that <s>bodhisattva</s> has committed the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) <s>karmas</s>, even those are completely exhausted for him, and within one lifetime-cycle he enters upon the first <s>bhūmi</s>. For one who has not committed the <s>ānantarya</s> [karmas], all other <s>karmas</s> are completely exhausted without remainder within that very lifetime, and within one lifetime-cycle he enters upon the first <s>bhūmi</s>. And even one who neither cultivates nor recites but merely hears and binds the turban of the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma) — <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river, abiding and dwelling in other world-realms, will give him their approval, and those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> will also confer upon him the prophecy of supreme perfect awakening, and before long that <s>bodhisattva</s>, by the relinquishing of the turban, will be consecrated into the position of crown prince, and he will become bound by a single birth to supreme perfect awakening. Likewise, whoever makes an offering with incense will also before long obtain the fragrance of supreme perfect awakening; having made an offering with flowers (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 30.
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 31.

children.text: ) buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyanti / evameva daśabhyo digbhyo gaṇanāsamatikrāntebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo gaṇanāsamatikrāntā bodhisattvāścandanāṃ lokadhātumupasaṃkrāntāścandrottamasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya vandanāya paryupāsanāya, idam eva sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ śrotuṃ" //
children.translated_text: ) beheld the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Likewise, from <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond calculation in the ten directions, <s>bodhisattvas</s> beyond calculation arrived at the <s>Candanā</s> world-realm for the worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One — to hear this very <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>."

body.translated_text: Behold, O sons of good family, by the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>, this great earthquake has occurred, and a great radiance — by which radiance infinite and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were pervaded with magnificent brilliance, by which radiance from infinite and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> these infinite and boundless <s>bodhisattvas</s> have come for the purpose of hearing this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>. And whatever infinite and boundless <s>devas</s> (gods) of the desire realm, <s>devas</s> of the form realm, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, humans, or non-humans in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm shall hear this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> — by the mere hearing, they become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) from supreme perfect awakening. And the one who copies it is never separated from seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, attending upon the <s>Saṅgha</s>, up to and including supreme <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; (

body.text: tatra kulaputra candrottamastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bodhisattvān mahāsattvān āmantrayate - "abhijānāmyahaṃ kulaputra ye bodhisattvā ekajātipratibaddhāsta imān daśāntarakalpān nirodhām avahitena cetasā viharitvāvaśiṣṭā bodhisattvā asya gaganamudrasya bodhisattvasya sakāśādimān daśāntarakalpān imameva sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ śrutavanto 'bhūvan" / imān daśāntarakalpān dharmaṃ śrutvā daśasu dikṣu teṣu gaṇanāsamatikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu teṣāṃ gaṇanātikrāntānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ bhagavatāmantike cittamabhiprasādya tena cittaprasādahetunāvaruptakuśalamūlā bhūtvā nānāvidhairbodhisattvavikurvitaiḥ candrottamasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā, bhagavantametadavocan - "eṣāṃ bhadanta (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 32.

children.text: ) daśānāmantarakalpānām atyayena gaganamudro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttaraṃ dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyati?" / candrottama āha - "evameva kulaputremam, eṣām daśānām antarakalpānāmatyayena gaganamudro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, tasyāmeva rātryāmatyayena dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyati, bodhisattvānāmiha daśāntarakalpānidameva sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ deśayiṣyati / tatra yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāntikāddharmaṃ śroṣyati taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā kuśalamulānyavaropayitvā, yasmin samaye gaganamudro bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate; so 'bhisaṃbuddhabodhiṃ dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravaracakraṃ avaivartikacakraṃ pravartayitvā bahubodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāvaivartikāṃ sthāpayitvā, ye bodhisattvā iha daśāntarakalpān tasya sakāśādimaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ dharmaṃ deśāmānaṃ śroṣyanti te tasmin samaye dharmaṃ śrutvā ekajātipratibaddhā bhaviṣyanti, ye tu kalpaṃ śroṣyanti te bodhisattvāstasmin samaye bhūmimavakramiṣyanti, avaivartikāśca bhaviṣyanti (
children.translated_text: ) after the passing of these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, will the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> turn the supreme righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>?' <s>Candrottama</s> said: 'Even so, O sons of good family — after the passing of these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> will attain supreme perfect awakening, and during the passing of that very night he will turn the righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and will teach to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> this very <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> shall hear the <s>Dharma</s> in his presence, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> and having planted roots of merit — at whatever time the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> attains supreme perfect awakening, he, having attained awakening, having turned the righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, the supreme wheel, the wheel of non-retrogression, and having established many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in non-retrogression — those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> shall hear this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> being taught by him, they at that time, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, will become bound by a single birth; and those who shall hear for a <s>kalpa</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> at that time will enter upon a <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) and will become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 33.

) anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, tasminneva samaye imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ paryantato lapsyante" ityuktvā, candrottamastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ vividhāni buddhaviṣayaprātihāryāṇi saṃdarśayitvā, gaganamudrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nārāyaṇaṃ samādhiṃ nidarśayitvā, vajramayamātmabhāvamadhitiṣṭhati prabhāvyūhaṃ samādhiṃ nidarśayati sma / yena pravartitaṃ dharmacakramiha daśāntarakalpān bodhisattvānāmidaṃ
sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu buddhānubhāvena lakṣaṇānuvyañjanairavabhāsitaḥ saṃdṛśyate, vajramaṇḍalasamādhiṃ nidarśayati / yena bodhyāsane supravartitadharmacakro bodhisattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, cakramālaṃ samādhiṃ nidarśayati / yena dharmacakraṃ pravartayamāno bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi avaivartikāṃ sthāpayati / dharmacakrapravartanāyeti viditvā gaganamudro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'parimitena bodhisattvasaṅghena bhagavatāḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā svakasvakeṣu kūṭāgāreṣu praviśya sthitāścandrottamo 'pi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastāmeva rātrimanupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaste (
children.translated_text: ) from supreme perfect awakening, and at that very time they will attain this <s>dhāraṇī</s> in its completeness.' Having spoken thus, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having displayed to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> various miraculous manifestations of the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain, having shown to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> the <s>Nārāyaṇa samādhi</s>, he empowered a vajra-like body, and displayed the <s>Prabhāvyūha samādhi</s> (Array of Radiance concentration). Having turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> he teaches this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and by the power of the <s>Buddha</s> is seen in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> resplendent with the marks and minor marks, and displays the <s>Vajramaṇḍala samādhi</s>. Having well turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> at the seat of awakening, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and displays the <s>Cakramāla samādhi</s> (Garland of Wheels concentration). By turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, he establishes many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of beings in non-retrogression. Knowing that the time for turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> [had come], the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s>, together with an immeasurable assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having performed worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, entered their respective pavilions and remained there. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, during that very night, entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder. And those (

children.text: ) ca bodhisattvāstasyāmeva rātryāmatyayāt tasya bhagavataḥ śarīre pūjāṃ kṛtvā svakasvakeṣu kūṭāgāreṣu praviśanti sma / apare punarbodhisattvāḥ svakasvakaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gatāḥ / ye ca tatra bodhisattvā ekajātipratibaddhāste nirodhasamādhānenaitān daśāntarakalpān atināmayanti / gaganamudro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhisattvān mahāsattvān ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati, teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ daśāntarakalpān kuśalamūlānyavaropitavān / so 'dyarātrāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ: tena cādya dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ, mahāprātihāryaṃ kṛtaṃ, anekāni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi avaivartikānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāni / asmin khalu punaḥ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśe bhāṣyamāṇe aśītīnāṃ bodhisattvanayutaśatasahasrāṇām anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilabdhā, dvānavatiśca prāṇakoṭyo 'vaivartikāṃ sthāpitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, dvāsaptatibhiśca bodhisattvanayutairiyaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśā dhāraṇī pratilabdhā, gaṇanātikrāntānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni" //
children.translated_text: ) <s>bodhisattvas</s>, after the passing of that very night, having performed worship of the body of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, entered their respective pavilions. Other <s>bodhisattvas</s> went to their respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> there who were bound by a single birth passed through these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> by means of the <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-attainment). The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s>, addressing the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, and during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> he planted roots of merit for those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. He has tonight attained supreme perfect awakening, and today the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> has been turned, a great miraculous display has been performed, and many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of beings have been established in non-retrogression from supreme perfect awakening. And while this <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s> was being spoken, eighty <s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained forbearance regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>, and ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of beings were established in non-retrogression from supreme perfect awakening, and seventy-two <s>nayutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained this <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>, and beings beyond calculation — <s>devas</s> and humans — generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: "There, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, addressed the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>: 'I recall, O sons of good family, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound by a single birth — they, having dwelt in cessation with absorbed minds for these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), are the remaining <s>bodhisattvas</s> who, during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, in the presence of this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s>, heard this very <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī-mukha-praveśa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva-piṭaka</s>.' Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> during these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, they generated faith in the presence of those <s>Bhagavāns</s> beyond calculation who abide, dwell, and sustain themselves in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond calculation in the ten directions, and by that cause of generating faith, having planted roots of merit, by manifold miraculous transformations of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, they performed worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable One, (

body.text: atha khalu ratnacandravairocano bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - "katamairbhadanta bhagavan dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate?" /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Ratnacandravairocana</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "With what <s>dharmas</s> (qualities), O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, must a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> be endowed in order to attain this <s>dhāraṇī</s>?"

body.text: bhagavān āha - "caturbhiḥ kulaputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate / katamaiścaturbhi?, iha bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścaturṣvāryavaṃśeṣu vyavasthito bhavati / katameṣu caturṣu?, iha bodhisattvo mahāsattva itaretareṇa cīvareṇa saṃtuṣṭo bhavati / itaretaracīvarasaṃtuṣṭaśca varṇavādī bhavati / sa na cīvarahetorapratirūpāṃ eṣaṇāṃ samāpadyate / alabdhacīvaro na paritapyate, labdhvā ca cīvaramaraktaḥ paribhuṅkte, asakto 'gṛddho 'grathito 'mūrcchito 'navadhyavasito 'nadhyavasānamāpannaḥ, ādīnavadarśī niḥsaraṇaṃ prajānaṃ paribhuṅkte / asmin prathame āryavaṃśe vyavasthito bhavati bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / yathā cīvaram evaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ śayyāsanaṃ / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva itaretareṇa glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāreṇa saṃtuṣṭo bhavati / itaretaraglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārasaṃtuṣṭaśca varṇavādī bhavati / sa (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 36.

children.text: ) glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārahetorapratirūpameṣaṇāṃ na samāpadyate / so 'labdhyaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyaṃ na paritapyate, pratilabdhvāraktaḥ paribhuṅkte 'gṛddho hyagrathito 'mūrcchito 'navadhyavasito 'nadhyavasānamāpanna ādīnavadarśī niḥsaraṇaṃ prajānaṃ paribhuṅkte / eṣu caturṣvāryavaṃśeṣu vyavasthito bhavati / ebhiścaturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate bhāvayati ca /
children.translated_text: ) does not engage in improper seeking for the sake of medicine and provisions for illness. Not having obtained medicine for illness, he does not grieve; having obtained it, he uses it without attachment, without greed, without bondage, without infatuation, without being fixed upon it, without having reached a state of fixation, seeing the danger and knowing the escape, he uses it. He is established in these four <s>āryavaṃśas</s> (noble lineages). Endowed with these four qualities, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> obtains and cultivates this <s>dhāraṇī</s>.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Endowed with four qualities, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> obtains this <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Which four? Here, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is established in the four <s>āryavaṃśas</s> (noble lineages). Which four? Here, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is content with whatever <s>cīvara</s> (robe) he receives. Being content with whatever robe, he speaks in praise of contentment. He does not engage in improper seeking for the sake of robes. Not having obtained a robe, he does not grieve; and having obtained a robe, he uses it without attachment, without greed, without bondage, without infatuation, without being fixed upon it, without having reached a state of fixation, seeing the danger and knowing the escape, he uses it. In this first noble lineage is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> established. As with robes, so too with <s>piṇḍapāta</s> (almsfood) and <s>śayyāsana</s> (bedding-and-seat). Furthermore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is content with whatever <s>glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāra</s> (medicine and provisions for illness). Being content with whatever medicine and provisions for illness, he speaks in praise of contentment. He (

body.text: aparaiḥ pañcabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate / katamaiḥ pañcabhir?, iha bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ātmanā śīlavāṃ viharati, prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtaḥ, ācāragocarasaṃpanno 'ṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī, samādāya śikṣati śikṣāpadeṣu, parānapi śīlavirahitāṃ dṛṣṭvā śīlasaṃpade samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena prathamena dharmaṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ dṛṣṭivyasanagatāṃ sattvāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyāṃ vyutthāpya samyagdṛṣṭyāṃ samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena dvitīyena (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 37.

children.text:
) dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nācāravyasanagatāṃ sattvān samyagācāre samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena tṛtīyena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / punaraparam āśayavipannān sattvān āśayasaṃpattau samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena caturtheṇa dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne saṃprasthitān sattvān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena pañcamena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / ebhiḥ pañcabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate /
aparaiḥ ṣaḍbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate / katamaiḥ ṣaḍbhir?, iha bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svayameva bahuśruto bhavati śrutādhāraḥ śrutasannicayaḥ, tasya ye te dharmā ādau kalyāṇā madhye kalyāṇāḥ paryavasāne kalyāṇāḥ svarthāḥ suvyañjanāḥ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) — with this quality is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed. Furthermore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> encourages, disciplines, establishes, and confirms beings who have fallen into misconduct in right conduct; with this third quality is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed. Furthermore, he encourages, disciplines, establishes, and confirms beings whose dispositions have gone astray in the accomplishment of right disposition; with this fourth quality is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed. Furthermore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> directs beings who have set out in the vehicle of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) toward the supreme perfect
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 38.

children.text: ) pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ abhivadamānā abhivadanti, tadrūpā anena dharmā bahavaḥ śrutā bhavanti dhṛtā vacasā paricitā manasā anvīkṣitā dṛṣṭyā supratividhāḥ, sa evaṃ bahuśrutaḥ samānaḥ parān aśrutān sattvān bāhuśrutye samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena prathamena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bhavati / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nīrṣyako bhavati amatsarī, sa parān īrsyāmātsaryābhibhūtān sattvān anīrṣyāyām tyāgasaṃpadi ca samādāpayati yāvat pratiṣṭhāpayati; anena dvitīyena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhavati / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāmaviheṭhanajātīyo bhavati abhayapradātā, nānopadravairupadrūtān sattvān upadravebhyaḥ parimocayati, akuhakaśca bhavatyalapako 'śaṭhaśca bhavatyamāyāvī śūnyatayā ca bahulīviharati / ebhiḥ ṣaḍbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate /
children.translated_text: ) the pure, pristine <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life), proclaiming it they proclaim. By this quality, many <s>dharmas</s> have been heard, retained, recited verbally, investigated mentally, examined with insight, and thoroughly penetrated. Being thus learned, he encourages, disciplines, establishes, and confirms other unlearned beings in great learning; with this first quality is he endowed.
