Furthermore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is free from envy and free from miserliness; he encourages beings overcome by envy and miserliness in freedom from envy and in the accomplishment of generosity, and so on until he confirms them; with this

body.translated_text: Endowed with five other qualities, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> obtains this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s> (the dhāraṇī of entry into the gateway of the form of omniscience). Which five? Here, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> himself abides in moral conduct, restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint, endowed with proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, having undertaken the training he trains in the training rules; and seeing others lacking in moral conduct, he encourages, disciplines, establishes, and confirms them in the accomplishment of moral conduct. With this first quality is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed. Furthermore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having the right view (

body.text: evaṃrūpairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvān samāsavistareṇa saptavarṣāṇīmān (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 39.

children.text: ) drāmiḍamantrapadāṃ triḥ kṛtvā divā pañcamaṇḍalena niṣadya kāyagatāṃ smṛtimupasthāpya śūnyatāvihāreṇa imā evaṃ dramiḍā mantrapadā utsārayitavyāḥ / uttiṣṭhatā samantato daśasu dikṣu tiṣṭhato dhriyato yāpayato buddhān bhagavataḥ smaratā satataṃ buddhānusmṛtiṃ bhāvayatā saptānāṃ varṣāṇāṃ atyayena imāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇīṃ pratilabhate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / asyā dhāraṇyāḥ pratilambhād bodhisattvo mahāsattvastadrūpam āryaṃ prajñācakṣuḥ pratilabhate, yena prajñācakṣuṣā daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tiṣṭhato dhriyato yāpayato mahāprātihāryavidarśayataḥ sarvāṃ paśyati, teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ smitavidarśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā caturaśītidhāraṇīmukhasahasrāṇi pratilabhate, dvāsaptatiśca samādhimukhasahasrāṇi pratilabhate, ṣaṣṭiśca dharmamukhasahasrāṇi pratilabhate / asyāṃ ca sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāmaitrīṃ pratilabhate, mahākaruṇāṃ pratilabhate / yena bodhisattvena mahāsattveneyaṃ dhāraṇī pratilabdhā bhavati tena yadi pañcānantaryāṇī karmāṇyācīrṇāni bhavati, tasya janmāntareṇa (
children.translated_text: ) <s>Drāmiḍa</s> mantra-verses, having recited them three times, sitting during the day in the five-fold <s>maṇḍala</s> posture, having established mindfulness directed toward the body, abiding in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) — these <s>Drāmiḍa</s> mantra-verses should be recited. Rising up, recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who stand, endure, and sustain in the ten directions all around, constantly cultivating <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Buddha) — after the passage of seven years, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> obtains this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s>. Through the attainment of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> obtains such a noble eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), by which eye of wisdom, in the ten directions
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 40.

children.text: ) parikṣayaṃ gacchanti, tṛtīye janmani niravaśeṣaṃ tāni karmāṇi naṣṭāni bhavanti, daśamīṃ ca bhūmimavakrāmati / yasya tu bodhisattvasya nānantaryāṇi karmāni kṛtāni bhavanti tasyānyāni sarvakarmāvaraṇāni parikṣayaṃ gacchanti, janmaparivartena daśabhūmīḥ samatikrāmati, na cirasyedānīṃ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣān dharmān pratilabhate, sarvajñajñānaṃ ca pratilabhate /
children.translated_text: ) are completely exhausted; in the third birth, those <s>karmas</s> are entirely destroyed, and he enters the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). But for a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has not committed the <s>ānantarya</s> (acts of immediate retribution), all other <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obstructions) are completely exhausted; in the course of a single birth he transcends the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, and before long he obtains the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (qualities conducive to awakening) and obtains <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (the knowledge of omniscience).

body.translated_text: Endowed with qualities of such a nature, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing all of these in brief and in detail, for seven years, these (

body.text: evaṃ bahukaraḥ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmayaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaḥ, satatasamitaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ smitavidarśanāt prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃrūpeṇa ṛddhiviṣayena samanvāgato bhavati / yad gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā nānāvidhasamādhikṣāntidhāraṇīṃ pratilabdhāḥ, imameva buddhakṣetramāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Thus greatly beneficial, O son of good family, is this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s> (gateway of entry into the dhāraṇī of the form of omniscience) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. Constantly and continuously, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having seen the miraculous display from the smile-manifestation of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, becomes endowed with such a domain of supernatural power. Having worshipped the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River in world-realms equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, and having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and having obtained various <s>samādhis</s>, <s>kṣāntis</s> (forbearances), and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, they come to this very <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field).

body.text: evaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaḥ karmaparikṣayāya saṃvartate kuśalābhivṛddhaye / ye ca kulaputra sattvā asyāḥ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇyā nāma śroṣyanti (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 41.

children.text: ) tasya ca bhagavataścandrottamasya tathāgatasya, teṣāṃ sarvakarmāvaraṇāni kṣayaṃ gamiṣyanti, niyatāśca bhaviṣyanti anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbuddheḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) and of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s> — all their <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obstructions) will be exhausted, and they will become destined for supreme perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: Thus, O son of good family, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, the <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s> (gateway of entry into the dhāraṇī of the form of omniscience) conduces to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> and to the increase of wholesome qualities. And those beings, O son of good family, who will hear the name of this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s> (

body.text: atha te bodhisattvā evamāhuḥ - "asmābhirbhadanta bhagavan gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu atīteṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu tiṣṭhatsu dhriyatsu yāpayatsu iyaṃ dhāraṇī śrutā ca pratilabdhā ca" / aparevamāhuḥ - "asmābhirdvigaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ", apare "tribhiḥ", apare "caturbhiḥ", apare "pañcabhiḥ", apare "ṣaḍbhiḥ", apare "saptabhiḥ", apare "aṣṭabhiḥ" / apare evam āhuḥ, "asmābhirnavasu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu samyaksaṃbuddheṣu atīteṣu tiṣṭhatsu dhriyamāneṣu yāpayatsu iyaṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇīṃ śrutvā sarvākāreṇa pratilabdhā" //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> spoke thus: "By us, O Venerable Blessed One, in the presence of past <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, while they stood, endured, and sustained, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was heard and obtained." Others spoke thus: "By us, in the presence of <s>Buddhas</s> equal to two times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>"; others said "three"; others "four"; others "five"; others "six"; others "seven"; others "eight." Others spoke thus: "By us, in the presence of nine times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River past Perfectly Awakened Ones, while they stood, endured, and sustained, this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s>

body.text: maitreyastu bodhisattvo mahāsattva evamāha - "mayā daśagaṅgānadīvālikāsamān kalpān atikramya santāraṇo nāma mahākalpo 'bhūt / tatredaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitaṃ nāmābhūt / sālendrarājo nāma buddho 'bhūd vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathīḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān / anantakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṇa bhikṣusaṅghena parivṛtaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 42.

children.text: ) tathā gaṇanātikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛta imāmeva sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśāṃ dhāraṇīṃ bhāṣitavān, tasyāntike mayeyaṃ dhāraṇī śrutā bhāvanā paripūryādhigatāḥ / evamaprameyeṣu kalpeṣu aprameyatareṣu asaṃkhyeyatareṣu atītānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ asaṃkhyeyairbodhisattvavikurvitaisteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā, ekaikasya buddhasya sakāśe aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyānyatulyāni aprameyāṇi kuśalamūlānyavaropya puṇyaskandhaḥ parigṛhītastenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena bahubhirbuddhasahasrairvyākṛtaḥ / kālamavekṣyāhaṃ praṇidhānaviṣayenaiva ciraṃ saṃsāre saṃsṛto, yena me pūrvaṃ saṃsāre saṃsarato 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirnābhisaṃbuddhā, so 'hamidānīṃ bhagavatā yauvarājyenābhiṣikto, vimuktipaṭṭaśca me prajñāśirasi baddho 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" /
children.translated_text: ) and likewise surrounded by <s>bodhisattvas</s> beyond calculation, he taught this very <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s>. In his presence, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was heard by me, and through cultivation it was fulfilled and realized. Thus, in immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, even more immeasurable, even more incalculable, having worshipped the past Perfectly Awakened Ones who stood, endured, and sustained, with incalculable <s>bodhisattva</s>-transformations, having worshipped those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, having planted in the presence of each and every <s>Buddha</s> immeasurable, incalculable, incomparable, boundless roots of merit, the mass of merit was gathered — by those roots of merit I have greatly

body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> spoke thus: "Having passed beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to ten times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, there was a great <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Santāraṇa</s>. There, this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) was named <s>Sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣita</s> ('Adorned with All Ornaments'). There was a <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Sālendrarāja</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was surrounded by an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) numbering infinite <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands (

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvametad avocat - "evametan maintreya yastvaṃ sālendrarājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādimāṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇīṃ pratilabdhavān / ākāṅkṣamāṇastvaṃ maitreya daśānāṃ kalpānāmatyayenānuttarāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 43.

children.text: ) samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, yathaiva te maitreyāśāparipūrṇāśaktastvaṃ maitreya śīghramevānuttareṇa jñānenānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau praveṣṭuṃ / yacca tvaṃ maitreya iyacciraṃ saṃsāre 'bhiratastat sarvaṃ praṇidhānavaśena kālaprekṣiṇā, tena te maitreya etarhi mamāntikādyauvarājyaṃ parigṛhītaṃ, atītānāmapi te tathāgatānāmantike yauvarājyaṃ parigṛhītaṃ" //
children.translated_text: ) perfect awakening you would fully awaken. Just as your aspirations are fulfilled, O <s>Maitreya</s> — you are capable, O <s>Maitreya</s>, of swiftly entering the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (nirvāṇa-realm) without remainder through supreme knowledge. But that you, O <s>Maitreya</s>, have delighted in <s>saṃsāra</s> for so long — all that is by the power of your <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vow), watching for the right time. Therefore, O <s>Maitreya</s>, you have now received from me the <s>yauvarājya</s> (consecration as crown prince), and in the presence of past <s>Tathāgatas</s> as well, you received the <s>yauvarājya</s>."

body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One said this to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "So it is, <s>Maitreya</s>. You obtained this <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sālendrarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. If you wished, O <s>Maitreya</s>, after the passage of ten <s>kalpas</s>, the supreme (

body.text: tatra bhagavān sarvāvatīṃ parṣadaṃ avalokayate, bodhisattvaparṣadaṃ bhikṣuparṣadaṃ bhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāparṣadaṃ devanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvamanuṣyāmanuṣyaṃ vyavalokya tasyāṃ velāyām imāni mantrapadānyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Thereupon, the Blessed One surveyed the entire assembly — the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), the assembly of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (laymen), and <s>upāsikās</s> (laywomen), and having surveyed the <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, humans, and non-humans, at that moment he uttered these mantra-verses:

body.text: "dāntabhūmiḥ damathabhūmiḥ smṛtibhūmiḥ prajñābhūmirvaiśāradyabhūmiḥ pratisaṃvidbhūmiranutkṣepabhūmiḥ samatāparikṣayopekṣabhūmirjātikṣayabhūmirmanuja vinmujaḥ malanmujaḥ visāgraḥ daśāvate veśataḥ teraṇa vesalagra śamuśavataḥ vimati vimati yopahira (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 44.

children.text: ) regamata vasisakrama iticāravate mekhemudra daharavate prajñākṣābubu dahakramitā sadoṣavantaḥ elaya tilaya ahusuṭā amundhamaṃ arthavati muruvati tehīnadvivā akaneti bakanate samake visābhaṭe iṭe iṭabale atra tatra kuruṣaṃ laruṣaṃ latatha katha sarvantaḥ sarvatarvaḥ aniruddhaḥ dihakhaṭambiphala bahuphala śataphala śīṣṭavate, api devānāṃ bhagavān pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyuktānyadhimuktipadāṇi prakāśayati, eṣu prakāśyamāneṣu ṣaṣṭibhirdevanayutaiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtamabhūt /
children.translated_text: ) <s>regamata vasisakrama iticāravate mekhemudra daharavate prajñākṣābubu dahakramitā sadoṣavantaḥ elaya tilaya ahusuṭā amundhamaṃ arthavati muruvati tehīnadvivā akaneti bakanate samake visābhaṭe iṭe iṭabale atra tatra kuruṣaṃ laruṣaṃ latatha katha sarvantaḥ sarvatarvaḥ aniruddhaḥ dihakhaṭambiphala bahuphala śataphala śīṣṭavate</s> — moreover, the Blessed One illuminates the <s>adhimuktipadāni</s> (syllables of resolute faith) connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) for the gods. When these are being illuminated, sixty <s>nayutas</s> (tens of millions) of gods attained the vision of truth.

body.translated_text: "The stage of taming, the stage of subduing, the stage of mindfulness, the stage of wisdom, the stage of confidence, the stage of analytical knowledge, the stage of non-regression, the stage of equanimity through exhaustion and equipoise, the stage of the exhaustion of birth — manuja vinmujaḥ malanmujaḥ visāgraḥ daśāvate veśataḥ teraṇa vesalagra śamuśavataḥ vimati vimati yopahira (

body.text: tatphalam agraphalaṃ lalaha alaha nilaṃhare vacatakhyā idaṃphalaṃ niyāmaphalaṃ namudaya vibhūkha prajñācakra sunirvṛticakra jñānīcakra, ebhiradhimuktipadairdaśānāṃ devakoṭīnāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni, tatraivāvaivartikā sthitāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>tatphalam agraphalaṃ lalaha alaha nilaṃhare vacatakhyā idaṃphalaṃ niyāmaphalaṃ namudaya vibhūkha prajñācakra sunirvṛticakra jñānīcakra</s> — by these <s>adhimuktipadāni</s> (syllables of resolute faith), the minds of ten <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of gods were generated toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and they became established there as <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing).

body.text: paśya momate anumato akumato akumatī chīdratrake (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 45

children.text: ) mantrasthā deśabala vipravastha iśasthita atimati tīkṣṇamati āloko sterituṣṇa, ebhiradhimuktipadaiścatuḥṣaṣṭīnāṃ nāgasahasrāṇāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni, tatraiva ca avaivartikāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>mantrasthā deśabala vipravastha iśasthita atimati tīkṣṇamati āloko sterituṣṇa</s> — by these <s>adhimuktipadāni</s> (syllables of resolute faith), the minds of sixty-four thousand <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) were generated toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and they became <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) there.

body.translated_text: Behold! <s>momate anumato akumato akumatī chīdratrake</s> (

body.text: aprabhā samadanā ahadyo bhagavadyo karaṇyākṣa siddhamati samantakṣau alabale piṭakaro mahābale ojadaro dharaṇe migalekṣe udākṣa kudākṣa kukākṣa viroyo virūpamukha akṣihasta saṃkṣibala asurovina asuropramardane, ebhiradhimuktipadairdvādaśānāṃ yakṣakoṭīnāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni, tatraivāvaivartikāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>aprabhā samadanā ahadyo bhagavadyo karaṇyākṣa siddhamati samantakṣau alabale piṭakaro mahābale ojadaro dharaṇe migalekṣe udākṣa kudākṣa kukākṣa viroyo virūpamukha akṣihasta saṃkṣibala asurovina asuropramardane</s> — by these <s>adhimuktipadāni</s>, the minds of twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s> were generated toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and they became <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) there.

body.text: arthe pilile tinithe saṃtīrthe katitene nakeme nanamaste ubherabhe mudame madame matime saniha śūre dhāraṇīya sendra sadeva sanāga sayakṣāsuradevā nāga nirukti parivāra niruktalāni smṛti prajñā parivāramati pratilābhī gatidhṛtiparivāra gatidhṛtilābhīḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 46

children.text: ) pūrvakeṣu hiteṣu caritavantaḥ abhiskāmavantaḥ śūravantaḥ ciravīryavantaḥ bhītavantaḥ sitabhāge mārgamudra diśāpakarṣaṇi kṣaparahu oharaṇo devaracatu suramudra yakṣamudra rākṣasamudra vedivedime tape tattape uṣṇāname prakhādye nanava dhāraṇīya āviśa diśāśodhane vākyaśuddhe jihvāśuddhe vāciparikarmaḥ prajñā buddhi smṛti mati gati dhṛti gaṇana pratisaraṇabuddhiḥ jayacakre śūnyacakre vyaya, ebhiradhimuktipadaiḥ ṣaṭpañcāśānāmasurasahasrāṇāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyakasaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāṇi, avaivartikāśca vyavasthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: ) having practiced beneficial deeds in the past, possessing ardent desire, possessing valor, possessing long-sustained effort, possessing caution; <s>sitabhāge mārgamudra diśāpakarṣaṇi kṣaparahu oharaṇo devaracatu suramudra yakṣamudra rākṣasamudra vedivedime tape tattape uṣṇāname prakhādye nanava dhāraṇīya āviśa diśāśodhane vākyaśuddhe jihvāśuddhe vāciparikarmaḥ</s> — wisdom, intelligence, memory, understanding, progress, firmness, enumeration, the intellect of taking refuge; <s>jayacakre śūnyacakre vyaya</s> — by these <s>adhimuktipadāni</s>, the minds of fifty-six thousand <s>asuras</s> (anti-gods) were generated toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and they became established as <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing).

body.translated_text: <s>arthe pilile tinithe saṃtīrthe katitene nakeme nanamaste ubherabhe mudame madame matime saniha śūre dhāraṇīya sendra sadeva sanāga sayakṣāsuradevā nāga nirukti parivāra niruktalāni smṛti prajñā parivāramati pratilābhī gatidhṛtiparivāra gatidhṛtilābhīḥ</s> (

body.text: tatra bhagavān vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇaṃ nāma bodhisattvamāmantrayate sma - "durlabhaṃ kulaputra tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo; durlabhā ime śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaparibhāvitā amī mantrapadāḥ; sattvānāṃ hitāya bodhisattvaguṇaniṣpādanārthaṃ kulaputra tathāgatena (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 47

children.text: ) pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā dānadamasaṃyamakṣāntivīryasamādhiprajñā parigṛhītā bahavo buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāḥ paryupāsitāḥ, kvacid dānān dattaṃ, kvaciccīlaṃ rakṣitaṃ, kvacid brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ, kvacid bhāvanā niṣevitā, kvacit kṣāntirbhāvitā, kvacid vīryamārabdhaṃ, kvacit samādhirniṣpāditā, kvacit prajñā sevitā, bahvaprameyaṃ vividhaṃ nānāprakāraṃ śubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ, yenaitarhi mamānuttaraṃ jñānaṃ pratilabdhaṃ / anekāṃ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṃ kulaputra tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā mṛṣāpaiśunyaparuṣasaṃbhinnapralāpā varjitāḥ, anekavidhaṃ kuśalaṃ vākkarma sevitaṃ bahulīkṛtaṃ, yenaitarhi prabhūtajihvatā pratilabdhā, na hi kulaputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anyathā kathayanti" /
children.translated_text: ) formerly, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, mastered <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>dama</s> (self-control), <s>saṃyama</s> (restraint), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>; sometimes gave gifts, sometimes guarded morality, sometimes practiced celibacy, sometimes cultivated meditation, sometimes developed patience, sometimes undertook effort, sometimes accomplished concentration, sometimes cultivated wisdom; performed abundant, immeasurable, varied, manifold, meritorious actions — by which I have now obtained unsurpassed knowledge. For countless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> formerly, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, abandoned falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and idle chatter; cultivated and made abundant manifold wholesome verbal action — by which I have now obtained the great tongue [sign of a <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>]. For <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, O son of good family, do not speak otherwise [than truthfully]."

body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇa</s> (Assembly of Fearlessness): "Rare, O son of good family, is the appearance in the world of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones; rare are these <s>mantra</s>-syllables permeated by <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), and <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation); for the benefit of beings and for the accomplishment of <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstataḥ parṣadaṃ ṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskārṣīt, yathābhisaṃskṛtenarddhyabhisaṃskāreṇa sarvapuṇyasamavasaraṇaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / mukhācca jihvendriyaṃ nirṇāmayitvā svaṃ mukhamaṇḍalaṃ pracchādya tasmājjihvendriyāt ṣaṣṭiraśmikoṭyaḥ pramuktāstaiśca raśmibhiḥ ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturudāreṇāvabhāsena (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 48

children.text: ) sphuṭo 'bhūt, taiśca raśmibhirnirayatiryagyoniyamalokadevamanuṣyāḥ sphuṭā babhūvuḥ / te ca raśmayo ye nairayikāḥ sattvā agninā prajvalitagātrā dahyante teṣāṃ śītalā vāyavo vānti yeṣāṃ spṛṣṭānāṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ sukhā vedanā prādurbabhūva / ekaikasya ca nairayikasya sattvasya purataḥ buddhanirmitaṃ tiṣṭhati dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtagātraḥ aśītibhiranuvyañjanairvirājitatanuryaṃ dṛṣṭvā te nairayaikāḥ sukhasamarpitā buddhadarśanāpyāyitāśarīrā buddhaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ cintayanto 'sya sattvasyānubhāvenāsmābhiḥ sukhā vedanā pratilabdhā; te bhagavataḥ sakāśe premaprasādaṃ gauravaṃ ca saṃjanayanti /
children.translated_text: ) illuminated with a magnificent radiance, and by those rays the beings in hells, the animal realm, <s>Yama's</s> world, and the realms of gods and humans were illuminated. And those rays — to those beings in hell whose bodies were being burned by blazing fire — cool winds blew upon them, and upon being touched by those [winds], pleasant sensations arose in them for that moment. And before each and every hell-being there stood a <s>Buddha</s>-emanation, with a body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, radiant with eighty minor characteristics, bearing the marks of a hundred merits, with a fathom-wide radiance, proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree, beautiful to behold. And those hell-beings, having seen him, were established in happiness, their bodies refreshed by the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>, and having seen the <s>Buddha</s>, they thought: 'By the power of this being, we have obtained pleasant sensations.' They generated love, faith, and respect toward the Blessed One.

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One applied a supernatural transformation to that assembly, and by the supernatural transformation thus applied, he entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Sarvapuṇyasamavasaraṇa</s> (Assembly of All Merit). And having extended his tongue from his mouth and covered his own face, sixty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of rays were emitted from that tongue, and by those rays this entire billion-world system was (

body.text: bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ kathayati - "bhoḥ sattvā evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣadhvaṃ, "namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṅghāya", nityamevaṃ sukhasamarpitā bhaviṣyatha" / tataste nairayikāḥ sattvā añjaliṃ pragṛhya vācamudīrayanti, "namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṅghāya" / atha te nairayikāḥ sattvāstena kuśalamūlena tena ca cittaprasādena tataścyavitvā ekatyā deveṣūpapannā, ekatyā manuṣyeṣu; ye 'pi śītanarakeṣūpapannāḥ sattvāsteṣām uṣṇā vāyavaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 49

children.text: ) pravāyanti, pūrvavad yāvan manuṣyeṣūpapadyante / evaṃ pretānāṃ piśācānāṃ kṣuttṛṣṇāprajvalitagātrāṇāṃ teṣāṃ te raśmayo bubhukṣāgniṃ nirvāṇaṃ kurvanti, sukhāṃ ca vedanāṃ saṃjanayanti / ekaikasya pretasya nirmitaṃ buddharūpamagrataḥ sthitaṃ bhavati dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaṃ aśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ; taṃ dṛṣṭvā te pretā buddhadarśanāt sukhā prīṇitagātrā evaṃ cintayantaḥ, "asya sattvasyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ sukhā vedanā pratilabdhā" / te bhagavataḥ sakāśe prasādaṃ premagauravaṃ cotpādayanti / bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ kathayati - "eta yūyaṃ sattvā, evaṃ vācamudīrayata, "namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṅghāyā", nityamevaṃ sukhasamarpitā bhaviṣyatha" / tataste pretā añjaliṃ pragṛhyaivaṃ vācamudīrayanti, "namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṅghāya" / atha te pretasattvāstena kuśalamūlena tataścyavitvā kecid deveṣūpapannāḥ ekatyā manuṣyeṣvevaṃ tiraścāṃ saṃcodayanti, evaṃ manuṣyāṃ saṃcodayanti /
children.translated_text: ) — as before, up to their rebirth among humans. Likewise for <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) and <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits) whose bodies were ablaze with hunger and thirst — those rays extinguished the fire of their hunger and generated pleasant sensations in them. Before each hungry ghost there stood an emanated <s>Buddha</s>-form, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, radiant with eighty minor characteristics. Having seen him, those hungry ghosts, joyful in body from the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>, thought: 'By the power of this being, we have obtained pleasant sensations.' They generated faith, love, and respect toward the Blessed One. The Blessed One said to them: 'Come, O beings, utter this speech: "<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṅghāya</s>" — thus you shall always be established in happiness.' Then those hungry ghosts, raising their palms together, uttered the speech: '<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṅghāya</s>.' Then those ghost-beings, by that root of merit, passing away from there, some were reborn among the gods, some among humans. Likewise they exhorted the animals, likewise they exhorted the humans.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said to them: 'O beings, utter this speech: "<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṅghāya</s>" (Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>) — thus you shall always be established in happiness.' Then those hell-beings, raising their palms together, uttered the speech: '<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṅghāya</s>.' Then those hell-beings, by that root of merit and by that mental faith, passing away from there, some were reborn among the gods, some among humans. And those beings who were reborn in the cold hells — warm winds blew upon them (

body.text: gaṇanātikrāntā devamanuṣyā bhagavatsakāśaṃ upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya / tena ca samayena gaṇanātikrāntā devamanuṣyakāyā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 50

children.text: ) anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayām āsuḥ / gaṇanātikrāntāścātra bodhisattvāḥ samādhikṣāntidhāraṇīṃ pratilabdhavantaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) generated their minds toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And innumerable <s>bodhisattvas</s> there attained <s>samādhikṣāntidhāraṇī</s> (the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of patient acceptance in concentration).

body.translated_text: Innumerable gods and humans approached the Blessed One, bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, and sat down to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And at that time, innumerable hosts of gods and humans (

body.text: iti śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīke mahāyānasūtre dvitīyo dhāraṇīmukhaparivartaḥ //2//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, the <s>Dhāraṇīmukhaparivartta</s> (Chapter on the Gateway of <s>Dhāraṇī</s>), in the holy <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of Compassion), a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>. //2//

body.text: III dānavisargas tṛtīyaḥ
body.translated_text: III. The Third [Chapter]: The Outpouring of Generosity (<s>Dānavisarga</s>).

body.text: atha khalu śāntimatir bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavatā svarddhyābhisaṃskāre pratiprasraṃbhite bhagavantam etad avocat / "ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yad anyeṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pariśuddhā buddhakṣetrā apagatakaluṣā apagatapañcakaṣāyā nānāguṇavyūhā buddhakṣetrāḥ, sarve cātra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nānāviddhaguṇaparipūrṇā nānāsukhasamarpitā, nāpi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nāmāpi vidyate, kutaḥ punar upapattiḥ? / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yad bhagavān pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetra upapannaḥ, āyuḥkaṣāye kalpakaṣāye sattvakaṣāye dṛṣṭikaṣāye kleśakaṣāye vartamāne anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ, catasraś ca pariṣadaḥ trīṇī yānāny ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati? / kasmād bhagavatā pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ na parigṛhītaṃ apagatapañcakaṣāyaṃ?" /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Śāntimati</s> (Peaceful Mind), when the Blessed One had relaxed his supernatural display, said this to the Blessed One: "What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that other <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, have pure <s>Buddha</s>-fields, free from impurity, free from the five corruptions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), arrayed with manifold virtues, and all the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> there are endowed with manifold qualities, established in manifold happiness, and the very name of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) does not exist there — let alone their actual birth? What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that the Blessed One has been born in a <s>Buddha</s>-field with the five corruptions — during the corruption of lifespan, the corruption of the <s>kalpa</s> (eon), the corruption of beings, the corruption of views, and the corruption of afflictions — and has awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> with reference to the four assemblies and three vehicles? Why has the Blessed One not taken up a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field free from the five corruptions?"

body.text: bhagavān āha / "praṇidhānavaśena kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇanti, praṇidhānavaśenāpariśuddhaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 52

children.text: ) buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇanti / mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatatvāt kulaputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā apariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhaṇanti / tat kasmād dhetos?, tathā mayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ yenāham etarhy evaṃ pratikaṣṭe pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetra upapannaḥ / tac cṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣīṣye 'haṃ te śāntimate" / "sādhu bhagavān" niti śāntimatir bodhisattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśroṣīt //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Buddha</s>-field. Because they are endowed with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), O son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> take up an impure <s>Buddha</s>-field. For what reason? Because I made such an aspiration by which I am now born in such a difficult <s>Buddha</s>-field with the five corruptions. Listen well and attentively; I shall speak to you, O <s>Śāntimati</s>." "Very well, Blessed One" — thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Śāntimati</s> listened to the Blessed One.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "By the power of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), O son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> take up a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field; by the power of aspiration they take up an impure (

body.text: bhagavāṃs tān idam avocat / "bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputraikagaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu asaṃkhyeyeṣv atikrānteṣu asmin buddhakṣetre dhāraṇo nāma mahākalpo babhūva / tasmiṃś ca mahākalpe buddhakṣetre tasyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ araṇemī nāma rājābhūc caturdvīpakaḥ cakravartī / tasya khalv āraṇeminaḥ samudrareṇur nāma brāhmaṇo 'bhūt purohitaḥ / tasya putro jāto dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ aśītibhir anuvyañjanair virājitaḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇo vyāmaprabhaḥ nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalo 'secanakadarśanaḥ / jātamātrasya ca devaśatasahasraiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā samudragarbha iti nāma sthāpitaṃ / so 'pareṇa samayena niṣkramya keśaśmaśrūṇy avatārya kāṣāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 53

children.text: ) anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ, ratnagarbho nāma tathāgata udapādi, dharmacakrapravartanena sa bhagavān bhahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṃ svargamokṣaphale pratiṣṭhāpitavān / so 'pareṇa samayena bahuśrāvakakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto grāmanagaranigama janapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu caryāṃ cañcūryamāṇo 'nupūrveṇānyataraṃ nagaraṃ anuprāpto, yatrāsau rājā cakravartī vasati / tatra "bahir nagarasya nātidūre jambūvano nāmodyāne ratnagarbhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho viharati sārdham anekaiḥ śrāvakakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrair" iti aśroṣīd, rājāraṇemī "ratnagarbhas tathāgato 'rhan samyakasaṃbuddho 'smākaṃ vijitam anuprāpto jambūvanodyāne viharati anekaiḥ śrāvakakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ / yan nūnam ahaṃ upasaṃkrāmayeyam, upasaṃkramya taṃ tathāgatam satkuryāṃ gurukuryāṃ mānayeyaṃ" / athāraṇemī rājārājarddhyā mahatā ca rājānubhāvenānekaiḥ prāṇikoṭīnayutāśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto nagarān nirjagāma, yena jambūvanodyānaṃ tenopajagāmopetya, yāvad eva yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena yātvā padbhyām evārāmaṃ prāviśad, yena (
children.translated_text: ) he awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) — a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnagarbha</s> (Jewel-Womb) arose. Through the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of <s>Dharma</s>), that Blessed One established many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of living beings in the fruit of heaven and liberation. In due course, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), wandering through villages, towns, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, he arrived at a certain city where that universal sovereign king resided. There, [the news spread:] 'In the <s>Jambū</s> grove, a park not far outside the city, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, dwells together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>.' King <s>Araṇemi</s> [heard this and thought:] 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, has arrived in our domain and dwells in the <s>Jambū</s> grove with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>. Surely I should approach him, and having approached, I should honor, revere, and respect that <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then King <s>Araṇemi</s>, with royal splendor and great royal power, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of living beings, went forth from the city and proceeded to the <s>Jambū</s> grove. Having gone as far as the ground was suitable for a vehicle, he dismounted and entered the park on foot, [going] to where (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 54

children.text: ) ratnagarbhas tathāgatas tenopajagāma; upetya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdad, ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānam araṇeminaṃ ratnagarbhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho dhārmyā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati / anekaparyāyeṇa dhārmyā kathayā saṃdarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvā tūṣṇīm abhūt /
children.translated_text: ) He approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted King <s>Araṇemin</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said this to them: "In the past, O son of good family, when incalculable [<s>kalpas</s>] equal to the sands of a single <s>Gaṅgā</s> river had passed, in this very <s>Buddha</s>-field there was a great <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Dhāraṇa</s> (Sustaining). In that great <s>kalpa</s>, in this <s>Buddha</s>-field, in that four-continent [world], there was a king named <s>Araṇemi</s> (Spokeless), a universal sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>) ruling four continents. That King <s>Araṇemi</s> had a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Samudrareṇu</s> (Ocean-Dust) as his royal priest. A son was born to him, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, radiant with eighty minor characteristics, bearing the marks of a hundred merits, with a fathom-wide radiance, proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree, beautiful to behold. And at his very birth, having been worshipped by hundreds of thousands of gods, he was given the name <s>Samudragarbha</s> (Ocean-Womb). In due course, having gone forth, shaving his hair and beard, and donning ochre robes (

body.text: atha rājāraṇemī utthāyāsanād ekāṃśaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā pādayor nipatya yena ratnagarbhas tathāgatas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ratnagarbham tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham etad avocat / "adhivāsayatu me bhagavān idam traimāsaṃ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena, ahaṃ bhagavantam upasthāsyae cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca" / adhivāsayati kulaputra ratnagarbhas tathāgato rājño 'raṇeminaḥ tūṣṇībhāvena / atha rājāraṇemī ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Araṇemin</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, falling at [the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s] feet, and joining his palms toward <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, spoke thus: 'May the Blessed One consent to accept from me for these three months, together with the community of monks — I shall attend upon the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick, and upon the community of monks as well.' The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, O son of good family, consented to King <s>Araṇemin</s>'s [invitation] by his silence. Then King <s>Araṇemin</s>, having understood the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>'s consent through his silence, bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated him three times, and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

body.text: atha rājāraṇemī koṭṭarājānāhūyāmātyamahāmātrān bhaṭabalāgrapaurajānapadān pauruṣeyān āmantryovāca - "yannūnaṃ grāmaṇyo jānīyurmayā ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha imaṃ traimāsaṃ sarvopakaraṇairupanimantritaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena / so 'haṃ yo me kaścid upabhogaparibhoga upasthānaṃ paricaryāntaḥpuraṃ ca gauraveṇa tatsarvaṃ bhagavato nivedayāmi bhikṣusaṅghasya ca / yad api yuṣmākaṃ paudgalikaṃ upabhogaparibhogopasthānaparicaryāntaḥpuraṃ gauraveṇa tatsarvaṃ bhagavato niryātayata bhikṣusaṅghasya ca" / tairapi niryātitaṃ / gṛhapatiratnamapi bhadramudyānaṃ sarvaṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayaṃ kṛtvā, tasmin nevodyāne bhagavato 'rthāya kūṭāgāraṃ māpayati saptaratnamayaṃ samantataḥ caturdiśaṃ cātra saptaratnamayāni dvārāṇi māpayati sma / sarvaṃ codyānaṃ saptaratnamayairvṛkṣairalaṅkṛtaṃ / te ca vṛkṣā nānāprakārairvastrairalaṅcakre nānāduṣyairnānācchatrairnānāvidhaiśca muktāhārairnānāprakāraiścābharaṇairnānāratnamayaiścābharaṇairvividhaiḥ (

children.translated_text: (<s>KpSū</s> 56)

children.text: ) sugandhaiḥ, sarvaratnamayaiśca puṣpaphalaistān vṛkṣānalaṅkṛtavān / sarvaṃ ca tadudyānamanekavidhairmaṇibhiralaṅkṛtamabhūt, nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ, nānāpaṭṭaduṣyaprāvaraṇaprāvārebhya āsanāni prajñaptāni / tad api cakraratnaṃ bahiḥ kūṭāgārasya bhagavata evābhimukhaṃ puruṣamātrapramāṇamuparyantarīkṣe sthitaṃ jvalati / hastiratnamapi sarvaśvetaṃ saptāṅgaṃ supratiṣṭhitaṃ, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthitvā bhagavata upari ratnavṛkṣaṃ dhārayati / sa ca vṛkṣo 'laṅkṛtaḥ saptabhī ratnairnānāvidhaiśca muktāhārairvicitraiścābharaṇairnānāvidhaiśca mālyairnānāraṅgaiśca paṭṭairnānāvidhaiśca duṣyairuparacitaṃ, tasya vṛkṣasya saptaratnamayaṃ chatraṃ sthāpitamabhūt / yā cāraṇemino rājño 'gramahiṣī sā bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitā, bhagavantaṃ gośīrṣacandanoragasāracandanacūrṇaiścāvakiramāṇā / yacca rājño 'raṇemino maṇiratnamabhūt prabhāsvaraṃ, tataḥ svayameva bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthāpayāṃ āsa / tatastayā maṇiratnābhayā sarvaṃ tadudyānaṃ satatasamitamudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭaṃ abhūt, buddhābhayāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ sarvamidaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) fragrances, and those trees were adorned with flowers and fruits all made of precious substances. The entire park was adorned with manifold jewels, strewn with various flowers, and seats were prepared from various silken and fine cloth coverings. The wheel-jewel (<s>cakraratna</s>) too stood outside the pavilion, facing the Blessed One, the height of a man, hovering in the sky above, blazing. The elephant-jewel too — entirely white, with seven limbs, well-established — stood behind the Blessed One, holding a jeweled tree above the Blessed One. That tree was adorned with the seven precious substances, various strings of pearls, colorful ornaments, various garlands, various colored silks, and diverse cloths arranged [upon it], and a parasol made of the seven precious substances was placed atop that tree. The chief queen of King <s>Araṇemin</s> stood before the Blessed One, sprinkling the Blessed One with <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood and <s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood powders. And whatever jewel-gem King <s>Araṇemin</s> possessed that was radiant — he himself placed it before the Blessed One. And by the radiance of that jewel-gem, the entire park was constantly and uninterruptedly illuminated with a great splendor, and by the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>, this entire triple-thousand great-thousand world system (
(<s>KpSū</s> 57)

children.text:
) satatasamitaṃ sphuṭamabhūt / ekaikasya ca śrāvakasya gauśīrṣasyaiva candanasya pādapīṭhaṃ sthāpitaṃ, ekaikasya ca śrāvakasya pṛṣṭhataḥ sarvaśveto hastināgaḥ sthāpita uparyevaṃrūpameva cakraratnaṃ puruṣapramāṇaṃ sthāpitaṃ yathā bhagavatastathā, ekaikasya ca śrāvakasyāgrataḥ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitā kanyā sthāpitā gośīrṣoragasāracandanacūrnairavakirati, ekaikasya ca śrāvakasyāgrato vaiḍūryamaṇiḥ
sthāpitaḥ / samantataścodyānasyābhyantare nānāvidhāni vādyāni vādyante, bahiścodyānasya samantena pariṇāyakaratnaṃ vijahāra sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena /
children.translated_text: ) was constantly and uninterruptedly illuminated. For each individual disciple (<s>śrāvaka</s>), a footstool of <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood was placed; behind each individual disciple, an entirely white elephant was stationed; above [each], a wheel-jewel of the same kind, the height of a man, was placed — just as for the Blessed One. Before each individual disciple stood a maiden adorned with all ornaments, sprinkling [him] with <s>gośīrṣa</s> and <s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood powders; before each individual disciple, a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem was placed. On all sides within the park, various kinds of musical instruments were played; outside the park, on every side, the general-jewel (<s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>) was stationed together with the fourfold army.

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Araṇemin</s> summoned the vassal kings, ministers, great councillors, soldiers, army commanders, townspeople, countryfolk, and servants, and addressed them: 'Let the village headmen know that I have invited the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, together with the community of monks, for these three months with all requisites. Whatever possessions and enjoyments I have, whatever attendants, servants, and inner palace — all that I respectfully dedicate to the Blessed One and to the community of monks. You too should respectfully dedicate to the Blessed One and to the community of monks whatever personal possessions, enjoyments, attendants, servants, and inner palace you have.' And they too dedicated [all]. The jewel-householder also transformed the entire <s>Bhadra</s> park into <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, and in that very park he had a pavilion (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>) built for the Blessed One, made of the seven precious substances, with gates made of the seven precious substances on all four sides. The entire park was adorned with trees made of the seven precious substances. Those trees were decorated with various kinds of cloths, various silks, various parasols, various strings of pearls, various ornaments, various jeweled ornaments, and diverse (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra rājāraṇemī divasedivase nagarānniryāti bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / tasya yāvad yānasya bhūmistāvad yānena yātvā yānād avatīrya padbhyāmevodyānaṃ prāviśat, praviśya yena ratnagarbhastathāgatastenopajagāmopetya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ trīnvārān pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā, ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya svayaṃ hastaśaucamadāt, svayaṃ ca praṇītena prabhūtena khādanīyabhojanīyena lehyapeyena svahastaṃ (

children.translated_text: (<s>KpSū</s> 58)

children.text: ) saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati, svahastaṃ saṃtarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā bhagavataṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātrapāṇiṃ svayameva vyajanamādāya bhagavantaṃ vījayāmāsa / ekaikasya ca śrāvakasya rājaputrasahasraṃ koṭṭarājasahasraṃ caivaṃrūpamupasthānaṃ kṛtvā vyajanaṃ gṛhītvā śrāvakān vījayati sma / samanantaraparyavasite bhakṣavisarge 'nekāni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyārāmaṃ praviṣṭāni dharmaśravaṇāya / gaganatale cānekairdevakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ puṣpavṛṣṭirabhivṛṣṭā divyāni vādyāni abhivādayanti, divyāni ca chatrāṇi vāsāṃsi ābharaṇāni ca pralambayanti / nīlavāsasaṃ ca yakṣāṇāṃ catvāriṃśacchatasahasrāṇi ye candanadīpāt gośīrṣasya candanasya kāṣṭhānyānayanti, bhagavato 'rthāyāhāraṃ pratijāgrati bhikṣusaṅghasya ca / rātrau svayameva rājāraṇemī bhagavataḥ purato bhikṣusaṅghasya cānekāni dīpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi jvālayati / atha kulaputra rājāraṇemī bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvā ekāṃ dīpasthālikāṃ śirasyupasthāpayitvā dvāvaṃśayordvau pāṇyordvau caraṇayordīpasthālīḥ, sarvarātrīrbhagavataḥ purato dīpaṃ jvālayamāno, bhagavato 'nubhāvenāklāntakāya (
children.translated_text: ). Having satiated and satisfied [him] with his own hands, and knowing the Blessed One had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl set aside, he himself took a fan and fanned the Blessed One. For each individual disciple, a thousand princes and a thousand vassal kings performed the same kind of service, and taking fans, fanned the disciples. Immediately upon the completion of the distribution of food, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of beings entered the park to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. In the sky above, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of gods rained down a shower of flowers, played divine instruments, and let hang down divine parasols, garments, and ornaments. Forty hundred-thousands of <s>yakṣas</s> clad in dark blue brought logs of <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood from <s>Candanadīpa</s> (Sandalwood Island) and kept watch over the food for the Blessed One and the community of monks. At night, King <s>Araṇemin</s> himself lit many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of lamps before the Blessed One and the community of monks. Then, O son of good family, King <s>Araṇemin</s>, standing before the Blessed One, placed one lamp-bowl on his head, two on his shoulders, two in his hands, and two on his feet, and throughout the entire night, burning lamps before the Blessed One, by the power of the Blessed One, [remained] with unfatigued body (
(<s>KpSū</s> 59)

children.text: ) evaṃrūpaṃ kāyasukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayati sma / tadyathāpi nāma tṛtīyadhyānasamāpannasya bhikṣorevamaklāntakāyaḥ aklāntacitto māsatrayaṃ bhagavantamupasthitavān / evaṃ sahasraṃ rājāputrāṇāṃ caturaśītiśca koṭṭarājasahasrāṇi anyāni ca prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi, ekaikaṃ śrāvakaṃ rājakīyenopakareṇena māsatrayamevaṃrūpeṇopasthānenopasthitavantaḥ / yathā rājāraṇemī ratnagarbhan tathāgatamupasthitavān tathāgramahiṣī devī māsatrayaṃ gandhapuspairupasthitavatī / evamanyairapi bahukanyākoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairekaikaḥ śrāvako māsatrayaṃ puṣpagandhairupasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) and experienced such bodily bliss. Just as a monk who has attained the third <s>dhyāna</s> — with thus unfatigued body and unfatigued mind — for three months he attended upon the Blessed One. Likewise, the thousand princes and eighty-four thousand vassal kings and many other <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of beings attended upon each individual disciple with royal requisites for three months with the same kind of service. Just as King <s>Araṇemin</s> attended upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, so too the chief queen attended [upon him] for three months with incense and flowers. Similarly, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of other maidens attended upon each individual disciple for three months with flowers and incense.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, King <s>Araṇemin</s> went forth from the city day by day to see, venerate, and attend upon the Blessed One. He rode in his chariot as far as the ground was suitable for a chariot, then descended from the chariot and entered the park on foot. Having entered, he approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and himself gave the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> water for washing the hands. He himself satiated and satisfied [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] with his own hands with excellent and abundant hard and soft foods, lickable and drinkable [foods] (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra rājāraṇemī trayāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayena caturaśītiṃ jāmbūnadamayāni niṣkasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati / cakraratnacakrapūrvaṃgamāni ca suvarṇamayāni caturaśītiścakraratnasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati / hastiratnapūrvaṃgamāni caturaśītirnāgasahasrāṇi sarvaśvetāni bhagavato niryātayati / aśvaratnapūrvaṃgamāni caturaśītiraśvasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati / maṇiratnapūrvaṃgamāni caturaśītiḥ sūryakāntimaṇisahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati sma / gṛhapatiratnapūrvaṃgamāni (

children.translated_text: (<s>KpSū</s> 60)

children.text: ) caturaśītirājaputrasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati sma / upasthānāya pariṇāyakaratnapūrvaṃgamāni caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi bhagavata upasthānāya niryātayati sma / añcuranagarapūrvaṃgamāni caturaśītinagarasahasrāṇi bhagavata upajīvyāni niryātayati bhikṣusaṅghasya ca / caturaśītiratnamayāni kalpavṛkṣasahasrāṇi caturaśītiratnarāśipuṣpasahasrāṇi caturaśītisaptaratnamayāni chatrasahasrāṇi caturaśītyudārāṇāṃ rājārhanāṃ vastrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturaśītisahasrāṇi ratnamayānāṃ mālānāṃ ābharaṇapīṭhaśīrṣanayanakuṇḍalasuvarṇasūtramuktāhāropānahaśayyāpādapīṭhabhājanabherīvādyaśaṅkhaghaṇṭādhvajāṃ bhṛṅgārārāmā dīpasthālikā bhagavato niryātayati sma / ratnamayāḥ śakunā ratnamayāśca mṛgāścaturaśītivyajanasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātayati sma / caturaśītirasāyanasahasrāṇi ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya niryātayati sma / evaṃ cāha, "ahaṃ bhagavan bahukṛtyo bahukaraṇīyaḥ, kṣamatu me bhagavān, asmākamupavane 'bhiramatu, bhagavān asminnupavane ramatu nityaṃ; punarapyahaṃ bhagavantamupasaṃkramiṣye darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya ca" / (
children.translated_text: ), he offered eighty-four thousand princes to the Blessed One. Led by his general-jewel, he offered eighty-four thousand vassal kings for the service of the Blessed One. Led by the city of <s>Añcura</s>, he offered eighty-four thousand cities for the livelihood of the Blessed One and the community of monks. [He also offered] eighty-four thousand wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>) made of precious substances, eighty-four thousand heaps of jeweled flowers, eighty-four thousand parasols made of the seven precious substances, eighty-four thousand sets of fine garments fit for a king, eighty-four thousand garlands of precious substances, ornamental pedestals, headpieces, eye-ornaments, earrings, golden threads, pearl necklaces, sandals, beds, footstools, vessels, kettledrums, musical instruments, conches, bells, banners, water-pitchers, pleasure gardens, and lamp-bowls — all these he offered to the Blessed One. He offered jeweled birds and jeweled deer and eighty-four thousand fans to the Blessed One. He offered eighty-four thousand elixirs (<s>rasāyana</s>) to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. And he spoke thus: 'I, Blessed One, have many duties and much to be done. May the Blessed One forgive me. May the Blessed One delight in our pleasure garden; may the Blessed One always take pleasure in this pleasure garden. And I shall again approach the Blessed One for seeing, venerating, and attending upon him.' (
(<s>KpSū</s> 61)

children.text: ) yacca rājño 'raṇeminaḥ putrasahasraṃ bhagavataḥ pādayornipatya bhagavantamekaikamidamavocat - "adhivāsayatvasmākamekaikasya traimāsaṃ vayaṃ bhagavantamupasthāsyāmaḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena" / adhivāsayati bhagavāṃstasya rājaputrasahasrasya tūṣṇībhāvena / teṣāṃ adhivāsitaṃ bhagavatā viditvātha rājāraṇemī bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca triskṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavanto 'ntikāt prakāntaḥ / atha teṣāṃ rājaputrāṇāṃ jyeṣṭho 'nimiṣo nāmā bhagavantaṃ traimāsamevaṃrūpeṇopasthānenopastiṣṭhati bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, tadyathā rājāraṇemī tathaivamanimiṣapramukhaṃ rājakumārasahasraṃ dinedine bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmati bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca śrotuṃ /
children.translated_text: ) And the thousand sons of King <s>Araṇemin</s>, falling at the Blessed One's feet, each spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'May [the Blessed One] consent — each of us for three months shall attend upon the Blessed One with all requisites, together with the community of monks.' The Blessed One consented to that thousand princes by his silence. When they learned of the Blessed One's consent, King <s>Araṇemin</s> bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and the community of monks, circumambulated them three times, and departed from the Blessed One's presence. Then the eldest of those princes, named <s>Animiṣa</s>, attended upon the Blessed One for three months with the same kind of service, and upon the community of monks. Just as King <s>Araṇemin</s> [had done], so too the thousand royal princes headed by <s>Animiṣa</s> approached the Blessed One day by day for seeing [him] and the community of monks and to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, King <s>Araṇemin</s>, at the end of three months, offered eighty-four thousand <s>niṣkas</s> (gold coins) made of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold to the Blessed One. Led by his wheel-jewel, he offered eighty-four thousand golden wheel-jewels to the Blessed One. Led by his elephant-jewel, he offered eighty-four thousand entirely white elephants to the Blessed One. Led by his horse-jewel, he offered eighty-four thousand horses to the Blessed One. Led by his gem-jewel, he offered eighty-four thousand <s>sūryakānti</s> (sun-stone) gems to the Blessed One. Led by his householder-jewel (

body.text: atha kulaputra bhagavato ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pitā samudrareṇurnāma brāhmaṇaḥ, sa sarvaṃ jambūdvīpamanvāhiṇḍya strīpuruṣadārakadārikābhyaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ yācate, sa taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ parigṛhītastaṃ sarvaṃ jambūdvīpanivāsilokaṃ triśaraṇagamane pratiṣṭhāpayati, pratiṣṭhāpayitvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayati / tenaivamanvāhiṇḍatā na sa kaścijjambūdvīpe manuṣyabhūto (

children.translated_text: (<s>KpSū</s> 62)

children.text: ) 'sti yaḥ samudrareṇunā brāhmaṇena piṇḍakena na parigṛhīto, yo vā na triśaraṇagamane pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, yasya vānuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittaṃ notpādayati, yo vā nānuttare jñāne samādāpito na pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ / bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi triśaraṇakriyāvastuṣu sthāpitāni, evamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāni niveśitāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni /
children.translated_text: ) who had not been received by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudraraṇu</s> with an alms-offering, or who had not been established in the taking of the Three Refuges, or in whom the mind [set upon] unsurpassed perfect awakening had not been aroused, or who had not been inspired and established in supreme knowledge. Many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of beings were established in the practice of the Three Refuges, and likewise were inspired, settled, and established in unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the father of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Samudraraṇu</s>. He wandered throughout all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, begging alms-food from women, men, boys, and girls. Having received that alms-food, he established all the people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the taking of the Three Refuges, and having established them, he aroused in them the mind [set upon] unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). As he wandered thus, there was no human being in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (

body.text: animiṣo 'pi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ māsatrayamevaṃrūpeṇopasthānenopasthitavān sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena yathā rājñāraṇeminā, so 'pi trayāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayena caturaśītiścakraratnasahasrāṇi niryātayati sarvasauvarṇāni nagarāṇi divyāni ca hastyaśvamaṇistrīgṛhapatipariṇāyakaratnāni sthāpayitvā caturaśītihastyaśvasahasrāṇi, evaṃ sūryakāntimaṇikanyākumārakalpavṛkṣapuṣparāśicchatravastramālyābharaṇaratnapīṭhaśīrṣanayanakuṇḍalasuvarṇasūtramuktāhāropānahaśayyāpādapīṭhabhājanabherīvādyaśaṅkhapaṭahadhvajabhṛṅgārāmadīpasthālikādīni nānāratnamayāśca śakunā nānāmṛgāṃśca ratnamayāṃ rasāyanāṃśca; ekaikaśaścaturaśītisahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātitavanta evaṃ bhikṣusaṅghasya ca /
body.translated_text: The prince <s>Animiṣa</s> also attended upon the <s>Bhagavan</s> for three months with such service, together with the community of monks (<s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>), just as King <s>Araṇemi</s> [had done]. He too, at the end of three months, presented eighty-four thousand wheel-jewels, all of gold, and divine cities, and the jewels of elephant, horse, gem, woman, householder, and general — except [these he offered] eighty-four thousand elephants and horses; likewise [he offered] sun-stone gems, maidens, youths, wish-fulfilling trees, heaps of flowers, parasols, garments, garlands, ornaments, jewel-thrones, head-ornaments, eye-ornaments, earrings, golden threads, pearl necklaces, shoes, couches, footstools, vessels, drums, musical instruments, conch-shells, kettle-drums, banners, water-pitchers, lamps, pots, and the like — also various birds made of jewels, various animals [made of jewels], and elixirs — eighty-four thousand of each he presented to the <s>Bhagavan</s> and to the community of monks.

body.text: atha sa rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ kṣamāpitavān bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, animiṣo rājakumāro bhagavantamevaṃrūpeṇopasthānenopasthitavān sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena yathā rājñāraṇeminā tathaiva dakṣiṇā dattā anantā / evamindragaṇena māsatrayaṃ bhagavān upasthito vibhavaśca parityaktaḥ, peyālaṃ, tathaivānaṅgaṇaḥ, abhayaḥ, ambaraḥ, aśajaḥ, middhaḥ, miṣaḥ, mārdavaḥ, paṅgagaṇaḥ, mādhvavaḥ, mānavo, māsaṃvo, mājavaḥ, aravaḥ, ājñavaḥ, mukhavaḥ, arthabahuḥ, alindraḥ, neravaḥ, reṇajaḥ, candranemī, sūryanemī, indranemī, vajranemī, kṣāntinemī, sthānanemī, javanemī, raṇemī, rāhuḥ, rāhubalaḥ, rāhucitraḥ, dāmacitraḥ, rājadhānaḥ, rāgabhramaḥ, rāndhavaḥ, rakṣakaḥ, kāyaḥ, śayamāḥ, yatravaḥ, syajalaḥ, yārmathaḥ, yadhvajaḥ, yamānaḥ, yasyanaḥ, namajyotiḥ, arañjanadhvaḥ, yāvad araṇemino rājñaḥ putrasahasreṇa ekaikena ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ (

children.translated_text: [KpSū page 64]

children.text: ) sārdhamaprameyena bhikṣusaṅghena, evaṃrūpeṇa bhagavata upasthānenopasthitaḥ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārairmāsatrayaṃ yathā jyeṣṭhena rājaputreṇa, tathaivaikaikaścaturaśītiḥ svarṇamayāścakrasahasrāṇi vistareṇa yāvaccaturaśītirasāyanasahasrāṇi bhagavato niryātitāni bhikṣusaṅghasya ca / evaṃrūpeṇa mahāprasādena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā kecid devatvaṃ kecicchakratvaṃ kecin māratvaṃ keciccakravartirājyaṃ kecin mahābhogatāṃ kecicchrāvakayānaṃ kecit pratyekabuddhayānaṃ prārthayanti, adhiṣṭhamānāśca dvau varṣaśatau pañcapañcāśacca varṣāṇi bhagavantaṃ kṣamāpayanti (
children.translated_text: ) together with the immeasurable community of monks, attended upon the <s>Bhagavan</s> with such service — robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick — for three months, just as the eldest prince [had done]. And likewise each one presented eighty-four thousand golden wheels, in detail up to eighty-four thousand elixirs, to the <s>Bhagavan</s> and to the community of monks. With such great faith (<s>prasāda</s>), having made aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): some [aspired to] divinity, some to the state of <s>Śakra</s>, some to the state of <s>Māra</s>, some to great wealth,
[KpSū page 65]

children.text:
) bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca / tatkāle samudrareṇurbrāhmano 'grapurohito 'bhyāgato 'drākṣīt taṃ bhagavantaṃ tai rājaputrairupasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā saptavarṣāṇi sarvopakaraṇairupanimantrayate, yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayyāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena / adhivāsayati bhagavān pituragrapurohitasya tūṣṇībhāvena / atha samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇa evaṃrūpeṇa sarvopakaraṇasaṃpannenopasthānena bhagavata upasthitaḥ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayyāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena
//
children.translated_text: ) and the community of monks. At that time, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudra-reṇu</s>, the chief priest (<s>agra-purohita</s>), came forth. He saw that <s>Bhagavan</s> being attended upon by those princes. Having seen [this], he invited [the <s>Bhagavan</s>] for seven years with all requisites — namely, robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick — together with the community of monks. The <s>Bhagavan</s> accepted the invitation of the father's chief priest through silence. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudra-reṇu</s>, with service complete in all requisites of such a kind, [attended upon] the <s>Bhagavan</s>—

body.translated_text: Then that prince asked the forgiveness of the <s>Bhagavan</s> and of the community of monks. The prince <s>Animiṣa</s> attended upon the <s>Bhagavan</s> with such service, together with the community of monks, just as King <s>Araṇemi</s> [had done], and likewise boundless gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) were given. In the same way, <s>Indragaṇa</s> attended upon the <s>Bhagavan</s> for three months and relinquished [his] wealth — [the text is] abbreviated (<s>peyāla</s>). Likewise <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, <s>Abhaya</s>, <s>Ambara</s>, <s>Aśaja</s>, <s>Middha</s>, <s>Miṣa</s>, <s>Mārdava</s>, <s>Paṅgagaṇa</s>, <s>Mādhvava</s>, <s>Mānava</s>, <s>Māsaṃva</s>, <s>Mājava</s>, <s>Arava</s>, <s>Ājñava</s>, <s>Mukhava</s>, <s>Arthabahu</s>, <s>Alindra</s>, <s>Nerava</s>, <s>Reṇaja</s>, <s>Candranemī</s>, <s>Sūryanemī</s>, <s>Indranemī</s>, <s>Vajranemī</s>, <s>Kṣāntinemī</s>, <s>Sthānanemī</s>, <s>Javanemī</s>, <s>Raṇemī</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Rāhubala</s>, <s>Rāhucitra</s>, <s>Dāmacitra</s>, <s>Rājadhāna</s>, <s>Rāgabhrama</s>, <s>Rāndhava</s>, <s>Rakṣaka</s>, <s>Kāya</s>, <s>Śayamā</s>, <s>Yatrava</s>, <s>Syajala</s>, <s>Yārmatha</s>, <s>Yadhvaja</s>, <s>Yamāna</s>, <s>Yasyana</s>, <s>Namajyoti</s>, <s>Arañjanadhva</s> — up to [all] the thousand sons of King <s>Araṇemi</s>, each one [attended upon] the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāpareṇa samayena samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyaivaṃ cetasaḥ parivitarka udapādi / "mayā tāvad bahuprāṇakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāni / na cāhamasya rājño 'raṇeminaḥ praṇidhānaṃ jāne, kim ayaṃ prārthayati devatvaṃ vā uta śakratvaṃ vā māratvaṃ vā mahābhogatāṃ vā śrāvakayānaṃ vā pratyekabuddhayānaṃ vānuttarāṃ vā samyaksaṃbodhim ākāṅkṣate / kaccid aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, atīrṇān sattvāṃstārayeyaṃ, amuktāmmocayeyaṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ, (

children.translated_text: [KpSū page 66]

children.text: ) aparinirvṛtān sattvān parinirvāpayeyaṃ / kaccit svapne nivedayatu devo vā yakṣo vā nāgo vā buddho vā śrāvako vā brāhmaṇo vā kin tāvad rājā devaśriyaṃ kāṅkṣate uta manuṣyaśriyaṃ atha śrāvakatvamatha pratyekabuddhabhūmimatha vānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ" /
children.translated_text: )—[able to] lead beings who have not yet attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> to <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>? Perchance in a dream, may a god, or a <s>Yakṣa</s>, or a <s>Nāga</s>, or a <s>Buddha</s>, or a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> reveal [this to me]: Does the king aspire to divine glory or to human glory, or to the state of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, or to the stage of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or to unsurpassed perfect awakening?'

body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, at another time, the following reflection arose in the mind of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudra-reṇu</s>: 'I have indeed inspired many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But I do not know the aspiration of this King <s>Araṇemi</s> — what does he desire? Does he desire divinity, or the state of <s>Śakra</s>, or the state of <s>Māra</s>, or great prosperity, or the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or does he aspire to unsurpassed perfect awakening? Am I perhaps not—

body.text: atha kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ agrapurohitaḥ svapne tathārūpamavabhāsamadrākṣīt, yenāvabhāsena daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyati / te ca buddhā bhagavantaḥ tasya brāhmaṇasya padmāni svarṇapatrāṇi rūpyadaṇḍāni vaiḍūryakarṇikāni aśmagarbhakeśarāṇi preṣayanti / sarveṣu ca teṣu padmeṣu sūryamaṇḍalaṃ dṛśyate / sūryamaṇḍalasyopari saptaratnamayaṃ chatraṃ saṃsthitaṃ / ekaikasmācca sūryamaṇḍalāt ṣaṣṭiraśmikoṭyo niścerustā raśmayaḥ sarvāstasya brāhmaṇasya vaktre praviśanti / sahasrayojanapramāṇamātmabhāvaṃ samanupaśyati pariśuddhaṃ tadyathā pariśuddhamādarśamaṇḍalaṃ / svakāyasya ca kukṣau ṣaṣṭibodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi padmeṣu paryaṅkopaviṣṭāṃ dhyāyamānāṃ paśyati / tānapi sūryavigrahānātmanaḥ śirasi mālān paśyati / chatraṃ copari cākāśe (

children.translated_text: [KpSū page 67]

children.text: ) yāvad brahmalokaparyante sthitaṃ paśyati / nānāpadmāni sāmantake sthitāni paśyati / tebhyaśca padmebhyo divyānyatikrāntamānuṣāṇi tūryāṇi niścaranti śṛṇoti ca / tatra ca rājānamāraṇeminaṃ paśyati, rudhiramrakṣitena kāyena dhāvantaṃ sūkaramukhena vividhān bahuprāṇino bhakṣayante, bhakṣayitvā cairaṇḍavṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇaṃ / vividhāśca prāṇinaḥ samāgamya taṃ rājānaṃ bhakṣayanti yāvad asthiśaṅkalāvaśeṣaṃ kṛtvā chorayanti / evaṃ punaḥ punastathaiva prādurbhavantaṃ sūkaramukhaṃ rudhiramrakṣitena kāyena bahuvidhān prāṇino bhakṣayitvā eraṇḍamūle niṣaṇṇaṃ, vividhaiḥ prāṇibhiḥ khādyamānamasthiśaṅkalāvaśiṣṭaṃ kṛtvā choritaṃ / punaraparaṃ rājaputrān paśyati sūkaramukhenāpare gajamukhenāpare mahiṣamukhenāpare siṃhamukhenāpare vṛkamukhenāpare śṛgālamukhenāpare śvamukhenāpare markaṭamukhena paśyati, śoṇitābhyukṣitagātrānanekavidhān prāṇino bhakṣayitvā eraṇḍavṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇān vividhaiḥ prāṇibhirbhakṣyamāṇān asthiśaṅkalāvaśiṣṭānutsṛṣṭān / punarapi tenaiva kāyena sthitān tathaiva prāṇino bhakṣayataḥ paśyati / anyāṃśca rājaputrān paśyati mahiṣarathābhirūḍhān sumanāpuṣpābhyalaṅkṛtān (
children.translated_text: )—extending up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world he sees standing. He sees various lotuses standing nearby. And from those lotuses, divine music surpassing human [music] issues forth, and he hears [it]. And there he sees King <s>Araṇemi</s>, with a body smeared with blood, running, [and] a pig-faced [being] devouring various living creatures in great number; and having devoured [them], seated at the foot of an <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor-oil) tree. And various living beings, having gathered together, devour that king until only a skeleton remains—
[KpSū page 68]

children.text:
) kupathena dakṣiṇābhimukhān gacchataḥ / śakrabrahmalokapālāścāgatvā brāhmaṇasya kathayanti
/ "imāni brāhmaṇa padmāni bhāgaṃ kuru, bhāgaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ prathamaṃ rājñaḥ saṃvibhāgamekaṃ padmamanuprayaccha, tata eṣāmapi rājaputrāṇāmekaikaṃ padmaṃ dada, avaśiṣṭāni koṭṭarājñāṃ prayaccha, aparāṃ janasya" / śrutvā brāhmaṇa prāha / "yathājñāpayanti devāḥ" /
children.translated_text: )—going southward by an evil path. And <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians (<s>Lokapālas</s>) came and told the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, divide these lotuses. Having divided them, first give one lotus as a share to the king; then give one lotus each to these princes as well; give the remaining ones to the subordinate kings; and the rest to the people.' Having heard [this], the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'As the gods command.'

body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudra-reṇu</s>, the chief priest, saw in his dream a vision of this kind: by the radiance of that vision, he saw <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavans</s> in <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in all ten directions. And those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavans</s> sent to that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lotuses with golden petals, silver stalks, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) pistils, and filaments of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (crystal). And in all those lotuses, a solar disc was visible. Above the solar disc, a parasol made of the seven jewels

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaḥ padmāni bhājayamāna eva pratibuddhaḥ, saṃvicintayamāna utthāyāsanāt punarvicintayati, "hīnapraṇidhirayaṃ rājā cakravartī saṃsārasukhābhirato hīnā vāsyādhimuktiḥ sārdhamekatyai rājaputrairekatyāḥ punā rājaputrāḥ śrāvakayānamākāṅkṣanti ye mayā mahiṣarathābhirūḍhā dṛṣṭāḥ sumanāpuṣpairalaṅkṛtā dakṣiṇābhimukhā gacchanti / yacca mayā sarvasattvārthaṃ mahāyajñasyārambhaṃ kṛtaṃ / yacca mayādhatriyāṃ varṣaśatāṃ jambūdvīpamanvāhiṇḍya sarvasattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau yāvat pratiṣṭhāpiṭāḥ / tad evaṃ mayā sarvajambūdvīpe gatānekāni prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi triṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu samādāpitāni niveśitāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni / tasyaitannimittaṃ yena mayā svapne mahāvabhāso dṛṣṭaḥ (

children.translated_text: [KpSū page 69]

children.text: ) daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavanto dṛṣṭāḥ / yacca mayā sarvaṃ jambūdvīpamanvāhiṇḍya strīpuruṣadārakadārikābhyaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ yācayitvā bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi triśaraṇakriyāvastuṣu sthāpitāni vinītāni niveśitāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni / yacca mayā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saptavarṣāṇyupanimantritaḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena, tena mama daśabhyo digbhyaḥ anyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyaḥ buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ padmānyanupreṣitāni / yacca mayānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tena te buddhā saptaratnamayāni chatrāṇi visarjayanti / yatpunarmayā teṣu padmeṣu sūryavigrahā dṛṣṭā, yacca raśmayo mukhe praviśamānā dṛṣṭāḥ, yaccāsau mahān ātmabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ, yacca sūryavigrahamālā dṛṣṭā, yacca kukṣau bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi padmeṣu paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇāni dhyāyamānāni, imā evaṃrūpāḥ svapnā dṛṣṭāḥ, yacca me śakrabrahmalokapāla dṛṣṭā ājñāpayantīmāni padmāni bhāgaṃ kuru, yacca mayā tāni padmāni bhāgaṃ kṛtvā dattāni / yannvaham imāḥ svapnā buddhāya bhagavata ākhyāsye, kiṃhetukāḥ kiṃpratyayā mayaivaṃrūpāḥ svapnā dṛṣṭā, yannvahaṃ (
children.translated_text: )—saw <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavans</s> in all ten directions. And that I wandered throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and having begged alms-food from men, women, boys, and girls, I established, trained, guided, and firmly grounded many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings in the Three Refuges (<s>triśaraṇa</s>). And that I invited the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, for seven years with all requisites, together with the community of monks — by that [merit], from the ten directions, from other <s>Buddha</s>-fields,
[KpSū page 70]
)—I shall ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> awoke while still in the process of distributing the lotuses. Reflecting [on the dream], having risen from his seat, he deliberates further: 'This <s>Cakravartin</s> king has a lowly aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), delighting in the pleasures of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Low indeed is his disposition (<s>adhimukti</s>), together with some of the princes. But other princes aspire to the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle — those whom I saw mounted on buffalo-carts, adorned with <s>sumanā</s> flowers, going southward. And [I consider] that I performed the commencement of a great sacrifice for the benefit of all beings. And that I—

body.text: atha samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ tasyā eva rātryā atyayena bhojanaṃ sajjīkṛtvā kālyate eva yena bhagavāṃstenopajagāma, upetya svayameva bhagavato hastaśaucamupanāmayati bhikṣusaṅghasya ca / hastaśaucamupanīya prabhūtena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati, saṃtarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā bhikṣusaṅghamanekaparyāyena saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ viditvā bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcamāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya / atha rājāraṇemī tatraivābhyāgataḥ sārdhaṃ putrasahasreṇānekaiśca prāṇisahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ, sa yāvad yānasya bhūmistāvad yānena yātvā yānād avatīrya padbhyāmevārāmaṃ prāvikṣat, praviśya ca yena bhagavāṃstenopajagāmopetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhikṣusaṅghasya ca bhagavataḥ purataḥ niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya / atha samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo yathādṛṣṭāṃ svapnāṃ bhagavato nivedayati /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudra-reṇu</s>, at the end of that very night, having prepared a meal, went early in the morning to where the <s>Bhagavan</s> was. Having approached, he himself offered water for washing the hands to the <s>Bhagavan</s> and to the community of monks. Having offered water for washing the hands, with abundant food both hard and soft, he satisfied and satiated [them] with his own hand. Having satisfied and satiated [them], having satisfied and satiated the community of monks in many ways, having acknowledged the <s>Bhagavan</s> and the community of monks, [having taken] a washed [bowl]—

body.text: bhagavān āha - "yattvaṃ brāhmaṇādrākṣīt mahāntamavabhāsaṃ yenāvabhāsena gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu (

children.translated_text: [KpSū page 71]

children.text: ) buddhā bhagavanto dṛṣṭā tava padmāni visarjayanti, teṣu ca padmeṣu sūryavigrahā dṛṣṭā raśmayaḥ pramuñcamānāste ca raśmayastava mukhe praviśanti / yattvayā brāhmaṇa adhatrikāyāṃ varṣaśatāṃ jambudvīpamāhiṇḍatā, tena tvayā gaṇanātikrāntāḥ sattvāstriṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāśca, gaṇanātikrāntāśca sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / yacca tvayā sarvasattvārthaṃ mahāyajñasyārambhaḥ kṛtastena tvaṃ brāhmaṇa buddhā bhagavanto vyākariṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, ye daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, yaiśca tava padmāni visarjitāni suvarṇapatrāṇi rūpyadaṇḍāni vaiḍūryakarṇikāni asmagarbhakeśarāṇi, teṣu ca sarveṣu padmeṣu sūryavigrahā dṛśyante / idaṃ tasya svapnasya pūrvanimittaṃ / yattvaṃ brāhmaṇādrākṣīt svapne ye daśausu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, tairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ saptaratnamayāni chatrāṇi visarjitāni, yāni chatrāṇi copari cākāśe yāvad (
children.translated_text: ) the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, were seen releasing lotuses for you, and in those lotuses sun-like forms were seen emitting rays, and those rays enter your mouth. Because you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, wandered through <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for a hundred years in the lowest period, you established and settled beings beyond counting in the three bases of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), beings beyond reckoning
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 72.

children.text:
) brahmalokaparyantaṃ saṃtiṣṭhanti / yasyāṃ eva rātrau tvaṃ brāhmaṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase tasyāṃ eva rātrau daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣūdāraḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgacchate, upari ca yāvad brahmalokaparyantaṃ kṛtvā na śakyante tava mūrdhānaṃ vyavalokayituṃ brahmādibhirdevalokairapi / idaṃ tasya svapnasya pūrvanimittaṃ / yattvaṃ brāhmaṇādrākṣit mahāntamātmabhāvaṃ yāvad brahmalokaṃ yacca sūryamaṇḍalānāṃ mālā śīrasi baddhā, tadye tvayā gaṇanātikrāntāḥ sattvāḥ samādāpitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, te ca tavābhisaṃbuddhabodherbrāhmaṇa buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu deśasu dikṣu sthitā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / sarve ye tvayā bodhau samādāpitā te tavābhīkṣṇaṃ varṇaṃ udāhariṣyanti, "anena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena vayaṃ prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā, yenāsmaitarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā, eṣa cāsmākaṃ kalyāṇamitraṃ" / te buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvān visarjayiṣyanti tava pūjākarmaṇe, tataste bodhisattvā mahāsattvā
vividhairbodhisattvavikurvitaistava (
children.translated_text: ) they stand extending up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. On the very night when you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, will attain supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), on that very night, in the ten directions, in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a great fame and renown and glory will arise, and reaching upward to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, they will be unable to behold the crown of your head—<s>Brahmā</s>
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 73.
