children.text: ) pūjāṃ kṛtvā, tatra tava sakāśāddharmaṃ śrutvā nānāvidhāḥ samādhirdhāraṇīḥ kṣāntiśca pratilapsyante / te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvā tava varṇaṃ uccārayiṣyanti ghoṣamanuśrāvayiṣyanti / idaṃ brāhmaṇa tasya svapnasya pūrvanimittaṃ / yattvayā brāhmaṇa svapne dṛṣṭā bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi tāni tava kukṣau praviśya padmeṣu paryaṅkopaviṣṭā dhyāyanti, abhisaṃbuddhabodhiśca tvaṃ brāhmaṇa bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi yānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayiṣyasi avaivartikāni sthāpayiṣyasyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / te tava parinirvṛtasya brāhmaṇānuttareṇa parinirvāṇena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu kalpeṣu paścāddaśāsu dikṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu te buddhā bhagavanto dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayantastava varṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyanti / "evam asaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣvatikrānteṣu evaṃnāmā tathāgato abhūd arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena vayamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃboddhau samādāpitā vinītā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā avaivartikāśca sthāpitā, yena vayametarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ, (
children.translated_text: ) having made offerings, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> in your presence there, they will attain various <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (mnemonic powers), and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience). Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), having gone to their respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), will proclaim your praise and broadcast the proclamation. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the portent of that dream. What you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, saw in the dream—the <s>bodhisattvas</s>
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 74.

children.text: ) dharmarājyaṃ ca pratilabdhāḥ" / idaṃ brāhmaṇa tasya svapnasya pūrvanimittaṃ / yattvaṃ brāhmaṇa svapne dṛṣṭavān sūkaramukhena yāvacchvamukhena rudhiramrakṣitena gātreṇānekavidhāṃ prāṇino bhakṣayitvā hīna eraṇḍamūle niṣaṇṇāste 'pyanye vividhaiḥ prāṇibhirbhakṣyante yāvadasthiśaṅkalāvaśeṣā utsṛjyante, punarapyāpyāyitakāyā rudhirābhyaktena kāyena yāvacchvamukhena bahuvidhāṃ prāṇino bhakṣayitvā punarhīnasyairaṇḍavṛkṣasya mūle niṣaṇṇā vividhaiśca prāṇibhiḥ khādyante / te tvayā mohapuruṣāstrividhe puṇyakriyāvastuni samādāpitā prātiṣṭhāpitā dāne yame saṃyame ca, te deveṣu cyavanaduḥkhamabhilaṣanti, manuṣyeṣu jarāvyādhimaraṇāpriyasaṃprayogapriyavinābhāvaduḥkhāṃ preteṣu kṣutpipāsaduḥkhaṃ tiryakṣvanyonyabhakṣaṇaduḥkhaṃ nārakeṣu dāhacchedavadhabandhananānāvidhakāraṇādiduḥkhamabhilaṣanti / trividhe ca puṇyakriyāvastuni pratiṣṭhāpitā deveṣu devarājyamabhilaṣanti manuṣyeṣu caikadvīpaiśvaryamākāṅkṣante / teṣāṃ tatra sarvasattvāḥ paribhogaṃ gacchanti, te 'pi ca sarvasattvānāmāhāraparibhogaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) and they obtained the sovereignty of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmarājya</s>)." This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the portent of that dream. What you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, saw in the dream—beings with pig faces and even dog faces, their bodies smeared with blood, having devoured many kinds of living beings, sitting wretchedly at the foot of a castor-oil tree (<s>eraṇḍa</s>), while others too are devoured by various creatures until only their bones and skeletons remain and are cast aside,
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 75.

children.text:
) gacchanti / evaṃ te mohapuruṣāḥ sarve tvayā trividhe puṇyakriyāvastuni
pratiṣṭhāpitāstavopāsakā bhaviṣyanti / idaṃ brāhmaṇa tasya svapnasya pūrvanimittaṃ / yattvaṃ brāhmaṇa svapnamadrākṣīt apare manuṣyā mahiṣarathābhirūdhāḥ sumanāmālālāṅkṛtaśirasaḥ apathena dakṣiṇābhimukhaṃ gacchanti, te 'pi tvayā brāhmaṇa kulaputrāḥ triṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ kevalamātmadamanārthaṃ ātmaśamanārthaṃ śrāvakayānasaṃprasthitāḥ, teṣāṃ śrāvakayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ brāhmaṇa pudgalānāmidaṃ purvanimittaṃ" //
children.translated_text: ) they go. Thus all those deluded persons, established by you in the threefold basis of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), will become your <s>upāsakas</s> (lay followers). This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the portent of that dream. What you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, saw in the dream—other people mounted on buffalo chariots, their heads adorned with garlands of <s>sumanā</s> flowers, going southward along a wrong path—they too, by you,

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, that great radiance which you saw in your dream — by that radiance, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra brāhmaṇaḥ samudrareṇū rājānamāraṇeminametadavocat - "durlabhaṃ mahārāja manuṣyatvaṃ, durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpat, durlabhamudumbarapuṣpasadṛśānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ prādurbhāvo loke, durlabhaḥ kuśaladharme chandaḥ, durlabhaṃ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ / duḥkhotpattibhūtaṃ mahārāja devarājatvaṃ, duḥkhotpattibhūtaṃ mahārāja manuṣyeṣu caikadvīpaiśvaryarājatvaṃ, duḥkhotpattibhūtaṃ dvistriścāturdvīpikarājatvaṃ / ciraṃ mahārāja saṃsāraduḥkhamanubhavitavyaṃ / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 76.

children.text: ) anavasthitā mahārāja vāyuvegacapalā devamanuṣyasaṃpattayo, dakacandropamā bālāḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇairatṛptā viṣayeṣu mattā devamāṇuṣāṃ śriyamabhilaṣanti / te bālāḥ punaḥ punarnarakeṣu kāraṇāduḥkhamanubhavanti tiryakṣu saṃmohaduḥkhaṃ preteṣu kṣutpipāsāduḥkhaṃ manuṣyeṣu priyaviprayogaduḥkhaṃ deveṣu cyavanaduḥkhaṃ punargarbhavāsaduḥkhaṃ parasparaśīrṣaprapātanaduḥkhaṃ anyonyabhakṣaṇaduḥkhaṃ, evaṃ bhramamāṇā bālā duḥkhamanubhavanti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ?, kalyāṇamitravirahitāḥ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ na kurvanti na vyāyamanti aprāptasya prāptaye 'nadhigatasyādhigamāyāsākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai / evaṃ mūrkhā bālāḥ khidyante bodhicittena yatra sarvaduḥkhakṣayo bhavati, saṃsāreṇa ca na khidyante nodvijanti yatra punaḥ punarduḥkhotpattirbhavati / parīkṣasva mahārāja yathā saṃsāraḥ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ bhājanabhūtaḥ / tasmāttarhi tvaṃ mahārāja kṛtādhikāro bhagavataḥ śāsane 'varopitakuśalamūlastriṣu ratneṣu labdhaprasādaḥ, bhagavato dattadāno (
children.translated_text: ) Unstable, O great king, are the fortunes of gods and humans, as fickle as the force of the wind. The foolish, like a reflection of the moon in water, unsatisfied by the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>), intoxicated by sense objects, desire the glory of gods and humans. Those fools again and again experience the suffering of punishment in the hells, the suffering of delusion among animals, the suffering of hunger and thirst among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), the suffering of separation from the beloved among humans, and among the gods
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 77.

children.text: ) mahābhogatāyai rakṣitaśīlaḥ svargopapattipratilābhāya śruto bhagavato 'ntikāddharmaṃ prajñāmahādharmapratilābhāya te saṃpatsyante / yaṣṭayajñastvaṃ mahārāja utpādāyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ" / āha, "alaṃ brāhmaṇa, nāhaṃ brāhmaṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhilaṣāmi saṃsārābhirataḥ, yanmahābrāhmaṇa mayā dānaṃ dattaṃ śīlaṃ rakṣitaṃ dharmaḥ śrutaḥ / durlabhā hi brāhmaṇānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) for great wealth, morality has been guarded; for the attainment of rebirth in heaven, the <s>Dharma</s> has been heard from the Blessed One; for the attainment of the great <s>Dharma</s> of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)—these will be accomplished. You should, O great king, generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)." He replied: "Enough, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! I, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, do not desire supreme perfect enlightenment, being delighted in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Whatever, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—

body.translated_text: Then indeed, O son of good family (<s>kulaputra</s>), the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> said this to King <s>Araṇemin</s>: "Rare, O great king, is human birth; rare is the attainment of the right moment (<s>kṣaṇasaṃpat</s>); rare, like the <s>udumbara</s> flower, is the appearance in the world of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones; rare is the desire for wholesome <s>dharma</s>; rare is right aspiration (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>). The arising of suffering—

body.text: dvirapi samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo rājānamāha - "śuddho mahārāja bodhimārgaḥ / āśayena praṇidhānaṃ kartavyaṃ / paripūryābhiprasannaḥ sa mārgo 'dhyāśayena viśuddhaḥ / ṛjuḥ sa mārgaḥ aśaṭhaḥ / śuddhaḥ sa mārgaḥ kleśapravāhakatvāt / vipulo 'sau mārgaḥ anāvarṇatvāt / samavasaraṇaḥ sa mārgaḥ cintanāya / nirbhayaḥ sa mārgaḥ sarvapāpākaraṇatayā / sumṛduḥ sa mārgaḥ dānapāramitayā / śītalaḥ sa mārgaḥ śīlapāramitayā / nirāśrayaḥ sa mārgaḥ kṣāntipāramitayā / adhiṣṭhānāśrayaḥ sa mārgaḥ vīryapāramitayā / anāvilaḥ sa mārgaḥ dhyānapāramitayā / suviditaḥ sa mārgaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 78.

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitayā / suprasannaḥ sa mārgo mahāmaitryā / svabhāvajñānānugataḥ sa mārgaḥ mahākaruṇayā / sadānanditaḥ sa mārgaḥ mahāmuditayā / akliṣṭaḥ sa mārgaḥ upekṣayā / apagatakaṇṭakaḥ sa mārgaḥ kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkaiḥ / kṣemaṃgamanaḥ sa mārgo 'pratihatacittatayā / dhūrtavirahitaḥ sa mārgaḥ rūpaśabdagandharasasparśaviditatvāt / nihatamārapratyarthikaḥ sa mārgaḥ dhātvāyatanasuvimṛṣṭatvāt / suprabodhaḥ sa mārgaḥ avidyāndhakāranirāvaraṇatvāt / dṛḍhavīryasattvacittagamanaḥ sa mārgaḥ apagataśrāvakapratyekabuddhamanasikāratvāt / utsoḍhaḥ sa mārgaḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitatvāt / mahāratnaniṣpādakaḥ sa mārgaḥ sarvajñatāratnānukūlatvāt / sadāprakāśitaḥ sa mārgaḥ asaṅgajñānasya bhagavataḥ / kuśalamūladeśakānucīrṇaḥ sa mārgaḥ sarvatathāgatānugṛhītatvāt / duṣṭakleśānukūlavigataḥ sa mārgaḥ anunayapratighaprahīṇatvāt / nihatarajaḥ sa mārgaḥ vyāpādakhilakrodhāpagatatvāt / (
children.translated_text: ) by the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). That path is very clear through great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). That path is accompanied by innate knowledge through great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). That path is always joyful through great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>). That path is unafflicted through equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). That path is free from thorns—from the thoughts of desire, ill-will, and harm (<s>kāma-vyāpāda-vihiṃsā-vitarka</s>). That path leads to safety through unobstructed mind. That path is free from rogues—from form (<s>rūpa</s>)—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 79.

children.text: ) sugatigamanīyaḥ sa mārgaḥ sarvākuśalavirahitatvāt / kṣemaṃgamo mahārāja saṃbodhimārgaḥ nirvāṇaparyavasānaḥ / utpādaya mahārāja bodhicittaṃ" / rājā prāha - "ayaṃ brāhmaṇa tathāgataḥ aśītivarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ loka utpanno, na śakyaṃ tathāgatena sarve 'pāyaḥ śamayituṃ / ye sattvā avaruptakuśalamūlaste sattvāḥ phale sthitāḥ, kecit samādhidhāraṇīkṣāntiṣu niṣpannāḥ, utkṛṣṭakuśalamūlāstu ye sattvāste bodhau avaivartyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, kecidavaruptakuśalamūlāḥ devamanuṣyaśriyamanubhavanti / svakasvakaiḥ sattvāḥ kuśalākuśalaiḥ karmabhirbhramanti / katame sattvā bhagavatā vinītāḥ sadekasattvasyāpi duḥkhaṃ na praśāntaṃ, kṣetrabhūtaḥ kevalaṃ bhagavata āśrayaḥ, nānavaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhamocanaṃ karoti / utpādayāmyahaṃ bodhicittaṃ / bodhisattvacaryāṃ caraṃstenāhaṃ mahājñānasamucchrayeṇa acintyenodāreṇa dharmamukhapraveśena sattvān vinayeyaṃ buddhakāryaṃ ca kuryāṃ / na kevalamasmiṃ kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre bodhāya cittaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) That path leads to good destinations because it is devoid of all unwholesomeness (<s>akuśala</s>). The path to enlightenment, O great king, leads to safety and culminates in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Generate the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>), O great king!" The king replied: "This <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, has appeared in the world among a people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years. It is not possible for the <s>Tathāgata</s> to pacify all the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>). Those beings whose roots of merit have been destroyed (<s>avaruptakuśala</s>)—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 80.

children.text: ) pariṇāmayeyaṃ / yadyahaṃ tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ labheyamutpādayeyamahaṃ bodhicittaṃ, tadāhaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi yadāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ ca spṛśeyaṃ, sarvaṃ ca tatra buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ praśamayeyaṃ" /

body.translated_text: A second time the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> said to the king: "Pure, O great king, is the path to enlightenment (<s>bodhimārga</s>). With aspiration, the vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) should be made. Having fulfilled it with faith, that path is purified by superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>). Straight is that path, without deceit. Pure is that path, because it carries away the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). Vast is that path, because it is without obstruction. That path leads to convergence for contemplation. Free from fear—

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastādṛśamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskṛtavān tadādarśavyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / tathā samāhitena bhagavatā ādarśavyūhe samādhau tathārūpāvabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, yenāvabhāsena daśasu dikṣvekaikasyāṃ diśi sahasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā lokadhātavaḥ sarvaguṇavyūhā dṛṣyante; keṣucid buddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvṛtāḥ, keṣucit parinirvāṇāya saṃsthitāḥ; yatra ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bodhivṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇā māraṃ parājayanti, yatra cācirābhisaṃbuddhā dharmacakraṃ pravartayanti, yatra cācirapravṛttadharmacakraṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti, yatra ca buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sphuṭāṃ buddhakṣetrāṃ, yatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmutpādo nāsti, yatra ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhā utpadyante, yatra ca śūnyaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ buddhebhyo bodhisattvebhyaḥ (

children.text: ) śrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyaḥ; kvacit kliṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pañcakaṣāyaṃ, kvacit pariśuddhamapagatapañcakaṣāyaṃ, kvacidutkṛṣṭāḥ sattvāḥ, kvaciddhīnāḥ, kvaciddīrghāyuṣkāḥ, kvacidalpāyuṣkāḥ; kānicidbuddhakṣetrānyagninā saṃvartante, kānicidudakena, kānicidvāyunā; kvacidvivartante, kvacidvivṛttāstiṣṭhanti; te sarva udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭāḥ saṃdṛśyante / sarvāvatī sā parṣattāṃ dṛṣṭvā buddhakṣetre guṇavyūhān, samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ punā rājānametadavocat - "paśya mahārājaitān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān, utpādaya mahārājanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ, gṛhāṇa mahārāja buddhakṣetraṃ yādṛśamākāṅkṣasi" /

body.text: athāraṇemī rājā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - "kena bhagavan karmaṇā bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti, kena karmaṇāpariśuddhaṃ; utkṛṣṭāḥ sattvāḥ kena karmaṇā, yāvaddīrghāyuṣkāḥ sattvā vistaraḥ" / bhagavān āha - "praṇidhānavaśena mahārāja bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti apagatapañcakaṣāyaṃ, praṇidhānenāpariśuddhaṃ" / rājā prāha - "ahaṃ bhadanta (

children.text: ) bhagavan nagaraṃ praviśyaikāgre niṣadya praṇidhānaṃ cintayiṣyāmi, tathārūpaṃ me buddhakṣetramapagatapañcakaṣāyaṃ rocate tatremā subhavacaryā pariṇāmayiṣyāmi" / bhagavān āha - "yasyedānīṃ mahārāja kālaṃ manyase" / atha khalu kulaputra rājāraṇemī bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakāntaḥ / nagaraṃ praviśya svake gṛha ekāgraḥ pratisaṃlīno niṣaṇṇaḥ, buddhakṣetrapraṇidhānaṃ vyūhaṃ cintayati /

body.text: atha khalu samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ rājaputramanimiṣamāmantrayati / "utpādaya tvamanimiṣānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ / yacca tvayā tribhiḥ puṇyakriyāvastubhiḥ śubhaṃ caratā puṇyamārjitaṃ tatsarvamanuttarayāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayā" / sa prāha - "ahamapyupādhyāya svagṛhaṃ gatvaikākī rahogato niṣadya buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃścintayiṣyāmi / yadi bodhāya cittamutpatsyate, punarāgamya bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ bodhicittaṃ pariṇāmayiṣyāmi" / ataḥ so 'pi rājaputro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakāntaḥ, (

children.text: ) svakaṃ niveśanaṃ gatvā ekākī rahogato niṣadya buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ cintayati / atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohito dvitīyaṃ rājaputraṃ nimantrayitvovāca, "utpādaya tvaṃ kumāra bodhicittaṃ", vistareṇa peyālaṃ yāvat, sarvarājaputrasahasraṃ bodhau samādāpayati, caturaśītiḥ koṭṭarājasahasrāṇi, anyāni ca navatiḥ koṭyaḥ sattvānāṃ bodhau samādāpayati / te 'pi sarva evamāhuḥ, "vayamapi svasvagṛhaṃ gatvaikākino niṣadya buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ cintayiṣyāmaḥ" / evamuktvā sarva eva svagṛhāṇi gatvaikākino niṣaṇṇāḥ saptavarṣāṇi buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhapraṇidhānāni cintayanti //

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyaivaṃ apareṇa samayena cetasaḥ parivitarka udāpādi / "mayā khalvanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi samādāpitāni / ayaṃ ca mayā buddho bhagavān saptavarṣāṇi sarvopakarṇairupanimantritaḥ sārdhamaparimitena bhikṣusaṅghena / yadi ca mamānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āśā paripūryate tathā cāyaṃ praṇidhānaṃ saṃpadyate yad ahaṃ devāsuragandharvayakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍān asmin mahāyajñe samādāpayāmi" /

atha kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ purohito vaiśravaṇamākāṅkṣate darśanāya / atha khalu vaiśravaṇo mahārājānekairyakṣaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇastenopajagāmopetya samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyāgrataḥ sthitvaitadavocat - "kiṃ brāhmaṇa matto hyākāṅkṣase?" brāhmaṇaḥ prāha - "ko bhavān?" vaiśrāvaṇaḥ prāha - "śrutaṃ tvayā brāhmaṇāsti vaiśravaṇo nāma yakṣādhipatiḥ / so ahaṃ; brāhmaṇa kim ājñāpayasi kiṃ karavāṇi?" / brāhmaṇaḥ prāha / "śṛṇu yakṣādhipate 'haṃ bhagavatpūjāṃ kariṣye, tvamatrautsukyamāpadyasva" / sa prāha - "tathāstu yathā tvaṃ brāhmaṇākāṅkṣase" / "tena hi tvaṃ mahārāja yākṣān asmākaṃ vacanenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpaya / evaṃ ca punaḥ samādāpaya, sacedyūyaṃ yakṣā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvarthikā gacchata, yūyaṃ pārāt samudrasya gośīrṣaṃ uragasāracandanamānayantu, apare bhagavato 'rthe gandhamapare vividhāṃ puṣpān, yenāhaṃ divasedivase bhagavataḥ pūjāṃ kariṣyāmi" / "evamastu brāhmaṇa", vaiśravaṇo mahārājā tasya brāhmaṇasya pratiśrutya tatraivāntarhitaḥ bherīmāhatya yakṣarākṣasāṃ sannipātyaitadavocat (

children.text: ) - "yat khalu mārṣā jānīyuḥ, ayaṃ jambudvīpe samudrareṇurnāma brāhmaṇo rājño 'raṇemino 'grapurohitaḥ, taṃ ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena saptavarṣāṇi sarvopakaraṇairupasthāsyati / tadyuṣmābhistat kuśalamanumoditavyaṃ, tena ca yūyaṃ kuśalamūlenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayatā" / tena khalu punaḥ samayena bahuyakṣarākṣasakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi añjaliṃ kṛtvocuḥ / "yaḥ samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasya puṇyābhisyandaḥ kuśalābhiṣyando ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saptavarṣāṇi sarvopakaraṇairupatiṣṭhati sārdhamaparimitena bhikṣusaṅghena, tatsarvaṃ vayaṃ puṇyaskandhamanumodāmastena ca kuśalamūlenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyemahi" / vaiśravaṇo mahārājaḥ prāha - "śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ, yaḥ kaścid yuṣmākaṃ kuśalamūlenārthikaḥ puṇyārthī sa saptavarṣān pārāt samudrasya gośīrṣoragasāracandanamānayatu, yena samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo bhagavato bhikṣusaṅghasya cāhāraṃ sajjīkuryāt" / tato dvānavatiyakṣasahasrāṇi ekakaṇṭhenodāhṛtavantaḥ / "vayaṃ mārṣā imān saptavarṣān gośīrṣamuragasāracandanamānayiṣyāmo, (

) yena samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo bhagavato 'rthāyāhāraṃ sajjīkariṣyati bhikṣusaṅghasya ca" / ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadyakṣasahasrāṇi kathayanti / "vayaṃ gandhamānayiṣyāmaḥ" / dvāpañcāśadyakṣasahasrāṇi kathayanti / "vayaṃ vicitrān puṣpān ānayiṣyāmaḥ" / viṃśadyakṣasahasrāṇi kathayanti / "vayaṃ vividharasāyanānāmojāṃ gṛhnīmo bhagavato 'rthāya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca, yadannapānasajjīkṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati tatraujāṃ prakṣepsyāmaḥ" / saptatiryakṣasahasrāṇi kathayanti / "vayaṃ mārṣā bhagavato 'rthāyāhāraṃ sajjīkariṣyāmo bhikṣusaṅghasya ca" /

And we have adorned the entire park for the sake of the Blessed One and the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s>. Therefore, rejoicing in this root of merit, generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) at the exhortation of the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s>." body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ ketapuriṃ nāma mahābrahmāṇamākāṅkṣate upasaṃkramaṇāya / yāvadbrāhmaṇasya sakāśāt pratiśrutya brahmalokāt, yāvad bahuprāṇikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayanti, tataścāvataranti bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca, bhagavataścāntikāddharmāśravaṇāya / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 93.

children.text: ) atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo dvitīyāyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ śakramākāṅkṣate suyāmaṃ saṃtuṣitaṃ sunirmitaṃ paranirmitavaśavartinaṃ ca devaputramākāṅkṣate darśanāya / te 'pi pañcadevarājāno bhagavato 'nubhāvena brāhmaṇasya sakāśamupasaṃkrāntastān brāhmaṇaḥ samanuśiṣṭavān / te 'pi svakāni bhavanāni gatvā svakāṃ parṣadaṃ brāhmaṇahastena samādāpayanti / evaṃ bahubhistrayastriṃśaddevaniyutaśatasahasrairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni sastrīpuruṣadārakadārikaiste ca sahaśakreṇemāṃ cāturdvīpikāmāgatā bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, bhagavataścāntikāddharmaṃ śrotuṃ / evaṃ suyāmaḥ saṃtuṣitaḥ sunirmitaḥ paranirmitavaśavartī devaputraḥ yāvat paranirmitavaśavartikān devān bodhāya samādāpayitvā bahubhiḥ paranirmitavaśavartidevakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sastrīpuruṣadārakadārikairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtacittotpādaiścāturdvīpikāmāgatā bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, bhagavataścāntikāddharmaṃ śrotuṃ / evaṃ dvitīyāyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ asurendrā mārā brahmāṇaḥ, (
children.translated_text: ) Then, O son of good family, in the second four-continent world-system, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> wished for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, and the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Paranirmitavaśavartī</s> to come for an audience. Those five divine kings too, by the power of the Blessed One, approached the brahmin, and the brahmin instructed them. They too, having gone to their own abodes, inspired their own assemblies by the brahmin's hand. Thus many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods — together with men, women, boys, and girls — generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and came to this four-continent world-system together with <s>Śakra</s> for the sight of the Blessed One, for veneration, for attendance, and to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> as well, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. Likewise <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, and the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Paranirmitavaśavartī</s>, having inspired the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartī</s> gods toward awakening — many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Paranirmitavaśavartī</s> gods, together with men, women, boys, and girls who had generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> — came to this four-continent world-system for the sight of the Blessed One, for veneration, for attendance, and to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> as well, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. Thus in the second four-continent world-system, the <s>asura</s> lords, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s> [were likewise inspired], (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 94.

children.text: ) evaṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ caturthyāṃ pañcamyāṃ śakrasuyāmasaṃtuṣitanirmāṇaparanirmitāsurendra mārā brahmāṇaḥ buddhānubhāvenemāṃ cāturdvīpikāṃ āgatāḥ sapariṣaṭkā yāvan te dharmaśravaṇāya / evaṃ yāvattrisāhasramahāsāhasrādbuddhakṣetrāt koṭīśataṃ śakrāṇāṃ koṭiśataṃ suyāmānāṃ koṭīśataṃ saṃtuṣitānāṃ koṭīśataṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ koṭīśataṃ paranirmitavaśavartīnāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ, koṭīśatamasurendrāṇāṃ koṭīśataṃ mārāṇāṃ koṭīśataṃ mahābrahmaṇāṃ ekaiko mahābrahmānekaiḥ koṭīniyutaśatasahasrairbrahmakāyikānāṃ devānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtacittotpādānāṃ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto bhagavadanubhāvenemāṃ cāturdvīpikāmāgato bhagavato darśanāyopasaṃkramaṇāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca bhagavataścāntikāddharmaṃ śrotuṃ / tadā ca trisāhasramahāsāhasrayāṃ lokadhātau nāsti sa kāścit pṛthivīpradeśo yo na sphuṭo 'bhūt //
children.translated_text: ) and likewise in the third four-continent world-system, the fourth, and the fifth — <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmita</s>, <s>asura</s> lords, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, came to this four-continent world-system with their retinues, for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, from throughout the entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field): a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śakras</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Suyāmas</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Saṃtuṣitas</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Paranirmitavaśavartī</s> <s>devaputras</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>asura</s> lords, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of great <s>Brahmās</s> — each great <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded and accompanied by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods who had generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> — came by the power of the Blessed One to this four-continent world-system to approach the Blessed One for an audience, for veneration, for attendance, and to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> as well, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. And at that time, in the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) realm, there was no spot of earth that was not completely filled.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> wished for the great <s>Brahmā</s> named <s>Ketapuri</s> to approach. <s>Brahmā</s>, having agreed in the presence of the brahmin, [descended] from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and descended for the sight of the Blessed One, for veneration, for attendance, and to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> as well, and for hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyaitadabhavat / "yadi mamānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvāśāparipūrirbhavati tadyathaivaṃ koṭīśataṃ vaiśravaṇānāṃ yāvat koṭīśataṃ mahābrahmaṇāṃ māmanuvartanti tathaivaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 95.

children.text: ) me bhagavān anuvartate / yadevaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ kuryāt yāvattrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau manuṣyāḥ tiryāñco yāmalokikā nairayikāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ duḥkhāvedanā praśāmyeta sukhāvedanotpadyeta, teṣāṃ caikaikakasyāgrato buddhanirmitaṃ tiṣṭhet yastāṃ sattvān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayet" / atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasya cetasā cittamājñāya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ pratāpaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / yathā samāhitena cittena bhagavān pratāpe samādhau bhagavataḥ kāyādaikaikasmād romakūpād gaṇanāsamatikrāntā raśmaya udgatāstaiśca raśmibhirayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ sphuṭo 'bhut / sa tatra kecid raśmayo narakaṃ gatvā śītanarakopapannānāṃ sattvānāmuṣṇā vāyavo vānti, ye uṣṇanarakopapannāḥ sattvāsteṣāṃ śītalā vāyavo vānti yena teṣāṃ nairayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvaṃ kṣuttarṣaśramaduḥkhaṃ praśāmyati sukhāvedanotpadyate / ekaikasya ca nairayikasya nirmito buddhavigraho 'gratastiṣṭhati dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇairalaṅkṛtagātraḥ aśītibhiranuvyañjanaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaśarīraḥ / atha teṣāṃ nairayikānāṃ sukhasamarpitānāmetadabhūt / (
children.translated_text: ) may the Blessed One assent to me, and may he perform such a great miracle that throughout the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) realm, the painful sensations of all humans, animals, beings in <s>Yama</s>'s world, and hell-beings would be pacified and sensations of happiness would arise, and before each and every one of those beings a <s>Buddha</s>-emanation would stand to inspire those beings toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)." Then, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, knowing the mind of the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> with his own mind, at that moment entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called <s>Pratāpa</s> (Radiant Power). As the Blessed One's mind was concentrated in the <s>Pratāpa</s> <s>samādhi</s>, from each and every pore of the Blessed One's body, rays beyond counting emerged, and by those rays this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) realm was filled. Some of those rays went to the hells — for beings reborn in cold hells, warm winds blew; for beings reborn in hot hells, cool winds blew — whereby all the suffering of hunger, thirst, exhaustion, and pain of those hell-beings was pacified and sensations of happiness arose. And before each hell-being appeared an emanated <s>Buddha</s>-form, with a body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being and a body embellished with the eighty minor marks. Then those hell-beings, having been established in happiness, had this thought: (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 96.

children.text: ) "kiṃ pratyayamasmākaṃ duḥkhapraśāntaṃ sukhaṃ ca prādurbhūtaṃ?" / te taṃ bhagavantaṃ paśyanti dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇairalaṅkṛtaṃ aśītyanuvyañjanavirājitagātraṃ / te taṃ dṛṣṭvaivamāhuḥ / "asya mahākāruṇikasya mahātmano 'nubhāvena vayamevaṃ sukhinaḥ saṃvṛttāḥ" / te prītisaumanasyajātaḥ prasannamanaso bhagavantaṃ prekṣante / teṣāṃ bhagavānāha - "sādhu yūyaṃ sattvā namo buddhāyeti vācaṃ bhāṣatāṃ, anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayata / evaṃ yuṣmākaṃ duḥkhāvedanā na bhūya utpadyate, nityaṃ ca sukhāyā vedanāyā lābhino bhaviṣyatha" / ta evaṃ āhuḥ / "namo buddhāyotpādayāmo vayamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ, taccāsmākaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ karmāvaraṇākṣayāya saṃvartatu" / tataśca kecit cyutvā manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupapadyante / ye nairayikāḥ sattvā agninā dahyante teṣāṃ te raśmayaḥ śītalān vāyūn pramuñcanti, te taiḥ spṛṣṭāḥ praśāntakṣuttarṣāścāduḥkhā bhavanti, yāvat kecit tataścyāvitvā manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ upapadyante / evaṃ tiryagyonirvaktavyā evaṃ yāvan manuṣyā vaktavyāḥ / sā ca prabhā pratinivṛtyā bhagavantaṃ triṣkṛtvaḥ (
children.translated_text: ) "For what reason has our suffering been pacified and happiness arisen?" They see that Blessed One adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with eighty minor marks. Having seen him, they say thus: "By the power of this greatly compassionate, great-souled one, we have become happy." Filled with joy and delight, with clear minds, they gaze upon the Blessed One. The Blessed One said to them: "Well done! You beings, utter the words 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>' and generate the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Thus painful feelings will no longer arise for you, and you will always be recipients of pleasant feelings." They said thus: "Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! We generate the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening; may our root of merit serve to exhaust our <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obscurations)." Then some, having departed from there, are reborn in the human realm. For those hellish beings who are being burned by fire, those rays release cool winds; touched by those winds, their hunger and thirst are pacified and they become free of suffering, and some, having departed from there, are reborn in the human realm. The same should be said for the animal realm, and likewise up to the human realm. And that radiance, having returned, circumambulated the Blessed One three times (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 97.

children.text:
) pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitā, dṛṣṭvā ca gaṇanātikrāntā devamanuṣyā yakṣarākṣasanāgāsurā avaivartikāḥ sthāpitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, gaṇanātikrāntaśca sattvāḥ samādhikṣāntidhāraṇī pratilabdhavantaḥ / yairjambūdvīpakairmanuṣyaiḥ śrutamañjure nagare rājadhānyāṃ jambūvanodyānaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca devairdivyairalaṅkāravibhūṣaṇairalaṅkṛtaṃ
/ "yannūnaṃ vayaṃ gatvā paśyemaḥ, tatra ca ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyema bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca / tatra gatvā bhagavataḥ sakāśād dharmaṃ śṛṇuyāmaḥ" / tena khalu punaḥ samayena divasedivase 'nekāni devamanuṣyebhyaḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikākoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi mañjurakaṃ nagaramāgacchanti bhagavato darśanāyopasaṃkramaṇāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, taṃ codyānāṃ didṛkṣavaḥ / tasya codyānasya viṃśaddvārasahasrāṇi saptaratnamayānyabhūvan / ekaikasminnudyānadvāre pañcapañcaśatāni ratnapīṭhānāṃ prajñaptāni, teṣu ca pañcapañcamāṇavakaśatānyupaviṣṭāni, ye te sattvā gatāstamudyānaṃ praviśanti tāṃste māṇavakā buddhasāraṇaṃ gamayanti dharmaśaraṇaṃ gamayanti saṅghaśaraṇaṃ gamayanti, anuttarāyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) and having circumambulated, disappeared into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance). Having witnessed this, innumerable gods, humans, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> were established as non-retrogressing in unsurpassed perfect awakening, and innumerable beings attained <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention). Those humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who heard that the <s>Jambūvana</s> garden in the royal capital, the city of <s>Mañjura</s>, had been adorned with divine ornaments and decorations by the gods for the sake of the Blessed One and the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s> — [they said:] "Let us go and see; let us see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> and the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>; having gone there, let us hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One." At that time, day after day, many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of gods, humans, men, women, boys, and girls came to the city of <s>Mañjuraka</s> to see, approach, and attend upon the Blessed One and the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>, and desiring to see that garden. That garden had twenty thousand gates made of the seven precious substances. At each garden gate, five hundred jeweled seats were arranged, and on them sat five hundred young men. Those beings who went and entered that garden — those young men led them to take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, take refuge in the <s>Saṅgha</s>, [and encouraged them] in unsurpassed (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 98.

children.text: ) samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayanti cittaṃ cotpādayanti, āsanasthā ye dūrasthāyinaḥ paścāttamudyānaṃ praviśanti bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca darśanāya /
children.translated_text: ) perfect awakening — they inspired them and generated their minds [toward it]. Those seated [at the gates] who came from far away would afterwards enter that garden to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One, and to see the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> had this thought: "If my aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) is to be fulfilled, then just as a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Vaiśravaṇas</s> and up to a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of great <s>Brahmās</s> follow me, so too (

body.text: evaṃ samudrareṇumā brāhmaṇenāgrapurohitena tāni saptavarṣāṇi gaṇanātikrāntā devā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā vinītā niveṣitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā, gaṇanātikrāntā nāgāḥ asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ kumbhāṇḍā gandharvāḥ pretāḥ piśācā nairayikā gaṇanātikrāntāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā vinītā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, yāvat tiryagyonigatā iti / sa teṣāṃ saptānāṃ varṣāṇāmatyayena samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaścaturaśītiścakrasahasrāṇi sthāpayitvā divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ, caturaśītihastisahasrāṇi saptaratnālaṅkāravibhūṣitāni sthāpayitvā hastiratnaṃ, yāvaccaturaśītirathasahasrāṇi niryātayati / teṣāṃ saptānāṃ varṣāṇāṃ atyayena rājño 'raṇeminaḥ na rāgacchanda utpadyate, na dveṣacchandaḥ na mohacchandaḥ na rājacchandaḥ na dhanacchandaḥ na (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 99.

children.text: ) putracchandaḥ na devīcchandaḥ nāhāracchandaḥ na pānacchandaḥ na vastracchandaḥ na gandhacchandaḥ na yānacchandaḥ na nidracchandaḥ nātmacchandaḥ, na paracchandaṃ kṛtavān / saptavarṣāṇi na pārśvaṃ nikṣiptavān / na cāsya rātrisaṃjñā utpannā, na divasasaṃjñā utpannā, na rūpasaṃjñāṃ na śabdasaṃjñāṃ na rasasaṃjñāṃ na gandhasaṃjñāṃ na sparśāsaṃjñāṃ utpāditavān / taiśca saptabhirvarṣaiḥ kāyaśramo notpannaḥ, nityaṃ satatasamitaṃ daśasu dikṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi sahasraṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paramāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ paśyati / na ca sumeruścakṣuṣo 'vabhāsamāgacchati, nānye parvatāḥ na cakravāḍamahācakravāḍāḥ na lokāntarikā na candrādityau na divyāni vimānāni cakṣuṣo 'vabhāsaṃ āgacchanti / yathā tāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhāṃ paśyati, tathaiva pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyan praṇidhānaṃ cintayati / yathāraṇemī rājā īdṛśena sukhaguṇavihāreṇa saptavarṣāṇi viharati, īdṛśān buddhakṣetraguṇavyuhān paśyati, pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ praṇidhānaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) desire for sons, no desire for queens, no desire for food, no desire for drink, no desire for clothing, no desire for fragrance, no desire for vehicles, no desire for sleep, no desire for self, and he harbored no desire for others. For seven years he did not lie down on his side. No perception of night arose in him, no perception of day arose; he did not generate perception of form, perception of sound, perception of taste, perception of smell, or perception of touch. During those seven years, no bodily fatigue arose; constantly and continuously, in each of the ten directions, in world-realms equal to the atoms of a thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields, he beheld the splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Neither <s>Sumeru</s> appeared before his eyes, nor other mountains, nor <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, nor the inter-world darkness, nor the moon and sun, nor divine palaces appeared before his eyes. Just as he beheld those pure <s>Buddha</s>-fields, so too, beholding the splendid qualities of pure <s>Buddha</s>-fields, he contemplated his aspiration. Just as King <s>Araṇemi</s> dwelt for seven years in such a blissful, virtuous abiding, beholding such splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, [contemplating] the aspiration for the splendid qualities of a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 100.

children.text:
) cintayanniṣaṇṇaḥ, evamanimiṣo jyeṣṭho rājaputraḥ, nimuḥ, indragaṇaḥ, evaṃ tadrājñaḥ sarvaṃ putrasahastaṃ ca caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi aparāṇi ca dvānavatiprāṇakoṭyaḥ sarvāṇyevameva saptavarṣāṇi ekākino rahogatāḥ pratisaṃlīnāḥ, daśasu dikṣvaikaikasyāṃ diśi sahasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān lokadhātūn paśyanti / na ca teṣāṃ saptānāṃ varṣāṇāṃ antareṇa rāgacchanda utpanno na dveṣacchando na mohacchandaḥ, yāvat na teṣāṃ śramasthānamutpannamabhūt / satatasamitaṃ ca daśasu dikṣvaikaikasyāṃ diśi sahasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyanti / na ca teṣāṃ sumeruścakṣuso 'vabhāsamāgacchati,
na cānye parvatā yāvanna divyāni vimānāni cakṣuṣo 'vabhāsamāgacchanti / yathaiva te buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ dṛṣṭāḥ tathaiva pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhapraṇidhānaṃ cintayanti / sarva evamīdṛśena guṇavihāreṇa saptavarṣān viharanti / kecit pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ cintayanti, kecid apariśuddhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ cintayanti //
children.translated_text: ) — sat contemplating; so too <s>Animiṣa</s>, the eldest prince, <s>Nimu</s>, <s>Indragaṇa</s> — thus that king's entire thousand sons, eighty-four thousand vassal kings, and the other ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of beings — all of them likewise for seven years, alone, in seclusion, in meditative retreat, beheld world-realms equal in number to the atoms of a thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields in each of the ten directions. During those seven years, no desire for passion arose in them, no desire for hatred, no desire for delusion, and no place of fatigue arose in them. Constantly and continuously, in each of the ten directions, they beheld the splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in world-realms equal to the atoms of a thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Neither <s>Sumeru</s> appeared before their eyes, nor other mountains, nor up to divine palaces appeared before their eyes. Just as they beheld those splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, so too they contemplated the aspiration for the splendid qualities of a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field. All of them dwelt for seven years in such a virtuous abiding. Some contemplated the splendid qualities of a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field; some contemplated the splendid qualities of an impure <s>Buddha</s>-field.

body.translated_text: Thus, during those seven years, by <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin, the chief priest, innumerable gods were inspired, trained, established, and grounded in unsurpassed perfect awakening; innumerable <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, hell-beings — innumerable beings were inspired, trained, established, and grounded in unsurpassed perfect awakening, and likewise those born in the animal realm. At the end of those seven years, <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin offered eighty-four thousand wheels along with the divine wheel-jewel, eighty-four thousand elephants adorned with ornaments of the seven precious substances along with the elephant-jewel, and up to eighty-four thousand chariots. At the end of those seven years, in King <s>Araṇemi</s> there arose no desire for passion, no desire for hatred, no desire for delusion, no desire for kingship, no desire for wealth, no (

body.text: atha khalu samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇastāni saptavarṣāṇi nirgatāni niṣṭhitāni viditvā saptaratnaṃ niryātayati / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 101.

children.text: ) yena ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - "mayā bhadanta bhagavan rājāraṇemī anutarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitaḥ, sa gṛhaṃ gatvaikākī rahogataḥ pratisaṃlīno niṣaṇṇaḥ, na cātra kasyacin manuṣyasya praveśo dīyate / evaṃ tatsahasraṃ rājaputrāṇāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitaṃ / evameva pratiprati svagṛhāṇi gatvā ekākinaḥ pratisaṃlayananiṣaṇṇaṃ, na cātra kasyacit praveśo dīyate / evaṃ yāvaccaturaśītiḥ koṭṭarājasahasrāṇi evamapare dvānavatiḥ prāṇakoṭyo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāḥ niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, sarve svakasvakāni gṛhāṇi gatvā hyekākino rahasi gatā niṣadya pratisaṃlīnā, na cātra kasyacit praveśo dīyate / bhagavāṃścaināṃ samanvāharatu yāvad rājāraṇemī tasmāt pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāyehāgacchet; te 'pi sarva ihagaccheyuḥ ye mayā sarve bodhau samādāpitāḥ acalāṃ ca buddhimanugṛhṇeyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, bhagavataścāntikādvyākaraṇaṃ prāpnuyurgotraṃ ca nāma ca buddhakṣetraṃ ca pratigṛhṇīyuḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) He approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, joined his palms in salutation, and said this to the Blessed One: "By me, Venerable Blessed One, King <s>Araṇemi</s> has been inspired toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. He has gone home, alone, in seclusion, seated in meditative retreat, and no human being is allowed entry there. Likewise, those thousand princes have been inspired toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. Each one likewise has gone to his own home, alone, seated in meditative retreat, and no one is allowed entry there. Likewise up to eighty-four thousand vassal kings, and the other ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of beings have been inspired, established, and grounded in unsurpassed perfect awakening; all have gone to their respective homes, alone, gone into seclusion, seated in meditative retreat, and no one is allowed entry there. May the Blessed One attend to them until King <s>Araṇemi</s> arises from that meditative retreat and comes here; may all those whom I have inspired toward awakening also come here; may they receive unshakeable resolve in unsurpassed perfect awakening; and may they receive from the Blessed One a prophecy, and accept their lineage, name, and <s>Buddha</s>-field."

body.translated_text: Then <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin, knowing that those seven years had elapsed and concluded, offered the seven precious substances. (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 102.

children.text: ) samyaksaṃbuddho nirhārapatiṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / yathā samāpannasya mukhānnīlapītalohitāvadātamañjiṣṭhāsphaṭikavarṇā arciṣo niścaranti / yāṃ niśṛtya teṣāṃ pratisaṃlīnānāṃ viharatāmagrato brahmanirmitaḥ sthita evamāha / "uttiṣṭhata mārṣā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramata vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca, parisamāptā mārṣā samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasya saptavārṣiko yajñaḥ / bhagavān punaranyena caryāṃ prakramiṣyati" / tataste sarve raśmibhiḥ saṃcoditāḥ, utthāya rājānamaraṇeminaṃ codayanti / sa taiḥ saṃcodito vyutthitaḥ prasthitaśca, prasthitasya ca tasya rājño devatā gaganatale bherīmṛdaṃgapaṭahādīn vādyāni pravādayanti /
children.translated_text: ) the Perfectly Awakened One, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Nirhārapati</s> ("Lord of Emanation"). As he entered it, from his mouth issued forth rays of blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal colors. Relying on those rays, before each of those who were dwelling in meditative retreat, a <s>Brahmā</s>-created apparition stood and spoke thus: "Arise, good sirs! Go to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One and the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>. The seven-year sacrifice of <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin is complete, good sirs. The Blessed One will now set forth on another course." Then all of them, urged by those rays, arose and urged King <s>Araṇemi</s>. Urged by them, he arose and set forth; and as the king set forth, deities in the sky sounded drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, kettledrums, and other instruments.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, (

body.text: atha khalu rājāraṇemī rathābhirūḍhaḥ tena putrasahasreṇa caturaśītibhiśca koṭṭarājasahasrairdvānavatibhiśca prāṇakoṭibhiḥ parivṛto nagarānniryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / sa yāvad yānasya bhūmistāvadyānena yātvā yānād avatarati, yānād avatīrya padbhyāmeva jambūvanaṃ praviveśa, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 103.

children.text: ) praviśya ca yena bhagavāṃstenopajagāma, upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śīrasābhivandya bhikṣusaṅghasya caikānte nyaṣīdat sārdham anekaiḥ prāṇakoṭibhiḥ / atha samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo rājānamaraṇeminaṃ prāha - "anumodatu mahārājemaṃ yacca tvayā māstrayaṃ bhagavataḥ upasthānaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ aparimitasya bhikṣusaṅghasya ca nānāvicitrāṇi ca ratnāni niryātitāni caturaśītiśca nagarasahasrāṇi, tadevānumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ yacca parityāgasahagataṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ sarvaṃ pariṇāmayānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / evaṃ tad rājñaḥ putrasahasraṃ samādāpayati tathaiva caturaśītiḥ koṭṭarājasahasrāṇi aparāśca bahuprāṇakoṭyaḥ, tenānumodanāsahagatena puṇyaskandhenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evaṃ cāha - "anumodata yūyamiha dakṣiṇāṃ niryātayata" / kathayati ca /
children.translated_text: ) and having entered, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>, and sat down to one side together with many <s>koṭīs</s> of beings. Then <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin said to King <s>Araṇemi</s>: "Rejoice, O great king! The service you rendered to the Blessed One with all provisions, and to the immeasurable <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s>, and the various and diverse jewels you offered, and the eighty-four thousand cities — dedicate that entire mass of merit accompanied by rejoicing, and the mass of merit accompanied by renunciation, toward unsurpassed perfect awakening." Thus he inspired the king's thousand sons, likewise the eighty-four thousand vassal kings and the many other <s>koṭīs</s> of beings; through that mass of merit accompanied by rejoicing, they were inspired and established in unsurpassed perfect awakening. And he said: "Rejoice, all of you! Offer the gift here." And he spoke:

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Araṇemi</s>, having mounted his chariot, surrounded by those thousand sons, eighty-four thousand vassal kings, and ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of beings, set forth from the city to the presence of the Blessed One, to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One. He went by vehicle as far as was passable by vehicle, then descended from the vehicle; having descended, he entered the <s>Jambūvana</s> garden on foot, (

children.translated_text: "By this gift, I seek not the abode of <s>Indra</s>, nor fruit in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>,
Nor do I desire the glory of kingship, fickle as the force of a swift wind.

children.text: dānasyāsya phalaṃ tu bhaktimahato yan me ha tenāpnuyāṃ /
children.translated_text: But by the fruit of this gift, born of great devotion, may I attain
The incomparable <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that brings mastery of mind, and may I ferry beings across."

body.text: iti śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīke dānavisargastṛtīyaḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, the Chapter on the Giving of Gifts, in the holy <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s>. // 3 //

body.text: IV bodhisattvavyākaraṇaparivartaścaturthaḥ
body.translated_text: IV. The Fourth Chapter: The Chapter on the Prophecy of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyaitad abhavat / "bahyo 'nena samudrareṇunā brāhmaṇena prāṇakoṭyo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā avaivartikabhūmau sthāpitāste ca mayā vyākartavyā buddhakṣetrāśca darśayitavyāḥ" / atha khalu bhagavān bodhicittāsaṃpramoṣaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / smitaṃ ca prāviṣkṛtavān, yena smitāviṣkaraṇenānantā paryantā buddhakṣetrā udareṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya rājño 'raṇemino 'nyeṣāṃ ca bahūnāṃ prāṇakoṭināṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ ādarśayati / tena khalu punaḥ samayena daśasu dikṣu gaṇanātikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ tamavabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā buddhānubhāvenemāṃ lokadhātuṃ samāgatā bhagavato darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca / te ca vividhairbodhisattvavikurvitairbhagavataḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ paryupāsya purato niṣaṇṇā bodhisattvapraṇidhānaṃ śrotukāmāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family (<s>kulaputra</s>), this thought arose in <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One: "Many <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of beings have been inspired, established, and settled by this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> in supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and placed on the stage of non-regression (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>), and they should be given prophecies by me, and their <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) should be shown." Then the Blessed One entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Bodhicittāsaṃpramoṣa</s> (Non-Forgetfulness of the Enlightenment-Mind). And he manifested a smile, by which manifestation of the smile immeasurable and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were illuminated with a great radiance, and to King <s>Araṇemin</s> and to many other <s>koṭīs</s> of beings—

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohitaḥ rājānamaraṇeminamāha - "tvaṃ tāvan mahārāja prathamaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva" / atha rājānaṇemī yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - "ahaṃ bhagavan bodhyarthikaḥ, yanmayā māsatrayaṃ bhagavato nānāvidhairupakaraṇairupasthānaṃ kṛtamaprameyasya ca bhikṣusaṅghasya tanmayā kuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitaṃ / imāni ca bhagavan mayā saptavarṣāṇi buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāścintitā; yatrāhaṃ bhagavan buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho yatra na nirayā syurna tiryagyonirna yamalokāḥ / ye ca sattvāścyavayuste mā durgatāvupapadyeyuḥ / sarve tatra sattvāḥ suvarṇvarṇā bhaveyuḥ / sarveṣāṃ tatra devamanuṣyāṇāṃ nānātvaṃ na syāt / sarve tatra sattvā jātismarāḥ / sarvasattvāścaivaṃrūpeṇa divyena cakṣuṣā samanvāgatāḥ syuryad buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhato yāpayato dharmaṃ ca deśayataḥ paśyeyuḥ / sarvasattvāścaivaṃrupeṇa divyena śrotreṇa samanvāgatāḥ syuḥ, yad buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 107.

children.text: ) śṛṇuyuḥ / sarvasattvāścaivaṃrūpeṇa paracittajñānena samanvāgatāḥ syuḥ, teṣāṃ bahubuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrasthitānāṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaritānyājāneyuḥ / sarvasattvāḥ tathāvidhenarddhikauśalyena samanvāgatāḥ syuryadekacittotpādena buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi atikrameyuḥ / mā ca tatra sattvā bhaveyuḥ parigrahavanto 'ntataḥ svaśarīre 'pyanāgṛhītamānasāḥ / sarvasattvāścāvaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / sarvasattvāścopapādukāḥ syuḥ / na tatra mātṛgrāmasya prajñaptirbhavet / na tatra sattvānāṃ āyuḥ pramāṇaparyantaḥ syād, anyatra praṇidhānavaśena / na tatra sattvānāmakuśalasya nāmāpi syāt / na tatra buddhakṣetre durgandhaṃ syāt, divyātikrāntena bhagavadgandhena tadbuddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ syāt / sarvasattvāśca dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtāḥ syuḥ / sarvasattvāścaikajātipratibaddhāḥ syuḥ, sthāpayitvā praṇidhānaṃ / sarvasattvāstatraikapūrvāhṇena buddhānubhāvena gaṇanātikrāntān buddhān paryupāsīran, yāvad vividhena bodhisattvavikurvitenākāṅkṣeyuḥ buddhānāṃ pūjāṃ kartuṃ tathaiva teṣāṃ siddhyeyuḥ, tenaiva pūrvabhaktena vivarteyuḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) they might hear. And all beings would be endowed with such knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>) that they would know the mental dispositions of beings dwelling in many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. All beings would be endowed with such mastery of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhikauśalya</s>) that with a single arising of thought they could traverse hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And there would be no beings with possessive attachments, not even grasping at their own bodies. All beings would be irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in supreme perfect enlightenment. All beings would be spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). There would be no designation of womankind there—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 108.

children.text:
) sarvasattvāśca buddhapiṭakaṃ kathayeyuḥ / sarvasattvāśca nārāyaṇabalasamanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ / na kaścit sattvo buddhakṣetraguṇālaṅkārasya varṇaparyantaṃ śaktaḥ syādgṛhītumantaśo divyenāpi cakṣuṣā / sarvasattvāstatra pratisaṃvitprāptāḥ syuḥ, asaṃkhyeyapratibhānāḥ / ekaikasya ca bodhisattvasya yojanasahasrapramāṇaṃ syāt / prabhāsvaraṃ ca tadbuddhakṣetraṃ syāt, samantena ca gaṇanātikrāntā buddhakṣetraguṇavyuhāstatra dṛśyeyuḥ / ye cātra sattvā upapadyeyuryāvadbodhiparyantena brahmacāriṇaḥ syuḥ / sarvasattvāḥ sadevakasya lokasya namasyanīyāḥ syuḥ, yāvad bodhiparyantena nendriyavikalā bhaveyuḥ / sahopapannāśca tatra sattvā divyātikrāntamāryaprītisukhaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / sarvasattvāśca tatra kuśalamūlasamavadhānāḥ syuḥ / sarvasattvāśca tatra navāni vastrāṇi kāśāyāṇi dhārayeyuḥ / sahopapannāśca tatra sattvāḥ suvibhaktivatīṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, yasya samādheḥ pratilābhādgaṇanātikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvā buddhān paryupasīran yāvad bodhiparyantenānupaśyeyuḥ
/ ye ca tatra bodhisattvā upapadyeyuḥ te yādṛgjātīyāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān ākāṅkṣeyuḥ tādṛgjātīyān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ (
children.translated_text: ) all beings would teach the <s>Buddhapiṭaka</s> (Buddha's collection). All beings would be endowed with the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. No being would be able to grasp the full extent of the glory of the ornamental qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, even with the divine eye. All beings there would have attained the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), with inexhaustible eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>). Each <s>bodhisattva</s> would be a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in stature. That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be luminous, and on all sides, qualities of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond reckoning would be visible there. And whatever beings would be reborn there, they would observe celibacy (<s>brahmacārya</s>) until the attainment of enlightenment. All—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 109.

children.text: ) teṣu ratnavṛkṣeṣu paśyeyuḥ / sahopapannāśca sattvāḥ samādhiṃ pratilabheyuryasya samādheḥ pratilābhāt daśasu dikṣu gaṇanātikrānteṣu anyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhāstiṣṭhato yāpayato nityaṃ paśyeyurye tatra sattvāḥ pratyājāyeyuḥ te sarva evaṃrūpeṇa cīvaravimānālaṅkārābharaṇavarṇarūpeṇa syuryathā paranirmitavaśavartino devāḥ / na tatra buddhakṣetre pāṃśuśilā kālaparvatā bhaveyuḥ, na cakravāḍamahācakravāḍā na sumerurna mahāsamudrāḥ; na tatrāvareṇanivaraṇakleśaśabdāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvataśca; tatra narakatiryagyoniyamalokaśabdo na syānnākṣaṇaśabdo na duḥkhaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) they would see in those jewel-trees. And beings born there would attain a <s>samādhi</s>, upon attaining which they would constantly see the <s>Buddhas</s> presiding in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond reckoning in the ten directions. Whatever beings would be reborn there, they would all have such appearance in robes, palaces, ornaments, adornments, complexion, and form as the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no dust, rocks, dark mountains, no <s>Cakravāḍa</s> or <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, no <s>Sumeru</s>, no great oceans; there would be utterly no words for hindrances, obstacles, or afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) anywhere whatsoever; there—

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest (<s>agrapurohita</s>), said to King <s>Araṇemin</s>: "You first, O great king, should accept the array of qualities of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field)." Then King <s>Araṇemin</s>, extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: "I, O Blessed One, am a seeker of enlightenment (<s>bodhyarthika</s>). The service I have rendered to the Blessed One for three months with various requisites, and to the immeasurable <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> (community of monks)—that root of merit I have dedicated to supreme perfect enlightenment. And, O Blessed One, for seven years I have contemplated the array of qualities of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; where I, O Blessed One, as a <s>Buddha</s>—

body.text: evaṃrūpeṇāhaṃ bhagavan buddhakṣetreṇārthī; tāvadahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvaduṣkaracaryāṃ cariṣye yāvannaivaṃrūpairguṇairbuddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayiṣye; evamahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan puruṣakāraṃ kariṣye, tataḥ paścādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsye / daśayojanasāhasrikaśca me bodhivṛkṣo bhavet, tatra niṣaṇṇaścāhamekakṣaṇenacittotpādenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeya / apramāṇā ca me prabhā syāt buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇām (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 110.

children.text: ) avabhāsayanti / aparimāṇā ca mamāyurbhavedaprameyakalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ na śakyaṃ kenacid gaṇayitumanyatra sārvajñena jñānena / aprameyaśca me bodhisattvasaṅghaḥ syāt śrāvakapratyekabuddhavarjito, yanna śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ anyatra sārvajñena jñānena / bodhiprāptasya ca mamāprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu anyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavanto varṇabhāṣaṇaṃ kuryurghoṣaṃ cānuśrāvayeyuryaśa udīrayeyuḥ / bodhiprāptasya ca mamāprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye sattvā nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuste sarve buddhakṣetre kuśalamūlapariṇāmanaṃ kṛtvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ, sthāpayitvānantaryakārakān sattvān saddharmapratikṣepakān / bodhiprāptasya me 'nyāsu gaṇanātikrāntāsu lokadhātuṣu sattvā bodhicittotpādaṃ kuryuḥ, mama buddhakṣetra upapattimākāṅkṣamāṇāḥ, tatra ca kuśalamūlapariṇāmanaṃ kuryuḥ; teṣāṃ cāhaṃ maraṇakālasamayeṣvagratastiṣṭheya bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ; te ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā prītiṃ prasādaṃ ca mamāntika utpādayeyuḥ, sarvāvaraṇatāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) illuminating [them all]. And my lifespan shall be immeasurable, beyond the reckoning of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), unable to be counted by anyone except through omniscient knowledge (<s>sārvajña jñāna</s>). And my assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> shall be immeasurable, without <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas), which cannot be counted except through omniscient knowledge. And when I have attained enlightenment, in immeasurable and countless other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, shall speak my praise, broadcast the proclamation, and extol my renown. And when I have attained enlightenment, in immeasurable and countless other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, those beings who hear my name—they, all—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 111.

children.text: ) ca nivartayeyuḥ, kālaṃ ca kṛtvāsmākaṃ buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ / ye ca tatra bodhisattvāste 'smākaṃ sakāśādaśrutapūrvāṃ dharmadeśanāmākāṅkṣeyuḥ śrotuṃ te yādṛśīmākāṅkṣeyustādṛśīṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / bodhiprāptasya ca mama gaṇanātikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ te 'vaivartikāḥ syuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, prathamāṃ kṣāntiṃ pratilabheyuḥ tathā dvitīyāṃ, yādṛśīṃ samādhiṃ dhāraṇīṃ cākāṅkṣeyuḥ tādṛśīṃ samādhiṃ dhāraṇīṃ ca pratilabheyuḥ / parinirvṛtasya ca mama gaṇanātikrānteṣu kalpeṣu paścād gaṇanātikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā paramāṃ prītiṃ prasādaṃ prāmodyaṃ ca prāpnuyurmāmeva namasyamānā āścaryaprāptā yaśakīrtiṃ ca varṇayeyuḥ; bodhisattvabhūtena ca yadā mayā buddhakāryaṃ abhiniṣpāditaṃ tataḥ paścādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyeyaṃ, abhisaṃbuddhasya ca mama paramaprasādapratilabdhā bodhisattvāḥ prathamāyāḥ kṣāntyā lābhinaḥ syurdvitīyāyāḥ tṛtīyāyāḥ, yādṛśīṃ ca samādhiṃ dhāraṇīṃ ākāṅkṣeyustādṛśīṃ pratilabheyuḥ, yāvadbodhiparyantenānupaśyeyuḥ / bodhiprāptasya ca me gaṇanātikrānteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu yāḥ striyo mama nāmadheyaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) shall turn away [from evil], and having died, shall be reborn in our <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> there who desire to hear from us a <s>Dharma</s> teaching not heard before—whatever kind they desire, such shall they hear. And when I have attained enlightenment, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond reckoning, <s>bodhisattvas</s> who hear my name shall become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in supreme perfect enlightenment; they shall attain the first <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and likewise the second; and whatever <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s> they desire, such <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s> they shall attain. And after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), for <s>kalpas</s> beyond reckoning—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 112.

children.text:
) śṛṇuyustāḥ paramaprītiprāmodyaṃ pratilabheyuḥ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayeyuḥ, yāvadbodhiparyantena na bhūyaḥ strītvaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / parinirvṛtasya ca me gaṇanātikrānteṣu kalpeṣu gaṇanātikrāntā yāḥ striyo mama nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ tāḥ paramaprītiprāmodyaṃ prasādaṃ ca prāpnuyuḥ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayeyuḥ, yāvadbodhiparyantena na bhūyaḥ strītvaṃ pratilabheyuḥ
/ īdṛśamahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan buddhakṣetramākāṅkṣāmi, īdṛśāśca pariśuddhāśayāḥ sattvā, īdṛśo 'haṃ bhagavan buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ" /
children.translated_text: ) they who hear them shall attain supreme joy and delight, and shall generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment, and until the attainment of enlightenment they shall never again obtain womanhood. And after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for <s>kalpas</s> beyond reckoning, women beyond reckoning who hear my name shall attain supreme joy, delight, and faith (<s>prasāda</s>), and shall generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment, and until the attainment of enlightenment they shall never again obtain womanhood. Such a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, O venerable Blessed One, I aspire to; such pure-minded beings; such a—

body.translated_text: "With such a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, O Blessed One, I am satisfied. I shall, O venerable Blessed One, practice the difficult conduct of a <s>bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvaduṣkaracaryā</s>) until I purify the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with such qualities. Thus, O venerable Blessed One, I shall make the effort, and after that I shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment. And my <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> (tree of enlightenment) shall be ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, and seated there, in a single instant of thought, I shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment. And my radiance shall be immeasurable, illuminating hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>—

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho rājño 'raṇeminaḥ sādhukāramadāt / "sādhu sādhu mahārāja, gambhīraste mahārāja praṇidhānaṃ pariśuddhaṃ te buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ / paśya mahārāja paścimāyāṃ diśi koṭīśatasahasrabuddhakṣetrāṇāṃ atikramya indrasuvirājitā nāma lokadhātuḥ, tatrendraghoṣeśvararājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati pariśuddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 113.

children.text: ) prajñaptirapyasti, utpādāya na tatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhakathā kriyate, śuddhā ca tatra mahāyānakathā / sarva evopapādukāḥ sattvā, na ca tatra mātṛgrāmasya nāmāpi jñāyate / sarva ete guṇāstatra buddhakṣetre yathā mahārājenāparimitaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhapraṇidhānam kṛtamamitāśayāḥ sattvā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāstena tvaṃ mahārāja indraghoṣeśvararājatathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya tasmin saddharme 'ntarhite ṣaṣṭīnāmantarakalpānāmatyayena sā lokadhāturmeruprabhā nāma bhaviṣyati / tatrācintyamatiguṇarājo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyatyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho / yathaivendraghoṣeśvararājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya indrasuvirājitāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaḥ tathaivācintyamatiguṇarājasya tathāgatasya meruprabhāyāṃ lokadhātau guṇavyūho bhaviṣyati / tasya cācintyamatiguṇarājasya tathāgatasya ṣaṣṭyantarakalpāṇyāyuḥpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / yadācintyamatiguṇarājastathāgataḥ parinirvāsyati tasya ṣoḍaśāntarakalpāḥ saddharmaḥ sthāsyati, tasya saddharme 'ntarhite sahasrāntarakalpātyayena viratirnāma sā lokadhāturbhaviṣyati / (
children.translated_text: ) even the designation [of suffering] exists, [yet] there the discourse of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) is not given — only the pure <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourse is taught there. All beings there are spontaneously born, and there not even the name of womankind is known. All these qualities exist in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), just as the great king made an immeasurable aspiration for the array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, and beings of limitless dispositions were accepted as those to be trained. Therefore, O great king, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indraghoṣeśvararāja</s> and the disappearance of his <s>Saddharma</s> (true Dharma), after the passage of sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), that world-realm shall be called <s>Meruprabhā</s> (Radiance of Meru). There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Acintyamatiguṇarāja</s> (King of Inconceivable and Surpassing Qualities) shall arise, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indraghoṣeśvararāja</s>'s array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities existed in the world-realm <s>Indrasuvirājitā</s>, so too shall the array of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Acintyamatiguṇarāja</s> exist in the world-realm <s>Meruprabhā</s>. And the lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Acintyamatiguṇarāja</s> shall be sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. When the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Acintyamatiguṇarāja</s> passes into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, his <s>Saddharma</s> shall endure for sixteen intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. After his <s>Saddharma</s> disappears, after the passage of a thousand intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, that world-realm shall be called <s>Virati</s> (Cessation). (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 114.

children.text: ) tatra raśmirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, peyālaṃ pūrvavat, samāścaiṣāmāyuḥ samā lokadhātuḥ / evaṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ saddharme 'ntarhite aparā nāma sā lokadhāturbhaviṣyati / tara ratneśvaraghoṣo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha utpatsyate / samo buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaḥ samaṃ cāntarakalpā sthāsyati yāpayiṣyati dharmaṃ ca deśayiṣyati / tasya parinirvṛtasya saptāntarakalpāṃ saddharmaḥ sthāsyati, tasmiṃśca saddharme 'ntarhite, peyālaṃ pūrvavat / evaṃ cāprameyāparimāṇān tathāgatāṃstatra buddhakṣetra upapannān paśyāmi parinirvṛtāṃśca, naivāsau lokadhātussaṃvartate na nivartate / tatrānāgate 'dhvani atikrānta ekasmin gaṅgāvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye pratiṣṭhe dvitīye nadīgaṅgāvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatī nāma bhaviṣyati / tatra tvaṃ mahārājanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, amitāyurnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyasi" /
children.translated_text: ) There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Raśmi</s> (Ray of Light) shall arise, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One — abbreviated as before — their lifespans being equal and their world-realms being equal. Thus, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [of each successive Buddha] and the disappearance of the <s>Saddharma</s>, that world-realm shall be called <s>Aparā</s> (The Other). There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratneśvaraghoṣa</s> (Voice of the Lord of Jewels) shall arise, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. The array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities shall be equal, and he shall endure for an equal number of intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, abiding, sustaining, and teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. After his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Saddharma</s> shall endure for seven intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, and after that <s>Saddharma</s> disappears — abbreviated as before. Thus I see immeasurable, incalculable <s>Tathāgatas</s> arising in that <s>Buddha</s>-field and passing into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, yet that world-realm is neither destroyed nor reverted. There, in the future time, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and entering the second incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, that world-realm shall be called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). There, O great king, you shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, gave his approval to King <s>Araṇemin</s>: "Excellent! Excellent, O great king! Profound is your aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), O great king; purified is the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> you have chosen. Behold, O great king, in the western direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, there is a world-realm (<s>lokadhātu</s>) called <s>Indrasuvirājitā</s>, where a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Indraghoṣeśvararāja</s> presides, dwells, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to purified beings. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there are no <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>—

body.text: rājāraṇemyāha - "kutra te bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ye 'smākaṃ prathamataraṃ tatra buddhakṣetre (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 115.

children.text: ) 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante?" / bhagavān āha - "ime te mahārāja bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ye 'prameyairasaṃkhyeyairatulyairaparimāṇairdaśabhyo digbhyaḥ tābhyastābhyo lokadhātubhya āgatā maṃ vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya, ye mama purato niṣaṇṇā ete 'tītairbuddhairvyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, pratyutpannairapi buddhairbhagavadbhirete kulaputrā vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye tatra buddhakṣetre prathamataramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante, ekaikaścaiṣa mahārāja bodhisattvo 'nekeṣāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ antike kṛtādhikāro 'varuptakuśalamūlo bhāvitaprajñaḥ, ta ete mahārāja kulaputrā ye tatra prathamataraṃ buddhakṣetre buddhā bhaviṣyanti" / rājāraṇemyāha - "ayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo yenāhaṃ sapariṣatko 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāḥ sa kiyatā kālenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate?" / bhagavān āha - "mahākāruṇika eṣa brāhmaṇaḥ samudrareṇuḥ, śroṣyasi tvaṃ yathaiṣa siṃhanādaṃ nadiṣyati" /
children.translated_text: ) The Blessed One said: "These, O great king, are those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who have come from immeasurable, incalculable, incomparable, and boundless world-realms in the ten directions to venerate me, to attend upon me, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s> — those who are seated before me. They have been prophesied by past <s>Buddhas</s> for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, and by present <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones too these sons of good family have been prophesied for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. They shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> first in that <s>Buddha</s>-field. And each of these <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O great king, has performed services under many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, has planted roots of merit, and has cultivated wisdom. These, O great king, are the sons of good family who shall first become <s>Buddhas</s> in that <s>Buddha</s>-field." King <s>Araṇemin</s> said: "O venerable Blessed One, this brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> by whom I, together with my retinue, was inspired toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> — after how long will he attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>?" The Blessed One said: "This brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> is greatly compassionate. You shall hear the lion's roar he will utter."

body.translated_text: King <s>Araṇemin</s> said: "Where, O venerable Blessed One, are those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who will attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) before us in that <s>Buddha</s>-field? (

body.text: rājā āha - "yadyeṣa me praṇidhiḥ samṛdhyati yathāhaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 116.

children.text: ) bhagavatā vyākṛtāḥ, tadyathāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pādavandanaṃ kuryāṃ pañcamaṇḍalena tadā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavaḥ prakampantu pracalantu / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhāḥ tiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti te ca māṃ vyākuryuḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) have been prophesied by the Blessed One, then when I make prostration at the Blessed One's feet with the five-point [body contact], may world-realms equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river tremble and quake! And may the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who abide, endure, and sustain in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields also prophesy me!"

body.translated_text: The king said: "If this aspiration of mine is fulfilled, that I (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra rājāraṇemī ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalakena pādayornipatitaḥ / yadaiva rājñaḥ śirasā pṛthivī spṛṣṭā tadā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhakṣetrāḥ kampitāḥ calitāḥ pracalitāḥ kṣubhitāḥ saṃprakṣubhitāḥ, gāṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhā vyākurvanti / "santīraṇe buddhakṣetre dhāraṇe kalpe 'śītivarṣasahasrāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho rājānamaraṇeminaṃ vyākaroti / bhaviṣyasi tvamanāgate 'dhvani atikrānte gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye praviṣṭe dvitīye 'saṃkhyeye sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvamitaśuddhāyāṃ amitāyurnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, samantato daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān lokadhātūn avabhāsayiṣyasi" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, King <s>Araṇemin</s> fell at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with the five-point [prostration]. The very moment the king's head touched the earth, <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> trembled, shook, quaked, shuddered, and greatly shuddered. <s>Buddhas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> prophesied: "In the <s>Buddha</s>-field <s>Santīraṇa</s>, in the <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Dhāraṇa</s>, among people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, prophesies King <s>Araṇemin</s>: 'You shall become, in the future time, after the passage of an incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and entering the second incalculable <s>aeon</s>, in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, in <s>Amitaśuddhā</s> (Infinite Purity), a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. You shall illuminate world-realms equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in all ten directions.'"

body.text: bhagavān āha -
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.translated_text: "Arise, O supreme being, knower of rites — you have been prophesied by the Ten-Powered Ones!
World-realms equal to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> [sands], with their trembling earth and mountains — you shall become the supreme tamer and charioteer of beings."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra rājāraṇemī tuṣṭa udagraḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ, atikramya nātidūre ekānte niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya //
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, King <s>Araṇemin</s>, joyful, elated, delighted, filled with rapture and happiness, passed beyond [the assembly] and sat down at one side, not too far away, to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo rājño 'raṇemino jyeṣṭhaputramanimiṣaṃ nāma rājakumāramāmantrayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the eldest son of King <s>Araṇemin</s>, the prince named <s>Animiṣa</s> (Unblinking).

body.text: animiṣo 'vocat / peyālaṃ pūrvavat, "avalokitā mayāpāyā ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāḥ pracaṇḍaghoraṃ duḥkhaṃ anubhavanti / avalokitā mayā svargā ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāḥ saṃkliṣṭacittāḥ punarapyapāyeṣu prapatanti / sarvasattvāśca mayāvalokitā akalyāṇamitrasaṃsṛṣṭā viharanti, dharmadurbhikṣāndhakāre kuśalamūlaparikṣīṇā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 118.

children.text: ) dṛṣṭigrāhagrastāḥ kumārgairvihanyate / svareṇāhaṃ bhagavan tān sattvān vijñapayāmi, sarvaṃ ca kuśalaṃ pariṇāmayāmi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / yad ahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ careyaṃ ye kecanasattvā duḥkhotpīḍā bhayatarjitā dharmadurbhikṣāndhakāre praviṣṭā līnā dīnā atrāṇā aśaraṇā aparāyaṇā māmanusmareyuḥ, nāma ca parikīrtayeyuḥ / yadyahaṃ divyena śrotreṇa śṛṇuyāṃ divyena cakṣuṣā paśyeyaṃ, na ca tāṃ sattvān vyasanebhyaḥ parimocayeyaṃ, nāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / yadāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan sattvahetościrapraṇidhānaviśeṣeṇa ciraṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi tadā me āśāparipūrirbhavatu / yadāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan mahārājāraṇemī atikrānte ekasmin gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye pratiṣṭhe dvitīye sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, amitāyurnāma bhaviṣyati tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, pariśuddhe buddhakṣetre pariśuddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyati, yāvatyāmitāyustathāgataḥ aparimāṇān kalpān buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā pariniṣṭhitabuddhakāryo 'nupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātau pravekṣyate, tasya praviṣṭasya yāvat saddharmaḥ sthāsyati (
children.translated_text: ) seized by the grip of wrong views, obstructed by wrong paths. With my voice, O Blessed One, I shall exhort those beings, and I shall dedicate all merit toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). While I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, may whatever beings are oppressed by suffering, threatened by fear, who have entered the darkness of a famine of <s>Dharma</s>, who are dejected, wretched, without protection, without refuge, without recourse — may they remember me and proclaim my name! If I should hear with the divine ear and see with the divine eye, yet not liberate those beings from their calamities, then may I not attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. When I, O venerable Blessed One, shall practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct for a long time through the excellence of my long-standing aspiration for the sake of beings, then may my aspiration be fulfilled.
