When, O venerable Blessed One, the great King <s>Araṇemin</s>, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and entering the second, shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and shall perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for purified beings in a purified <s>Buddha</s>-field, and when the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, having performed the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, his <s>Buddha</s>-work accomplished, shall enter the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder — and after his entry, for as long as the <s>Saddharma</s> shall endure, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 119.

children.text: ) tāvacciramahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi, bodhisattvabhūto 'haṃ buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyāmi / yadāmitāyuṣastathāgatasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya rātryāḥ prathame yāme saddharmo 'ntardhāsyati tasyāmeva rātryāṃ paścime yāme 'hamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / vyākarotu māṃ bhagavān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / evamevāhaṃ daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāsu lokadhātuṣu ye buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti tān api buddhān bhagavataḥ svareṇa vijñapayāmi vyākurvantu māṃ te buddhā bhagavanto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" /
children.translated_text: ) for that long shall I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct; while still a <s>bodhisattva</s>, I shall perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. When, in the first watch of the night, the <s>Saddharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, shall disappear, in the last watch of that very same night, I shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). May the Blessed One prophesy me for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>! Likewise, I exhort with my voice the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who abide, endure, and sustain in world-realms equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions — may those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones also prophesy me for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>."

body.translated_text: <s>Animiṣa</s> spoke — abbreviated as before: "I have surveyed the lower realms and the beings reborn there who experience fierce and terrible suffering. I have surveyed the heavens and the beings reborn there who, with defiled minds, fall once again into the lower realms. I have surveyed all beings dwelling in association with unwholesome friends, in the darkness of a famine of <s>Dharma</s>, with their roots of merit exhausted, (

body.text: vyākṛtaḥ kulaputra ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatenānimiṣo rājaputraḥ / evaṃ cāha - "yattvayā kulaputrāvalokitā apāyāḥ avalokitāḥ svargā avalokitaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃjanitaṃ kāruṇyacittaṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhamocanārthaṃ kleśapraśamanārthaṃ, tasmāttvaṃ kulaputrāvalokiteśvaro nāma bhaviṣyasi / tvamavalokiteśvara bahūnāṃ sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ duḥkhamocakaḥ / bodhisattvabhūtastvaṃ kulaputra buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyasi / parinivṛte cāmitābhe tathāgate 'vaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye, yasyāmeva rātryāṃ prathame (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 120.

children.text: ) yāme saddharmo 'ntardhāsyati tasyāmeva rātryāṃ paścime yāme tvaṃ kulaputrānekavyūhe bodhivṛkṣamūle vajrāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarājo nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / ṣaṇṇavatikalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tavāyurbhaviṣyati / parinirvṛtasya te triṣaṣṭikalpakoṭyaḥ saddharmaḥ sthāsyati" /
children.translated_text: ) watch [of the night] when the <s>Saddharma</s> shall disappear, in the last watch of that very same night, you, O son of good family, seated on the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne) at the foot of the <s>bodhi</s>-tree in <s>Anekavyūha</s>, shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja</s> (King of the Glorious Peak from Whom Rays Shine Forth in All Directions), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. Your lifespan shall be ninety-six hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. After your <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, your <s>Saddharma</s> shall endure for sixty-three <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>."

body.translated_text: The prince <s>Animiṣa</s> was prophesied, O son of good family, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>. And he spoke thus: "Because you, O son of good family, have surveyed the lower realms, surveyed the heavens, and surveyed the suffering of all beings, and have generated the mind of compassion for the sake of liberating beings from suffering and pacifying their afflictions, therefore you, O son of good family, shall be called <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> (Lord Who Looks Down). You, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, shall liberate many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings from suffering. While still a <s>bodhisattva</s>, O son of good family, you shall perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, in the remaining second incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, on that very night, in the first (

body.text: avalokiteśvara āha - "yadi bhagavan nimā mamāśā paripūryate tadyadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ karomi tadā ye buddhā bhagavanto daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti te vyākurvantu māṃ, calatu ca dharaṇī sarvagaṅgānadīvālikāsamāsu daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu, sarvaparvatapāṣāṇaśikharavṛkṣebhyaḥ pañcāṅgikānāṃ tūryāṇāṃ śabdo niścaratu, sarvasattvāśca virāgacittaṃ pratilabhantu" / yadā cāvalokiteśvareṇa bodhisattvena ratnagarbhastathāgataḥ pañcamaṇḍalakena vanditastadā gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 121.

children.text: ) buddhakṣetreṣu dharaṇī pracalitā, te ca buddhā bhagavanto vyākurvanti peyālaṃ pūrvavat, sarvaparvatapāṣāṇaśikharebhyaḥ pañcāṅgikasya tūryasya śabdo niścarati, sarvasattvāśca virāgacittena sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) the earth trembled, and those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones prophesied — abbreviated as before — and from all mountains, rocks, and peaks the sound of five-part musical ensembles issued forth, and all beings abided with minds free from attachment.

body.translated_text: <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said: "If, O Blessed One, this aspiration of mine is to be fulfilled, then when I make prostration at the Blessed One's feet, may the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who abide, endure, and sustain in world-realms equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions prophesy me! May the earth tremble in all world-realms equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions! May from all mountains, rocks, peaks, and trees the sound of five-part musical ensembles issue forth, and may all beings attain a mind free from attachment!" And when the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> made prostration to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with the five-point [contact], then in [<s>Buddha</s>-fields] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (

body.text: bhagavān āha -
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.translated_text: "Arise, O one rich in compassion and merit, with joyful mind — you have been prophesied in the ten directions, bearer of the supreme body!

children.text: prakampitā dharaṇīsakṣetra ṣaḍvikāro bhaviṣyasi jināgrapugalo maharṣī" //
children.translated_text: The earth with its fields trembled with a sixfold quaking — you shall become the foremost person among the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), the great sage!"

body.text: atha khalu samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohito dvitīyaṃ rājaputraṃ nimirnāmāmantrayāmāsa / "evaṃ cānumoda tvaṃ kulaputremaṃ mahāparityāgaṃ, yacca tvayā śubhamupārjitaṃ tatsarvaṃ sattvahetoḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmaya, utpādaya cittamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" /
body.translated_text: Then the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest, addressed the second prince, named <s>Nimir</s>: "Rejoice likewise, O son of good family, in this great renunciation, and whatever merit you have accumulated, dedicate all of it for the sake of beings toward omniscience; generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)."

body.text: atha nimī rājakumāro bhagavataḥ purastānniṣadyedamavocat - "yat mayā bhagavān upasthitaḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sārdhamaparimitena bhikṣusaṅghena, yaścānumodanodgataḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 122.

children.text: ) puṇyaskandhaḥ, yacca kāyavāṅmanaḥ sucaritaṃ puṇyaṃ pariṇāmayāmi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / na kevalamasmin kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre bodhimahaṃ spṛśeyaṃ; yatrāvalokiteśvaraḥ kumāraḥ sarvaratnasannicayāyāṃ lokadhātāvanekaratnavyūhe bodhivṛkṣe niṣaṇṇo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate samantaraśmyabhudgataśrīkūṭarājo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyati, tamahaṃ adhyeṣayeyaṃ dharmadeśanāyāṃ yāvaccāsau tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayet tāvadahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ careyaṃ, tasya tathāgatasyāstaṃgatasya saddharme 'ntarhite tasyānantareṇāhaṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / evaṃrūpaṃ me buddhakṣetraṃ bhavedguṇavyūhena, evamevāhaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kuryāṃ, evameva parinirvāpayeyaṃ, evameva parinirvṛtasya saddharmaściraṃ tiṣṭhet, sarva eva guṇavyūhaḥ yathā samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarājasya tathāgatasya" /
children.translated_text: ) mass of merit, and whatever merit of good conduct of body, speech, and mind — I dedicate toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). I would not attain awakening merely in this defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field); where the prince <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, seated at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree adorned with manifold jewels in the world-realm called <s>Sarvaratnasannicayā</s> (Treasury of All Jewels), will attain supreme perfect awakening and will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja</s> — him I would entreat for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and for as long as that <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, so long would I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct. And when that <s>Tathāgata</s> has passed away and the <s>Saddharma</s> (True Dharma) has disappeared, immediately after him I would attain supreme perfect awakening. May my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> be of such a form in its array of qualities, and thus would I perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work, and thus would I bring beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation), and thus would the <s>Saddharma</s> long endure after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — all the arrays of qualities just like those of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja</s>."

body.translated_text: Then the prince <s>Nimir</s>, sitting before the Blessed One, said this: "That I have attended upon the Blessed One with all provisions, together with the immeasurable <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s>, and the merit arisen from that rejoicing (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "mahāsthāmante kulaputra prārthitaṃ / prāpsyasi tvaṃ kulaputraivaṃrūpaṃ sthānaṃ yathā svayaṃ parigṛhītaṃ / prāpsyasi tvaṃ kulaputra tasmin buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ / supratiṣṭhitaguṇamaṇikūṭarājo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi / yathā sthāmante (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 123.

children.text: ) kulaputra mahāsthānaṃ parigṛhītaṃ, tena tvaṃ kulaputra mahāsthāmaprāpto bhavasva" /
children.translated_text: ) son of good family, a great position has been undertaken, therefore, O son of good family, become <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> (One Who Has Attained Great Power)."

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "A great position, O son of good family, has been aspired to by <s>Sthāmanta</s>. You, O son of good family, will attain such a station as you yourself have undertaken. You, O son of good family, will attain supreme perfect awakening in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. You will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Supratiṣṭhitaguṇamaṇikūṭarāja</s>. Just as, O <s>Sthāmanta</s> (

body.text: sa prāha - "yadi me bhagavanneṣāśā paripūryate, tadyadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pañcamaṇḍalakena kāyena pādau vandāmi tadā me daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhā bhagavanto vyākurvantu, sumanāvarṣaśca pravarṣatu" / yadā kulaputra mahāsthāmaprāptena satpuruṣeṇa ratnagarbhasya pañcamaṇḍalakena pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtaṃ tadā gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamairbuddhairbhagavadbhirvyākṛtaḥ, ṣaḍvikāraṃ ca mahāpṛthivī pracalitā, sumanāvṛṣṭiśca prapatitā /
body.translated_text: He said: "If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, this wish of mine is to be fulfilled, then when I bow at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with my body in the five-point prostration, may the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the ten directions, equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river, confer their prophecy upon me, and may a rain of <s>sumanā</s> flowers shower down." When, O son of good family, the good man <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> performed the five-point prostration at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, then in the ten directions, in realms equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river conferred their prophecy upon him, and the great earth trembled in six ways, and a rain of <s>sumanā</s> flowers fell.

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:
"Arise, O one of firm power, strength, and merit, prophesied by the Protectors of the World in the ten directions!

children.text: calitā mahāpṛthivī vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭā sumanā varṣairbhaviṣyasi tvaṃ suranarabrahmabhūtaḥ" //
children.translated_text: The great earth has trembled and a rain of <s>sumanā</s> flowers has showered down; you shall become [a refuge] for gods, humans, and <s>Brahmās</s>."

body.text: atha samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇastṛtīyaṃ rājaputramindragaṇaṃ nāmamantrayati sma / peyālaṃ pūrvavat, pratigṛhyāñjaliṃ ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatametadavocat - "yanmayā bhagavān sarvopakaraṇairupasthitaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena, yacca me kāyavāṅmanaḥ sucaritaṃ, idaṃ cānumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ, etatsarvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayāmi / na tu kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, na cātikṣipraṃ prāpnuyāṃ / na yāvaccāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ tāvadbodhicaryāṃ caran, daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyeyaṃ / ye mayā prathamaṃ bodhāya samādāpitā yeṣāṃ mayā tatprathamaṃ bodhicittamutpāditaṃ bodhicitte pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, pāramitāsu ca ye mayā samādāpitā niveśitā pratiṣṭhāpitā bodhicaryāṃ caratā, tān ahaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā gaṅgānadīvālikāsame buddhakṣetre paramāṇurajaḥsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhān bhagavato dharman deśayataḥ paśyeyaṃ, ye mayā bodhāya samādāpitāḥ / evamahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran buddhakāryaṃ kuryāṃ, tāvadahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ careyaṃ sattvānāmāśayapariśodhayamānaḥ yāvantaḥ kecit sattvā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 125.

children.text: ) mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeran ta evaṃvidhāḥ syuḥ tadyathā brahmakāyikā devāḥ; tathā ca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ pariśodhayeyaṃ yathā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ ekaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ syāt / tasya ca buddhakṣetrasya bhavāgraparyantāni prākārāṇi anekaratnasaṃsthitāni nānāratnapratyuptāni ca syuḥ, sarvā ca tatra buddhakṣetre śuddhavaiḍūryamayī pṛthivī syāt, apagatarajaḥpāṣāṇaśarkarāpagatakaluṣasaṃsparśā dharaṇī syāt / na tatra mātṛgrāmasyanāma prajñaptiḥ syāt, sarvasattvāścopapādukāḥ syurna tatra sattvāḥ kavadīkārāhārāḥ syuḥ, sarve ca tatra sattvā prītyāhārā dharmāhārāḥ syuḥ / na tatra buddhakṣetre śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ prajñaptiḥ syāt, śuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmapagatakhilamaladveṣamrakṣāṇāṃ śuddhānāṃ brahmacāriṇāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhaṃ syāt / sarve tatra bodhisattvā muṇḍāḥ kāṣāyavastradhāriṇaḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ, samanantaraprādurbhūtānāṃ mahāvabhāsaṃ bhavet, teṣāṃ dakṣiṇe haste ratnapātrī nānārasapūrṇā prādurbhavet; samanantaraprādurbhūtānāṃ evaṃrūpāṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabheyurnāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ ye vayaṃ kavaḍīkārāhāramāharema, (
children.translated_text: ) are reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be of such a kind — namely, like the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods. And I would purify such an array of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities that a <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world universe) equal in number to Gaṅgā river-sands would be a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. And that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>'s enclosing walls would extend up to the summit of existence, established with many jewels and inlaid with various gems. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, the entire earth would be made of pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), the ground free from dust, stones, and gravel, free from impure contact. There would not even be the designation of womankind. All beings would be born by apparitional birth; there beings would not consume solid food — all beings there would be nourished by <s>prīti</s> (joy) and nourished by the <s>Dharma</s>. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no designation of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones); it would be the purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of pure <s>bodhisattvas</s>, free from hostility, stain, hatred, and malice — pure <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate practitioners). All <s>bodhisattvas</s> there would appear with shaven heads wearing saffron robes; as soon as they appear, there would be a great radiance; in their right hands would appear jewel-bowls filled with various essences. As soon as they appear, they would attain such a recollection: 'It is not proper for us to consume solid food; (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 126.

children.text:
) yannūnaṃ vayamanyāsu lokadhātuṣu gatvā buddhān bhagavatastiṣṭhato yāpayato 'nenāhāreṇa pratimānayāmo buddhaśrāvakāṃśca duḥkhitaṃ ca janaṃ pratimānayāmaḥ, pretabhavaneṣu ca gatvā kṣuttarṣaprajvalitagātrān sattvān anenāhāreṇa pratimānayāmaḥ" / sahacittotpādena te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā acintyacāritravatīṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, tasya ca samādheḥ pratilābhādasajjanā daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gaccheyuḥ, tiṣṭhato yāpayato buddhān bhagavata āhāreṇa pratimānayeyuḥ śrāvakāṃścānyāṃśca sattvāṃ, prītyā pratimānya dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtvā tenaiva pūrvabhaktena svabuddhakṣetraṃ āgaccheyuḥ / evaṃ cīvararatnāni, yāvat tenaiva pūrvabhaktena svakaṃ buddhakṣetramāgatyānyonyaṃ cīvareṇa prāvarayeyuḥ / yāvanti ca tatra buddhakṣetre teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmupabhogaḥ paribhogā
bhaveyustaiḥ sarvairbuddhaiḥ śrāvakaiścānyaiśca sattvaiḥ sahasādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā paścādātmanā paribhuñjeyuḥ / aṣṭākṣaṇavarjitaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ bhavet, na ca tatra duḥkhaśabdo bhavet, (
children.translated_text: ) rather, let us go to other world-realms and with this food sustain the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who abide and dwell there, and sustain the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and those in distress, and going to the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realms, sustain with this food the beings whose bodies are ablaze with hunger and thirst.' With the very arising of that thought, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> would attain a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called <s>Acintyacāritravatī</s> (Endowed with Inconceivable Conduct), and through the attainment of that <s>samādhi</s>, without leaving, they would go to immeasurable other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, sustain with food the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who abide and dwell there, and the <s>śrāvakas</s> and other beings; having sustained them with joy, having given a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, they would return to their own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> within that very morning meal-time. Likewise with jewel-robes — abbreviated — within that very morning meal-time, having returned to their own <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, they would clothe one another with robes. And whatever enjoyments and provisions those <s>bodhisattvas</s> would have in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, all those they would first share with the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, and other beings, and only afterward partake themselves. And the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be free from the eight inopportune states, and there would be no sound of suffering, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 127.

children.text: ) na śikṣāgrahaṇaśabdaḥ, āpattivyutthānaśabdo 'pi na bhavet / anekaratnaśatasahasropacitaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ syāt, anekaratnapratyuptaṃ maṇisandarśanasadṛśaṃ bhavet, yāni maṇiratnāni daśasu dikṣvadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi tāni aśrutapūrvāṇi tāni maṇiratnāni pracareyuḥ, yeṣāṃ maṇiratnānāṃ nāmadheye nirdiśyamāne varṣakoṭyo 'pi kṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ / yaśca bodhisattvaḥ ākāṅkṣeta svarṇamayaṃ eva buddhakṣetraṃ paśyeyaṃ tasya svarṇamayaṃ eva tiṣṭheta / yo rūpyamayamākāṅkṣeta sa rūpyamayaṃ paśyet, na cāsya suvarṇamayaṃ parihāyeyaṃ, peyālaṃ pūrvavat / ya ākāṅkṣeta sphatikamayaṃ vaiḍūryamayaṃ aśmagarbhamayaṃ lohitamuktāmayaṃ musālagalvamayaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ paśyema, ityākāṅkṣeyuḥ / agarumayaṃ tagaramayaṃ tamālapatramayaṃ yo bodhisattva ākāṅkṣeduragasāracandanamayaṃ goṣīrṣacandanamayaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ draṣṭuṃ tasya tathaiva syāt / yathā yathā yādṛśamākāṅkṣeyuḥ tathā tathā tādṛśaṃ syāt; na caiko dvitīyasya praṇidhiḥ syāt, sarveṣāṃ eva praṇidhiḥ paripūryate / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre sūryācandramasau (
children.translated_text: ) nor the sound of undertaking precepts, nor even the sound of rising from transgressions. That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be adorned with many hundreds of thousands of jewels, inlaid with various gems, resembling a crystal display. Those jewel-gems that had never before been seen or heard of in the ten directions would be prevalent there — jewel-gems whose names, even if enumerated, would take <s>koṭīs</s> of years to exhaust. And whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> wished to see the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> as made of gold — for him it would appear made of gold. One who wished to see it made of silver would see it made of silver, without the golden [appearance] being diminished — abbreviated as before. One who wished to see it made of crystal, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), red pearl, or <s>musāragalva</s> (coral) — 'may we see the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in such a form,' they would wish. One who wished to see it made of <s>aguru</s> (aloewood), <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay leaf), <s>uragasāracandana</s> (serpent-heart sandalwood), or <s>goṣīrṣacandana</s> (ox-head sandalwood) — for him it would be just so. Whatever form they wished to see, in whatever manner, so it would appear; and one person's aspiration would not conflict with another's — the aspirations of all would be fulfilled. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, neither sun nor moon (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 128.

children.text: ) prajñāyeyātāṃ, svayaṃ prabhāśca tatra bodhisattvāḥ pratyājāyeyuḥ, anyāṃ yādṛśīṃ prabhāmākāṅkṣeran tādṛśīmutsṛjeyuḥ, antato buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣvapi / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre rātridivasānāṃ nāmadheyamapi prajñāyate, anyatra kusumavikasanatayā / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre śītoṣṇaṃ prajñāyate na vyādhirna glānyaṃ na jarāmaraṇamanyatra yo bodhisattva ākāṅkṣedbodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ so 'nyatra lokadhātāvuṣitvā āyuḥ kṣapayitvā bodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta / na tatra buddhakṣetre maraṇaṃ bhaveyuḥ, anuttaraparinirvāṇena uparyantarīkṣe tathāgataparinirvāṇaṃ syāt / yādṛgjātrīyāṃśca bodhisattva upabhogaparibhogāmākāṅkṣeran tādṛgjātīyā abhinirvarteyuḥ / sarvatra ca buddhakṣetre gaganatale tūryakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrā vādyeyuḥ / na ca tebhyastūryebhyaḥ kāmopasaṃhitāḥ śabdā niścareyuḥ, anyatra pāramitā śabdā niścareyuḥ, buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabdo bodhisattvapiṭakadharmaparyāyaśabdo niścaret / yathādhimuktā bodhisattvāstādṛgjātīyāṃ śabdāṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) would be perceived; the <s>bodhisattvas</s> there would be reborn as self-luminous beings, and whatever radiance they wished, such radiance they would emit, even across <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, not even the designation of night and day would be perceived, except by the opening and closing of flowers. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no cold or heat, no illness, no fatigue, no old age or death — except that a <s>bodhisattva</s> who wished to attain awakening, having dwelt in another world-realm and exhausted his lifespan, would attain awakening. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no death; the supreme <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation) would be the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> above in the sky. And whatever kind of enjoyments and provisions the <s>bodhisattvas</s> wished for, of just such a kind they would manifest. And throughout the entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, in the sky, <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of musical instruments would play. And from those instruments no sounds connected with sensual desire would issue forth; rather, sounds of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) would issue forth — the sound of <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of <s>Dharma</s>, the sound of <s>Saṅgha</s>, the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>-discourses of the <s>bodhisattva-piṭaka</s> (collection of bodhisattva teachings) would issue forth. Whatever sounds the <s>bodhisattvas</s> were inclined toward, just such sounds they would hear. (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 129.

children.text:
) bodhisattvacārikāmahaṃ bhagavaṃścaramāṇo yāvan mayāprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā dṛṣṭāste vyūhāste 'laṅkārāstāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni tāni sthānāni tāni praṇidhānāni sarva eva mama buddhakṣetre praviśeyuḥ, sthāpayitvā śrāvakapratyekabuddhavyūhāṃ pañcakaṣāyikāṃśca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre narakatiryakpretāḥ prajñāyeyurna sumerurna cakravāḍamahācakravāḍā na śīlāpāṃśuparvatāḥ prajñāyeyuḥ, na mahāsamudrā; na cānye kāṣṭhavṛkṣā bhaveyurdivyātikrāntairnānāvṛkṣaistadbuddhakṣetramākīrṇaṃ
syāt, anyatra divyaiḥ kusumairmāndāravamahāmāndāravairna ca tatra durgandhaṃ syānnānāgandhairudārodāraistadbuddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ syāt / sarve tatraikajātipratibaddhā bodhisattvā utpadyeran, na tatraikasattvaḥ syādyastataścyavitvānyatra pratyājāyeta, anyatra tuṣitebhyaḥ tataścyuto 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta / tāvadahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi yāvannaivaṃvidhaṃ mahāpuruṣakāramabhiniṣpādayiṣyāmi / evaṃrūpaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi, evaṃrūpaiḥ śuddhāśayaiḥ sattvairekajātipratibaddhairbodhisattvaiḥ (
children.translated_text: ) While I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, whatever arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities I have seen in immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> — those arrays, those ornaments, those characteristics, those marks, those stations, those aspirations — may they all enter into my <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, excluding the arrays of <s>śrāvaka</s>-<s>pratyekabuddha</s> [fields] and the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities of the five-fold degenerate age. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, neither hells, animals, nor <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) would be perceived; no <s>Sumeru</s>, no <s>Cakravāḍa</s> or <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, no rock-mountains or dust-mountains would be perceived; no great oceans; nor would there be other common trees — that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be filled with various trees surpassing even the divine, except for divine flowers of <s>Māndārava</s> and <s>Mahāmāndārava</s>; and there would be no foul odor — that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be pervaded with various sublime fragrances. All <s>bodhisattvas</s> reborn there would be bound by a single birth; there would not be a single being who, having fallen from there, would be reborn elsewhere — except from <s>Tuṣita</s> [heaven], having fallen from there, one would attain supreme perfect awakening. So long, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct until I accomplish such a great and heroic endeavor. I shall establish such a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, with such pure-minded beings, <s>bodhisattvas</s> bound by a single birth (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 130.

children.text: ) sārdhaṃ tadbuddhakṣetramākīrṇaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmi / na tatra bodhisattvaḥ syād yo na mayā prathamaṃ bodhāya samādāpitaḥ syāt; sarve te tatra bodhisattvāḥ pratyājāyeyuḥ ye mayā prathamaṃ bodhāya samādāpitāḥ pāramitāsu niveśitāḥ; tatraivedaṃ buddhakṣetramantargataṃ kuryāṃ sarve cāmī duḥkhā praśamayeyaṃ / bodhisattvabhūto 'haṃ bhadanta bhagavan evaṃrūpaṃ puruṣakāraṃ niṣpādayeyaṃ, tataḥ paścāt tatra buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / daśacāturdvīpikasahasrapramāṇo me bodhivṛkṣaḥ pariṇāhena syāt, saptaratnavicitrasandarśano nāma bhavet / daśatrisāhasraḥ samantapariṇāhena; tasya ca bodhivṛkṣasya gandhenābhayā ca kṛtsanaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ syāt; tasya mūle pañcacāturdvīpikapramāṇaṃ me nānāratnavicitraṃ vajrāsanaṃ syāt, praśamakṣamasuvicitrajñānagandhasamavasaraṇaṃ nāma bhaveccaturaśītiyojanānyuccatvena; tasyāhaṃ bodhivṛkṣasya mūle vajrāsane niṣīdeyaṃ, paryaṅkamābhujya tenaiva muhūrtenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ yāvat parinirvāṇakālaṃ tatparyaṅkaṃ na (
children.translated_text: ) together [with them] I shall fill and establish that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. No <s>bodhisattva</s> would be there who had not first been inspired by me toward enlightenment; all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who were first inspired by me toward enlightenment and established in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) would be reborn there; and I would incorporate this very <s>buddhakṣetra</s> within it and pacify all these sufferings. While still a <s>bodhisattva</s>, O venerable Blessed One, I would accomplish such an effort, and after that, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, I would attain supreme perfect enlightenment. My <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> (tree of enlightenment) would measure ten thousand four-continent world-systems—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 131.

children.text:
) bhindyāṃ na muceyaṃ na tasmād bodhivṛkṣamūlāduttiṣṭheyaṃ / bodhivṛkṣamūlastha evāhaṃ vajrāsane niṣaṇṇo 'haṃ nirmitān buddhān bodhisattvāṃśca gaṇanātikrānteṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu preṣayeyaṃ, ekaiko buddha ekapūrvabhaktena sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayet, tenaiva pūrvabhaktena gaṇanātikrāntān sattvān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayeyuḥ pratiṣṭhāpayeyuḥ avaivartikāṃ sthāpayeyuḥ, evaṃ nirmitā bodhisattvā bodhisattvakāryaṃ kuryuḥ / bodhiprāptasya me gaṇanātikrānteṣu daśasu dikṣvanyāsu lokadhātuṣu mama kāyo dṛṣyet, yeṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ mama kāyo lakṣaṇālaṅkṛtaścakṣurindriyasyābhāsamāgacchet sarve te sattvā niyatā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yāvad bodhiparinirvāṇena te sattvā avirahitā bhaveyurbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ / na tatrendriyavikalā bhaveyurye ca tatra bodhisattvā māṃ draṣṭuṃ iccheyuste yena yenaiva gaccheyuḥ parivarteyuḥ caṃkrameyurniṣīdeyuḥ tiṣṭheyuḥ,
sarve te bodhisattvāḥ samanantarotpāditena buddhanamaskāracittena māṃ bodhivṛkṣaniṣaṇṇaṃ paśyeyuḥ, dṛṣṭvā ca yasya dharmasaṃśayaḥ syāt so 'sya sahadarśanena vigacchettīrṇavacikitsāḥ syādanupadiṣṭasya dharmapadasyārthamājāneyuḥ / apramāṇaṃ me (
children.translated_text: ) I would not break [my resolve] nor would I release [my effort] nor would I rise from the foot of that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>. Seated upon the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne) at the foot of the <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, I would send forth emanated <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> to <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beyond reckoning. Each emanated <s>Buddha</s>, in a single morning meal-time, would teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, and in that same morning meal-time would inspire, establish, and place countless beings in irreversibility (<s>avaivartika</s>) toward supreme perfect enlightenment; likewise the emanated <s>bodhisattvas</s> would perform the work of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. When I have attained enlightenment, in countless [<s>buddhakṣetras</s>] in the ten directions, in other world-realms—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 132.

children.text: ) āyurbhavet na śakyate kenacid gaṇayituṃ anyatra sārvajñena jñānena, apramānāśca tatra bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / yasmiṃśca kṣaṇe 'haṃ tatra buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ tasmin kṣaṇe tatra buddhakṣetre bodhisattvā muṇḍāḥ kāṣāyavastrāḥ saṃbhaveyuḥ, yāvan mama parinirvāṇānna cātra buddhakṣetra ekasattvo 'pi dīrghakeśaḥ syāt śuklaprāvaraṇo vā, sarva eva śramaṇavarṇāḥ syuḥ śramaṇapratirūpāstiṣṭheyuḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) the lifespan would be such that no one could reckon it except through omniscient knowledge (<s>sārvajña jñāna</s>), and immeasurable <s>bodhisattvas</s> would dwell there. And at the very moment when I would attain supreme perfect enlightenment in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, all <s>bodhisattvas</s> there would appear with shaven heads and wearing saffron robes (<s>kāṣāyavastra</s>), and until my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, not a single being in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would have long hair or wear white garments—all would have the appearance of <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and would stand in the form of <s>śramaṇas</s>."

body.translated_text: Then the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the third prince named <s>Indragaṇa</s>. Abbreviated as before: having joined his palms, he said to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>: "Whatever merit I have accumulated by attending upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> (community of monks) with all provisions, and whatever merit of good conduct of body, speech, and mind, together with this mass of merit accompanied by rejoicing — all this I dedicate toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). But I would not attain supreme perfect awakening in a defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, nor would I attain it too quickly. Until I attain supreme perfect awakening, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, I would behold the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> in infinite and boundless other world-realms in the ten directions. Those whom I first inspired toward awakening, in whom I first generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) and established them in the mind of awakening, and whom I inspired, settled, and established in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — them I would behold with the divine eye, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to Gaṅgā river-sands, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to atoms, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, [and] those whom I inspired toward awakening. Thus, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, I would perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work; so long would I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, purifying the dispositions of beings, so that whatever beings (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, tvamapi paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī atīvaśobhanaṃ te praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, atīvaguṇavāstvamatīvajñānavān; yatastvaṃ kulaputra sarvasattvānāmarthāyaivaṃrūpāṃ pravarāṃ praśastāṃ matiṃ kṛtavān pravaro buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaḥ parigṛhītaḥ, tataste kulaputra mañjuśrīrnāma bhavatu / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ mañjuśrīranāgate 'dhvani atikrāntayordvayornadīvālikāsamayorasaṃkhyeyayoḥ praviṣṭe ca tṛtīye 'saṃkhyeye dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi śuddhavirajaḥsannicayo nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati, tatra ca sahālokadhāturantargatā bhaviṣyati, anupraviṣṭaśca evaṃrūpayā guṇavyūhayā tadbuddhakṣetraṃ prādurbhaviṣyati / tatra tvaṃ mañjuśrīranuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 133.

children.text: ) samantadarśī nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / evaṃrūpā ca te bodhisattvaparṣadbhaviṣyati sarve caite praṇidhānāstvayi saṃpatsyante yathā tvayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ; bodhisattvabhūtena tatastvaṃ bahubuddhakoṭīṣvavaruptakuśalamūlo bhaviṣyasi, āśayapariśodhakaśca kleśapramardakaḥ, ye ca te mañjuśrīssattvā nāmaṃ śroṣyanti teṣāṃ sarvakarmāvaraṇakṣayo bhaviṣyati, kuśalavivardhakaśca bhaviṣyasi" /
children.translated_text: ) you shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samantadarśin</s> (All-Seeing), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One. And such shall be your assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and all these aspirations shall be fulfilled in you, just as you have made the aspiration. As a <s>bodhisattva</s>, you shall have destroyed the roots of unwholesomeness under many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and you shall be a purifier of intentions and a crusher of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). And those beings, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who shall hear your name—for all of them there shall be the destruction of all karmic obscurations (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>), and you shall be an augmenter of wholesome [qualities]."

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Excellent! Excellent, O good man (<s>satpuruṣa</s>)! You too are wise, discerning, and intelligent. Exceedingly beautiful is the aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) you have made; exceedingly endowed with qualities you are, exceedingly endowed with knowledge. Since you, O son of good family, have produced such a supreme and excellent resolve for the benefit of all beings, and have chosen a supreme array of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities, therefore, O son of good family, let your name be <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. You, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in the future age, having passed beyond two incalculable aeons equal to the sands of a river, and having entered the third incalculable aeon, in the southern direction there will be a world-realm called <s>Śuddhavirajassannicaya</s> (Accumulation of Pure and Stainless [Qualities]), and there—

body.text: mañjuśrīrāha - "yadi me bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśāparipūrirbhavediti yathā me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā caiva māṃ buddhā bhagavanto vyākurvantu ye daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti sattvānāṃ ca dharmaṃ deśayanti / tathāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhakṣetrāḥ prakaṃpantu / sarvasattvāścaivaṃrūpeṇa sukhena samarpitā bhavantu, tadyathā dvitīyadhyānakrīḍāvyūhasamāpannasya bodhisattvasya / tathāprameyāsaṃkhyeyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo divyamāndāravapuṣpāṇyabhipravarṣantu, tebhyaśca māndāravebhya evaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścaratu yaduta buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabdaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 134.

children.text: ) pāramitāśabdaḥ balavaiśāradyaśabdaśca niścaratu / yadā cāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandeya tadā caivaṃrūpaṃ nimittaṃ prādurbhavet" / yadā ca mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtaṃ tadā tatkṣaṇādevamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhakṣetrāḥ prakaṃpitā, divyāni ca māndāravāṇyabhipravarṣitāni, sarvasattvāścaivaṃrūpeṇa sukhena samarpitā abhavanyathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / ye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāsteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti te tān buddhān bhagavataḥ paripṛcchanti, "ko 'tra hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ evaṃrūpāṇāṃ nimittānāṃ prādurbhāvāya?" te ca buddhā bhagavanto mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ vyākurvanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
children.translated_text: ) may the sound of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and the sound of the powers and confidences (<s>bala-vaiśāradya</s>) ring forth. And when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with the fivefold prostration (<s>pañcamaṇḍala</s>), then may such a sign appear." And when the princely youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> performed the prostration at the feet of the Blessed One, at that very instant immeasurable and countless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> trembled, divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers rained down, and all beings were endowed with such happiness, just as the aspiration had been made. And the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who hear the <s>Dharma</s> from those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, asked those <s>Buddhas</s>—

body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "If, O Blessed One, such a fulfillment of my hope should come about, just as I have made the aspiration, then may the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who preside, dwell, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in immeasurable and countless world-realms in the ten directions, give me their prophecy. May immeasurable and countless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> tremble. May all beings be endowed with such happiness as that of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered the playful array of the second <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). May divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers rain down from immeasurable and countless <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, and from those—

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said:
"Arise, O one of supreme wisdom and vast understanding! You have been given prophecy by the Lords of the World in the ten directions.

children.text: calitā kṣitiḥ tarpitāḥ sattvāḥ saukhyaiḥ puṣpāḥ pravṛṣṭā bheṣyase buddha loka" // iti //
children.translated_text: The earth has trembled, beings have been satisfied with happiness, flowers have rained down—you shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaścaturthaṃ rājaputramānaṅgaṇaṃ nāmāmantrayati / peyālaṃ yathā mañjuśriyā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / tasya bhagavān sādhukāramanuprādāsīt, "sādhu sādhu kulaputra, bodhisattvabhūtastvaṃ kulaputrāprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ kleśaparvatāṃ bhetsyasi, buddhakāryaṃ ca kariṣyasi, tataḥ paścādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / tena tvaṃ kulaputra vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsaśrīrnāma bodhisattvo bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsānāgate 'dhvanyatikrāntānāmekagaṅgānadīvālikānāmasaṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsaṃkhyeye purimāyāṃ diśi daśagaṅgānadīvālikāsamān buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāllokadhātūnatikramya tatrānimiṣā nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati, tatra tvaṃ kulaputra bodhimabhisaṃbhotsyasi, samantabhadro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampanno bhaviṣyasi yāvad buddho bhagavān / evaṃrūpaṃ ca te buddhakṣetramanekaguṇavyūhitaṃ bhaviṣyati yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the fourth prince named <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>. [The passage is abbreviated:] just as <s>Mañjuśrī</s> had made his aspiration. The Blessed One gave his approval: "Excellent! Excellent, O son of good family! As a <s>bodhisattva</s>, you, O son of good family, shall shatter the mountains of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of immeasurable and countless beings, and shall perform the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, and after that you shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment. Therefore, O son of good family, let your name be <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsaśrī</s> (Splendor of Diamond-Cutting Wisdom-Light). You, <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa</s>, in the future age, having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and having entered the second—

body.text: samanantaravyākṛtaśca kulaputra ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena vajracchedaprajñāvabhāso bodhisattvo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, gaganatalagatānyanekāni devakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi sādhukāramadurgośīrṣoragasāracandanāgarutamālacūrṇaṃ ca pravārṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: And as soon as <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> was given prophecy by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>devas</s> (gods) in the sky gave their approval and rained down <s>gośīrṣa</s> (ox-head) sandalwood, <s>agaru</s> (aloe), <s>tamāla</s>, and powdered incense.

body.text: sa āha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpāśā paripūryeta tadyadāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pañcamaṇḍalena vandeyaṃ tadā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāllokadhātavo divyātikrāntenodāreṇa gandhena sphuṭā bhaveyuḥ / ye ca tatra lokadhātuṣu sattvā upapannā bhaveyuḥ nairayikā vā tairyagyonikā vā yāmalaukikā vā devā vā manuṣyā vā te sarve taṃ gandhaṃ ghrāyeyuḥ, teṣāṃ kāyavyādhiḥ kāyaduḥkhaṃ cittavyādhiḥ cittaduḥkhaṃ ca tāvacciraṃ praśāntaṃ bhavedyāvadahaṃ śīrṣeṇa pṛthivīṃ spṛśeyaṃ" /
body.translated_text: He said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with the fivefold prostration, may world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> be pervaded with a divine, surpassing, and sublime fragrance. And whatever beings have been born in those world-realms—whether in the hells, among animals, in the realm of <s>Yama</s>, among gods, or among humans—they should all smell that fragrance, and their bodily illness, bodily suffering, mental illness, and mental suffering should be pacified for as long as I touch the earth with my head."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra vajracchedaprajñāvabhāso bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandate / atha tavadeva gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavo divyātikrāntenodāreṇa gandhena sphuṭā babhūvuḥ, sarveṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ kāyavyādhiścittavyādhiḥ kāyaduḥkhaṃ cittaduḥkhaṃ ca praśāntaṃ pratiprasrabdhaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa</s> bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with the fivefold prostration. And at that very moment, world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were pervaded with a divine, surpassing, and sublime fragrance, and the bodily illness, mental illness, bodily suffering, and mental suffering of all beings were pacified and relieved.

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said:
"Arise, O diamond-cleaver! The fields are pervaded with fragrance.
You bring happiness and joy to beings—you shall become a supreme father of the world."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ rājaputramabhayaṃ nāmāmantrayate sma / peyālaṃ, "na ca kevalamasmiṃ kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre, tatrāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ yatra na narakā bhaveyurna tiryagyonirna yamalokāḥ, yatra nīlavaiḍūryamayī bhūmirvistareṇa yathā padmāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetre guṇavyūhā tathā vaktavyāḥ / abhayaśca rājaputro ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyāgrataḥ padmaṃ sthāpayitvāha / "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tadahaṃ bhagavato 'nubhāvena darśanavyūhaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheyaṃ, yenāhaṃ bhagavato 'grato daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāsu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsaṃkhyai rathacakrapramāṇamātraiḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 138.

children.text: ) padmaiḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣet vayaṃ ca paśyema" / sahodīrate vākye buddhānubhāvena darśanavyūhaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabdhavān, daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamai rathacakrapramāṇāmātraiḥ padmaiḥ padmavarṣaṃ pravarṣitaṃ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvābhayo rājakumāraḥ paramaprītisaumanasyajāto babhūva /
children.translated_text: ) may a rain of lotus flowers fall, and may we see [it]." As soon as the words were uttered, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, he attained the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Darśanavyūha</s> (Array of Vision), and in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions, a rain of lotuses fell—lotuses the size of chariot wheels, as numerous as the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. Seeing this, Prince <s>Abhaya</s> was filled with supreme joy and gladness.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the fifth prince named <s>Abhaya</s>. [The passage is abbreviated:] "And not only in this defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s>—rather, O venerable Blessed One, I would attain enlightenment where there would be no hells, no animal realm, no realm of <s>Yama</s>; where the ground would be made of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli)—to be described in full as the qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in the <s>Padmā</s> world-realm. And Prince <s>Abhaya</s>, having placed a lotus before <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then when I pay homage to the Blessed One—

body.text: bhagavān āha - "atīva kulaputra śobhanaṃ tvayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, śobhanaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ, atiśīghraṃ ca te samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ, satyavacanena padmavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitāḥ" /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Exceedingly beautiful, O son of good family, is the aspiration you have made, and beautiful is the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> you have chosen, and very swiftly did you attain the <s>samādhi</s>; by your truthful speech, a rain of lotuses has fallen."

body.text: sa āha - "yadi mamānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvāśāparipūrirbhaveta tadete padmā gagane tiṣṭhantu tathaiva gagane sthitā varṣantu" /
body.translated_text: He said: "If my hope for supreme perfect enlightenment should be fulfilled, then may these lotuses remain standing in the sky, and while remaining in the sky, may they continue to rain down."

body.text: bhagavān āha - "atikṣipraṃ kulaputra gaganatalaṃ padmairmudritaṃ, tena hi tvaṃ kulaputra gaganamudro nāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ gaganamudro 'nāgate 'dhvani atikrānte ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi koṭīśatasahasraṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikrāmayitvā tatra padmā nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati, tatra tvaṃ bodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 139.

children.text: ) padmottaraśca nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpanno yāvadbuddho bhagavān aprameyena śuddhena bodhisattvasaṅghena, aparimāṇā ca te āyurbhaviṣyati / sarvaiścaitairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ lapsyasi tadetatpraṇidhāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ" / gaganamudro bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā nipapāta /
children.translated_text: ) and you shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmottara</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, and so on up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, with an immeasurable pure assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and your lifespan shall be immeasurable. Endowed with all these qualities, you shall obtain what you have vowed." The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Very swiftly, O son of good family, has the sky been sealed with lotuses. Therefore, O son of good family, let your name be <s>Gaganamudra</s> (Sky-Seal). You, <s>Gaganamudra</s>, in the future age, having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> and having entered the second, in the east-southern direction, having traversed hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there will be a world-realm called <s>Padmā</s> (Lotus), and there you shall attain enlightenment—

children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said:
"You shall become a benefactor in the world, one who pacifies the defilements of afflictions,
bearing qualities equal to the atoms of a <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), you shall attain awakening just as the former <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones)."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ rājaputramambaraṃ nāmāntrayati sma / peyālaṃ, "na ca kevalamasmiṃ kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre", yāvad yathā gaganamudreṇa bodhisattvena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / "yadi me bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tad daśadiśī gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāsu (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 140.

children.text: ) lokadhātuṣu sarvagaganeṣu saptaratnamayāḥ chatrāḥ prādurbhavantu hemajālapraticchannāḥ saptaratnamayābhirghaṇṭābhiralaṅkṛtāḥ / tatra chatraghaṇṭājālairevaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścaret yaduta buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabdaḥ pāramitāśabdo balaśabdo 'bhijñāśabdo vaiśāradyaśabdaḥ, sarve ca te sattvā evaṃrūpaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ te śrutvā sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayeyuḥ / ye cātra sattvāḥ pūrvamutpāditabodhicittāste 'vaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / samanantaravyāhṛte 'smiṃ vyāhāre atha daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvagaganatalāt peyālaṃ evaṃrūpāḥ śabdā niścaranti / bhagavataścānubhāvāt svayamevādrākṣīt, punarevaṃ āha - "sacenme bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta yathā me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tadahaṃ bhagavataḥ purato jñānavairocanaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheya, yena mama kuśalā dharmā nivarteyuḥ, pratilabdhe ca samādhau māṃ bhagavāṃ vyākuryāt" / bhagavataścānubhāvena jñānavairocanasamādhiḥ pratilabdhā /
children.translated_text: ) in all the skies of those world-realms, may parasols made of the seven precious substances appear, covered with golden nets, adorned with bells made of the seven precious substances. From those nets of parasol-bells, may such a sound issue forth — namely the sound of '<s>Buddha</s>,' the sound of '<s>Dharma</s>,' the sound of '<s>Saṅgha</s>,' the sound of '<s>pāramitās</s>,' the sound of 'powers,' the sound of '<s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges),' the sound of 'fearlessness' — and may all those beings hear such a sound, and having heard it, may they all generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening. And those beings who have previously generated the mind of awakening — may they become irreversible in supreme perfect awakening." No sooner was this utterance spoken than in the ten directions, in world-realms equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, from all the surfaces of the sky, abbreviated, such sounds issued forth. And by the power of the Blessed One, he himself beheld this, and furthermore said: "If, O Venerable Blessed One, my aspiration of such a nature is fulfilled according to my vow, then may I, in the presence of the Blessed One, obtain the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Jñānavairocana</s> ('Radiance of Wisdom'), by which my wholesome qualities would not decline; and when this <s>samādhi</s> is obtained, may the Blessed One give me a prophecy." And by the power of the Blessed One, the <s>Jñānavairocana-samādhi</s> was obtained.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the sixth prince named <s>Ambara</s>. Abbreviated — "not only in this defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s>," and so on, just as the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> made his vow. "If, O Blessed One, my aspiration of such a nature were to be fulfilled, then in the ten directions, in world-realms equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, udāraṃ te praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tena tvaṃ puṇyābhisyandena daśasu (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 141.

children.text: ) dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhakṣetrā bahavaścaikapramāṇāḥ, śatasahasramanojñaśabdasaṃcodito buddhakṣetraḥ, tatastvaṃ kulaputra vegavairocano nāma bhagasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ vegavairocanātikrānte 'nāgate 'dhvanyekanadīgaṅgāvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye purastimāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavo 'tikramitvā ādityasomā nāma lokadhātuḥ tatra tvaṃ bodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, dharmavaśavartīśvararājo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpanno yāvad buddho bhagavān" / sa ca vegavairocano bodhisattvastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pañcamaṇḍalena vandati ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, all of one measure, urged on by the delightful sound of a hundred thousand — that shall be your <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. From that, O son of good family, you shall be called <s>Vegavairocana</s>. You shall become, after <s>Vegavairocana</s>, in a future time, having entered a second incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>] equal to the sands of one river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the eastern direction, having passed beyond world-realms equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, in a world-realm named <s>Ādityasomā</s> — there you shall attain awakening, <s>Dharmava</s>-

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Well done, well done, O good man! Your vow is noble. By the overflowing of your merit, in the ten directions (

children.translated_text: He said:

children.text: "uttiṣṭha suvrata surata dāntacitta sattvebhyaḥ tīvrakaruṇā mahatī pravṛttā /
children.translated_text: "Arise, O <s>Suvrata</s> (one of good vows), O <s>Surata</s> (one of good delight), O one of tamed mind! Great and intense compassion has arisen for beings.

children.text: tāre hi sattvān duḥkhārṇavatīraṃ saṃsthā yāvanna budhyasi anuttarabuddhabodhiṃ" //
children.translated_text: Deliver beings to the shore beyond the ocean of suffering; maintain your resolve until you awaken to the supreme awakening of a <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ saptamaṃ rājaputramaṅgajamāmantrayāṃ āsa / peyālaṃ, "na cāsmiṃ kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre tatrāhaṃ bodhimabhisaṃbuddheyaṃ / yatra ca na narakā na tiryagyoniḥ na yamalokaḥ prajñāyate, na mātṛgrāmo na ca sattvānāṃ garbhavāsaḥ, na sumeruḥ na cakravāḍamahācakravāḍā na pāṃśuśailaparvatā notsadaśarkarakaṭhallakaṇṭakagahanā na kāṣṭhavṛkṣā na mahāsamudrā, na ca tatrādityacandrā na tārakarūpā na rātridivasā na tamaskandhā, na ca tatra sattvānāmuccāraprasrāvakheṭasiṅghāṇakaṃ na kāyakhedadurgandhaṃ, na ca sattvānāṃ kāyaklamatā bhavet na cittaklamatā; na ca tatra pāṃśubhūmirbhavet ; sarvā ca tatra bhūmiraśmagarbhamayī bhavet anekaratnaśatasahasrālaṅkṛtā bhavet, māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ca tad buddhakṣetraṃ nānāratnavṛkṣālaṅkṛtaṃ bhavet; te ca ratnavṛkṣā nānāratnajālālaṅkṛtā bhaveyuḥ; nānāratnaduṣyā nānāratnavastrā nānāratnamālā nānāratnābharaṇālaṅkārālaṅkṛtā nānāmālyebhyo nānāvādyairnānāratnabhājanairnānāpuṣpaiśca te ratnavṛkṣālaṅkṛtā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 143.

children.text: ) bhaveyuḥ; na tatra rātriḥ prajñāyeta, anyatra yadā puṣpāḥ saṃkuceyurvādyāśca vādyeyuḥ / saṃkucitebhyaśca puṣpebhyaḥ bodhisattvā pratyājāyeyuḥ; samāpannāśca tatra bodhisattvā darśanavyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, yena samādhinā pratilabdhena daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhato yāpayato buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyeyuḥ; tatkṣaṇe caivaṃrūpaṃ viśuddhaṃ divyaśrotraṃ pratilabheyuḥ, yena daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / sahopapannāśca sattvāḥ sarve jātismarā bhaveyuste ca buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān anusmareyuḥ / sahopapannāśca te sattvāḥ sarve evaṃrūpaṃ divyaṃ cakṣuḥ pratilabheyuḥ, yat samantāddaśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ paśyeyuḥ / sahopapannāśca te sattvāḥ sarva evaṃrūpeṇa paracittajñānakauśalyena samanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ, yadekakṣaṇena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāṃ vijāneyuryāvadbodhiparinirvāṇāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) should there be; no night should be perceived there, except when the flowers close and the musical instruments play. And when the flowers have closed, may the <s>bodhisattvas</s> be born from them; and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are established there may obtain a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Darśanavyūha</s> ('Array of Vision'), by which <s>samādhi</s>, once obtained, they would see the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, standing and sustaining in other world-realms in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; and at that very moment, such a purified divine ear
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 144.

children.text:
) te sattvāstāṃ samādhiṃ praṇāmeyū; rātryāḥ pratyuṣakālasamaye caturdiśaṃ sugandhāḥ prītikarāśca mṛdusukhasaṃsparśā vāyavo vāyeyuḥ, ye tān puṣpān vikāsayeyuḥ / te ca bodhisattvāstābhyaḥ samādhibhyo vyutthihitvā tebhyaḥ puṣpakeśarebhya uttiṣṭheyuḥ; tathārūpaṃ ca ṛddhiviṣayaṃ pratilabheran yad ekacittakṣaṇene buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānyekaikāṃ diśaṃ gaccheyuḥ, tiṣṭhato yāpayato buddhān bhagavato vanditvā paryupāsitvā tadā nivarteyuḥ, tatra ca māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpakeśareṣu paryaṅkamābadhvā niṣīdeyuḥ, dharmasukhamanasikāreṇa tathāgataṃ prekṣeyuryena yena ca niṣīdeyuḥ parivarteyurvā sarvadiśāsu ca māmeva paśyeyuḥ / yathārūpaṃ ca tatra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ kāṅkṣāvimatidharmeṣu saṃśayotpadyeta tatsarvaṃ mama darśanavyavalokanamātreṇa vigaccheyuḥ / yathārūpaṃ ca dharmadeśanān te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ākāṅkṣeyuḥ tathārūpaṃ dharmadeśanāṃ mama vyavalokanamātreṇājāneyuḥ / amamā aparigrahāśca
tatra sattvā bhaveyuḥ, antaśaḥ svakāyajīvitenāpyanarthikāḥ / sarve ca tatra bodhisattvā avaivartikā bhaveyuḥ / na tatrākuśalasya nāma (
children.translated_text: ) those beings would attain that <s>samādhi</s>. At the time of dawn at the end of the night, may fragrant, delightful, gentle, pleasantly-touching breezes blow from the four directions, which would cause those flowers to bloom. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having risen from those <s>samādhis</s>, would rise from those flower-pistils; and they would obtain such a domain of supernatural power that in a single mind-moment they would travel in each direction to world-realms equal in number to the atoms of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, standing and sustaining
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 145.

children.text: ) bhavenna ca tatra buddhakṣetre śikṣāgrahaṇasya nāma bhavet, na cāpattivyūtthāpanakathā, yathā yāvatsarvasattvā dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ / sarve ca nārāyanabalikā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatraikasattvo 'pīndriyavikalo bhavet yāvadbodhinirvāṇena / sarve ca tatra sattvā muṇḍā navakāṣāyacīvaraprāvṛtāḥ pratyājāyeyuḥ; suvibhaktaṃ ca samādhiṃ pratilabheyuḥ; yāvadbodhiparyantena praṇāmeyuḥ / sarve ca tatra samavadhānakuśalamūlā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ jarāvyādhiduḥkhaṃ prajñāyeta / yeṣāṃ sattvānāmāyuḥparikṣayo bhavet te sarve paryaṅkena parinirvāyeyuḥ, svakācca śarīrāttejodhātuṃ pramuñceyuryenātmanaḥ śarīraṃ sādhyeyuḥ, caturdiśaśca vāyava āgaccheyuḥ ye tāni bodhisattvaśarīrāṇi śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu kṣipeyuḥ / evaṃrūpāśca mahāmaṇiratnāḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ tadyathā rājñaścakravartinaḥ prabhāsvaraṃ maṇiratnaṃ; ye ca tatra sattvāstāṃ maṇiratnaprabhāṃ paśyeyuḥ taṃ vā maṇiratnaṃ paśyeyuḥ spārśeyurvā te sarve narakatiryagyamalokaduḥkhāni yāvadbodhinirvāṇena mā pratisaṃvedayeyuḥ / te ca tataścyavitvā tatropapadyeyuḥ yatra tiṣṭhanto (
children.translated_text: ) there should be — and in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there should not even be the name of the taking up of precepts, nor any discourse on the confession of transgressions, for all beings there would be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being. And all would be of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-like strength. And not even a single being there would be deficient in faculties, up to the point of the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of awakening. And all beings there would be born tonsured, clad in new saffron robes; and they would obtain the well-analyzed <s>samādhi</s>; up to the culmination of awakening
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 146.

children.text: ) yāpayanto buddhā bhagavantaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti / tatropapannāśca te sattvāsteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśāddharmaṃ śṛṇuyuste ca bodhicittamutpādayeyuḥ, sahotpādite ca bodhicitte 'vaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / na kaścitsattvo mama buddhakṣetre 'samāhitaḥ kālaṃ kuryāt, na duḥkhavedanāyā na parasparavyāvadhacittāviprayogamaraṇāya tataśca mārākṣaṇeṣupapadyeyuḥ, yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ buddhadarśanenāvirahitā bhaveyuḥ dharmaśravaṇena saṅghopasthānenāvirahitā bhaveyuḥ / sarve ca tatra sattvā apagatakhiladveṣamrakṣerṣyāmātsaryā bhaveyuḥ / vivarjitaṃ ca taṃ buddhakṣetraṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhairbhavet, śuddhaiśca bodhisattvaistaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavet / snigdhacittā mṛducittā avairacittā akilviṣacittāḥ śāntacittāḥ samāhitacittāśca bhaveyuḥ tatra ye sattvā upapadyeyuḥ / prabhāsvaraṃ ca me tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhavet, mahadguṇavyūhaṃ ca me tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhavet / daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ lokadhātubhirdṛśyeta gandhena ca sphuret / (
children.translated_text: ) the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, standing and sustaining, would teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. And those beings who have been reborn there, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — they would generate the mind of awakening, and as soon as the mind of awakening is generated, they would become irreversible in supreme perfect awakening. No being in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would die in a state of mental distraction, nor through painful feeling, nor through death with a mind of mutual obstruction and non-separation — and from there they would be reborn free from the inopportune states of <s>Māra</s>, up to the point of awakening
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 147.

children.text:
) nityasukhasamarpitāśca tatra sattvā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre duḥkhaśabdaḥ śrūyeta / tāvaccāhaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi yāvadahaṃ bodhisattvabhūtaścaivaṃrūpābhirbuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasaṃpadābhiḥ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi, evaṃrūpaiḥ pariśuddhāśayaiḥ sattvaistadbuddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi; tataḥ paścād ahaṃ tatra buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / bodhiprāptasya ca me 'pramāṇā prabhā bhavet; sahasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu ca daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu lakṣanālaṅkṛto me kāyaḥ saṃdṛśyediti
/ ye ca tatra sattvā māṃ paśyeyuḥ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ rāgaḥ praśamayet, dveṣo moherṣyā mānamrakṣasarvakleśopakleśāḥ praśameyuḥ; sarve bodhicittamutpādayeyuḥ; yathāvidhāśca samādhidhāraṇīrākāṅkṣeta tathārūpā māṃ dṛṣṭvā pratilabheyuḥ / ye ca tatra sattvāḥ śītanarake pratyājātā bhaveyusteṣāṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhāvedanā prādurbhavet, tathārūpāṃ ca sukhāṃ vedanāṃ pratilabheran yathāpi nāma dvitīyadhyānasamāpannasya bhikṣoste ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā parameṇa kāyacaitasikena sukhena samarpitā bhaveyuste ca sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) and those beings there would be established in perpetual happiness. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, the sound of suffering would not be heard. And I shall practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct for so long until, while still a <s>bodhisattva</s>, I shall establish a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with such arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s>-qualities, and I shall fill that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with beings of such purified dispositions; and after that, I shall, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, fully awaken to supreme perfect awakening
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 148.

children.text: ) samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayeyuste ca tataścyavitvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeran, tatra cānaivartikā bhaveyuḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye ca sattvāḥ pretabhavaneṣūpapannāḥ mama paśyeyuḥ, peyālaṃ avaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; evaṃ tiryagyonigatā vaktavyāḥ / evaṃ devāḥ dviguṇā ca me prabhāsayeyaṃ / apramāṇā ca me āyurbhavet, yanna śakyaṃ kenacidgaṇayituṃ anyatra sarvajñajñānena / bodhiprāptasya ca me daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvaparimāṇeṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavanto mama varṇaṃ bhāṣeranyeṣāṃ anuśrāvayeyaṃ; ye ca tatra sattvā mama varṇaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ te tatra mama buddhakṣetre kuśalamūlaṃ pariṇāmayeyuḥ, te kālaṃ kṛtvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ sthāpayitvānantaryakārakāṃ saddharmapratikṣepakāṃ āryāpavādakāṃ / bodhiprāptasya ca me ye sattvā aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu mama nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ mama ca buddhakṣetra upapattiṃ ākāṅkṣeyuḥ, teṣāmahaṃ maraṇakālasamayeṣvanekagaṇaparivṛto vitimirasamādhiṃ samāpannāḥ tathārūpeṇa subhāṣitena tān sattvān saṃtoṣayeyaṃ, teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhaṃ praśamet, tenaiva prasādena niścitāṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, (
children.translated_text: ) may they generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and having passed away from there, may they be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), and there may they become irreversible in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And whatever beings reborn in the realms of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) see me — abbreviated — may they become irreversible in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>; likewise for beings gone to animal births. Likewise for the gods, and may I illuminate them twofold. And may my lifespan be immeasurable, such that no one can calculate it except by omniscient knowledge. And when I have attained awakening, may <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in immeasurable and boundless other world-realms in the ten directions proclaim my qualities and announce them to others; and may whatever beings hear my qualities dedicate their roots of merit toward my <s>Buddha</s>-field, and having died, may they be reborn in my <s>Buddha</s>-field — except for those who commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, who reject the <s>Saddharma</s>, or who slander the Noble Ones. And when I have attained awakening, whatever beings in immeasurable and incalculable world-realms hear my name and aspire to rebirth in my <s>Buddha</s>-field, may I, at the time of their death, surrounded by a multitude, having entered the <s>Vitimira</s> (Cloudless) <s>samādhi</s>, satisfy those beings with such well-spoken words, may all their suffering be pacified, and by that very faith may they attain a firm <s>samādhi</s>, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 149.

children.text: ) cittaspṛhaṇāṃ dharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, kālaṃ ca kṛtvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ / ye ca punaranyatra buddhakṣetreṣu saptadhanavirahitāḥ sattvā anarthikāḥ tribhiryānairanarthikā devamānuṣikābhiḥ saṃpattibhiranarthikāḥ kuśalaparyeṣṭyā tribhiḥ puṇyakriyāvastubhiḥ adharmarāgaraktā viṣamalobhābhibhūtā mithyādharmaparītāsteṣāṃ prabhāsamādhinā maraṇakālasamaye purataḥ tiṣṭheyaṃ, anekagaṇaparivṛto dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, teṣāṃ svakaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ darśayeyaṃ, bodhau ca samādāpayeyaṃ / te sattvā mamāntike paramaprītiprasādaṃ prāmodyaṃ pratilabheyuḥ bodhau ca cittānyutpādyeyuḥ, teṣāṃ sarvaduḥkhā vedanāḥ praśameyuḥ, te sūryapradīpaṃ ca samādhiṃ pratilabheran, mohapraṇāhaṃ caiṣāṃ bhavet, kālaṃ ca kṛtvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) may they attain the <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of dharmas) that delights the mind, and having died, may they be reborn in my <s>Buddha</s>-field. And furthermore, whatever beings in other <s>Buddha</s>-fields are bereft of the seven treasures, who take no interest in the three vehicles, who take no interest in divine and human attainments, who take no interest in the pursuit of merit through the three bases of meritorious action — who are attached to unwholesome desires, overwhelmed by extreme greed, beset by wrong <s>dharmas</s> — may I, by the <s>Prabhāsa</s> (Radiance) <s>samādhi</s>, stand before them at the time of their death, surrounded by a multitude, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and show them my own <s>Buddha</s>-field, and inspire them toward awakening. May those beings attain supreme joy, delight, and gladness in my presence, and may they generate the mind of awakening, and may all their painful sensations be pacified, and may they attain the <s>Sūryapradīpa</s> (Sun-Lamp) <s>samādhi</s>, and may their delusion be dispelled, and having died, may they be reborn in my <s>Buddha</s>-field."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the seventh prince named <s>Aṅgaja</s>. Abbreviated — "not in this defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall I attain awakening. But where there are no hells, no animal realm, no world of <s>Yama</s> perceived, no womankind, no dwelling in a womb for beings, no <s>Sumeru</s>, no <s>Cakravāḍa</s> or <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, no dust-mountains or rocky mountains, no thorns, dense thickets, gravel, or brambles, no dead trees, no great oceans, and there no sun-

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, śodhanaṃ te praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ" / sa prāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tathā ca daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣūragasāracandanacūrṇaṃ pravarṣatu / ye ca sattvāstaṃ gandhaṃ ghrāyeyuḥ te sarve bodhau cittamutpādayeyuḥ / ahaṃ caitarhi (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 150.

children.text: ) praṇītadyutiṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheyaṃ, yat svayaṃ eva paśyeyaṃ / utpāditaśca kulaputra praṇītadyutiḥ samādhiḥ svayamevādrākṣīt tadbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu uragasāracandanacūrṇaṃ pravarṣitaṃ, daśasu dikṣvekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṇanātikrāntāḥ sattvāḥ prāñjalibhūtā adrākṣuḥ, ye bodhāya cittānyutpādayanti" /
children.translated_text: ) attain the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Praṇītadyuti</s> (Exquisite Radiance), so that I myself may see [the fulfillment]." And, O son of good family, the <s>Praṇītadyuti</s> <s>samādhi</s> was produced, and he himself saw that in the ten directions, in other world-realms equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, a rain of <s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood powder had fallen, and in the ten directions, in each direction, beings beyond counting, with palms joined, were seen — those who were generating the mind of awakening.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, O good man! Your aspiration for purification has been well made." He said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such an aspiration of mine is to be fulfilled, then may a rain of <s>uragasāra</s> (serpent-essence) sandalwood powder fall in other <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And may whatever beings smell that fragrance all generate the mind of awakening. And may I now (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "atiśīghraṃ kulaputra gandhavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitā, gaṇanātikrāntāśca sattvā bodhau samādāpitāstena tvaṃ kulaputra siṃhagandho bhavasva / atikrānte siṃhagandha ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsaṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye uparimāya diśāyeto buddhakṣetrāddvicatvāriṃśatgaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya tatra nīlagandhaprabhāsavirajo nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati, tatra tvaṃ siṃhagandhānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, prabhāsavirajaḥsamucchrayagandheśvararājo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi arhan samyaksaṃbuddho yāvad buddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Most swiftly, O son of good family, was the rain of fragrance showered, and beings beyond counting were inspired toward awakening. Therefore, O son of good family, you shall be called <s>Siṃhagandha</s> (Lion Fragrance). In the future, O <s>Siṃhagandha</s>, after the passage of the first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and entering the second, passing beyond forty-two <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> from the upward direction from this <s>Buddha</s>-field, there shall be a world-realm called <s>Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja</s> (Pure Radiance of Blue Fragrance). There, O <s>Siṃhagandha</s>, you shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prabhāsavirajaḥsamucchrayagandheśvararāja</s> (King, Lord of Fragrance, Exalted in Pure Radiance), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra siṃhagandho bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vanditavān /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃhagandha</s> made prostration at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with the five-point [contact].

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said to him:
"Arise, O one worshipped by <s>asuras</s>, humans, and gods — liberate you the beings tormented by the suffering of existence!

children.text: chittvā tvaṃ bhavaduḥkhakleśabandhanāṃ bheṣyasi narajina āryapudgalaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Having cut the bonds of suffering, affliction, and existence, you shall become a <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) among humans, a noble person!"

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'ṣṭamaṃ rājaputramamighaṃ nāmāmantrayāṃ āsa / peyālaṃ, "tāvadahaṃ bhagavan kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre bodhisattvabhūto bodhisattvacārikāṃ cariṣyāmi yāvadahaṃ daśasahasrān kliṣṭān buddhakṣetrānevaṃrūpāṃ pariśuddhāṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi, yathā nīlagandhaprabhāsavirajaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ tathā bhaviṣyati / evaṃrūpairavaruptakuśalamūlaiḥ pariśuddhāśayairmahāyānasaṃprasthitairbodhisattvaistadbuddhakṣetraṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 152.

children.text: ) sphuṭaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi, paścādahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyāmi / tathārūpāmahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvacārikāṃ cariṣyāmi yathā nānye bodhisattvāścaranti / yadahaṃ bhadanta bhagavannimāni saptavarṣāṇi buddhaguṇabodhisattvaguṇapariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇapariśuddhaṃ rahogata ekākī saṃcintayamāno niṣaṇṇaḥ, darśanavyūhasamādhipūrvaṃgamena ekadaśabodhisattvasamādhisahasrāṇi yāni mayātrotpāditāni pratilabdhāni bhāvitāni, eṣā mama bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvabhūtasya bodhisattvacārikā; ye 'pi te daśasu dikṣvanantāparyantāsvanyāsu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti yāpayanti sattvānāṃ hitāya sukhāya dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, ye trādhvasamatikrāntā dhvajāgrākeyūrā buddhakṣetrāstāṃ paripūrṇāṃ jinaiḥ paśyeyaṃ āvarteyaṃ / tena ca samādhināhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan paramāṇurajaḥsamān buddhān bhagavato bodhisattvaśrāvakagaṇaparivṛtān paśyeyaṃ / ekaikasyāhamaniśritāsamādhibalena buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamaiḥ kāyairvandeyaṃ / (
children.translated_text: ) with such <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have planted roots of merit, who are of purified intentions, and who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and afterward I shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Such, O venerable Blessed One, shall be my <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, unlike that of any other <s>bodhisattvas</s>. For, O venerable Blessed One, these seven years I have sat in solitude, alone, contemplating the purified <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities, and <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, and preceded by the <s>Darśanavyūha</s> (Vision Array) <s>samādhi</s>, eleven thousand <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s> were produced, attained, and cultivated by me here. This, O venerable Blessed One, is my <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct while still a <s>bodhisattva</s>. And whatever <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones abide and sustain in other world-realms in the infinite and boundless ten directions, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit and happiness of beings — may I see those <s>Buddha</s>-fields that have transcended the three times, whose banners and diadems are supreme, filled with <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), and may I revolve [among them]. And by that <s>samādhi</s>, O venerable Blessed One, may I see <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones equal in number to atoms, surrounded by assemblies of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>. And to each one, by the power of the <s>Aniśritā</s> (Unattached) <s>samādhi</s>, may I bow with bodies equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 153.

children.text:
) ekaikena cāhaṃ kāyenānuttarairvicitrai ratnaiḥ puṣpairanuttarairvicitrairgandhairmālyaiśca curṇavilepanairvādyaiḥ sarvābhiścānuttarābhirvyūhābhirekaikaṃ pūjayeyaṃ / ekakṣetre cāhaṃ samudravālikāpramāṇān kalpāṃ careyaṃ, yadā cāhaṃ sarvakāyavibhāvanena samādhinaikakṣaṇenaikaikasya buddhasya buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhagocarān ājāneyaṃ / guṇākarasamādhinā cāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan nekaikasya buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairanuttaraistavaistaveyaṃ / animiṣasamādhinā cāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan nekarajāgracittapramāṇena sarvabuddhakṣetrān pūrṇāṃ jinaiḥ paśyeyaṃ / araṇāsamādhinā cāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan nekacittakṣaṇena sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvānatītānāgatapratyutpannān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyeyaṃ / śūraṅgamasamādhinā cāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavannarakeśvavataritvā
nairayikamātmabhāvamabhinirmiṇitvā nairayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, bodhāya ca samādāpayeyaṃ, tatastān sattvān bodhāya cittamutpādayeyaṃ, tataścyavitvā manuṣyāṇāṃ sahabhāvyatāyāmupapadyeyuḥ (
children.translated_text: ) And with each body, may I worship each one with supreme and varied jewels, flowers, supreme and varied fragrances, garlands, incense powders, ointments, music, and all supreme arrays. And in a single <s>Buddha</s>-field may I practice for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the ocean. And when, by the <s>samādhi</s> of manifesting all bodies, in a single instant, I know the domains of each <s>Buddha</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And by the <s>Guṇākara</s> (Mine of Qualities) <s>samādhi</s>, O venerable Blessed One, may I praise each one with praises equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields.
