And by the <s>Animiṣa</s> (Unblinking) <s>samādhi</s>, O venerable Blessed One, may I see all <s>Buddha</s>-fields filled with <s>Jinas</s>, with a mind as minute as the tip of a single dust-mote. And by the <s>Araṇā</s> (Conflict-Free) <s>samādhi</s>, O venerable Blessed One, may I in a single mind-moment see in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields the past, future, and present <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities. And by the <s>Śūraṅgama</s> (Heroic Progress) <s>samādhi</s>, O venerable Blessed One, may I descend into the hells, emanate a hell-being's body, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to hell-beings, inspire them toward awakening, cause those beings to generate the mind of awakening, and having passed away from there, may they be reborn in the company of humans (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 154.

children.text: ) yatra buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśāddharmaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ, avaivartikabhūmau ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; evaṃ tiryakṣu, evaṃ preteṣu, evaṃ yakṣeṣu, evaṃ rākṣaseṣu, evamasureṣu, evaṃ nāgeṣu, evaṃ kinnaramahorageṣu, evaṃ piśācapūtanakaṭapūtaneṣu, evaṃ manuṣyacaṇḍāleṣu, evaṃ vaṇijeṣu gaṇikāsu; yathārūpeṣu ca bhagavan sattvāḥ kuleṣūpapadyante, yathārūpaśca teṣāṃ ātmabhāvapratilābhaḥ, yathārūpeṇa ca sattvāḥ karmapratyayena sukhāṃ vedanāṃ duḥkhāṃ vā pratisaṃvedayanti, yathārūpeṣu ca śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu prasaktāḥ, tathārūpamātmabhāvaṃ nirmiṇitvā tathārūpaśilpasthānakarmasthāneṣūdyogaṃ nidarśayeyaṃ, tathārūpeṇa cakṣaravyāhāreṇa sattvānāṃ cittamārādhayeyaṃ, dharmaṃ ca deśayeyaṃ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayeyaṃ niveśayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, avaivartikāṃśca sthāpayeyaṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tāvadahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvacārikāṃ cariṣyāmi yathā daśasu sarvabuddhakṣetrasahasreṣu sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ cittasantatiṃ tathā pariśodhayeyaṃ yathā pūrvakarmakleśāṃ na kuryuḥ, yadekasattvasyāpi (
children.translated_text: ) where <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones abide, and may they hear the <s>Dharma</s> from those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, and may I establish them on the stage of irreversibility. Likewise among animals, likewise among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), likewise among <s>yakṣas</s>, likewise among <s>rākṣasas</s>, likewise among <s>asuras</s>, likewise among <s>nāgas</s>, likewise among <s>kinnaras</s> and <s>mahoragas</s>, likewise among <s>piśācas</s>, <s>pūtanas</s>, <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>, likewise among human <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts), likewise among merchants and courtesans. In whatever kinds of families, O Blessed One, beings are reborn, whatever kinds of bodily existence they obtain, through whatever kinds of karmic conditions beings experience pleasant or painful sensations, in whatever kinds of crafts and occupations they are engaged — may I emanate such a bodily form and demonstrate engagement in such crafts and occupations, and with such speech and discourse may I delight the minds of beings, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and inspire, establish, and ground them in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and place them in irreversibility toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. For as long, O venerable Blessed One, shall I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct until I purify the mind-streams of all beings in all ten thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields such that they would not commit former karmic afflictions, and until even for a single being (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 155.

children.text: ) catvārā mārāścittasantatipathaṃ na prajānīyuḥ, tadahaṃ daśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇyevaṃrūpāṃ pariśuddhāṃ sthāpayeyaṃ, yathā prabhāsavirajāsamucchrayagandheśvararājajyotistathāgatasya nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraje buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāstathā bhaveyaṃ / evaṃ mayā svabuddhakṣetrasya svaparṣāyā ca yathā siṃhagandhena bodhisattvena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tathā daśasu buddhakṣetrasahasreṣu sattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni praśāmyantu, sarve ca mṛducittā bhavantu, karmaṇyacittā bhavantu, svakasvakāyāścaturdvīpikāyāḥ tiṣṭhanto buddhān paśyantu / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ vicitraratnā vicitrapuṣpagandhavilepanacūrṇacchatradhvajapatākāḥ prādurbhavantu, yena te sattvāḥ tān buddhān pūjayeyuḥ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayeyuḥ / ahaṃ ca bhagavan darśanavyūhasamādhānabalena svayaṃ paśyeyaṃ, sahodīritayāṃ vācāsminnevameva svayaṃ paśyati yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ" iti /
children.translated_text: ) the four <s>Māras</s> would not know the path of their mind-stream — then I shall establish those ten thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields as purified, such that they shall be like the array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhāsavirajaḥsamucchrayagandheśvararājajyotis</s> in the <s>Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja</s> [world-realm]. Thus I have made the aspiration for my own <s>Buddha</s>-field and my own assembly, just as the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃhagandha</s> made his aspiration. If, O venerable Blessed One, such an aspiration of mine is to be fulfilled, then may the suffering of all beings in the ten thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields be pacified, may all become gentle-minded, may all become workable-minded, and while standing in their own respective four-continent world-systems, may they see the <s>Buddhas</s>. And may there appear before those beings varied jewels, varied flowers, fragrances, ointments, incense powders, parasols, banners, and pennants, with which those beings may worship those <s>Buddhas</s> and generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And may I, O Blessed One, by the power of the <s>Darśanavyūha</s> (Vision Array) <s>samādhi</s>, see it myself, and even as my words are spoken, may I myself see it just as the aspiration was made."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the eighth prince, named <s>Amigha</s>. Abbreviated: "For as long, O Blessed One, shall I, while still a <s>bodhisattva</s>, practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in defiled <s>Buddha</s>-fields, until I establish ten thousand defiled <s>Buddha</s>-fields as purified, just as the <s>Buddha</s>-field <s>Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja</s> is. I shall fill that <s>Buddha</s>-field (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvaṃ kulaputra samantake ca svake ca buddhakṣetre daśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇi pariśuddhāni sthāpayiṣyasi / aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 156.

children.text: ) ca sattvānāṃ santatiṃ pariśodhayiṣyasi / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāyāṃ pūjāyāmautsukyamāpatsyase / tena tvaṃ kulaputra samantabhadro nāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ samantabhadrānāgate 'dhvani atikrānta ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye parivartāvaśiṣṭe dvitīya uttarāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrāt ṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramitvā tatra jñānatāpasuviśuddhaguṇā nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati; tatra tvaṃ samantabhadrānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, jñānavajravijṛmbhiteśvaraketurnāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
children.translated_text: ) beings. Thus you will be zealous in immeasurable and incalculable worship of immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones. Therefore, O son of good family, you shall be called <s>Samantabhadra</s> (Universally Good). You, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, in the future time, after the passage of the first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second, passing beyond sixty <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> from the northern direction from this <s>Buddha</s>-field, there shall be a world-realm called <s>Jñānatāpasuviśuddhaguṇā</s> (Qualities Purified by the Austerity of Wisdom). There, O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, you shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānavajravijṛmbhiteśvaraketu</s> (Banner of the Lord Expanded by the Vajra of Wisdom), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One."

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, O son of good family, that you will establish your own surrounding <s>Buddha</s>-field and ten thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields in purity. You will purify the mind-streams of immeasurable and incalculable (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādayoḥ śirasā nipapāta /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> fell at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with his head, with the five-point [prostration].

body.text:
ratnagarbhastathāgatastvāha -
"uttiṣṭha surata suvrata dāntacittā sattvāna santati viśodhya dṛḍhapratijñatvaṃ /

children.text: sattvān tāraya kleśanadīsughorān tvaṃ jñāna ulkadhara bheṣyasi buddha loke" //
children.translated_text: Liberate beings from the terrible river of afflictions — O bearer of the torch of wisdom, you shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world!"

body.translated_text:
The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said:
"Arise, O delightful one, of good vows, tamed mind — having purified the mind-streams of beings, firm in your resolve,

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kulaputra samayena daśakuśīdaprāṇasahasrāṇi ekakaṇṭhena vācaṃ babhāṣire / "bhaviṣyāma vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan te pariśuddheṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, yāṃ suviśuddhāśayāḥ samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhisattvacārikāṃ carāmāṇaḥ pariśuddhāṃ sthāpayati / evaṃ ca vayaṃ ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayitvā tatra buddhakṣetra upapadyema" /
body.translated_text: At that time, O son of good family, ten thousand indolent beings spoke with one voice: "We shall become, Venerable Blessed One, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in those pure <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in which the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, of supremely pure intention, practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, establishes purity. And having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), may we be reborn in that <s>Buddha</s>-field."

body.text: evaṃ kulaputra ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena daśaprāṇisahasrā vyākṛtāḥ / "yadā samantabhadro 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate tadā yūyaṃ teṣu sāmantakeṣu lokadhātuṣvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyadhve / sahasraikanāmakāstathāgatā bhaviṣyathaḥ yaduta sahasraṃ jvālakuṇḍeśvaraghoṣā nāma bhaviṣyatha tathāgatāḥ, aparaṃ (

) vajrapradīpaḥ, vyūharājā, jayasaṃkhyā, supratiṣṭhitaḥ, maticandrarājā, kramavinarditarājā, sālendrasiṃhavigrahaḥ, nārāyaṇavijitagarbhaḥ, ratnaguṇasaṃnicaryaḥ, jyotigarbhaḥ, nakṣatravibhavakīrtiḥ, puṇyabalasālarājā, jñānaghoṣaḥ, brahmottaraḥ, dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ / aparaṃ sahasraṃ gandhapadmavijitakīrtirājā nāmano bhaviṣyanti, raśmimaṇḍalajyotiprabhāsarājā, gandhapadmottaravegaḥ, anantaguṇasāgarajñānottaraḥ, jambucchāyaḥ, guṇaśailadhvajaḥ, siṃhaketuḥ, nāgavivarjitakusumatejarājā, sugandhabījanairātma, amṛtaguṇatejarājakalpinami
bhaviṣyati / aparaṃ sahasraṃ visṛṣṭadharmarājāno nāgendravimuktibuddhalokasāgaralocanaśailanāmā bhaviṣyanti tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ / ekakāle ekadivase 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyanti, anyonyāsu lokadhātuṣu daśāntarakalpāyuḥpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati" / te 'pi daśaprāṇasahasrā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā nipetuḥ /

Another thousand will be <s>Tathāgatas</s> named <s>Gandhapadmavijitakīrtirāja</s>; <s>Raśmimaṇḍalajyotiprabhāsarāja</s>; <s>Gandhapadmottaravega</s>; <s>Anantaguṇasāgarajñānottara</s>; <s>Jambucchāya</s>; <s>Guṇaśailadhvaja</s>; <s>Siṃhaketu</s>; <s>Nāgavivarjitakusumateja</s>; <s>Sugandhabījanairātma</s>; <s>Amṛtaguṇatejarāja</s> — they shall be. At one time, on one day, they shall attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, in one another's world-realms, with a lifespan measuring ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>." Those ten thousand beings also fell at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, bowing with the five-point prostration.

body.translated_text: Thus, O son of good family, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, ten thousand beings were prophesied: "When <s>Samantabhadra</s> attains unsurpassed perfect awakening, then you will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening in those neighboring world-realms. You will be <s>Tathāgatas</s> sharing one name among thousands — namely, you will be a thousand <s>Tathāgatas</s> named <s>Jvālakuṇḍeśvaraghoṣa</s>; another (

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said —
"Arise with the steadfast roar of a <s>nāga</s>, and accumulate wholesome treasures;
Exert yourselves vigorously in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — you shall become leaders of <s>asuras</s>, humans, and the world."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo navamaṃ rājaputramāmantrayate sma amighaṃ nāma / peyālaṃ, sa prāha - "tathārūpamahaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ cariṣyāmi yathā me daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāstiṣṭhanto yāpayantaḥ buddhā bhagavanto bodhicārikāṃ carataḥ sākṣibhūtā bhaviṣyanti bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ / yadahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan tvatpurato bodhāya cittamutpādayāmi, yāvaccānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsye / atrāntareṇa me bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇasya na vipratisāracittamutpadyeta, yāvadbodhiparyantamupādāya dṛḍhapratijño bhaveyaṃ yathāvādī tathākārī, na cānyasya sattvasya cittasaṃkṣobho bhaveyaṃ, na (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 162.

children.text: ) ca me śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne cittamutpadyeta, mā ca kāmarāgacittacaitasikā utpadyeran, mā styānamiddhasahagatā mauddhatyasahagatā mā kaukṛtyasahagatā na vicikitsāsahagatā na prāṇātipātaṃ nādattādānaṃ nābrahmacaryaṃ na mṛsāvādaṃ na paiśunyaṃ na pāruṣyaṃ nābhidhyā na vyāpādaṃ na mithyādṛṣṭiḥ na saṃbhinnapralāpaṃ na mātsaryasahagataṃ na dharme 'gauravacittatā na visaṃvādanacittatā / yāvadbodhiparyantān mama bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇasya ime dharmā na saṃvidyeyuḥ / yāvadbodhiparyantamupādāya padavītihārakamapi buddhānusmṛtirnityaṃ cittacaitasikāḥ pravarteran / yāvadbodhiparyantena nāhaṃ buddhadarśanena virahito bhaveyaṃ na dharmaśravaṇena na saṅghopasthānena / sarvatra ca jātiṣu pravrajyāṃ pratilabheyaṃ / sarvāsu jātiṣu pāṃśukūliko bhaveyaṃ, traicīvarikaḥ vṛkṣamūlikaḥ naiṣadyikaḥ āraṇyakaḥ piṇḍapātikaḥ alpecchaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ dharmadeśakaḥ ādeyavākyaḥ aparimāṇapratibhānasaṃpanno bhaveyaṃ / na ca mūlāpattimāpadyeyaṃ / na mṛṣāvādasahagatairmantraiḥ parapravādino vimardeyaṃ / śūnyatāpratisaṃyuktaṃ ca mātṛgrāmasya dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, śūnyatāmanaskāreṇa ca mātṛgrāmasya na dantavidarśanaṃ kuryāt, (
children.translated_text: ) mind toward the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) or <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakener) vehicle arise in me; may no mental factors of sensual desire arise; may no mental factors accompanied by sloth and torpor, accompanied by restlessness, accompanied by remorse arise; may no doubt arise; may I not commit killing, stealing, unchastity, false speech, slander, harsh speech, covetousness, malice, wrong views, or idle chatter; may no mental factors accompanied by miserliness arise, nor disrespect for the <s>Dharma</s>, nor a mind of deception. Until the point of awakening, while I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, may these qualities not be found in me. Until the point of awakening, may recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> constantly operate as mental factors, even with every step I take. Until the point of awakening, may I never be separated from seeing <s>Buddhas</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, or serving the <s>Saṅgha</s>. In every birth, may I obtain the going forth. In every birth, may I be a wearer of refuse-rags, a keeper of three robes, a dweller at the foot of a tree, a sitter, a forest-dweller, an alms-gatherer, of few desires, content, a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s>, one whose words are heeded, endowed with immeasurable eloquence. May I not commit a root transgression. May I not defeat rival debaters with incantations accompanied by false speech. May I teach the <s>Dharma</s> connected with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) to women, and with mental attention on <s>śūnyatā</s>, may I not show my teeth [in a smile] to women, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 163.

children.text:
) na hastavikāreṇa dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / nityaṃ cāhaṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śāstṛsaṃjñāmutpādayeyaṃ / yasya cāhaṃ dharmabhāṇakasya sakāśāddharmaṃ śṛṇuyāṃ śāstṛsaṃjñān tasyāntike utpādayeyaṃ, satkṛtya cāhaṃ taṃ dharmabhāṇakaṃ yathā tathāgataṃ tathā satkuryāṃ gurukuryāṃ mānayeyaṃ pūjayeyaṃ yāvadātmamāṃsairapi dharmabhāṇakamupasthiteyaṃ / na cāhaṃ pātramapātraṃ cāvekṣya dānaṃ dadyāṃ, na mama dharmadānamātsarikā cittacaitasikā utpadyeyuḥ / svajīvitadānenāhaṃ bodhyarthikān sattvān paritrāyeyaṃ, svavīryabalapraṇidhānopārjitena cāhaṃ dravyena vyasanagatān sattvān vyasanebhyaḥ parimocayeyaṃ / na cāhaṃ pravrajitaliṅginaṃ vā gṛhasthaliṅginaṃ vā āpattyānāpattyā vā codayeyaṃ / nityaṃ cāhaṃ lābhasatkāraśloke 'gniviṣaśastrasaṃjñāmutpādayeyaṃ
/ yadi ca me bhadanta bhagavannime praṇidhānā yāvadbodhiparyantamupādāya saṃṛdhyeyuḥ yathā bhagavataḥ purataḥ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tadubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ divyāścakraratnāḥ prādurbhavantu sahasrārāḥ sanābhikāḥ sanemikāḥ ādityavarṇaprabhāsvarāḥ" / sahabhāṣitāyāṃ asyāṃ vāci amighena rājaputreṇobhāyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ tathārūpāṇi cakrāṇi (
children.translated_text: ) nor teach the <s>Dharma</s> with hand gestures. May I always generate the perception of the Teacher toward <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). And from whatever <s>Dharma</s>-preacher I hear the <s>Dharma</s>, may I generate the perception of the Teacher toward that person; may I honor, respect, esteem, and worship that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher just as I would the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and may I serve that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher even with the flesh of my own body. May I not give gifts while discriminating between worthy and unworthy recipients; may no mental factors of miserliness regarding the gift of <s>Dharma</s> arise in me. May I protect with the gift of my own life those beings who seek awakening, and with wealth acquired through my own vigor, strength, and aspiration, may I liberate beings fallen into calamity from their calamities. May I not reproach one who bears the mark of a renunciant or one who bears the mark of a householder, whether in offense or not in offense. May I always generate the perception of fire, poison, and weapons toward gain, honor, and fame. If, Venerable Blessed One, these aspirations of mine are fulfilled until the point of awakening, as the aspiration was made before the Blessed One, then may divine wheel-jewels appear in both my hands — with a thousand spokes, with hub, with rim, radiant with the color of the sun." As soon as these words were spoken by Prince <s>Amigha</s>, in both his hands such wheels (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 164.

children.text: ) prādurbhūtāni yathāyācitāḥ / punarāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta yāvadbodhiparyantena tadime cakrāḥ śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gacchantu, evaṃrūpeṇoccaśabdena yathā nandopanandā nāgarājā gacchanti tathā sarvāvantaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ svareṇa vijñāpayantu bodhisattvavyākaraṇasmṛtyasaṃpramoṣajñānadarśanaśūnyatābhāvanāpracārabuddhaviṣayaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ cārayituṃ / ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ śrotrendriyeṣvayaṃ dharmaparyāyamābhāsamāgacchatu, nipatitamātre ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ rāgaḥ praśamatu, dveṣo moho mānerṣyā mātsaryaḥ praśamatu, sarvabuddhānusmṛtimanasikāreṇānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayantu" /
children.translated_text: ) appeared, just as he had requested. He further said: "If, Venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled until the point of awakening, then may these wheels go to the empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations, and with a loud sound, just as the <s>nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> go, may they pervade the entire <s>Buddha</s>-field with their sound, proclaiming the <s>Dharma</s> discourse on the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> — the practice of cultivating emptiness through the knowledge of unfailing mindfulness in the prophecy of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And for those beings who have been reborn there, may this <s>Dharma</s> discourse become manifest to all their faculties of hearing; and as soon as it reaches them, may their passion be pacified, may their hatred, delusion, pride, jealousy, and miserliness be pacified; and with mental attention on the recollection of all <s>Buddhas</s>, may they generate the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin addressed the ninth prince named <s>Amigha</s>. [The text is abbreviated.] He said: "I shall practice such a <s>bodhisattva</s> course that in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, dwelling and abiding, shall be my witnesses as I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Venerable Blessed One, as I generate the mind for awakening before you, and until I attain unsurpassed perfect awakening — in the meantime, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, may no mind of regret arise in me; may I be of firm resolve up to the point of awakening, practicing what I preach; may I not cause mental disturbance to any other being; may no (

body.text: preṣitau ca kulaputrāmighena rājaputreṇa tau dvau cakraratnau tau caivaṃrūpeṇa javena gacchatastadyathā buddhā bhagavanto buddhajavena gacchanti; evameva tau dvau cakraratnau gacchataḥ daśasu diśāsvaprameyeśvasaṃkhyeyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvā sattvānāṃ bodhisattvavyākaraṇasmṛtyasaṃpramoṣajñānāntargatābhāvanāpracārabuddhadharmaparyāyaṃ cārayanti / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāmayaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 165.

children.text: ) dharmaparyāyaṃ śrotrendriyasyābhāsamāgacchati, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ rāgo yāvan mātsaryacittacaitasikāḥ praśāntāḥ, sarve ca buddhajñānaviṣayaṃ manaskāreṇānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditavanto, muhūrtamātreṇa ca te cakrāḥ pratinivṛtyāmighasya rājaputrasya purataḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>Dharma</s> discourse became manifest to their faculty of hearing; in all of them, passion and all mental factors up to miserliness were pacified; and all of them, with mental attention on the domain of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. And in just a moment, those wheels returned and stood before Prince <s>Amigha</s>.

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, those two wheel-jewels sent forth by Prince <s>Amigha</s> went with such speed as <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones go with the speed of a <s>Buddha</s>; just so, those two wheel-jewels went to immeasurable, incalculable <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations in the ten directions, and there they proclaimed to the beings the <s>Dharma</s> discourse on the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> — the practice of cultivating the knowledge contained within the unfailing mindfulness in the prophecy of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And for those beings, this (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgataḥ amighasya rājaputrasya sādhukāramadāt, "sādhu sādhu kulaputra, tvayātīva śobhanaḥ praṇidhiḥ kṛta, ime ca divyāścakraratnāḥ śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu preṣitā, bahūni ca prāṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyakaluṣacittānyavasthāpitāni, bodhau ca samādāpitāni / tena tvaṃ kulaputrākṣobhyo nāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvamakṣobhyo lokasya pariṇāyakaḥ, gṛhṇa tvamakṣobhya buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāni yādṛṣānyākāṅkṣasi" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> gave his commendation to Prince <s>Amigha</s>: "Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You have made an exceedingly beautiful aspiration, and these divine wheel-jewels have been sent to the empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings have been established with unpolluted minds and inspired toward awakening. Therefore, O son of good family, let your name be <s>Akṣobhya</s> (Imperturbable). You shall become <s>Akṣobhya</s>, a guide for the world. Accept, O <s>Akṣobhya</s>, the splendid qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-field such as you desire."

body.text: akṣobhya āha - "tādṛśamahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhamākāṅkṣāmi yathā sarvalokasvarṇabhūrbhavet, samāpāṇitalopamā divyamaṇiratnavyavakīrṇā apagataśarkarakaṭhallā apagataśilāstaṃbhapāṣāṇaparvatā mṛdukā kācalindikasukhasaṃsparṣā, nikṣipte pādatale 'vanamedutkṣipte pādatale punarunnamet / na cātra narakatiryagyoniyamalokapretaviṣayāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 166.

children.text: ) prajñāyeyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre durgandhā bhāvā bhaveyuḥ, divyātikrāntena gandhena tadbuddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavet, divyaiśca māndāravamahāmāndāravaiḥ puṣpaistadbuddhakṣetramākīrṇaṃ / na ca tatra sattvānāṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇaṃ bhavet, na ca parasparabhayaṃ na ca parasparaviheṭhā na ca sattvānāmakālamaraṇaṃ vipratisāramaraṇaṃ nāsamāhitamaraṇaṃ / buddhānusmṛtimanaskāreṇa tatra sattvā bhaveyuḥ / na ca durgatiṣūpapadyeyuḥ, na pañcakaṣāyeṣu śūnyesu buddhakṣetreṣūpapadyeyuryāvadbodhiparinirvāṇāt buddhadarśanāvirahitā bhaveyurdharmaśravaṇena saṅghopasthānenāvirahitā / alparāgāśca tatra sattvā bhaveyuralpadveṣā alpamohāḥ, sarve ca tatra daśakuśalāṃ karmapathān samādāya varteyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ śīlpagrahaṇaṃ bhavet, na nāmanimittaṃ, na ca tatra sattvānāṃ mārāvatāraṃ mārgena / na ca tatra sattvā durvarṇā bhaveyuḥ, na ca tatra sattvā vaimātra bhaveyuḥ, yadutāryo vā dāso vā, amamā aparigrahāśca tatra sattvā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatra śrāvakānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vā śuklamokṣaṇaṃ bhavet, antataḥ svapnāntaragatānāmapi; (
children.translated_text: ) would be perceived. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no foul-smelling things; that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be pervaded with fragrance surpassing the divine, and strewn with divine <s>Māndārava</s> and <s>Mahāmāndārava</s> flowers. And there beings would have no old age, illness, or death, no mutual fear, no mutual harm, no untimely death, no death from remorse, no death from lack of concentration. The beings there would abide with minds of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Buddha). They would not be reborn in the lower realms, nor be reborn in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid of the five degeneracies — until <s>bodhi</s> and <s>parinirvāṇa</s> they would be inseparable from seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and from attending upon the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The beings there would have little desire, little hatred, and little delusion, and all would undertake and abide by the ten wholesome courses of action. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no undertaking of precepts by beings, no nominal marks, no entry of <s>Māra</s> by way of the path for beings. Beings there would not be of ugly complexion, nor would beings there be unequal — whether noble or slave — and beings there would be without possessiveness and without acquisitiveness. And there would be no seminal emission for <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>bodhisattvas</s>, not even in the course of dreams; (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 167.

children.text: ) sarve ca tatra sattvā dharmakāmā dharmaparyeṣṭiparā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetra ekasattvo 'pi viparītadṛṣṭiko bhavet na cānyatīrthiko, na ca tatra sattvānāṃ kāyaklamatā bhavet cittaklamatā vā bhavet; sarve ca te tatra sattvāḥ pañcābhijñā bhaveyuḥ / na ca tatra sattvānāṃ tṛṣṇā vā bhukṣā vā viheṭhayet, yādṛśaṃ cāhāramākāṅkṣeyuḥ tādṛśaṃ ratnabhājaneṣu purataḥ prādurbhavet yathā kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāṃ / na coccāraprasrāvakheṭasiṅghāṇamaśru vā kāye svedo vā bhavet, na ca tatra śītaṃ noṣṇaṃ bhavet, sugandhaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ bhavet, mṛdusaṃsparśāśca vāyavo vāyuyuḥ / te ca tatra devamanuṣyāṇāṃ gandhakṛtyaṃ kurvīranyadākāṅkṣeyuḥ yādṛśamākāṅkṣeyuḥ, ya ekaḥ śītalaṃ vāyumākāṅkṣet, dvitīya uṣṇa, apara utpalagandhaṃ vāyumākāṅkṣeyuḥ, apara uragasāracandanagandhaṃ vāyuṃ, apare kālānusārigandhaṃ, apare tagaragandhaṃ, apare 'garugandhaṃ, apare sarveṇa sarvaṃ vāyunākāṅkṣeyuḥ, teṣāṃ yathā cittotpādenākṣiptaṃ tathā saṃpadyet / evamapagatapañcakaṣāyā lokadhāturbhavet / tatra ca sattvānāṃ saptaratnamayāḥ kūṭāgārā bhaveyuḥ / teṣu ca kūṭāgāreṣu saptaratnamayāḥ paryaṅkāḥ stritāḥ (
children.translated_text: ) and all beings there would be desirers of the <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to the pursuit of the <s>Dharma</s>. Not even a single being in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would hold wrong views, nor would there be adherents of other doctrines. Beings there would have no bodily fatigue or mental fatigue; and all those beings there would possess the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Beings there would not be tormented by thirst or hunger; whatever food they wished for, just such food would appear before them in jewel vessels, just as for the gods of the desire realm. There would be no excrement, urine, phlegm, mucus, tears, or sweat on the body, nor would there be cold or heat; it would be fragrant and delightful, and gentle, pleasant breezes would blow. And those breezes would serve the fragrance-needs of gods and humans — whatever they wished, whatever kind they wished: one who wished for a cool breeze, another for a warm one; some would wish for a breeze with the fragrance of <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), others for a breeze with the fragrance of <s>uragasāracandana</s> (serpent-heart sandalwood), others for the fragrance of <s>kālānusāri</s> (black aloe), others for the fragrance of <s>tagara</s> (valerian), others for the fragrance of <s>aguru</s> (aloewood), others for a breeze of every kind whatsoever — as their minds incline, so it would manifest. Thus the world-realm would be free from the five degeneracies. And there, beings would have pavilions made of the seven precious substances. In those pavilions, couches made of the seven precious substances would be spread (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 168.

children.text:
) tūlikopadhānairmṛdukācalindikasaṃsparśāḥ prādurbhaveyuryatra manuṣyā vihareyuḥ / samantataśca kūṭāgāreṣu puṣkariṇīparipūrṇāṣṭāṅgopetenodakena prādurbhavet, yatra te sattvā udakenodakakāryaṃ kuryuḥ / sumanātālavṛkṣāṇāṃ vā vṛkṣāvalīralaṅkṛtā bhaveyuḥ, nānāpuṣpairnānāphalairnānāgandhairnānāvastrairnānācchatrairnānāmuktikāhārairnānābharaṇaiste vṛkṣā alaṅkṛtā bhaveyuḥ / yathārūpā ca tatra sattvā vastrābharaṇaṃ ākāṅkṣeyuḥ te tān tebhyaḥ kalpavṛkṣebhyo gṛhītvā prāvareyuḥ,
evaṃ puṣpairyāvadābharaṇāṃ gṛhītvā bandheyuḥ / saptaratnamayaśca me bodhivṛkṣo bhavet, yojanasahasramuccatvena yojanaṃ skandhapariṇāhena yojanasahasraṃ śākhāpariṇāhena / vāyusamīritaśca tato bodhivṛkṣāddivyātikrāntaḥ snigdho manojñaḥ pāramitā abhijñendriyabalabodhyaṅgaśabdo niścaret, ye ca sattvāstaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇuyuste virāgacittāḥ smṛtiṃ pratilabheyuḥ / sarvaguṇopetaśca tatra buddhakṣetre mātṛgrāmo bhavet tadyathā tuṣitadevanikāye 'psarāḥ / na ca tatra mātṛgrāmo durgandho bhavet, na dvijihve nerṣyāmātsaryaparicite / na ca tatra manuṣyā mātṛgrāmeṇa (
children.translated_text: ) with cushions and pillows soft to the touch like <s>kācalindika</s> cotton, where humans would dwell. And on all sides of the pavilions, lotus ponds filled with water possessing the eight excellent qualities would appear, where those beings would perform their water-needs. And there would be rows of <s>sumanā</s> and palm trees beautifully adorned, adorned with various flowers, various fruits, various fragrances, various garments, various parasols, various pearl necklaces, and various ornaments on those trees. And whatever garments and ornaments the beings there wished for, they would take from those <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) and clothe themselves, and likewise they would take flowers and even ornaments and adorn themselves. And my <s>Bodhi</s>-tree would be made of the seven precious substances, a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, a <s>yojana</s> in trunk-circumference, a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in branch-spread. And from that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, stirred by the breeze, sounds surpassing the divine — smooth, pleasant, of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), and <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) — would issue forth; and those beings who would hear that sound would attain dispassionate minds and gain mindfulness. And womankind in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be endowed with all virtues, just like the <s>apsarās</s> (celestial nymphs) in the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine assembly. And the women there would not be foul-smelling, not double-tongued, not beset by jealousy and envy. And there the men with the women (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 169.

children.text: ) sārdhaṃ maithunakāyasaṃsargamāpadyeyuḥ / yasya ca tatra puruṣasya sarāgacittamutpadyeta, gatvā mātṛgrāmaṃ sarāgena cittena prekṣate muhūrtena puruṣasya rāgaḥ praśāmyeta, mahatodvegena ca prakramet, śubhavirajaṃ ca samādhiṃ pratilabheta, tena ca samādhinā mārapāśebhyaḥ parimucyeyuḥ, na ca bhūyo raktacittamutpādayeyuḥ / yā ca tatra strī puruṣaṃ sarāgaṃ nirīkṣeta gurviṇī bhavet, nirīkṣitamātreṇa cobhayo rāgaḥ praśamet / ye garbhavāsairdārakadārikā evaṃ kāyacaitasikaṃ sukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayeyuḥ, tadyathā devāstrayastriṃśā nandanti pramodanti kāyacaitasikaṃ sukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayanti / evaṃrūpaśca tatra buddhakṣetre garbhavāsā dārakadārikāḥ saptarātriṃdivasāni sukhaṃ saṃvedayeyuḥ / tāśca striyo garbhiṇyaḥ evaṃrūpaṃ sukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayeyuḥ, tadyathā dvitīyadhyānasaṃpanno bhikṣuḥ / na ca te sattvā aśucinā garbhamalena kliśyeyuḥ, saptame ca divase paramasugandhena parameṇa ca sukhopadhānena samarpitāḥ pratyājāyeyuḥ / na caiva sā strī duḥkhāṃ pratyanubhaved, ubhau ca puṣkariṇīmavataritvā snātvā ca sā strī evaṃrūpāṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabheta, yayā virāgaśubhaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheta, tena ca samādhinā mārakarmaṇā (
children.translated_text: ) would not engage in sexual bodily contact. And if a man there should give rise to a thought of desire, having gone and looked at a woman with a desirous mind, within a moment the man's desire would be pacified, and with great disenchantment he would proceed, and he would attain the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) of purity and dispassion, and through that <s>samādhi</s> they would be freed from <s>Māra</s>'s snares, and they would not again give rise to a mind of desire. And whatever woman there would look upon a man with desire, she would become pregnant; by the mere act of looking, the desire of both would be pacified. The boys and girls in the womb would experience such bodily and mental happiness as the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods enjoy — they rejoice, are delighted, and experience bodily and mental happiness. And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, boys and girls in the womb would experience such happiness for seven days and nights. And those pregnant women would experience such happiness as a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) endowed with the second <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Those beings would not be afflicted by impurity or womb-filth, and on the seventh day they would be born, delivered with supreme fragrance and supreme comfortable bedding. That woman would not experience suffering, and both would descend into a lotus pond and bathe; and that woman would attain such mindfulness by which she would attain the <s>samādhi</s> of dispassion and purity, and through that <s>samādhi</s>, from <s>Māra</s>'s works (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 170.

children.translated_text: ) she would be freed and would become constantly concentrated. And whatever <s>karma</s> of such a nature had been performed and accumulated in a previous birth, by which one would have to experience the female state for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — through the arising of that <s>samādhi</s>, the female state would be completely and entirely exhausted, and until <s>parinirvāṇa</s> she would not again obtain a female state. And those beings who had performed and accumulated such <s>karma</s> that for <s>kalpas</s> beyond reckoning they would have to be reborn through perpetual womb-birth and experience suffering — if they hear my name when I have attained <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) and generate faith, then, having passed away from there, they would be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and be reborn through womb-birth, and there that <s>karma</s> would be completely and entirely exhausted; until the end of <s>bodhi</s>, those beings would not again be reborn through womb-birth. Those beings whose roots of merit have been planted would be reborn in lotuses; those beings whose roots of merit have not been planted would be reborn through womb-birth. Through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, womankind and womb-birth would [eventually] be perceived [no more]; those beings in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> would be established in unalloyed happiness. And from the <s>sumanā</s> and palm trees, stirred by the breeze, such a delightful sound would issue forth — sounds of '<s>duḥkha</s>' (suffering), 'impermanence,' '<s>anātman</s>' (non-self), and '<s>śūnyatā</s>' (emptiness) would ring forth. And by that sound, there (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 171.

children.text: ) manuṣyā ulkāvatīṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheyustena ca samādhinā te sattvāḥ śūnyatāvabhāsāṃ gambhīrān dharmān avabudhyeyuḥ / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre kāmopasaṃhitaḥ śabdo bhavet / bodhivṛkṣamūlaniṣaṇṇaścāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan muhūrtenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāpnūyāṃ / bodhiprāptasya ca me tatra buddhakṣetre na bhūyaścandrasūryāṇāṃ prabhā prajñāyeta, anyatra kusumasaṃkocanena; evaṃrūpāṃ cāhaṃ prabhāṃ pramuñceyaṃ yena divyena cakṣuṣāprameyāsaṃkhyeyairanyairbuddhakṣetraistiṣṭhato buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyeyaṃ / bodhiprāptaścāhamevaṃrūpeṇa svareṇa dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ yena svareṇa trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ buddhakṣetramāpūrayeyaṃ, ye ca tatra sattvāḥ syuḥ te sarve buddhānusmṛtiṃ pratilabheyuste yena yena gaccheyuḥ caṃkrameyurniṣīdeyurvā parivarteyurvā, te satatasamitaṃ māṃ paśyeyuryathārūpeṣu dharmeṣu dharmasaṃśayā bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ mama darśanamātreṇa vyavalokanamātreṇa ca teṣāṃ saṃśayā vigaccheyuḥ / bodhiprāptasya ca me ye sattvā daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu śrāvakayānikā vā pratyekabuddhayānikā vānuttarayānikā vā mama nāmaṃ vā varṇaṃ va śṛṇuyuḥ, te tataścyavitvā (
children.translated_text: ) the humans would attain a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ulkāvatī</s> (Torch-Bearing), and through that <s>samādhi</s> those beings would comprehend the profound <s>dharmas</s> illuminated by <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no sound connected with sensual desire. And seated at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, in a single moment I would attain supreme perfect awakening. And when I have attained <s>bodhi</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> the light of the sun and moon would no longer be perceived, except by the closing of flowers. And I would emit such a radiance that with the divine eye I would behold the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> abiding in immeasurable and incalculable other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. And having attained <s>bodhi</s>, I would teach the <s>Dharma</s> with such a voice that I would fill the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with my voice, and whatever beings there would be, they would all attain <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Buddha); wherever they go, walk, sit, or turn, they would constantly and perpetually see me. Whatever doubts about <s>dharmas</s> they might have, by the mere seeing of me, by the mere beholding of me, their doubts would vanish. And when I have attained <s>bodhi</s>, whatever beings in immeasurable and incalculable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions — whether followers of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or the supreme vehicle — hear my name or praise, they, having passed away from there (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 172.

children.text: ) mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ / te tatra mama dharmaṃ śrutvā ye śrāvakayānikāste 'ṣṭavimokṣadhyāyino 'rhanto bhaveyuḥ, ye ca pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ te pratyekāṃ bodhimabhigaccheyuḥ, ye ca tatra bodhisattvā mahāyānikāste mat sakāśāddharmaṃ śrutvā gambhīrāṃ samādhikṣāntidhāraṇīṃ ca pratilabheyuḥ, te tatraivāvaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / aprameyaśca me śrāvakasaṅgho bhaved yo na śakyaṃ kenacidgaṇayituṃ anyatra svayaṃ tathāgatena / bodhiprāptaścāhaṃ yena yena gaccheyaṃ yatra yatra ca pādatalena pṛthivīṃ spṛśeyaṃ tatra tatra sahasrapatrāṇi padmāni suvarṇāvabhāsāni prādurbhaveyuḥ, te ca padmāḥ śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvā mama varṇaśabdaṃ ghoṣaṃ niścārayeyuḥ; te ca sattvā mama nāma varṇaṃ yaśaśca śrutvā prītiprasādaprāmodyamutpādayeyuḥ, te prasādajātā mama buddhakṣetra upapattimākāṅkṣeyuḥ, tatra ca tāni kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayeyuḥ, te tataścyavitvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeyuḥ / apagataśramaṇamalaśca me śrāvakasaṅgho bhavet, apagataśramaṇavākyāpagataśramaṇakauṭilyāpagataśramaṇaśāṭhyā apagataparṣā (
children.translated_text: ) would be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. There, having heard my <s>Dharma</s>, those who follow the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle would become meditators on the eight liberations and become <s>arhats</s>; and those who follow the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle would attain individual awakening; and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who follow the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from me, would attain profound <s>samādhi</s>, <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>dhāraṇī</s> — they would become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) there from supreme perfect awakening. And my assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> would be immeasurable, such that no one could reckon it except the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself. And having attained <s>bodhi</s>, wherever I go, wherever I touch the earth with the sole of my foot, there thousand-petalled lotuses of golden radiance would appear; and those lotuses, going to the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid [of Buddhas], would emit the sound of my name and praise. And those beings, having heard my name, praise, and renown, would generate <s>prīti</s> (joy), faith, and delight; and filled with faith, they would aspire to be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and would dedicate those roots of merit there. Having passed away from there, they would be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. And my assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> would be free from the stain of asceticism, free from the speech of asceticism, free from the crookedness of asceticism, free from the deceit of asceticism, free from factions (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 173.

children.text: ) bhaveddharmagurukā na pariṣkāragurukā na lābhasatkāragurukā, anityaduḥkhānātmaśūnyatābhiratā ārabdhavīryā ca sā parṣadbhaveddharmaśravaṇā saṅghaprāgbhārā / ye ca tatrāvaivartikā bodhisattvā bhaveyuste 'nāgatapraviṣṭāḥ smṛtiṃ pratilabheyuste jātivyativṛttā prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ kathayeyuḥ, yāvadbodhiparyantena te dharmā na saṃpramoṣaṃ gaccheyuḥ / yāvadbodhiprāptaścāhaṃ daśamahākalpasahasrāṇi tiṣṭheyaṃ, parinirvṛtasya ca me kalpasahasraṃ saddharmastiṣṭhet" /
children.translated_text: ) — revering the <s>Dharma</s>, not revering material gains, not revering profit and honor. That assembly would delight in impermanence, suffering, non-self, and emptiness, would be of vigorous effort, devoted to hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and inclined toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>. And those <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing) <s>bodhisattvas</s> there would gain mindfulness upon entering the future, having transcended births, they would discourse on topics connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom); until the end of <s>bodhi</s> those <s>dharmas</s> would not be forgotten. And having attained <s>bodhi</s>, I would abide for ten thousand great <s>kalpas</s>, and after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> the <s>Saddharma</s> (True Dharma) would endure for a thousand <s>kalpas</s>."

body.translated_text: <s>Akṣobhya</s> said: "I desire, Venerable Blessed One, such splendid qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>-field that the ground of the entire world would be of gold, level as the palm of a hand, strewn with divine <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, free from gravel and pebbles, free from stones, pillars, boulders, and mountains, soft and pleasant to the touch like <s>kācalindika</s> cotton; when the foot is placed down, it would sink, and when the foot is lifted, it would rise again. And there would be no realms of hell, animal birth, <s>Yama</s>'s world, or the <s>preta</s> domain (

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, pariśuddhaṃ te buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ / bhaviṣyasi tvamakṣobhyānāgate 'dhvani atikrānte hyekasmin gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeya 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye purastimāyāṃ diśi, ataḥ sahasrime buddhakṣetre 'bhiratirnāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati, evaṃrūpayā guṇavyūhayā saṃpannā yathā tvayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / tatra tvaṃ anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, evamevākṣobhyo nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Excellent! Excellent, O good man! The <s>buddhakṣetra</s> you have undertaken is pure. You shall be, in the future age, having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river and entering the second, in the eastern direction, a thousand <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from here — a world-realm called <s>Abhirati</s> (Supreme Delight) shall come to be, endowed with such an array of qualities as you have made your aspiration. There you shall attain supreme perfect awakening; you shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Akṣobhya</s> (Unshakeable), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, and so forth up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>."

body.text: akṣobhya āha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpāśā paripūryeta tatsarvatra lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaparigṛhītā (

children.text: ) ye ca sattvāḥ sattvasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhītāste sarve maitracittā bhavantvavairacittā akaluṣacittāste evaṃrūpaṃ kāyasukhaṃ saṃvedayeyuḥ tadyathāpi nāma daśabhūmisthitasya bodhisattvasya padmasamādhiṃ samāpannasya yenāśayaprahāṇaviśuddhirbhavati, evaṃrūpeṇa sattvāḥ kāyacaitasikena sukhena samārpitā bhavantu / yadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandeta tadā sarvapṛthivī svarṇāvabhāsā bhavatu" / sa ca kulaputra ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandati tadā ca tasmin samaye sarvasattvā evaṃrūpeṇa sukhena samarpitā yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tadā dharaṇī sarvā svarṇāvabhāsā dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: ) and may all beings gathered through the gathering of beings (<s>sattvasaṃgraha</s>) have minds of loving-kindness, minds free from enmity, minds free from impurity; may they experience such bodily happiness as that of a <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding on the tenth stage who has entered the lotus <s>samādhi</s> (<s>padmasamādhi</s>), through which purification of the abandonment of [unwholesome] intentions arises—may beings be endowed with such bodily and mental happiness. And when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with the fivefold prostration, may the entire earth become radiant with gold." And when, O son of good family, he bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with the fivefold prostration, then at that time the entire—

"Arise, O one of supreme wisdom, <s>Akṣobhya</s>! With the wheel established in the palm of your hand, O supreme wheel-turner,

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo daśamaṃ rājaputraṃ himaṇiṃ nāmāmantrayate sma / peyālaṃ himaṇī rājaputra evaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānamakārṣīt tadyathākṣobhyena kṛtaṃ / "yadi me bhadanta bhagavan nevaṃrūpāśā paripūryeta tatsarvasattvā buddhālaṃbanamanaskāraṃ pratilabhantu / sarveṣāṃ coragasāracandanagandho haste prādurbhavatu, te ca sarve taṃ gandhaṃ buddhavigraheṣu pariṇāmayantu" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the tenth prince named <s>Himaṇi</s>. [The passage is abbreviated:] Prince <s>Himaṇi</s> made an aspiration of such a kind as <s>Akṣobhya</s> had made: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then may all beings attain mindfulness focused on the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhālaṃbanamanaskāra</s>). And may the fragrance of <s>uragasāra</s> (serpent-heart) sandalwood appear in the hands of all, and may they all direct that fragrance toward the forms of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: bhagavān āha - "sādhu sādhu kulaputra, udāraṃ te praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, yacca tvayā sarvasattvā uragasāracandanahastā sthāpitā buddhamanaskāraścāśayenotpāditaḥ, tena tvaṃ kulaputra gandhahastirnāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ gandhahaste 'tikrāntānāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ avaśiṣṭe dvitīye nadīgaṅgāvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'kṣobhye tathāgate 'rhati samyaksaṃbuddhe parinirvṛte saddharme 'ntarhite saptame dviase tvaṃ gandhahaste tatra lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, suvarṇapuṣpo nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Excellent! Excellent, O son of good family! Sublime is the aspiration you have made. Since you have established all beings with hands [holding] <s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood and have generated mindfulness of the <s>Buddha</s> through aspiration, therefore, O son of good family, let your name be <s>Gandhahasti</s> (Fragrant Elephant). You, <s>Gandhahasti</s>, having passed beyond incalculable aeons equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remainder of the second incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, after <s>Akṣobhya</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared, on the seventh day, you, <s>Gandhahasti</s>, in that world-realm shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment; <s>Suvarṇa</s>—

body.text: gandhahastirapyāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpāśā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 176.

children.text: ) paripūryeta tadyadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandeyaṃ tadā sarvasminnārāme campakapuṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣatu" / yadā khalu kulaputra gandhahastirbodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandati tadā sarvasminnārāme campakapuṣpavarṣamabhiprāvarṣat /
children.translated_text: ) should be fulfilled, then when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with the fivefold prostration, may a rain of <s>campaka</s> flowers fall throughout the entire grove." And when, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gandhahasti</s> bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with the fivefold prostration, then throughout the entire grove a rain of <s>campaka</s> flowers fell.

body.translated_text: <s>Gandhahasti</s> also said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine—

children.translated_text: <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said:
"Arise, O one of supreme qualities! With fragrant mind, these excellent <s>campaka</s> flowers have rained down.

children.text: darśaya śubhapatha varapraṇītaṃ sthāpaya bahujagamabhaye pāre" //
children.translated_text: Show the beautiful and supreme, exalted path; establish the many beings safely on the further shore."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇa ekādaśamaṃ rājaputraṃ siṃhaṃ nāmāmantrayāmāsa / peyālaṃ, yathā gandhahastinā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, ratnagarbhāya tathāgatāya ratnamayaṃ dhvajaṃ niryātitaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the eleventh prince named <s>Siṃha</s>. [The passage is abbreviated:] just as <s>Gandhahasti</s> had made his aspiration, [<s>Siṃha</s>] offered a jeweled banner (<s>dhvaja</s>) to <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, ratnaketurnāma bhavasva, bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ ratnaketo 'nāgate (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 177.

children.text: ) 'dhvani atikrānte gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'vaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye tatrābhiratyāṃ lokadhātau parinirvṛte svarṇapuṣpe tathāgate tasya ca saddharme 'ntarhite trayāṇāṃ antarakalpānāmatyayena tadbuddhakṣetraṃ jayasomaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati, tatra tvamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase nāgavinarditeśvaraghoṣo nāma bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān / evaṃrūpaṃ te buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati buddhakṣetre guṇavyūhena yathākṣobhyasya tathāgatasya" /
children.translated_text: ) having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remainder of the second incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the world-realm <s>Abhirati</s>, after <s>Suvarṇapuṣpa</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared, after the passage of three intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be called <s>Jayasoma</s>, and there you shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment. You shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nāgavinarditeśvaraghoṣa</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. And your <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be such in its array of qualities as that of <s>Akṣobhya</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.translated_text: <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said: "Excellent! Excellent, O good man! Let your name be <s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel-Banner). You, <s>Ratnaketu</s>, in the future age—

body.text: ratnaketurāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpāśā paripūryeta tadyadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pādau vande tadā sarvasattvā evaṃrūpāṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabheyuḥ, yathā bodhisattvā ye mahābodhiṃ saṃprasthitāḥ sarvasattvānāmarthāya karuṇāyamānāḥ saṃbodhau prasthitā na nivarteyuḥ" / evameva kulaputra ratnaketurbodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pādau vanditvā, evameva sattvā evaṃrūpāṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabdhavanto yaduta karuṇācittāḥ sarvasattvāḥ sthāpitāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnaketu</s> said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One, may all beings attain such mindfulness as that of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have set out for great enlightenment—who, out of compassion for all beings, having set out for enlightenment, do not turn back." And just so, O son of good family, when the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnaketu</s> bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, just so did beings attain such mindfulness—that is, all beings were established with minds of compassion.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato ratnaketuṃ bodhisattvamāha -

children.text: "uttiṣṭha dhairya sumate paramarūpa sattvahetu sudṛḍhakṛta pratijñā /
children.translated_text: "Arise, O steadfast one of excellent wisdom, of supreme form! For the sake of beings you have made a firm resolve.

children.text: sthāpayasi bahujana virajacitte bhaviṣyase naravaro pravarabuddhaḥ" //
children.translated_text: You establish the many in a mind free from defilement—you, O best of men, shall be a supreme <s>Buddha</s>."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnaketu</s>:

body.text: evaṃ peyālaṃ, mārdavapūrvaṃgamaiḥ pañcabhi rājaputraśatairevaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, kṛtvaivaṃrūpā buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ parigṛhītā yathā gaganamudreṇa bodhisattvena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāśca parigṛhītāḥ / sarve ca ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāḥ / "evamevaikakāle 'nyonyeṣu lokadhātuṣvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim spṛśiṣyatha" /
body.translated_text: Thus [the passage is abbreviated]: five hundred princes led by <s>Mārdava</s> made aspirations of such a kind, and having made them, chose arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities such as the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> had chosen. And all were given prophecy by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment: "Thus, at one and the same time, in your respective world-realms, you shall all attain supreme perfect enlightenment."

body.text: apare catvāraḥ śatā rājaputrāṇāṃ yairevaṃrūpaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ yathā vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsena, te 'pi sarve ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau anyonyeṣu lokadhātuṣu /
body.translated_text: And four hundred other princes chose <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of such a kind as <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa</s> [had chosen]. They too were all given prophecy by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment, in their respective world-realms.

body.text: aparairekonanavatibhī rājaputrairevaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, evaṃrūpaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 179.
) as <s>Samantabhadra</s> [had chosen].

body.translated_text: And ninety-one other princes made aspirations of such a kind and chose <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of such a kind—

body.text: sarvaiścaturaśītibhiḥ koṭṭarājasahasraiḥ pṛthakpṛthagviśiṣṭaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, pṛthakpṛthaśca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / sarve ca ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, anyonyeṣu lokadhātuṣvekakāle bodhiṃ prāpsyanti /
body.translated_text: All eighty-four thousand vassal kings (<s>koṭṭarāja</s>) each made distinct aspirations and each chose distinct arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities. And all were given prophecy by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment; they shall all attain enlightenment at one and the same time in their respective world-realms.

body.text: evameva tribhiḥ prāṇakoṭibhiḥ pṛthakpṛthak praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, pṛthakpṛthaśca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāśca parigṛhītāḥ / sarve ca ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena vyākṛtāanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, "evameva yūyamapyekakāle 'nyonyeṣu lokadhātuṣvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyadhve" //
body.translated_text: Likewise, three <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of beings each made distinct aspirations and each chose distinct arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities. And all were given prophecy by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment: "Thus you too, at one and the same time, in your respective world-realms, shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment."

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyāśītiputrā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya bhrātaraḥ, teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ samudreśvarabhuvirnāma māṇavaḥ / atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaḥ samudreśvarabhuviṃ māṇavaṃ āmantrayāmāsa / "pratigṛhāṇa tvaṃ māṇava pariśuddhāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ" / samudreśvarabhuvirmāṇavāha - (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 180.

children.text: ) "tvaṃ tāvattāta prathamataraṃ siṃhanādaṃ nadasva" / samudrareṇurāha - " tvaṃ tāvat putra praṇidhānaṃ kuruṣva, paścādahaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kariṣye" / sa āha - "kiṃ tāvat pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pratigṛhṇāmyutāhosvidapariśuddhaṃ?" / agrapurohita āha - "ye mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatā bodhisattvāste kliṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇanti, kliṣṭāśayāṃ viparītadṛṣṭikāṃ sattvānvaineyān pratigṛhṇanti / yathā punastvaṃ māṇava svaṃ jāniṣe" /
children.translated_text: ) "You first, father, roar the lion's roar (<s>siṃhanāda</s>)." <s>Samudrareṇu</s> said: "You first, son, make your aspiration; afterwards I shall make mine." He said: "Should I then accept a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, or an impure one?" The chief priest replied: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are endowed with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) accept a defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and accept as their disciples beings of defiled dispositions and perverted views. But you, young man, should decide as you know yourself."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> had eighty sons who were the brothers of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. The eldest among them was a young man (<s>māṇava</s>) named <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s>. Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s> addressed the young man <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s>: "Accept, O young man, the purified array of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities." The young man <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s> said—

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudreśvarabhuvirmāṇavako yena ratnagarbhas tathāgatastenopasamakrāmadupasaṃkramya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purataḥ sthitvaivamāha - "evamahaṃ bhadanta bhagavannanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimākāṅkṣāmi, aśītivarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ pravarāṃ bodhiṃ spṛśeyaṃ / yathaitarhi bhagavan sattvā mandarāgā mandadveṣā mandamohā udvignāśayāḥ saṃsāre bhayadoṣadarśinastathā tatra buddhakṣetre sattvā bhaveyuḥ, yatrāhamabhisaṃbuddheyaṃ, te ca mamāntike pravrajeyuḥ, tribhiśca yānairahaṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / yadi bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tad vyākarotu māṃ bhagavānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the young man <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s> approached <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, and having approached, standing before <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, spoke thus: "Thus, O venerable Blessed One, I aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment. Among a people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, may I attain supreme enlightenment. Just as, O Blessed One, beings now have little passion, little hatred, little delusion, and dispositions inclined to renunciation, seeing the fear and faults in <s>saṃsāra</s>—so may beings be in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> where I shall attain enlightenment; and they should go forth under me, and by the three vehicles (<s>yāna</s>) I shall—

body.text: ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇavānāgate 'dhvani atikrānta ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye utpalasantīraṇe kalpe cāturdvīpikā baliṣṭhā nāma bhaviṣyati, imaṃ buddhakṣetramaśītivarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ bodhimabhiprapsyasi, ratnakūṭo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said: "You, young man, in the future age, having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> and having entered the second incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Utpalasantīraṇa</s>, there will be a four-continent world-system called <s>Baliṣṭhā</s>. In this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, among a people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, you shall attain enlightenment. You shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> (Jewel-Peak), and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One."

body.text: sa āha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tadiha sarvatrārāme lohitamuktiḥ pravarṣatu, sarvavṛkṣebhyaśca pañcāṅgikaṃ tūryaṃ niścaratu" / yadā ca kulaputra samudreśvarabhuvirmāṇavako ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vandati tadā sarvatrārāme lohitamuktimayavarṣaṃ pravarṣitaṃ, sarvavṛkṣebhyaśca pañcāṅgikaṃ tūryaṃ niścaritaṃ /
body.translated_text: He said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then may red pearls (<s>lohitamukti</s>) rain down throughout the entire grove, and may the sound of a five-part orchestra (<s>pañcāṅgikatūrya</s>) issue from all the trees." And when, O son of good family, the young man <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s> bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with the fivefold prostration, then throughout the entire grove a rain of red pearls fell, and from all the trees the sound of a five-part orchestra issued forth.

children.translated_text: <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said:
"Arise, O one of supreme strength, treasury of inexhaustible wisdom, compassionate toward beings, seeking their welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness!

children.text: abhiprāya tubhya paripūryatu śuddha sattvāna arthakaru bheṣyasi buddha loke" //
children.translated_text: May your aspiration be fulfilled for the benefit of purified beings—you shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world."

body.text: dvitīyaśca brāhmaṇasya putraḥ saṃbhavo nāma, sa evaṃ vadati yathā samudreśvarabhuviḥ / ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "tvamapi māṇavotpalasantīraṇe kalpo 'syāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau baliṣṭhe buddhakṣetre vardhamānāśītivarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ vairocanakusumo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: The second son of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, named <s>Saṃbhava</s>, spoke in the same way as <s>Samudreśvarabhūvi</s>. <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said: "You too, young man, in the <s>kalpa</s> <s>Utpalasantīraṇa</s>, in this four-continent world-realm <s>Baliṣṭhā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, among a growing people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vairocanakusuma</s> (Sun-Blossom), and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One."

body.text: peyālaṃ, tṛtīyastvāha - "dvivarṣasahasrasya jyotigandho nāma bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān" / vyākaraṇaṃ peyālaṃ, evaṃ sumanastathāgataḥ śailarājā saṃvṛtalocano brahmottaro jambūcchāyaḥ pūrṇamuttaro ratnaśailaḥ samudragarbho nārāyaṇaḥ śikhī kanakamunirmunīndraḥ kauṇḍinyaḥ siṃhavikramo jñānadhvajo buddhaśravo 'parājito vikasitojjayo hiteṣī prajñāvabhāso mahendraḥ śāntaprajñākaro nando nyagrodharājaḥ kanakalocanaḥ sahitaḥ sūryanandiḥ ratnaśikhī sumetro brahmaḥ sundo brahmarṣabhaḥ praṇādo dharmacandraḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 183.

children.text: ) arthadarśī yaśonandī yaśottaraḥ abhirūpaḥ sugandhaścaturaḥ pravaralocanaḥ sunijastaḥ sārthavrataḥ sumanoratho varaprajñaḥ kanakadhvajaḥ sunetro devaśuddhaḥ śuddhodanaḥ sudarśanaḥ virūḍhadhvajo virūpākṣo brahmasvaraḥ śrīsaṃbhavaḥ śrīmahāvirajo maṇibhadraḥ mārīciḥ śākyamunirghoṣeśvaraḥ satyasaṃbhavaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃbhavapuṣpaḥ sukusumaḥ akṣobhyaḥ sūryagarbho ratīśvaro nāgadanto vajraprabhāsaḥ kīrtirājā vyāghraraśmiḥ sanetyajñānasaṃbhavaḥ gandhasvaraḥ sālendraḥ nārāyaṇagataḥ jyotigarbhaḥ / yastu tatra kulaputra sarvapaścimakaḥ purohitaputraḥ vigatabhyasaṃtāpo nāma, sa ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purutaḥ sthitvāha / "ime bhadanta bhagavannekonāśītirmāṇavakāḥ sarve vyākṛtā utpalasaṃtīraṇe kalpe vardhamānadvaye 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / utpādayāmyahaṃ bhagavannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ, kṣīyamāṇe bhadanta bhagavannutpalasaṃtīraṇe (
children.translated_text: ) <s>Arthadarśin</s>, <s>Yaśonandin</s>, <s>Yaśottara</s>, <s>Abhirūpa</s>, <s>Sugandha</s>, <s>Catura</s>, <s>Pravaralocana</s>, <s>Sunijasta</s>, <s>Sārthavrata</s>, <s>Sumanoratha</s>, <s>Varaprajña</s>, <s>Kanakadhvaja</s>, <s>Sunetra</s>, <s>Devaśuddha</s>, <s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Virūḍhadhvaja</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Brahmasvara</s>, <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s>, <s>Śrīmahāviraja</s>, <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, <s>Mārīci</s>, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Ghoṣeśvara</s>, <s>Satyasaṃbhava</s>, <s>Śreṣṭha</s>, <s>Saṃbhavapuṣpa</s>, <s>Sukusuma</s>, <s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, <s>Ratīśvara</s>, <s>Nāgadanta</s>, <s>Vajraprabhāsa</s>, <s>Kīrtirāja</s>, <s>Vyāghraraśmi</s>, <s>Sanetyajñānasaṃbhava</s>, <s>Gandhasvara</s>, <s>Sālendra</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇagata</s>, <s>Jyotigarbha</s>. And the one who—

children.text: ) taṃ ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputrānāgate 'dhvani anupraviṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye ratnaprabhāse kalpe ratnasañcayaṃ nāma buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati, asmiṃ cāturdvīpike ratnacchatrābhyudgataraśmirbhaviṣyasi tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavān" / atha kulaputra jyotikṣabho bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā nipapāta /
children.translated_text: ) the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said to him: "You, O son of good family, in a future time, having entered a second incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, in the <s>Ratnaprabhāsa</s> <s>kalpa</s>, there shall be a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> named <s>Ratnasañcaya</s> ('Jewel Collection'), and in this four-continent world you shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnacchatrābhyudgataraśmi</s> ('Rays Risen from a Jewel Parasol'), and so on up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One." Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Jyotikṣabhaka</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> in the five-fold prostration.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the young man <s>Jyotikṣabhaka</s> was filled with supreme delight; (

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said:
"Arise, O one free from dust, O pure being! Prophesied are many <s>koṭis</s> of beings.

children.text: bhaviṣyasi varaśuddhamārgaḥ bodhaye bhaviṣyasi varajinaḥ sattvanāyakaḥ" //
children.translated_text: You shall become the supreme pure path, and you shall become a supreme <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), a leader of beings."

body.text: peyālaṃ, sahasro māṇavakānāṃ trayaḥ koṭyo māṇavakānāṃ yairasmin buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 193.

children.text: ) praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ; sarve ca te ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena vyākṛtāḥ, yāvadvipaśyī śikhī viśvabhuvaḥ paścimā buddhā babhūvuḥ / sarve māṇavakā vyākṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) made their vows; and all of them were prophesied by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, up to <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, and <s>Viśvabhu</s> who were the last <s>Buddhas</s>. All the young men were prophesied.

body.translated_text: Abbreviated — a thousand young men, three <s>koṭis</s> of young men, who in this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> regarding supreme perfect awakening (

body.text: tatra sahasravedapāṭhakānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ yasteṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ gurusaṃmato vāyuviṣṇurnāma / sa āha - "ahaṃ punaḥ pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ spṛśyeyaṃ / tīvrarāgānāṃ tīvradveṣāṇāṃ tīvramohānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ" /
body.translated_text: Among those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who were reciters of a thousand <s>Vedas</s>, there was their eldest, honored as teacher, named <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s>. He said: "I would attain supreme perfect awakening in a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the five degenerations. I would teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings of intense passion, intense hatred, and intense delusion."

body.text: jyotipālo nāma māṇavakaḥ / sa āha - "kimarthavaśaṃ samanupaśyamāno 'yaṃ bho upādhyāya vāyuviṣṇuḥ pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre praṇidadhāti?" / purohita āha - "sakalamahākaruṇāsamanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre bodhimanuprāpnoti; atrāṇānāmaparāyaṇānāṃ kleśairupadrutānāṃ dṛṣṭivyasanaprāptānāṃ sattvānāmarthakaro bhavati; trāṇam parāyaṇaṃ bhavati; janmasamudrācca sattvān uttārayati; samyagdṛṣṭyāṃ ca sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayati; nirvāṇāmṛtarasena sattvān saṃtarpayati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya mahākaruṇā dṛśyata ye pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre praṇidadhanti" /
body.translated_text: a student named <s>Jyotipāla</s>. He said: "Seeing what purpose, O teacher, does this <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> make his aspiration in a <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five defilements?" The chief priest said: "A <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with complete great compassion attains awakening in a <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five defilements. He becomes a benefactor to beings who are without protection, without recourse, afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), and fallen into the calamity of wrong views; he becomes their protector, their refuge. He ferries beings across the ocean of birth, establishes them in right view, and satisfies them with the nectar-taste of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This is the great compassion of a <s>bodhisattva</s> that is seen in those who make their aspiration in a <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five defilements."

body.text: ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ vāyuviṣṇo atikrāntānāmekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmasaṃkhyeyānāmavaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye purastimāyāṃ diśāyāṃ buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramitvā tatra kaṣāyadhvaja nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati / tatra tvaṃ satpuruṣānutarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, śālendrarājo nāma tathāgato bhavisyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān" / vāyuviṣṇurāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta yadāhaṃ bhagavataḥ pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vande tadā me bhagavān chatapuṇyalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtāvubhau caraṇau mūrdhni sthāpayatu" /
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "You, <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s>, in the future, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, passing beyond <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the eastern direction from this <s>Buddha</s>-field, there shall be a world-realm called <s>Kaṣāyadhvaja</s> (Banner of Defilements). There, O good man, you shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śālendrarāja</s> (King, Lord of Śāla Trees), up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One." <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, such an aspiration of mine is to be fulfilled, then when I make prostration at the Blessed One's feet with the five-point [contact], may the Blessed One place both of his feet, adorned with the marks of a hundred merits, upon my head."

children.text: yadā kulaputra vāyuviṣṇurmāṇavo bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirasā nipapāta tadā ratnagarbhastathāgataḥ ubhau caraṇau vāyuviṣṇorbodhisattvasya mūrdhni sthāpayitvāha -
children.translated_text: When, O son of good family, the student <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> fell at the Blessed One's feet with his head, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> placed both feet upon the head of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> and said:
"Arise, O compassionate one of sharp wisdom — practice the conduct for the sake of supreme awakening!
Cut, O steadfast one, the firm bonds of affliction — you shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate and beneficent!"

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra jyotipālo māṇavako ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthvyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpyāha - "utpādayāmyahaṃ bhadanta bhagavannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ / asmin buddhakṣetre rāgadveṣamohasabhāgacittānāmavyavasthitakuśalākuśalāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ ' / ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - 'atikrāntānāṃ ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ avaśiṣṭe dvitīye sahā nāmāyaṃ lokadhāturbhaviṣyati / kena kāreṇena sahetyucyate? ' sahāste sattvā rāgasya sahāste dveṣasya sahāste mohasya sahāste kleśabandhanānāṃ, tena kāreṇena sā lokadhātuḥ sahetyucyate / tatra sahāyāṃ lokadhātau bhadrako nāma bhaviṣyati mahākalpaḥ / kena kāraṇenocyate bhadraka iti? / bhadrake mahākalpe rāgadveṣamohacaritānāṃ sattvānāṃ sahasraṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmutpatsyate / tvamapi satpuruṣānupraviṣṭe bhadrake mahākalpe catvāriṃśadvarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 196.

children.text: ) prajāyāṃ sarvaprathamamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, krakutsando nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavāṃstribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayiṣyasi, gaṇanātikrāntān sattvān saṃsāranadyāmuhyamānānuttārayiṣyasi, nirvāṇapāre ca sthāpayiṣyasi ' / atha khalu kulaputra jyotipālo bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'tikramya tasthau /
children.translated_text: ) lifespan, shall be the very first to attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Krakucchanda</s>, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. You shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> by means of the three vehicles and shall ferry beings beyond counting who are drowning in the river of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), and establish them on the far shore of <s>nirvāṇa</s>." Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Jyotipāla</s>, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with his head in the five-point [prostration], passed to one side and stood there.

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the student <s>Jyotipāla</s>, setting his right knee upon the ground before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, said: "I generate, O venerable Blessed One, the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). In this <s>Buddha</s>-field, among people whose lifespan is forty thousand years, for beings whose minds partake of attachment, aversion, and delusion, whose wholesome and unwholesome dispositions are unstable, may I attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>." The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "After the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second, this world-realm shall be called <s>Sahā</s>. For what reason is it called <s>Sahā</s> (Endurance)? Those beings endure attachment, endure aversion, endure delusion, endure the bonds of affliction — for that reason the world-realm is called <s>Sahā</s>. There, in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, there shall be a great <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) called <s>Bhadra</s> (Fortunate). For what reason is it called <s>Bhadra</s>? In the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, for beings of attachment, aversion, and delusion, a thousand greatly compassionate <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones shall arise. You too, O good man, having entered the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, among people of forty thousand years' (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra dvitīyastumbururnāma māṇavako ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purato niṣaṇṇaḥ / "bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan krakutsandasya tathāgatasyānusaṃdhau triṃsadvarṣasahasrāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ buddho loke" / ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇavakātikrānta ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'vaśiṣṭe dvitīye nadigaṅgāvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye sahe buddhakṣetre 'nupraviṣṭe bhadrakalpe krakutsandasya tathāgatasyānusaṃdhau triṃśadvarṣasāhasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ kanakamunirnāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi arhan samyaksaṃbuddho vighuṣṭaśabdo lokasya" / sa bhagavataḥ sakāśādvyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 197.

children.text: ) ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyābhimukhamāsthāt, puṣpairbhagavataḥ kāyamavakiramāṇaḥ prañjalibhūto bhagavantaṃ gāthābhistuṣṭhāva /
children.translated_text: ) he bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with his head, circumambulated him, and stood facing the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, scattering flowers over the Blessed One's body, and with palms joined, praised the Blessed One with these verses:

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the second student, named <s>Tumburu</s>, sat before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> [and said]: "May I become, O venerable Blessed One, a <s>Buddha</s> in the world in the succession of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, among people whose lifespan is thirty thousand years." The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "You, O student, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, having entered the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, in the succession of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, among people of thirty thousand years' lifespan, you shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kanakamuni</s> (Golden Sage), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, of widely proclaimed fame." Having heard the prophecy from the Blessed One, (

children.text: "susahita sumudita sumadhura vacanā askhalita aluḍita akaluṣa vimalā /
children.translated_text: "Well-composed, well-delighted, with sweet words, unfailing, unperturbed, untainted, and stainless,

children.text: abhiśaya atiyati atimati matimā ṛṣivara jvala tuma munivara vṛṣabhī //
children.translated_text: Surpassing, transcendent in discipline, transcendent in wisdom, O wise one, supreme among sages, shine forth, O bull among the silent sages!

children.text: bahu tuma guṇadada guṇaśata bharitā sukhakara munivara naramanu namitā /
