children.translated_text: You, bestower of many virtues, filled with hundreds of qualities, bringer of happiness, supreme sage, bowed to by human minds,

children.text: na hi anyu sattva vidyati tvayi samu tṛbhave tvayi adyi bahusattva bodhimārgi vyākṛtā" //
children.translated_text: No other being in the three realms is found equal to you — today many beings have been prophesied by you on the path to awakening!"

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra viśvagupto nāma māṇavako ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purataḥ saptaratnamayaṃ pīṭhaṃ sthāpayitvā śatasahasramūlyena prajñapanena prajñapya, tatra pīṭhe suvarṇapātraṃ sthāpayitvā saptaratnaparipūrṇasuvarṇamayaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ saptaratnamayā yaṣṭirbuddhapramukhe bhikṣusaṅghe niyojitavān / sa āha - "bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ bhadanta bhagavannanāgate 'dhvanyatikrānta ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'vaśiṣṭe dvitīye tasmiṃśca bhadrakalpe tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpanno hīyamāne āyuṣi utpanne kaliyuganimitte tīvrarāgadveṣamohamānerṣyāmātsaryaparyutthitānāṃ sattvānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyakalyāṇamitrasanniśritānāṃ sattvānāmakuśalamūlaparyutthitacittānāṃ kuśalamūlaparihīṇacittānāṃ samyagdṛṣṭivivarjitacittānāṃ mithyājīvākuśalacittānāṃ, parinirvṛte kanakamunau tathāgate saddharme 'ntarhite 'ndhe loke 'nāyake viṃśativarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ ahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ" /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, a student named <s>Viśvagupta</s>, having placed before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> a seat made of the seven jewels, furnishing it with a covering worth a hundred thousand [coins], and having placed upon that seat a golden vessel and a golden ewer filled with the seven jewels and a staff made of the seven jewels, offered them to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. He said: "May I become, O venerable Blessed One, in the future, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second, in that <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, when lifespans are declining, when the signs of the <s>kaliyuga</s> (age of strife) have appeared, among beings beset by intense attachment, aversion, delusion, pride, jealousy, and miserliness, among beings who rely on wrong views and unwholesome friends, whose minds are overwhelmed by unwholesome roots, whose minds have lost their roots of merit, whose minds lack right view, whose minds are engaged in wrong livelihood and unwholesomeness — after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kanakamuni</s> and the disappearance of the <s>Saddharma</s>, in a blind world without a guide, among people whose lifespan is twenty thousand years, may I attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>."

body.text: tasya kulaputra viśvaguptasya brāhmaṇasya ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "sādhu sādhu brāhmaṇa mahāvidvān jñānasamanvāgataḥ, tvaṃ satpuruṣotpanne kaliyuganimitte (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 199.

children.text: ) yāvadviṃśativarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāmandhe loke 'nāyake praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / tena tvaṃ satpuruṣa vidvagañjakaruṇāśrayo nāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ vidvagañjakaruṇāśrayānāgate 'dhvanyatikrāntānāmekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmavaśiṣṭe dvitīye sahāyāṃ lokadhātau anupraviṣṭe bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
children.translated_text: ) among people of twenty thousand years' lifespan, in a blind world without a guide, have made your aspiration. Therefore, O good man, you shall be called <s>Vidvagañjakaruṇāśraya</s> (Refuge of Compassion, Treasury of Learning). You, <s>Vidvagañjakaruṇāśraya</s>, in the future, after the passage of a first incalculable <s>aeon</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the remaining second, in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, having entered the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, among people of twenty thousand years' lifespan, you shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One."

body.translated_text: To that student <s>Viśvagupta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "Excellent, excellent, O brahmin of great learning, endowed with wisdom! You, O good man, when the signs of the <s>kaliyuga</s> have appeared, (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra vidvagañjakaruṇāśrayo bodhisattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt, ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ puṣpamālyagandhacūrṇairavakirati, ābhiśca gāthābhirabhistavamānaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vidvagañjakaruṇāśraya</s>, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with his head in the five-point [prostration], stood at one side, scattering flowers, garlands, fragrances, and incense powders upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and praising him with these verses:

children.translated_text: "O supreme among humans, benefactor, delighter, progenitor,
Of smiling countenance, joyful, with sweet words,
Skilled in knowing the appropriate occasion, beneficent, bearer of the ten powers, supreme,
Perfected in wisdom, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), liberation, and the <s>pāramitās</s> — homage to you, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)!
Having practiced much conduct, with radiant face, prophesied for incomparable awakening,

children.text: tvayā bahubodhisattvanayutā vandāma te naravarā sugatā" /
children.translated_text: By you many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> [have been prophesied] — we bow to you, O supreme among humans, O <s>Sugata</s>!"
Thus.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇaścaturthaṃ vimalavaiśāyanaṃ māṇavakaṃ saṃcodayāṃ āsa / atha khalu kulaputra vimalavaiśāyano māṇavako ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purataḥ sthitvāha - "evamevāhamasmin bhadrake kalpe bodhimākāṅkṣāmi, na ca kevalamevaṃrūpaṃ kaliyuge / yathā kāśyapasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya daśavarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ dānadamaparikṣīṇāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ saptadhanavirahitānāṃ akalyāṇamitre śāstṛsaṃjñāpratipannacittā bhavanti, anarthikāstribhiḥ puṇyakriyāvastubhirbhavanti, virahitāstribhiḥ sucaritairudyuktāstriṣu duṣcariteṣu kleśāndhakāravyākulacittā bhavanti, anarthikāstribhiryānairna śakyaṃ tatkālaṃ kenacidbodhicaryāṃ niṣpādayituṃ / kiṃ punarvarṣasahasrikāyāṃ; yāvatte (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 201.

children.text: ) sattvā varṣaśatāyuṣkā bhavanti, tatkālaṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlasya nāsti nāma, kiṃ punaḥ kuśalamūlacaryā; tāvat pañcakaṣāye loke hāyamānā daśavarṣāyuṣkā bhavanti, śastrāntarakalpe pratyupasthite tatkālamahaṃ devebhyo 'vatīrya sattvān paritrāyeyaṃ, akuśalaṃ riñcitvā kuśale niyojayeyaṃ, yāvaddaśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, kleśāṃśca sattvānāṃ kuśalebhiḥ karmapathebhiḥ pariśodhayeyaṃ, pañcakaṣāyaṃ ca parihāyeyaṃ / yāvadaśītivarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ ahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, mandarāgadveṣamohānāṃ avidyerṣyāmatsariṇāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, triṣu ca yāneṣu saṃniyojayeyaṃ / yadi me bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta vyākarotu māṃ bhadanta bhagavannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / yadāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ na lapsyāmi, na śrāvakabhūmiṃ prārthayāmi na ca pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ yena yānena śīghraṃ saṃsārādvimucyāmi" /
children.translated_text: ) beings have lifespans of a hundred years — at that time, there is not even the name of roots of merit among beings, how much less the practice of roots of merit! And when, in a world of the five defilements, lifespans have declined to ten years and the <s>śastrāntarakalpa</s> (age of weapons) is at hand, at that time may I descend from the gods and protect beings, causing them to abandon the unwholesome and engage in the wholesome, establishing beings in the ten wholesome courses of action, purifying the afflictions of beings through the wholesome courses of action, and overcoming the five defilements. Until, among people of eighty thousand years' lifespan, may I attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings of mild attachment, aversion, and delusion, of ignorance, jealousy, and miserliness, and may I yoke them to the three vehicles. If, O Blessed One, such an aspiration of mine is to be fulfilled, may the venerable Blessed One prophesy me for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And if, O venerable Blessed One, I do not receive such a prophecy, I shall not seek the <s>śrāvaka</s>-stage, nor the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-stage, nor any vehicle by which I might quickly be liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s> urged the fourth student, <s>Vimalavaiśāyana</s>. Then, O son of good family, the student <s>Vimalavaiśāyana</s>, standing before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, said: "Likewise do I aspire for awakening in this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, and not merely in such a <s>kaliyuga</s>. After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, among people of ten thousand years' lifespan, among beings whose disposition toward generosity and self-discipline has been exhausted, who are bereft of the seven treasures, whose minds regard unwholesome friends as teachers, who take no interest in the three bases of meritorious action, who are bereft of the three kinds of good conduct, who are devoted to the three kinds of bad conduct, whose minds are bewildered by the darkness of affliction, who take no interest in the three vehicles — at such a time no one is able to accomplish the conduct of awakening. How much less among those of one thousand years' lifespan! Until those (

body.text: ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "catvārīmāni brāhmaṇa bodhisattvānāṃ kuśīdavastūni; yaiḥ kuśīdavastubhiḥ samanvāgatā ekatyā bodhisattvā dīrghasaṃsāralābhino dṛṣṭiprapāte saṃsāracārake duḥkhānyanubhavanti, na ca kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimanuprāpnuvanti / katamāni catvāri? / ihaikatyo bodhisattvo hīnācāro bhavati, hīnasahāyaḥ, hīnaparityāgaḥ, hīnapraṇidhiḥ / kathaṃ ca bodhisattvo hīnācāro bhavati? ihaikatyo duḥśīlo bhavati, kāyavāṅmanasā cāsaṃvṛtacārī bhavati, śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃsargacārī bhavati, na ca sarvaparityāgī na sarvatraparityāgī bhavati, devamanuṣyaśrīsukhābhilāṣī dānaṃ dadāti, na cādhyāśayena buddhakṣetraguṇavyuhān pratigṛhṇāti vaineyamanavekṣya praṇidhānaṃ pratigṛhṇāti / ebhiścaturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ kuśīdo bodhisattvaḥ ciraṃ saṃsāracārake duḥkhamanubhavati, na ca kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimanuprāpnoti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "There are, O brahmin, four causes of slothfulness for <s>bodhisattvas</s>; endowed with these causes of slothfulness, certain <s>bodhisattvas</s> gain long <s>saṃsāra</s>, fall into the abyss of wrong views, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> experiencing suffering, and do not quickly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. What are the four? Here, a certain <s>bodhisattva</s> is of inferior conduct, of inferior companions, of inferior renunciation, and of inferior aspiration. And how is a <s>bodhisattva</s> of inferior conduct? Here, a certain one is immoral, unrestrained in body, speech, and mind in conduct, keeps company with those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, is not one who renounces all, not one who renounces everywhere; gives gifts with desire for divine and human fortune and happiness; does not accept the array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities with deep intention; and accepts aspirations without examining those to be trained. Endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s>, a slothful <s>bodhisattva</s> experiences suffering for a long time wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> and does not quickly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text: caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / katamaiścaturbhiḥ? śīlavān bhavati kāyavāṅmanaḥ saṃvṛtacārī, mahāyānasaṃprasthitaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃsargacārī bhavati, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 203.

children.text: ) sarvaparityāgī sarvatraparityāgī sattvānāṃ duḥkhaparimocanārthaṃ karuṇācittotpādaṃ dadāti, adhyāśayena buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhānvaineyaṃ avekṣya praṇidhānaṃ pratigṛhṇāti / ebhiścaturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃsaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate /
children.translated_text: ) renounces all, renounces everywhere, gives with a mind of compassion for the sake of liberating beings from suffering, and accepts the array of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities with deep intention, examining those to be trained before accepting aspirations. Endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> quickly attains <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Endowed with four <s>dharmas</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> quickly attains <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Which four? He is virtuous, restrained in body, speech, and mind in conduct, keeps company with those who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, (

body.text: catvāra ime dharmā bodhisattvamārgasyopastambhakarāḥ / katame catvāraḥ? / pāramitāsvabhiyogaḥ, sattvānāṃ saṃgrahavastūtsargaḥ, brahmavihārābhiniṣpādanatā, abhijñāvikrīḍanātā / caturbhirdharmairbodhisattvenātṛptavihāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ, dānātṛptatayā dharmaśravaṇātṛptatayā bhāvanātṛptatayā sattvebhyaḥ saṅgrahavastvatṛptatayā viharatavyaṃ / catvāra ime bodhisattvenākṣayā nidhayaḥ paripūrayitavyāḥ / katame catvāraḥ? śraddhā bodhisattvenākṣayo nidhiḥ paripūrayitavyaḥ, dharmadeśanā pariṇāmanā daridrasattvaparigrahaścākṣayo nidhiḥ paripūrayitavyaḥ / catasra imā bodhisattvapariśuddhiḥ / katamāścatasraḥ? nairātmyatayā śīlapariśuddhiḥ, niḥsattvatayā samādhipariśuddhiḥ, nirjīvatayā prajñāpariśuddhiḥ, niṣpudgalatayā vimuktipariśuddhiḥ vimuktijñānadarśanatayā ca / catvāro dharmā bodhisattvena paripūrayitavyāḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 204.

children.text: ) yairbodhisattvāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyanti, ākāśacakraṃ pravartayanti, acintyacakramatulyacakraṃ anabhilāpyacakraṃ nairyāṇikacakraṃ nairvedhikacakraṃ apravṛtticakraṃ pravartayanti /
children.translated_text: ) by which <s>bodhisattvas</s> swiftly attain supreme perfect enlightenment and turn the wheel of space, the wheel of the inconceivable, the wheel of the incomparable, the wheel of the inexpressible, the wheel leading to liberation (<s>nairyāṇika</s>), the wheel of penetration (<s>nairvedhika</s>), and the wheel of non-arising (<s>apravṛtti</s>).

body.translated_text: These are four <s>dharmas</s> that support the <s>bodhisattva</s> path. What are the four? Devotion to the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), generosity of the means of gathering beings (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), accomplishment of the <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings), and playful mastery of the supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). A <s>bodhisattva</s> should dwell with four kinds of insatiability: insatiability in giving (<s>dāna</s>), insatiability in hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, insatiability in meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and insatiability in [applying] the means of gathering beings. These are four inexhaustible treasuries that a <s>bodhisattva</s> should fulfill. What are the four? Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>)—this is an inexhaustible treasury a <s>bodhisattva</s> should fulfill; teaching the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadeśanā</s>), dedication of merit (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>), and [generosity toward] impoverished beings—

body.text: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ vimalavaiśāyanānāgate 'dhvanyatikrānta ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'cirapraviṣṭe bhadrake kalpe praśānte pañcakaṣāye kāle vardhamāne āyuṣi aśītivarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, maitreyo nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavān" /
body.translated_text: You, <s>Vimalavaiśāyana</s>, in the future age, having passed beyond one incalculable aeon equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, recently entered into the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the five corruptions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) have subsided and lifespans are increasing among a people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, you shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment. You shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Maitreya</s>, and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One.

body.text: atha vimalavaiśāyano brāhmaṇo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvaikānte sthitvā puṣpamālyacurṇairbhagavataḥ pūjodyukto gāthābhirabhiṣṭauti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vimalavaiśāyana</s>, having bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with the fivefold prostration and standing to one side, devoted to worshipping the Blessed One with flowers, garlands, and powdered incense, praised him with verses:

children.translated_text: "O Protector with a broad forehead, with a beautiful <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft) white as snow,
resembling a peak of a golden mountain—O you who are a refuge for the protectorless!

children.text: kaste na nayu muni vṛṣabhā lokapradīpā guṇaśatabharitā
children.translated_text: Who would not honor you, O sage, O bull [among men], O lamp of the world, endowed with a hundred virtues?
This is the time for me; it has been declared—become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world!"

body.text: sarve samudrareṇunā brāhmaṇena purohitena sahasraṃ vedapāṭhakānāṃ bodhau samādāpitāṃ / yathā krakutsandaḥ kanakamuniḥ kāśyapo maitreyo vyākṛta evaṃ siṃhaḥ pradyotaḥ yāvaddvirūnaṃ sahasraṃ vedapāṭhakānāṃ māṇavakānāṃ sarve 'smin bhadrake kalpe 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavantaḥ, sarve ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatenāsminneva bhadrake kalpe 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyavasthāpitāḥ /
body.translated_text: All one thousand <s>Veda</s>-reciters were inspired toward enlightenment by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest. Just as <s>Krakutsanda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and <s>Maitreya</s> were given prophecy, so too <s>Siṃha</s>, <s>Pradyota</s>, and all nine hundred and ninety-eight <s>Veda</s>-reciting young men—all made aspirations for supreme perfect enlightenment in this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), and all were established by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect enlightenment in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>.

body.text: yasteṣāṃ sarvakanyasaḥ purohitena saṃcoditaḥ / "kiṃ bho mahābalavegadhārī dīrghaṃ nirīkṣase? / utpādayasva sattveṣu mahākaruṇāṃ" / imābhiśca gāthābhirvijñāpayati /
body.translated_text: He who was the very youngest among them was urged by the chief priest: "Why, O <s>Mahābalavegadhārī</s> (Bearer of Great Powerful Force), do you gaze into the distance? Generate great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward beings!" And he admonished him with these verses:

body.text: "ye sattvā jarāvyādhimṛtyubhirbhayā tṛṣṇā nadī patitā /

children.text:
prakṣiptā bhavacārake pratibhayaṃ skandhe niviṣṭā narāḥ /
pītvā kleśaviṣaṃ parasparavadhaṃ duḥkhārṇave saṃsthitā /
mohe andhe praṇaṣṭamārge aśubhasaṃsārayantre bhraman /
duḥkhena jālitabhūta sarvatribhaveya mithyāya dṛṣṭi sthitāḥ /
sarvaprāṇa bhramanti pañcagatibhiścakraṃ yathā vartate /
dharmā cakṣu vihīna pañcagatibhiratrāṇa sattvān smarī /
bhāve prajña jahitvā kaṅkṣavimati bodhāya candaṃ jane /
tṛṣṇāśokanudo bhavāhi jagato sattvāna bandhurbhavā /
children.translated_text:
cast into the terrifying cycle of existence (<s>bhavacāraka</s>), with [suffering] settled upon their shoulders—
those people, having drunk the poison of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), established in the ocean of suffering with mutual slaughter,
wandering in the blind darkness of delusion on a lost path, in the wheel of impure <s>saṃsāra</s>,
burning with suffering throughout all three realms of existence, established in wrong views,
all living beings wander through the five destinies (<s>gati</s>) as a wheel turns.
Devoid of the eye of <s>Dharma</s>, without protection in the five destinies—remember these beings!
Abandoning worldly wisdom, giving up doubt and uncertainty, generate the fierce mind for enlightenment!
Become the remover of craving and sorrow for the world! Become a kinsman of beings!

children.text:
kleśabandhanamokṣaṇārthaṃ jagato bodhāya cittaṃ name /
dharmacakṣurvihīna mohavigatamārgaṃ ca śreṣṭa dada /
saṃsārabhavacārakeṣu jvalitāṃ dharmarasena tarpayā /
tvaṃ śīghraṃ upasaṃkramya hitakarapādā nipatyaṃ mune /
children.translated_text:
For the sake of liberating the world from the bondage of afflictions, I bow my mind to enlightenment.
Give the eye of <s>Dharma</s> to those devoid [of it], give the supreme path free from delusion!
Satisfy with the taste of <s>Dharma</s> those burning in the wanderings of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Swiftly approach, and fall at the feet of the beneficent sage!

children.text: sarvā bho praṇidhi praśastra sudṛḍha buddho bhava nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: May all your excellent and firm aspirations [be fulfilled]—become a <s>Buddha</s>, a leader!
Become the breath of life for beings in the world! Rescue them from the ocean of beings!
May you become the giver of the path to liberation, of the faculties, powers, and limbs of enlightenment (<s>indriya-bala-bodhyaṅga</s>)!
Release the rain of <s>Dharma</s>, [be] the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud, and pacify the suffering of beings!"

body.translated_text: "Those beings fearful of old age, disease, and death, fallen into the river of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>),

body.text: sa ca kulaputra mahābalavegadhārī māṇavaka āha - (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 208.

children.text: ) "nāhaṃ bho upādhyāya saṃsārābhirāmāṃ śrīmākāṅkṣāmi, na ca punaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānābhilāśī; anuttarayānamākāṅkṣāmi / muhūrtaṃ bho upādhyāya pratīkṣāhi, śṛṇuṣva yathāhaṃ siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi" //
children.translated_text: ) "I, O teacher (<s>upādhyāya</s>), do not desire the glory of delighting in <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor do I aspire to the vehicles of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas). I aspire to the supreme vehicle (<s>anuttarayāna</s>). Wait a moment, O teacher; listen as I roar the lion's roar (<s>siṃhanāda</s>)."

body.translated_text: And that young man <s>Mahābalavegadhārī</s>, O son of good family, said—

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇastato 'bhiniṣkramya svakāṃ pañcabrāhmaṇadārakānupasthāyakānāmantrayitvovāca - "bho dārakā utpādayatānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ" / te 'pyāhuḥ / "nāsmākaṃ kiñcid asti yad vayaṃ buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṅghasya niryātayāmaḥ / kathaṃ ca vayamanavaruptakuśalamūlā bodhicittamutpādayāmaḥ?"
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, having gone out from there, summoned his five <s>brāhmaṇa</s> boy-attendants and said: "O boys, generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>)." They too replied: "We have nothing that we could offer to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. How can we, who have not [yet] planted roots of merit, generate <s>bodhicitta</s>?"

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohitaḥ prathamaḥ karabhujo nāmopasthāyakaḥ tasya saptaratnamayaṃ karṇavibhūṣaṇaṃ datvā, dvitīyaḥ sthālabhujo nāmopasthāyakaḥ tasya dvitīyaṃ saptaratnamayaṃ karṇaveṭhakaṃ datvā, tṛtīyaḥ jalabhujo nāmopasthāyakastasya saptaratnamayaṃ pīṭhaṃ dadāti, ceturthaḥ vegabhujo (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 209.

children.text: ) nāmopasthāyakastasya saptaratnamayaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadāti, pañcamaḥ sārabhujo nāmopasthāyakastasya sarvasauvarṇabhṛṅgāraṃ datvovāca / "gacchata yūyaṃ māṇavakā imāni vastūni buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṅghasya niryātayitvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayatha" /
children.translated_text: ) the attendant named [<s>Vegabhuja</s>], he gave a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) made of the seven precious jewels; the fifth attendant named <s>Sārabhuja</s>, he gave a golden water-pitcher (<s>bhṛṅgāra</s>) and said: "Go, young men, and having offered these articles to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment."

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest, gave to the first attendant named <s>Karabhuja</s> an ear-ornament made of the seven precious jewels; to the second attendant named <s>Sthālabhuja</s> he gave a second ear-wrapping made of the seven precious jewels; the third attendant named <s>Jalabhuja</s> he gave a seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) made of the seven precious jewels; the fourth, <s>Vegabhuja</s>—

body.text: atha te pañcopasthāyakā gatvā bhagavatsakāśaṃ tāni vastuni yathā nikṣiptāni buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṅghasya niryātayitvaivamāhuḥ / "vyākarotvasmākaṃ bhagavānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, tasmiṃśca bhadrake kalpe vayemanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyamahi" / peyālaṃ, vyākṛtāḥ kulaputra ratnagarbheṇa tathāgatena karabhujo māṇavako bodhāya bhadrakalpe dṛḍhasvaro nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ, sthālabhujastadantare sukhendriyamatirnāma bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ, tasyānantare jalabhujaḥ sārthavādirnāma bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ, tasyānusaṃdheḥ vegabhujaḥ priyaprasanno nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 210.

children.text: ) tasyānusaṃdheḥ sārabhujo nāma māṇavako haripatracūḍo nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: ) and following in that succession, the young man named <s>Sārabhuja</s> shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Haripatracūḍa</s>.

body.translated_text: Then those five attendants went into the presence of the Blessed One, offered those articles as deposited to the <s>bhikṣusaṅgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, and said: "May the Blessed One give us prophecy for supreme perfect enlightenment, and may we attain supreme perfect enlightenment in this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>." [The passage is abbreviated:] They were given prophecy, O son of good family, by <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. The young man <s>Karabhuja</s> for enlightenment in the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dṛḍhasvara</s> (Firm Voice); <s>Sthālabhuja</s>, after him, shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sukhendriyamati</s> (Wisdom of Pleasant Faculties); after him, <s>Jalabhuja</s> [shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s>] named <s>Sārthavādin</s>—

body.text: samanantaravyākṛtāste pañcabhadrakalpikā māṇavakāḥ purohitaḥ punarapi mahābalavegadhāriṇamāha - "mahābalavegadhārī gṛhṇāhi buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān, karohi praṇidhānaṃ bhagavataḥ sakāśādyādṛśamākāṅkṣasi, nimantrayāhi sarvasattvān dharmarasena, carāhi ca dṛḍhavīryeṇa svakaṃ bodhicārikāṃ / mā bhūyo dīrghaṃ nirīkṣasva" / bāhunā ca gṛhītvā bhagavato 'ntikamupanītaḥ /
body.translated_text: As soon as those five young men of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> received their prophecy, the chief priest again said to <s>Mahābalavegadhārī</s>: "O <s>Mahābalavegadhārī</s>, accept the array of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities, make your aspiration before the Blessed One—whatever kind you desire—invite all beings with the taste of <s>Dharma</s>, and practice your <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct with firm vigor. Do not gaze into the distance any longer!" And taking him by the arm, he led him into the presence of the Blessed One.

body.text: sa ca kulaputra mahābalavegadhārī māṇavako bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇaścāha - "kiyadbahavo bhagavannanāgate 'dhvani munibhāskarā asmin bhadrakalpe udayanti?" ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "tasmin māṇavaka bhadrake kalpe caturuttaraṃ sahasraṃ munibhāskarāṇāṃ udayaḥ / māṇavaka āha - "yāvatteṣāṃ bhadanta bhagavan bhadrake mahākalpe nirvṛtānāṃ jinasūryāṇāṃ paścimako sārabhujo (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 211.

children.text: ) nāma māṇavako 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate haripatracūḍo nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgata, tāvacciramahaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ cariṣyāmi vividhavratatapacaryādānadamasaṃyamaśrutavīryakṣāntisauratyapuṇyaprajñāsaṃbhāraṃ samudānayamānaḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca bhadrakalpikānāmacirābhisaṃbuddhānāṃ prathamaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dadyāṃ; parinirvṛtānāṃ ca śarīrapūjāṃ kuryāṃ; teṣāṃ ca saddharmadhārako bhaveyaṃ / śīlavirahitān sattvān śīlasaṃpadi samādāpayeyaṃ niveśayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; dṛṣṭivirahitān saṅkaṭaprāptān sattvān samyakdṛṣṭyāṃ samādāpayeyaṃ niveśayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; evamāśayavirahitān samyagāśaye pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; evamācāravirahitānācāre pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; nānāvidhānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalacaryāṃ nidarśayeyaṃ / teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmacirāstāṅgate saddharme punarahaṃ saddharmanetrī saddharmaparigrahaṃ saddharmasyotpādaṃ saddharmapradīpaṃ loke jvālayeyaṃ / śastrāntarakalpakālasamaye sattvān prāṇātipātavairamaṇyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ yāvat samyagdṛṣṭyāṃ; daśākuśalakarmapathebhyaḥ sattvān kumārgāduddhṛtya samyakpathe sthāpayeyaṃ; duścaritāndhakāraṃ (
children.translated_text: ) the young man named [<s>Sārabhuja</s>] shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment and shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Haripatracūḍa</s>—for that long I shall practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, accumulating the provision of merit and wisdom (<s>puṇya-prajñā-saṃbhāra</s>) through various austerities, ascetic practices, giving, self-control, restraint, learning, vigor, patience, and gentleness. And to all the <s>Buddhas</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, soon after their enlightenment, I shall offer the first alms-food (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>); and when they pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I shall worship their relics; and I shall be a upholder of their true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharmadhāraka</s>). Those beings bereft of morality I shall inspire, establish, and settle in the accomplishment of morality (<s>śīla</s>); those bereft of [right] views, who have fallen into difficulty—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 212.

children.text: ) ca nāśayeyaṃ; sucaritālokaṃ ca nidarśayeyaṃ; kalpakaṣāyaṃ yāvaccāyurdṛṣṭikleśakaṣāyaṃ ca loke nāśayeyaṃ / durbhikṣāntarakalpakālasamaye 'haṃ sattvāṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ niyojayeyaṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samādāpayeyaṃ niveśayeyaṃ; ṣaṭpāramitāsvahaṃ sattvān niyojayamānaḥ sarvadurbhikṣāndhakārakalikaluṣaraṇavairavigrahavivādaṃ śamayeyaṃ; sattvānāṃ santatau kleśānalaṃ śamayeyaṃ / rogāntarakalpakālasamaye cāhaṃ sattvāṃ ṣaṭpārāyaṇīyeṣu samādāpayeyaṃ; caturṣu saṅgrahavastuṣu niyojayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; rogāndhakāraṃ ca sattvānāṃ vidhvaṃsayeyaṃ, yāvat sattvānāṃ santatau kleśaṃ praśamayeyaṃ / sarve sahe buddhakṣetre bhadrakalpe sattvānevaṃrūpairvyasanaiḥ parimocayeyaṃ / yadā caturuttaraṃ sahasraṃ buddhā bhagavanto bhadrake mahākalpe utpannā nirvṛtāśca bhaveyuḥ, sarveṇa sarvaṃ ca saddharmanetrī antarhitā bhavet, tataḥ paścādahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / yāvāṃścaturuttarasahasrāṇāṃ bhadrakalpikānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmāyurbhavet tāntakam mama bodhiprāptasya dīrghamāyurbhavet; yāvāṃśca teṣāṃ śrāvakasaṅgho bhavet tāvān mamaikasya śrāvakasaṅghaḥ syāt; (
children.translated_text: ) I shall destroy; and I shall show the light of good conduct; and I shall destroy in the world the corruption of the <s>kalpa</s> and even the corruption of lifespan, views, and afflictions (<s>āyur-dṛṣṭi-kleśa-kaṣāya</s>). During the time of the intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of famine, I shall engage beings in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) and inspire, establish, and settle them up to the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>); and while engaging beings in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, I shall pacify all famine, darkness, strife, impurity, conflict, enmity, and quarrel; I shall pacify the fire of afflictions in the continuum of beings. And during the time of the intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of disease, I shall inspire beings in the six objects of going-beyond (<s>pārāyaṇīya</s>); I shall engage and establish them in the four means of gathering beings (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>)—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 213.

children.text:
) yāvataśca te kalpaiścaturuttaraṃ
buddhasahasraṃ sattvān viniyet tāvataḥ sattvān ahaṃ vinayeyaṃ / ye ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śrāvakaśikṣāyāṃ skhaleyurdṛṣṭiprapāte vā prapateyurbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśe 'gauravacittāḥ praduṣṭacittā bhaveyuḥ, dharme saṅghe ca skhalitacittā bhaveyuḥ, rāgacittā āryāpavādāḥ ānantaryakārāśca bhaveyurbodhiprāptaścāhaṃ sarvān saṃsārapaṅkāduddhareyaṃ, abhayapure ca nirvāṇanagare prāveśayeyaṃ / yāvan mama parinirvṛtasya saddharmakṣayo na bhavet tāvad bhadrakamahākalpe 'kṣayo bhaveyaṃ; niṣṭhite mama saddharme niṣṭhite bhadrakalpe, ye mama dhātavo janmaśarīraḥ te 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyāstathāgatavigrahāḥ saṃtiṣṭheran dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtagātrāḥ, ekaikaṃ lakṣaṇamaśītibhiranuvyañjanaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaṃ bhavet / te ca tathāgatavigrahā daśasu dikṣvaprameyebhyo 'saṃkhyeyebhyaḥ śūnyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo (
children.translated_text: ) and as many beings as those one thousand and four <s>Buddhas</s> shall discipline over those <s>kalpas</s>, so many beings shall I discipline. And those who stumble in the training of <s>śrāvakas</s> under those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, or who fall into the precipice of wrong views, or who become disrespectful and hostile toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, or who become of wavering mind toward the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, or who become full of passion, slanderers of the <s>Āryas</s> (noble ones), and committers of the heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>)—when I have attained enlightenment, I shall lift them all out of the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> and cause them to enter the fearless city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And until the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s> after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for as long as the <s>Bhadra</s> great—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 214.

children.text: ) gatvā ekaiko buddhavigraho 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyāṃ tribhiryānaiḥ sattvān samādāpayet niveśayet pratiṣṭhāpayed; yatra buddhakṣetre 'ntarakalpe na nāśo bhavet tatra tathāgatavigrahaḥ sattvān paritrāyedyathā pūrvoktaṃ tathā paścāccintāmaṇiḥ prādurbhavet; yeśu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvā ratnavirahitā bhaveyuḥ teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvā ratnavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣānnidhayaśca saṃdarśayeyuḥ; yeṣu ca buddhakṣetreṣu sattvāḥ kuśalakriyāvirahitā bhaveyuḥ vyādhibhīḥ kliṣṭāsteṣu buddhakṣetresu gośīrṣoragasārakālānusārī gandhavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣeyuḥ, sā ca gandhavṛṣṭiḥ sattvānāṃ kleśavyādhīrdṛṣṭivyādhīḥ kāyavyādhīśca praśamayet; tataste sattvāḥ puṇyakriyāvastuṣvabhiyuktā bhaveyuḥ svargaparāyaṇā bhaveyuḥ / evaṃrūpamahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇaḥ sattvān paritrāyeyaṃ / bodhiprāptaścāhamevaṃrūpaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kuryāṃ; parinirvṛtaścāhamevānantāparyantebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyaḥ sattvān paritrāyeyaṃ / yadi me bhadanta bhagavannaivaṃrūpā āśā paripūryetā na ca sattvānāṃ bhaiṣajyabhūto (
children.translated_text: ) having gone, each <s>Buddha</s>-form would encourage, establish, and confirm immeasurable and incalculable beings through the three vehicles. In whatever <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there would be no destruction during an intermediate <s>kalpa</s>, there the <s>Tathāgata</s>-form would protect beings as previously described, and thereafter a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) would appear. In whatever <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beings would be deprived of jewels, having gone to those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, may rains of jewels pour down and may treasures be revealed. And in whatever <s>buddhakṣetras</s> beings would be deprived of wholesome deeds, afflicted by the fear of disease, in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> may a rain of fragrance of <s>gośīrṣa</s> (ox-head sandalwood), serpent-essence, and black aloe pour down, and may that rain of fragrance pacify the affliction-diseases, view-diseases, and bodily diseases of beings. Then those beings would be devoted to the bases of meritorious activity and would be destined for heaven. Practicing such a <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, O Venerable Blessed One, I would protect beings. And having attained awakening, I would perform such <s>Buddha</s>-work. And even after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I would protect beings from infinite and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. If, O Venerable Blessed One, my aspiration of such a nature is not fulfilled, and I do not become a healing refuge for beings (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 215.

children.text: ) bhaveyaṃ, visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyurye daśasu dikṣvanatāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti, mā me bhagavān vyākuryādanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / ye 'pi te saṃpratipannāṃ bhagavan bahuprāṇakoṭyo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāḥ sattvāstān ahaṃ buddhān bhagavato virādhayeyaṃ, mā cārādhayeyaṃ, mā ca me bhūyo bodhihetoḥ saṃsāre saṃsāramāṇasya buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabdaḥ kuśalaśabdaḥ kuśalakarmakriyāśabdaḥ śrotrapatheṣu nipatet, nityamahamavīciparyāpanno bhaveyaṃ, yadi me bhagavannaivaṃrūpā āśā paripuryeta" /
children.translated_text: ) then may I be one who has deceived the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who stand, endure, sustain, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in infinite and boundless world-realms in the ten directions. May the Blessed One not prophesy me for supreme perfect awakening. And those many <s>koṭis</s> of living beings who have been prophesied, O Blessed One, for supreme perfect awakening — may I offend those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and may I not please them. And may the sound of '<s>Buddha</s>,' the sound of '<s>Dharma</s>,' the sound of '<s>Saṅgha</s>,' the sound of 'wholesome,' the sound of 'wholesome action' never again fall upon my ears while I wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of awakening. May I be permanently confined to <s>Avīci</s> [hell] if, O Blessed One, my aspiration of such a nature is not fulfilled."

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the young man <s>Mahābalavegadhārī</s>, seated before the Blessed One, said: "How many sages, shining like suns (<s>munibhāskara</s>), O Blessed One, will arise in this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> in the future age?" <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> replied: "In that <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, young man, one thousand and four sages shining like suns shall arise." The young man said: "For as long, O venerable Blessed One, as the <s>Buddhas</s> of the <s>Bhadra</s> great <s>kalpa</s> have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>—until the very last, <s>Sārabhuja</s>—

body.text: atha ratnagarbhastathāgato mahābalavegadhāriṇo māṇavakasya sādhukāramadāt / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa sattvānāṃ bhaiṣajyabhūtaḥ duḥkhebhyaśca parimocakastena tvaṃ satpuruṣa bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimalo nāma bhavasva / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimalānāgate (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 216.

children.text: ) 'dhvanyekasmin gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'tikrānte 'nupraviṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye bhadrake kalpe caturuttarasya buddhasahasrasyācirābhisaṃbuddhānāṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dāsyasi yāvadyathā svayaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, nirvṛtasya ca haripatracūḍabhadrasya tathāgatasya saddharme 'ntarhite 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, rocaśca nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi yāvadbuddho bhagavān / ardhakalpaṃ ca te āyurbhaviṣyati, yāvacca tasya caturuttarasya buddhasahasrasya bhadrakalpikānāṃ śrāvakasaṅgho bhaviṣyati tāvacca tavaikasya śrāvakasaṅgho bhaviṣyati, tāvataśca sattvān vinayiṣyasi / parinirvṛtasya ca saddharmāntardhānaṃ bhadrakasya mahākalpasya kalpakṣayo na bhaviṣyati; etāvantaśca buddhavigrahā bhaviṣyanti, yāvacchūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gandhavṛṣṭiḥ sattvānāṃ kleśavyādhirdṛṣṭivyādhīḥ kāyavyādhīśca śamayiṣyati, triṣu caiva puṇyakriyāvastuṣu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyanti svargaparāyaṇāṃśca" /
children.translated_text: ) time, having passed beyond one incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River and having entered a second incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, in the <s>Bhadra</s> <s>kalpa</s>, you shall offer <s>piṇḍapāta</s> (almsfood) to the one thousand and four <s>Buddhas</s> soon after their awakening, and so on, just as you yourself made your vow. And when the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Haripatracūḍabhadra</s> has disappeared after his <s>nirvāṇa</s>, you shall fully awaken to supreme perfect awakening, and you shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Roca</s>, and so on up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. And your lifespan shall be half a <s>kalpa</s>, and up to the <s>śrāvaka</s>-assembly of that one thousand and four <s>Buddhas</s> of the <s>Bhadra</s> <s>kalpa</s>

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> gave his approval to the young man <s>Mahābalavegadhārin</s>: "Well done, well done, O good man! You shall become a healing refuge for beings and a liberator from sufferings. Therefore, O good man, be called <s>Bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimala</s> ('Stainless Light of the King of Medicine'). You, <s>Bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimala</s>, in a future (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimalo bodhisattva āha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tathā me bhagavān satapuṇyalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtena pāṇinā mūrdhānāṃ sparśatu" / atha khalu kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgataḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtena pāṇinā bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimalasya bodhisattvasya mūrdhānaṃ parimārjayitvā tasthau / atha khalu kulaputra bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimalo bodhisattvastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditacitto ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā vanditavaikānte 'tikramya sthitaṃ / samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo divyena kauśikavastreṇācchādayitvovāca / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, śobhanaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / na bhūyastvayā mamopasthānaṃ kartavyaṃ / yathā sukhameva viharasva" //
body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimala</s> said: "If, O Venerable Blessed One, my aspiration of such a nature is fulfilled, then may the Blessed One touch my head with his hand adorned with the marks of a hundred merits." Then, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, with his hand adorned with the marks of a hundred merits, stroked the head of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimala</s> and remained standing. Then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarājajyotirvimala</s>, delighted, elated, joyful, with a gladdened mind, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> in the five-fold prostration.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasyaitadabhavat - "mayā bahavaḥ prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāni, yathedaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 218.

children.text: ) sarvāvantaṃ parṣadaṃ paśyāmi sarvaiścemairmahāsattvairudārodārāṇi praṇidhānāni kṛtāni prasannāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇi parigṛhītāni sthāpayitvā vāyuviṣṇunānyairbodhisattvaiḥ kaliyugaṃ parivarjitaṃ / mayāpi kaliyugakāle vartamāne sattvā dharmarasena tarpayitavyā, dṛdhaśca vyavasāyaḥ kartavyaḥ / tathārūpeṇa ca mayā praṇidhānena siṃhanādo naditavyaḥ / yatheyaṃ sarvā bodhisattvaparṣadāścaryaprāptā bhavet, sarvāvatī ceyaṃ parṣā sadevagandharvamāṇuṣāsuraśca loko 'yaṃ māṃ prāñjalībhūto namasyeta pūjāṃ ca kuryād / ayaṃ ca me buddho bhagavān sādhukāramanuprayacchet vyākuryāt, tathā ye ca daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ tiṣṭhanti yāpayanti sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti te 'pi buddhā bhagavanto mama siṃhanādaṃ nadataḥ sādhukāraṃ pradadyuḥ, vyākuryuścānutarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, dūtāṃśca preṣayeyuryat sarvāvatīyaṃ parṣat śṛṇuyāt tāṃśca dūtān paśyet / ye 'pi ca tasyāṃ paścātkāle mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatā bodhisattvāste 'pyevaṃrūpaṃ kliṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ mahākaliyugakāle bodhiṃ (
children.translated_text: ) entire assembly, I see that all these <s>mahāsattvas</s> have made noble and sublime vows and have taken up purified <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — except for <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> and the other <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have avoided the degenerate age. I too, while the degenerate age prevails, must satisfy beings with the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s>, and I must make a firm resolve. And I must roar a lion's roar with such a vow that this entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> would be struck with wonder, and that this entire assembly together with the world of <s>devas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s> would honor me with joined palms and worship
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 219.

children.text: ) praṇidhānena pratigṛhṇīyurdharmadurbhikṣakāntāre kleśaughairuhyamānān sattvān paritrāyeyuḥ, buddhakāryaṃ ca kuryuḥ, sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyuḥ / yāvat parinirvṛtasyāpi me 'cintyāḥ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrātikrānte daśasu dikṣvatulyebhyo 'parimāṇebhyaśca buddhakṣetrebhyo 'parimāṇā buddhā bhagavanto mama parinirvṛtasya varṇaṃ bhāṣeran, yaśaśca ghoṣaṃ ca cārayeyuḥ, bodhisattvānāṃ cāgrato mama praṇidhānanetrīmudbhāvayeyuḥ / te ca bodhisattvā mama karuṇāparibhāvitādhiṣṭānaṃ praṇidhānaṃ śrutvā paramāścaryaprāptā bhaveyuḥ, te 'pi sattvebhyo mahākaruṇāṃ sarjayeyuḥ; tataśca te evaṃrūpaṃ eva praṇidhānaṃ pratigṛhṇīyuryathāhametarhi pratigṛhṇāmi, te 'pyevaṃrūpe kliṣṭe buddhakṣetre bodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyuḥ / caturbhiroghaiḥ sattvān pratyuhyamānānuttārayeyuḥ, tribhiśca yānairvinayeyuḥ, yāvannirvāṇapathe sthāpayeyuḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) through their vows they would protect beings carried away by the floods of afflictions in the wilderness of <s>Dharma</s>-famine, and they would perform <s>Buddha</s>-work and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. And even after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having passed beyond inconceivable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, from incomparable and immeasurable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, would proclaim the praise of me after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and spread my fame and renown, and set forth my vow-guidance before the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having heard my vow permeated by compassion and empowered

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief chaplain, had this thought: "By me, many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of living beings have been encouraged toward supreme perfect awakening. Now, when I see this (

body.text: evaṃrūpaṃ kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo agrapurohito mahākaruṇāparibhāvaṃ praṇidhānaṃ sarjayitvā, ekāṃśaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya yena ratnagarbhastathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmati (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 220.

children.text: ) sma / tena khalu punaḥ samayena bahudevakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi gaganatale divyāni tūryakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi vādyanti puṣpavṛṣṭiśca pravarṣitā, ekakaṇṭhena codāharanti / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, upasaṃkrama tvaṃ bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ / gṛhṇa tvaṃ pravarapraṇidhānaṃ / kleśavyākule loke praśamayiṣyasi duḥkhaskandhaṃ sattvānāṃ jñānatoyena praśamayiṣyasi" / sarvāvatī sā parṣatprāñjalībhūtā abhimukhā ekakaṇṭhena vadati / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, pravarapaṇḍitāsmākaṃ hitakara kuruṣva dṛḍhapraṇidhānaṃ pravarabuddhimayaṃ śṛṇomaḥ" / purohitaścopasaṃkrāmati yadā ca nikṣiptaṃ purohitena bhagavataḥ sakāśe jānumaṇḍalaṃ, tāvaccāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ sarvāvatīdaṃ saṃtaraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ kaṃpati prakaṃpati calati pracalati kṣubhyati prakṣubhyati vedhati pravedhati, aghaṭṭitāni tūryāni pravādyanti; ye ca mṛgapakṣiṇaste sarve manojñaṃ snigdhaṃ ca śabdamudīrayanti, vṛkṣāśca puṣpāṇi pramuñcanti / ye kecidasmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau pṛthivīṃ niśritya bhūtāḥ prativasanti ye bodhau samādāpitā ye na ca samādāpitāḥ, sthāpayitvā nairāyikāṃ yāmalaukikāṃ ca, sarve (
children.translated_text: ). At that time, many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>devas</s> on the surface of the sky played <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of divine musical instruments and showered a rain of flowers, and with a single voice they exclaimed: "Well done, well done, O good man! Approach the presence of the Blessed One! Take up the supreme vow! In the world turbulent with afflictions, you will pacify the mass of suffering of beings; with the waters of knowledge you will pacify them." And that entire assembly, with joined palms, facing him, with a single voice said: "Well done, well done, O good man, our supremely learned benefactor! Make your firm vow
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 221.

children.text: ) hitacittāḥ kalyāṇacittā avairacittā akaluṣacittā maitricittā āścaryacittā babhūvuḥ / ye sattvāḥ svargacarāste khe sthā evaṃ paramaprītimanasaḥ, puṣpairmālyairgandhairvādyai ratnacchatrairdhvajaiḥ patākābhirvastraduṣyaiḥ snigdhamanojñaṃ śabdaṃ brāhmaṇasya praṇidhānaṃ śravaṇāyodyuktāḥ pūjākarmaṇe / caivaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaparyantā devā jambūdvīpaṃ avatīrya gaganatale sthitvā divyairgandhairyāvadduṣyairbrāhmaṇasya praṇidhānaṃ śravaṇārthamudyuktāḥ pūjākarmaṇe /
children.translated_text: ) they were of benevolent mind, virtuous mind, non-hostile mind, unpolluted mind, mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), and mind of wonder. Those beings who were sky-dwellers, standing in the sky with supremely delighted minds, with flowers, garlands, incense, music, jewel-parasols, banners, flags, cloths and silks, uttering gentle and pleasant sounds — they were intent on hearing the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s vow and on performing worship. And thus, up to the <s>devas</s> from the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven-realm, having descended to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and standing on the surface of the sky, with divine fragrances and so on up to silks — they were intent on hearing the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s vow and on performing worship.

body.translated_text: Thus, O son of good family, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief chaplain, having generated such a vow permeated by great compassion, having wrapped his robe over one shoulder, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> (

body.text: brāhmaṇaścāñjaliṃ pragṛhyābhirgāthābhī ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamabhituṣṭāva /
body.translated_text: And the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having joined his palms, praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with these verses:

body.text:
"dhyānebhirvikrīḍasi brahmarivā rūpeṇa prabhāvasi śakrarivā /
dhanadhānya prayacchasi rājarivā ratanāgravaro muniśreṣṭhirivā /
giri saumya vinardasi siṃharivā na ca kaṃpase dṛḍhamerurivā /
na ca kṣobhyase udadhīṣarivā guṇadoṣavahī samudravāririvā /

children.text:
mala sarva pravāhasi toyurivā dahi kleśvanaṃ muniragnirivā /
na ca sajjase kvacidvāyurivā muni tattve nidarśaka devurivā /
muni dharma pravarṣasi nāgurivā jaga sarvaṃ tarpayasi vṛṣṭirivā /
anyatīrthaṃ pramardasi siṃharivā guṇagandha pramuñcasi puṣparivā /
madhuragira bhāṣasi brahmarivā jaga duḥkhapramuñcaka vaidyarivā /
samacittamupasthihi mātarivā jaga nityānugṛhṇasi mitrarivā /
kira māna arī dṛḍha vajrarivā chindi tṛṣṇalatā muniśatrurivā /
jaga tārayase naditārurivā dahi jñānatṛṇāṃ munināgarivā /
dadi śītaprabhā municandrarivā nara padma vibodhayi sūryarivā /
caturagraphalān dadhi vṛkṣarivā riṣisaṅghavṛto munipakṣirivā /
children.translated_text:
You wash away all impurity like water, you burn the forest of afflictions like fire, O sage,
you cling to nothing anywhere like the wind, O sage, you reveal the truth like a <s>deva</s>.
O sage, you rain the <s>Dharma</s> like a <s>nāga</s>, you satisfy the whole world like rainfall,
you crush other doctrines like a lion, you release the fragrance of virtues like a flower.
You speak with sweet voice like <s>Brahmā</s>, you liberate the world from suffering like a physician,
you stand with an equal mind like a mother, you constantly bless the world like a friend.
You are the enemy of pride, firm like <s>vajra</s>, you cut the creeper of craving, O sage, like an enemy,
you ferry the world across like a ferryman on a river, you burn with the fire of knowledge, O sage, like a <s>nāga</s>

children.text:
jinabuddha viṣāla samudrarivā samacitta jage tṛṇakāṣṭharivā /
śūnyadharma nirīkṣasi svapnarivā samalokānuvartasi vāririvā /
children.translated_text:
O <s>Jina</s> <s>Buddha</s>, vast like the ocean, equal-minded toward the world like grass and wood,
you behold empty <s>dharmas</s> like a dream, you conform to the impure world like water.

children.text: muni bodhiya vyākṛta sattva tvayā varalakṣaṇadhāri sukāruṇikā /
children.translated_text: O sage, beings have been prophesied by you for awakening, bearers of supreme marks, of beautiful compassion.

children.text: tvayi sattva vinīta anantabahū mama vyākari bodhiya agravare /
children.translated_text: Beings disciplined by you are infinite and many — prophesy me too for the supreme, highest awakening.

children.text: varaprajñā mahāriṣi satyaruceḥ mama vyākari bodhiya chindi matīṃ /
children.translated_text: O great sage of supreme wisdom, of <s>Satyaruci</s> ('Delighting in Truth') — prophesy me for awakening, cut through my doubt.

children.text: bhavi buddha jage kalikleśaraṇiḥ sthapi sattvaśatāṃśi viśāntapathe" //
children.translated_text: May I become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world, a refuge in the degenerate age of afflictions; may I establish hundreds of beings on the path of peace."

body.translated_text:
"You sport in <s>dhyānas</s> like <s>Brahmā</s>, you shine in form like <s>Śakra</s>,
you bestow wealth and grain like a king, you are the best of jewel-lords like the supreme sage.
You roar on the mountain, O gentle one, like a lion, and you do not tremble like firm <s>Meru</s>,
you are not shaken like the ocean, bearing merits and faults like the waters of the sea.

body.text: yadā kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohito ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamābhirgāthābhiḥ stutvā tasthau, tāvadeva sā sarvāvatī parṣā sadevagandharvamāṇuṣā sādhukāramadāt //
body.translated_text: When, O son of good family, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief chaplain, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with these verses, stood there, at that very moment that entire assembly together with <s>devas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and humans gave their approval.

body.text: purohita āha - "mayā bhadanta bhagavan bahuprāṇakoṭyo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāstaiśca (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 224.

children.text: ) svakasvakodārodārāṇi buddhakṣetrāṇi parigṛhītāni pariśuddhāśayāvaruptakuśalamūlāḥ suvinītāḥ sattvā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / ime ca jyotipālapūrvaṃgamānāṃ caturuttarasahasraṃ vedapāṭhakāṇaṃ ye tathāgatena bhadrakalpikā vyākṛtāḥ, te 'pi satpuruṣā rāgadveṣamohamānacaritāṃstribhiryānairvinayanti; tadapi taistīvrakleśāvaraṇakaliyugakaṣāyāḥ parivarjitāstairutsṛṣṭā ānantaryakārakāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakāḥ āryāpavādakā mithyādṛṣṭaya āryasaptadhanavirahitā amātṛjñā apitṛjñā aśrāmaṇyā abrāhmaṇyā akṛtyakārakā apuṇyakarāḥ paralokabhayādarśino viparītatattvabodhino 'nāthakāstriṣu sucariteṣu, tathā devamānuṣikābhiḥ śrīsaṃpattibhirudyuktāḥ triṣu duścariteṣu saṃpratipannāḥ daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu virahitāḥ sarvakalyāṇamitrai riñcitāḥ sarvapaṇḍitaiḥ prakṣiptā bhavacārake 'nuśrotamuhyantaḥ kṣāranadyāṃ sīdantaḥ saṃsārapaṅkairmohāndhakārāvirahitā nirmuktāḥ sarvakuśalakriyāyāṃ sarve śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣūjjhitāḥ sakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatāḥ kumārgavihanyanto mahāsaṅkaṭaprāptāstasmin (
children.translated_text: ) each has accepted their own magnificent <s>Buddha</s>-fields; they have accepted as disciples beings who are well-trained, of purified intention, with planted roots of merit. And these one thousand and four Veda-reciters headed by <s>Jyotipāla</s>, whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> prophesied as [Buddhas] of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> — those worthy ones discipline beings of passionate, hateful, and deluded conduct through the three vehicles. Yet those abandoned and forsaken by them — beings with intense afflictive obscurations, the depravities of the degenerate age, those who commit the acts of immediate retribution, those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>, those who revile the noble ones, those of wrong views, those bereft of the seven noble treasures, those ungrateful to mother and father, those without the nature of a renunciant or brahmin, those who do wrong deeds, who create no merit, who do not see the danger of the next world, who understand reality in a perverted way, who are without protectors in the three good conducts — endowed with divine and human glories and prosperity yet engaged in the three evil conducts, bereft of the ten wholesome courses of action, abandoned by all virtuous friends, rejected by all the wise, drifting downstream in the cycle of existence, sinking in the river of brine, not freed from the darkness of delusion in the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s>, empty of all wholesome activity, forsaken in all empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields, having arrived at the exhaustion of their roots of merit, obstructed on the wrong path, fallen into great peril — in that (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 225.

children.text: ) kāle sahe buddhakṣetre daśavarṣāyuṣkā bhadrakalpe manuṣyā bhaviṣyanti, sarva ime satpuruṣaiḥ paṇḍitairutsṛṣṭā ujjhitāḥ / tatkālaṃ bhavāvartake saṃsāracakre 'trāṇā aśaraṇā aparāyaṇā duḥkhabhājanabhūtāḥ sattvāstāṃ parivarjayitvā svakasvakā buddhakṣetrāḥ pradhānapradhānāḥ parigṛhītāḥ, suvinītāśca pariśuddhāśayāḥ avaruptakuśalamūlāḥ ārabdhavīryā bahubuddhakṛtādhikārā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / na evaṃ, bhadanta bhagavan?" ratnagarbhastathāgata āha - "evaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yathābhiprāyāḥ sattvāḥ praṇidhānaṃ kurvanti buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāśca parigṛhītāstatraiva ca mayā vyākṛtāḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) time, in this <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, during the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, humans will have a lifespan of ten years. All these have been abandoned and forsaken by those worthy and wise ones. At that time, beings who are without shelter, without refuge, without resort in the turning of <s>saṃsāra</s>'s wheel, who have become vessels of suffering — having set aside those beings, each [<s>bodhisattva</s>] has accepted their own chief and foremost <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and has accepted as disciples beings who are well-trained, of purified intention, with planted roots of merit, of exerted vigor, who have performed service under many <s>Buddhas</s>. Is this not so, Venerable Blessed One?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> said: "It is so, O brahmin. Beings make aspirations according to their intentions, and accept the splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and there indeed I have prophesied them."

body.translated_text: The chaplain said: "By me, O Venerable Blessed One, many <s>koṭis</s> of living beings have been encouraged toward supreme perfect awakening. And by them (

body.text: brāhmaṇaḥ prāha - "mamāpi bhadanta bhagavan hṛdayaṃ kaṃpati tadyathāpi kiṃśukapatraṃ paramadīnamānaso 'haṃ sarvaśarīraṃ ca me āyāsitaṃ, yadi me bhadanta bhagavan sattvāḥ karuṇāspadabhūtā bodhisattvaistatkālamutsṛṣṭā mahākaliyugāndhakāraprakṣiptāḥ sarvaparivarjitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The brahmin said: "My heart too trembles, Venerable Blessed One, like a <s>kiṃśuka</s> leaf; I am of supremely wretched mind, and my entire body is exhausted. For, Venerable Blessed One, those beings who are objects of compassion have been abandoned by the <s>bodhisattvas</s> at that time, cast into the darkness of the great degenerate age, forsaken by all.

body.text: ahamapi bhadanta bhagavannanāgate 'dhvani atikrānte ekagaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'vaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye tasmiṃśca bhadrake mahākalpe daśavarṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ kālaṃ pratīkṣamāṇāstāvacciramahaṃ saṃsāre na parikhidyeyaṃ bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇa, utsahāyi cāhaṃ samādhānabalena cirapācanayānvaineyān pratigṛhṇāmi, ṣaṭpāramitāścaramāṇo vaineyān pratigṛhṇāmi / śrutaṃ ca mayā bhagavataḥ sakāśād "vastunimittaṃ parityāgeyaṃ dānapāramitā" / tathārūpamahaṃ dānapāramitāṃ cariṣyāmi yathā janmāntareṣvaprameyāḥ sattvā yācanakā āgamiṣyanti teṣāṃ tathārūpāṃ parityāgaṃ parityajeyaṃ, tadyathānnapānakhādyabhojyapeyalehyavastraśayyāsanāśrayapratiśrayamālyagandhavilepanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyadānaṃ chatradhvajapatākādhanadhānyahastyaśvarathasuvarṇarūpyahiraṇyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍarajatajātarūpadakṣiṇāvartasarvāmahamevaṃ parityāgaṃ paramaprāsādakāruṇyamānasaḥ sattvānāṃ datvāphalābhikāṅkṣī (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 227.

children.text: ) sattvaparipācanārthaṃ vaineyasattvānugrahārthaṃ tyāgasaṃbhāraṃ parityajeyaṃ / ye ca punaḥ sattvā atityāgayācanakā āgatvā yācayeran tadyathā dāsadāsīgrāmanagararājyabhāryāputraduhitṛhastaparityāgapādaparityāgakarṇanāsānayanajihvācarmarudhirāsthikāyajīvitaśiraḥparityāgaṃ, evaṃrūpāḥ parityāgāḥ paramaprasannaḥ kāruṇyamānasaḥ aphalābhikāṅkṣī sattvānāṃ dānaṃ dadyāṃ vaineyānukaṃpārthaṃ / tathārūpāyāmahaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ cariṣyāmi, yanna kadācit pūrvaṃ kenacit sattvena evaṃrūpāḥ parityāgāḥ parityaktāḥ syurna ca punaḥ paścāt kaścid bodhisattvaḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇaḥ evaṃrūpāḥ parityāgāḥ parityājet / yadahaṃ teṣu janmāntareṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣvanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇaḥ dānapāramitāyāṃ careyaṃ / yadahaṃ mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatānāṃ paścimakānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ parityāganetrīguṇān sthāpayeyaṃ / "yā praśamā raṇikleśānāmiyaṃ śīlapāramitā" / tathāhamanuttarāyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) for the sake of ripening beings and out of kindness toward those to be disciplined, I shall practice the accumulation of giving. And further, those beings who come as supplicants requesting excessive relinquishments — such as the relinquishment of slaves male and female, villages, cities, kingdoms, wife, son, daughter, hands, feet, ears, nose, eyes, tongue, skin, blood, bones, body, life, and head — such relinquishments I shall make with supreme serenity, with a compassionate mind, without desire for reward, giving to beings out of sympathy for those to be disciplined. I shall practice such a <s>dānapāramitā</s> that no being before has ever made such relinquishments, nor will any <s>bodhisattva</s> afterward, while practicing the course of unsurpassed perfect awakening, make such relinquishments. For immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> in those future births, while practicing the course of unsurpassed perfect awakening, I shall practice the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. And I shall establish for the later <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with great compassion the guiding quality of relinquishment. 'That which is the pacification of the afflictions of conflict — that is the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality).' Thus I, while practicing the course of unsurpassed (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 228.

children.text:
) samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇo vividhaśīlavratanirantaraduṣkaracārikāṃ careyaṃ, yathā pūrvoktaṃ / "yā viṣayeṣvakṣaṇyanatā ātmapratyavekṣaṇā iyaṃ kṣāntipāramitā" / tathārūpamahaṃ kṣāntiṃ bhāvayamāno, yathā pūrvoktaṃ / "yā vivekatā sarvasaṃskṛtā bhāvanā udyujyanā sarvāsaṃskṛtaśāntamanuttaracaryayā avivartanā iyaṃ vīryapāramitā" / "yā sarvasaṃskāreṣu viparyāsaprahāṇāya śūnyatā samudācāraḥ iyaṃ dhyānapāramitā" / "yā prakṛtyanutpattikadharmakṣāntiriyaṃ prajñāpāramitā" / yā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu dṛḍhotsāhabalavegacaryā, yathā pūrvoktaṃ, na kaścid bodhisattvo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇaḥ evaṃ dṛḍhotsāhabalavegena
prajñāpāramitāyāṃ cīrṇaḥ syāṃ, na ca punaḥ paścātkaścid (
children.translated_text: ) perfect awakening, shall practice the difficult course of various uninterrupted moral observances and vows, as previously stated. 'That which is forbearance toward sense objects, self-examination — that is the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience).' Thus I shall cultivate such patience, as previously stated. 'That which is seclusion from all conditioned things, cultivation, exertion, and non-regression through the unsurpassed course of all unconditioned peace — that is the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor).' 'That which is the practice of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) for the abandonment of perversions in all formations — that is the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation).' 'That which is the patience of the inherent non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — that is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom).' For immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, [I shall practice] the course of firm enthusiasm, strength, and vigorous force, as previously stated. No <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the course of unsurpassed perfect awakening has ever practiced the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> with such firm enthusiasm, strength, and vigorous force, nor will anyone afterward (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 229.

children.text: ) bodhisattvo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇaḥ evaṃ dṛḍhotsāhabalavegena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caret, tathāhaṃ careyaṃ; paścimakānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatānāṃ netrīguṇaṃ sthāpayeyaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) — no <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the course of unsurpassed perfect awakening shall practice the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> with such firm enthusiasm, strength, and vigorous force — thus shall I practice; and I shall establish the guiding quality for the later <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with great compassion.

body.translated_text: I too, Venerable Blessed One, in the future time, when one incalculable [aeon] equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> has passed and the second incalculable [aeon] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> remains, in that <s>Bhadra</s> great <s>kalpa</s>, when the generation has a lifespan of a thousand years — waiting for that time, for that long may I not grow weary in <s>saṃsāra</s> while practicing the course of awakening. And I am able, by the power of my resolve, to accept those disciples who must be ripened over a long time, and while practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), I accept those to be disciplined. I have heard from the Blessed One: 'The <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) is the renunciation of material things.' I shall practice such a <s>dānapāramitā</s> that in [my] future births, when immeasurable beings come as supplicants, I shall make such relinquishments for them — namely, gifts of food, drink, hard food, soft food, beverages, syrups, clothing, beds, seats, dwellings, shelters, garlands, fragrances, ointments, medicines for the sick, parasols, banners, flags, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, chariots, gold, silver, coins, <s>maṇi</s>-gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, stone, coral, silver, fine gold, and right-turning [conch shells] — all these relinquishments I shall make to beings with a mind of supreme faith and compassion, without desire for reward, (

body.text: prathamacittotpādenāhaṃ paścimakānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāṃ nivartayeyaṃ, yāvadanuttaraparinirvāṇena bodhisattvāścāścaryaprāptā bhaveyurityarthamahaṃ tyāgasyāmanyanatā careyaṃ, śīlāniśrayatā kṣāntyāmanyanatā vīrye 'nāyūhanatā dhyāneṣvapratiṣṭhitatā prajñāyāmadvayatāṃ careyaṃ / aphalākāṅkṣī āryasaptadhanavirahitānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvaśūnyabuddhakṣetrojjhitānāmānantaryakārakānāṃ saddharmapratikṣepakānāmāryāparvādakānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭikānāmakuśalamūlasamavadhānasaṅkaṭaprāptānāṃ kumārge vihanyamānānāṃ sattvānāmarthāyāhaṃ pāramitāstīvrabalavegotsāhena careyaṃ / ekaikasya sattvasyārthe cāhaṃ kuśalamūlabījasaṃtatyāḥ pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ daśamahākalpān (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 230.

children.text: ) avīcinarake duḥkhāṃ vedanāmutsaheyaṃ, evaṃ tiryakpreteṣu yakṣadaridreṣu manuṣyadaridreṣu duḥkhāṃ vedanāmutsaheyaṃ / yathā caikasattvasya santatyāṃ kuśalamūlabījaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ tathā sarvasattvānāṃ evaṃrūpāṃ riktamuṣṭisadṛśasantānāṃ vaineyāṃ pratigṛhṇīyaṃ / yāvat kalpaparyantenāhamanārthako divyasukhopapattibhiḥ, sthāpayitvā ekajātipratibaddhatuṣitabhavanakālāparikṣīcaramabhaviko bodhyabhisaṃbodhanārthaṃ; tāvacciramahaṃ saṃsāre buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ paryupāsitvā ekaikasya ca buddhasyāhaṃ buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃ vividhāṃ
children.translated_text: ) likewise among animals and <s>pretas</s>, among impoverished <s>yakṣas</s> and impoverished humans, I shall endure painful feelings. Just as I would establish the seed of wholesome roots in the continuity of one being, so too for all beings — I shall accept such disciples whose continuity is like an empty fist. Until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, I have no use for rebirth in divine happiness, except for the time bound to one more birth in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven as one in his final existence for the sake of attaining awakening. For that long in <s>saṃsāra</s>, having attended upon <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, I shall make offerings to each <s>Buddha</s> as various as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields,

body.translated_text: From the first generation of the mind, I shall turn [beings] away from [lack of] the great compassion of the later <s>bodhisattvas</s>; and so that <s>bodhisattvas</s> may attain wonder through unsurpassed <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — for that purpose I shall practice non-pride in giving, reliance on morality, non-pride in patience, non-exertion in vigor, non-abiding in <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and non-duality in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Without desire for reward, for the sake of beings bereft of the seven noble treasures, forsaken by all empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who commit acts of immediate retribution, who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>, who revile the noble ones, who hold wrong views, who have fallen into the peril of the accumulation of unwholesome roots, who are obstructed on the wrong path — for the sake of such beings I shall practice the <s>pāramitās</s> with intense strength, vigor, and enthusiasm. For the sake of each and every being, for the establishment of the continuity of roots of wholesome seeds, I shall endure painful feelings in the <s>Avīci</s> hell for ten great <s>kalpas</s>; (

body.text: pūjāṃ kuryāṃ, ekaikasya ca buddhasya sakāśādbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān guṇān adhigaccheyaṃ, buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca sattvān bodhau samādāpayeyaṃ / evaṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānāmevaṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ yathābhiprāyāṃśca sattvān tathāhaṃ samādāpayeyaṃ / asati buddhotpāde loka ṛṣivratenāhaṃ sattvāṃ daśakuśalakarmapatheṣu niyojayeyaṃ samādhāvabhijñāsu ca niyojayeyaṃ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 231.

children.text: ) dṛṣṭivyasanamaheśvarabhaktāṃ maheśvararūpeṇāhaṃ sattvān kuśaleṣu niyojayeyaṃ, nārāyaṇabhaktāṃścandrasūryabhaktāṃ yāvadbrahmabhaktān brahmarūpeṇāhaṃ sattvān kuśaladharmeṣu niyojayeyaṃ / evaṃ garuḍarūpeṇa garuḍapakṣiṇaḥ kuśalacaryāsu niyojayeyaṃ, yāvacchakrarūpeṇa / bubhūkṣitān sattvān svamāṃsarudhireṇa saṃtarpayeyaṃ, vyasanagatāṃśca sattvāṃ svakena kāyena jīvitena ca paritrāyeyaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) those beings devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s> who are afflicted by the calamity of wrong views — in the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>, I shall establish those beings in wholesome [dharmas]; those devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, those devoted to the moon and sun, and up to those devoted to <s>Brahmā</s> — in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, I shall establish those beings in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise, in the form of a <s>Garuḍa</s>, I shall establish <s>Garuḍa</s> birds in wholesome practices, and so on up to in the form of <s>Śakra</s>. I shall satisfy hungry beings with my own flesh and blood, and I shall rescue beings fallen into calamity with my own body and life.

body.translated_text: and from each <s>Buddha</s> I shall attain qualities as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and I shall inspire beings as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields toward awakening. Likewise for those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, likewise for those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle — I shall inspire beings according to their intentions. When no <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world, through the practice of a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), I shall establish beings in the ten wholesome courses of action, and I shall establish them in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), (

body.text: tāvacciramahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan dagdhasantānānāṃ kuśalamūlaparihīnānāmarthāyātibalavegena cārikāṃ caraṃ, tāvacciraṃ cāhaṃ saṃsāre sattvahetorvividhacaṇḍaghoradāruṇāṃ duḥkhāṃ praticcheyaṃ: yāvadatikrāntānekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ nirgatānām avaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvāikāsame 'saṃkhyeye 'nupraviṣṭe bhadrake mahākalpe yadā jyotipālo māṇavako 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyati krakutsando nāma tathāgato bhaviṣyati tadāhaṃ tasmin samaye āryeṇa prajñācakṣuṣā daśasu dikṣu sahasrabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāsu lokadhātuṣu pravartitadhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ tiṣṭhato yāpayato buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyeyaṃ / ye mayā dagdhasantānā akuśalamūlasamādhānāḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 232.

children.text: ) saptadhanavirahitāḥ sarvaiḥ śūnyairbuddhakṣetrairujjhitā ānantaryakārakāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakā āryāpavādakā yāvatkumārge vihanyantaḥ mayā saṅkaṭaprāptāḥ prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / mayā te sattvāḥ prathamaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ samādāpitā yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ niveśitāḥ syurmayā ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tatkuśalamūlabījamanuttare nirvāṇe prakṣiptaṃ syāt, apāyebhyaśca parimocitāḥ syuḥ, prajñāpuṇyasaṃbhāre ca niyojitāḥ syustiṣṭhanto yāpayantasteṣu ca buddhakṣetresu buddheṣu bhagavatasūpanītāḥ syuryadānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākaraṇapratilabdhā bhaveyuḥ, samādhidhāraṇīkṣāntipratilabdhāśca syurbhūmyavakrāntāśca syurmayā ca te sattvā buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā praṇidhānaṃ samādāpitāḥ śikṣāpitāśca syuryathārūpaṃ ca te buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ pratigṛhṇeyuste ca tān ahaṃ tasmin samaye 'nupraviṣṭe bhadrakalpe krakutsande jinasūrya udgate daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhān bhagavataḥ (
children.translated_text: ) bereft of the seven treasures, forsaken by all empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who commit acts of immediate retribution, who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>, who revile the noble ones, up to those obstructed on the wrong path, who have fallen into peril — those I shall have first inspired, established, and grounded in unsurpassed perfect awakening. By me, those beings shall have first been inspired in the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, and up to established in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; and by me, the seed of their roots of merit shall have been cast into unsurpassed <s>nirvāṇa</s>; and they shall have been liberated from the lower realms; and they shall have been established in the accumulation of wisdom and merit, dwelling and abiding; and they shall have been brought near to the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields; so that they may receive prophecy in unsurpassed perfect awakening; and they shall have attained <s>samādhi</s>, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience); and they shall have entered upon the stages; and by me, those beings shall have been inspired toward the aspiration for the splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields and shall have been trained. And they shall accept such splendid qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields as they wish — and those, at that time, when the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> has been entered, when the sun of the <s>Jina</s> <s>Krakutsanda</s> has risen, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 233.

children.text:
) tiṣṭhato yāpayataḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayataḥ paśyeyaṃ; tadāhaṃ krakutsandasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyācirābhisaṃbuddhasya sakāśamupasaṃkrameyaṃ, upasaṃkramya vividhāṃ pūjāṃ kuryāṃ, praśnaṃ ca pṛccheyaṃ, pravrajeyaṃ, śīlaśrutasamādhāvabhiyujyeyaṃ, agradharmadeśakaśca bhaveyaṃ / ye ca tasmin samaye dagdhasantānāḥ sattvā akuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dṛṣṭimārgasaṃpratipannā ānantaryakārakāḥ kumārgavihanyamānāsteṣāṃ mahāsaṅkaṭaprāptānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, tāṃścāhaṃ vaineyāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāṃ / astāṃgate jinasūrye tadāhamanābhogena buddhakāryaṃ kuryāṃ yāvadvarṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ triṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu sattvānniyojayeyaṃ / tasmiṃśca kāle 'tikrānte devalokaṃ gatvā devānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, vaineyāṃśca pratigṛhṇīyāṃ, yāvadviṃśativarṣaśataṃ sattvānāmāyurbhaviṣyati / sattvā aiśvaryakularūpamadamattā matsariṇo bhaviṣyanti / pañcakaṣāyāndhakāraprakṣiptāḥ sattvāḥ tīvrarāgāstīvradveṣāstīvramohāstivramānāstīvrapāperṣyāmatsariṇo 'dharmarāgaraktā adharmabhogaparyeṣṭino mithyādṛṣṭayo viparītadarśanā
āryasaptadhanavirahitā (
children.translated_text: ) abiding and teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, I would behold him; then I would approach the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakutsanda</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, soon after his awakening, and having approached, I would perform various acts of worship, ask questions, go forth into homelessness, and apply myself to moral conduct, learning, and concentration, and I would become a foremost teacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. And at that time, whatever beings whose mental continua are scorched, who have fallen into the accumulation of unwholesome roots, who have entered upon the path of wrong views, who commit the <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds, who are obstructed on wrong paths — to those beings who have reached great distress I would teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and I would accept those who are to be trained. When the sun of the Conqueror has set, then I would effortlessly perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work, even among people whose lifespan is a hundred years, engaging beings in the three bases of meritorious action. And when that time has passed, I would go to the heavenly realm and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>devas</s> (gods), and accept those who are to be trained, until the time when beings' lifespan will be two hundred years. Beings will be intoxicated by the pride of sovereignty, family, and beauty, and will become envious. Beings cast into the darkness of the five degeneracies will have intense desire, intense hatred, intense delusion, intense pride, intense sinful jealousy and envy — attached to unrighteous desires, seeking unrighteous enjoyments, holding wrong views, of perverted vision, devoid of the seven noble treasures (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 234.

children.text: ) amātṛjñā apitṛjñā aśrāmaṇyā abrāhmaṇyā akṛtyakarā apuṇyakarā aparalokabhayadarśino 'nabhiyuktāstriṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu anarthikāstribhiryānairanabhiyuktāstriṣu sucariteṣu abhiyuktāstriṣu duścariteṣu anabhiyuktā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu abhiyuktā daśasvakuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu caturviparyāsopahatāścaturvipattisaṃsthānāścaturmāravaśagatāścaturbhiroghairuhyamānāḥ pañcanīvaraṇavaśagatāḥ sattvā bhaviṣyanti / ṣaḍindriyamadamattā aṣṭamithyātvapratipannāḥ kāmasaṅkaṭaprāptā anuśayasamutthāpakā anarthikā devamanuṣyaśrīsaṃpattibhirviparītadṛṣṭikāḥ kumārge vihanyamānā ānantaryakārakāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakā āryāpavādakāḥ sarvakuśalamūlaparihīṇā dhvāṅkṣāmukharā akṛtajñā muṣṭasmṛtayaḥ kuśalajugupsakā duḥprajñā alpaśrutā duḥśīlāḥ kuhakā matsariṇaḥ parasparābhāṣakā anyonyāgauravāḥ kuśīdā vikalendriyā durbalāścīvaravirahitā akalyāṇamitrasaṃgṛhītā garbhāśayasmṛtipraṇaṣṭā vividharogapahatāḥ kliṣṭā durvarṇā avahoṭimakā ahrīkā anapatrāpyāḥ parasparabhītā (
children.translated_text: ) — not knowing their mothers, not knowing their fathers, without respect for ascetics, without respect for brahmins, not doing what ought to be done, not performing meritorious deeds, not seeing the fear of the next world, not devoted to the three bases of meritorious action, without interest in the three vehicles, not devoted to the three kinds of good conduct, devoted to the three kinds of bad conduct, not devoted to the ten wholesome courses of action, devoted to the ten unwholesome courses of action — beings will be afflicted by the four perversions, established in the four calamities, gone under the power of the four <s>Māras</s>, carried along by the four floods, gone under the power of the five hindrances.
