Intoxicated by the pride of the six sense-faculties, having entered upon the eight wrong paths, fallen into the straits of sensual desire, arousing the latent tendencies, without interest in the prosperity of gods and humans, of perverted views, obstructed on wrong paths, committing <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds, rejecting the <s>Saddharma</s> (True Dharma), reviling the noble ones, having lost all wholesome roots of merit, crow-tongued, ungrateful, of lost mindfulness, disgusted by wholesome deeds, of poor wisdom, of little learning, of poor morality, deceitful, envious, slandering one another, without mutual respect, lazy, with defective sense-faculties, weak, bereft of robes, taken in by bad companions, having lost the memory of womb-existence, afflicted by various diseases, defiled, of ugly complexion, stooped, shameless, without moral dread, mutually fearful (

children.translated_text: ) — within a single morning meal they commit much bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct; those beings will be adherents of the praised eternalist view. With minds obsessed with the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), with minds greedy for the five strands of sensual pleasure, with malicious minds, with corrupt minds, with hostile minds, with minds bent on harm, with turbid minds, with harsh minds, with agitated minds, with untamed minds, with minds intent on harm, with distracted minds, with minds obsessed with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), with unsettled minds, with minds of mutual aggression, with minds of mutual killing, with minds devoid of <s>Dharma</s>, with immature minds, with minds hostile to <s>dharmas</s>, with minds that have generated unwholesomeness, with minds not seeking peaceful <s>nirvāṇa</s>, with minds unworthy of offerings, with minds that give rise to all fetters and bonds, with minds not understanding sickness, old age, and death, with minds dominated by all fetters, with minds embracing all hindrances, with minds that cast down the banner of <s>Dharma</s>, with minds that raise up the banner of views, with minds that disparage one another, with minds that devour one another, with minds that oppress others through power and authority, with minds that harbor hatred, with minds that strike one another, with minds insatiable in sensual pleasures (

bhaviṣyanti / ime cātra śabdāḥ parasparāntikācchṛṇvanti, narakaśabdastiryagyoniśabdo yamalokaśabdo vyādhiśabdo jarāśabdo maraṇaśabdo vadhakaśabdo 'kṣaṇaśabdo nityāriśabdo haḍinigaḍabandhanacārakaśabdo daṇḍapīḍanāśabdo 'varṇakrośanaparibhāṣaṇāśabdaḥ saṃdhicchedanaśabdo gaṇacchedanaśabdaścauryaśabdaḥ paracakraśabdo durbhikṣaśabdaḥ kāmamithyācāraśabdo mṛṣāvādaśabda utpātaśabdaḥ paiśunyaśabdaḥ paruṣaśabdaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpaśabda īrṣyāmātsaryaśabda āgrahaparigrahaśabdo 'haṅkāramamakāraśabdaḥ priyāpriyaśabda iṣṭāniṣṭaśabdaḥ priyaviprayogaśabdaḥ krayavikrayaśabdo 'nyonyadāsaviheṭhanāśabdo garbhavāsaśabdo durgandhaśabdaḥ śītaśabda uṣṇaśabdo jighatsāpipāsāśabdaḥ śrāntaklāntavedanāśabdaḥ kṛṣikarmāntaśabdo vividhakarmaśilpaparikhinnaśabdo (
children.translated_text: ) with minds of stinginess toward all possessions, with ungrateful minds, with minds that violate others' wives, with minds of malice and harm, with minds without aspiration — such will beings be at that time. And these sounds they will hear from one another: the sound of hell, the sound of the animal realm, the sound of <s>Yama</s>'s world, the sound of sickness, the sound of old age, the sound of death, the sound of killing, the sound of inopportune birth, the sound of perpetual enmity, the sound of chains, fetters, bonds, and prison guards, the sound of punishment and torment, the sound of blame, abuse, and insult, the sound of breaking joints, the sound of severing limbs, the sound of theft, the sound of invading armies, the sound of famine, the sound of sexual misconduct, the sound of falsehood, the sound of calamity, the sound of slander, the sound of harsh speech, the sound of idle chatter, the sound of jealousy and envy, the sound of grasping and possessiveness, the sound of ego and 'mine,' the sound of pleasant and unpleasant, the sound of desired and undesired, the sound of separation from the beloved, the sound of buying and selling, the sound of mutual servitude and harm, the sound of womb-existence, the sound of foul smells, the sound of cold, the sound of heat, the sound of hunger and thirst, the sound of weariness, exhaustion, and pain, the sound of agricultural toil, the sound of weariness from various works and crafts (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 237.

children.text: ) vividharogopahataśabdaḥ, imāṃśca te sattvāḥ parasparasyāntikācchṛṇvanti / evaṃrūpaiḥ parihīṇakuśalamūlaiḥ parihīṇakalyāṇamitrairduṣṭacittaiḥ sattvaistasmin kāle sahālokadhāturākīrṇā bhaviṣyati / ujjhitāśca te sattvā bhaviṣyanti sarvajñaiḥ śūnyairbuddhakṣetrairyathānnapānadamasaṃyamakuśalakarmakriyākuśalasamavadhānā āryāṣṭāṅgena mārgeṇa virahitāstamastamaḥparāyaṇāḥ pragāḍhakarmapratyayena te sattvāstasmin samaye bhadrakalpe viṃśottaravarṣaśatāyuṣkeṣu pratyājāyiṣyanti / teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ karmapratyayena sahabuddhakṣetraṃ hīnaṃ bhaviṣyati, sarvairavaruptakuśalamūlaiḥ sattvaiḥ parivarjitaṃ, salavaṇā ca pṛthivī bhaviṣyati, pāṣāṇaśarkarapāṃśuśīlā parvatotkūlā ca dharaṇī bhaviṣyati, paruṣadaṃśamaśakāśīviṣacaṇḍamṛgapakṣibhirākīrṇā bhaviṣyati, viṣamakālakaluṣā vāyavo vāsyanti, viṣamakālavirasalavaṇavimiśrā aśanivarṣā patiṣyanti; tathārūpāḥ pṛthivyāṃ śaṣpauṣadhitṛṇavṛkṣā patrapuṣpaphalā dhānyarasāḥ sattvānāmannapānabhogaparibhogaviṣamāḥ (
children.translated_text: ) the sound of being afflicted by various diseases — these sounds those beings hear from one another. With such beings — bereft of wholesome roots, bereft of good companions, of malicious minds — at that time the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm will be filled. Those beings will have been abandoned by the omniscient ones, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid [of Buddhas]; without food, drink, taming, restraint, wholesome actions, ritual activities, or wholesome accumulations, bereft of the noble eightfold path, heading into ever deeper darkness — through the conditions of profound <s>karma</s>, those beings at that time will be reborn in the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon) when lifespan is one hundred and twenty years. Through the <s>karma</s>-conditions of those beings, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> itself will become degraded, abandoned by all beings who have planted wholesome roots; the earth will be saline, filled with stones, gravel, dust, and rocks, the ground will be mountainous and uneven, infested with biting flies, mosquitoes, venomous snakes, and fierce beasts and birds; unwholesome, untimely, turbid winds will blow; unwholesome, untimely, tasteless, saline, mixed hailstorms will fall. Such will the grasses, herbs, plants, trees, leaves, flowers, fruits, and grains on the earth be — the food, drink, enjoyments, and provisions of beings will be unwholesome (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 238.

body.translated_text: For that long, Venerable Blessed One, for the sake of those whose continuity is burnt, who are bereft of roots of merit, I shall practice the course with exceedingly intense vigor and force; and for that long in <s>saṃsāra</s>, for the sake of beings, I shall endure various fierce, terrible, and dreadful sufferings — until, when many incalculable [aeons] equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> have passed and the second incalculable [aeon] equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> has been entered, in the <s>Bhadra</s> great <s>kalpa</s>, when the young man <s>Jyotipāla</s> attains unsurpassed perfect awakening and becomes the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Krakutsanda</s> — at that time, with the noble eye of wisdom, I shall behold in the ten directions, in world-realms as numerous as the atoms of a thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones dwelling and abiding, having turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. Those whose continuity is burnt, who have the accumulation of unwholesome roots, (

yadāhaṃ māturdakṣiṇe kukṣāvabhiniṣkrameyaṃ, punarapi ca sarvāvantaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetramudāreṇāvabhāsena aphureyaṃ; (

) — they would all see, touch, and recognize that radiance. While reflecting on <s>saṃsāra</s>, filled with revulsion toward suffering, they would generate at least the wish for <s>nirvāṇa</s> and minds desiring the pacification of afflictions. This would be the first planting of the supreme seed of the path. When I, knowing all the methods of <s>dharmas</s>, expounding all <s>samādhis</s>, through the one <s>Dharma</s>-gateway and by the teaching of the final <s>kalpa</s>, with concentrated mind, would dwell for ten months in my mother's womb; and as many beings as I would liberate from <s>saṃsāra</s> — those wearied ones — when I have attained Buddhahood, those beings would behold me dwelling in the mother's womb for ten months, seated cross-legged with concentrated mind, like a jewel-embryo visible [through crystal]. And when the ten months have elapsed, through the accumulation of all merit and by <s>samādhi</s>, I would cause this entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and the earth to tremble in six ways — upward to the limit of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> abode and downward to the limit of the golden wheel, I would cause it to tremble in six ways. And whatever beings at that time are reborn in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — in the hells, or up to among humans — them I would awaken.
When I would emerge from my mother's right side, again I would suffuse this entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with magnificent radiance; (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 240.

children.text: ) tadāpi tasmin samaye sarvān sahe buddhakṣetre sattvān saṃcodayeyaṃ, anavaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ santāne nirvāṇabījaṃ prakṣipeyaṃ, avaropitanirvāṇabījasantatīnāṃ sattvānāṃ samādhyaṅkuramavaropayeyaṃ / yadā cāhaṃ caraṇatalena dharaṇīṃ spṛśeyaṃ sarvāvatī tasmin samaye sahe buddhakṣetre ṣaḍvikāraṃ dharaṇīṃ cālayeyaṃ prakaṃpayeyaṃ kṣobhayeyaṃ yāvat kāñcanacakraparyantena; tadāhaṃ tasmin samaye sattvān jalaniśritāṃ kṣitiniśritāṃ khaniśritāṃ caturyoniparyāpannāṃ pañcagatisaṃniśritāṃ tān sarvān ahaṃ pratibodhayeyaṃ, yeṣāṃ santāne sattvānāmanutpannaṃ samādhānāṅkuraṃ ropayeyaṃ, dṛḍhasamādhānāṅkurāṃ tribhiryānairavaivartikāṃ sthāpayeyaṃ / sahajātamātrasya ca me yāvadeva tasmin sahe buddhakṣetre mahābrahmāṇo vā mārā vā śakrā vā candrā vā sūryā vā lokapālā vā mahānāgarājā vāsurendrā vā aupapādukā vā maharddhikā vā yakṣarākṣasanāgāsurā vā sarve mama pūjākarmaṇe upasaṃkrāmeyuḥ / sahajātamātraścāhaṃ saptapadāni prakrāmeyaṃ / sarvapuṇyasamuccayenāhaṃ samādhinā tathārūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ yattatsarvāvatī sā parṣattribhiryānaiḥ (
children.translated_text: ) and at that time too I would rouse all beings in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. For those beings whose wholesome roots have not been planted, I would cast the seed of <s>nirvāṇa</s> into their mental continua; for those beings in whose continua the seed of <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been planted, I would plant the sprout of <s>samādhi</s>. And when I would touch the earth with the sole of my foot, at that time in the entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> I would cause the earth to tremble, quake, and shake in six ways, down to the limit of the golden wheel. Then at that time I would awaken all beings — those dwelling in water, those dwelling on land, those dwelling in the sky, those belonging to the four modes of birth, those abiding in the five destinies — all of them I would awaken. For those beings in whose continua the sprout of concentration has not yet arisen, I would plant it; for those with firmly established sprouts of concentration, I would establish them in non-retrogression through the three vehicles. And at the very moment of my birth, however many great <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Māras</s>, <s>Śakras</s>, moons, suns, <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), great <s>Nāga</s> kings, <s>Asura</s> lords, or beings of spontaneous birth, or powerful <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> there are — all would come to worship me. And at the very moment of my birth, I would take seven steps. Through the accumulation of all merit and by <s>samādhi</s>, I would teach such a <s>Dharma</s> that the entire assembly through the three vehicles (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 241.

children.text: ) prasādaṃ pratilaṃbhayet / ye ca tatra parṣadi sattvāḥ śrāvakayānikā bhaveyuste caramabhavikā mama vaineyā bhavikā; ye ca tatra sattvāḥ pratyekabuddhayānikā bhaveyuste vairocanakusumāṃ kṣāntiṃ pratilabheyuḥ; ye ca tatra sattvā anuttaramahāyānikā bhaveyuste sarve vajradharasamudrasaṃkopitaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheran, tena ca samādhinā tisrā bhūmīḥ samatikrāmeyuḥ / yadahaṃ snāpanamiccheyaṃ ye ca tatra mahānāgarājāno viśiṣṭatarā bhaveyuḥ te māṃ snāpayeyuḥ; ye ca sattvā māṃ snāpayamānaṃ paśyeyuste sarve tribhiryānairevaṃrūpān guṇānadhigaccheyuḥ yathā proktaṃ / ye ca māṃ sattvā rathamabhirohantaṃ samanupaśyeyurvistareṇa kumārakrīḍavividhaśilpasthānakarmasthānāsanāni ca dadarśa śikṣāpanayogyaṃ stryagāre pañca kāmaguṇaratikrīḍārdharātrāvudvignaniṣkramaṇālaṅkāravibhūṣaṇacchoraṇaṃ lohitavastrābhīkṣṇaṃ kāṣāyavastraparyeṣaṇabodhivṛkṣopasaṃkramaṇaṃ, ye ca sattvā māmupasaṃkrāmantaṃ paśyeyuḥ, teṣāṃ cāhaṃ sattvānāṃ sarvapuṇyasamuccayena (
children.translated_text: ) would attain faith. And those beings in that assembly who follow the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle — they, in their final existence, would be those to be trained by me, capable of it. And those beings there who follow the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle would attain the forbearance called <s>Vairocanakusuma</s>. And those beings there who follow the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) — they would all attain the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vajradharasamudrasaṃkopita</s> (Agitation of the Vajra-Holding Ocean), and through that <s>samādhi</s> they would transcend three <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). When I would wish to be bathed, the most distinguished among the great <s>Nāga</s> kings would bathe me; and whatever beings would see me being bathed — they would all, through the three vehicles, attain such qualities as have been described. And whatever beings would see me mounting a chariot — and in detail: would see the princely sports, various craft-stations, work-stations, and seats, the training-worthy instruction, the five strands of sensual pleasure and sport in the women's quarters, the disenchanted departure at midnight, the casting off of ornaments and adornments, the repeated [donning of] red garments, the seeking of saffron robes, the approach to the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree — and whatever beings would see me approaching, to those beings I, through the accumulation of all merit (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 242.

) samādhinā tathārūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ yathā te sattvāstribhiryānaistīvracchandā udyujyeyuḥ / ye ca tatra sattvāḥ pratyekabuddhayānikāste sarve vairocanakusumāṃ kṣāntiṃ pratilabheyuḥ; yaiśca mahāyānabījaṃ prakṣiptaṃ bhavet te sarve vajradharasamudrasaṃkopitaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabheyustena ca samādhinā tisro bhūmiratikrāmeyuḥ / svayaṃ cāhaṃ tṛṇasaṃstaraṇaṃ gṛhṇīyāṃ bodhivṛkṣamūlavajrāsane prajñapayeyaṃ niṣīdeyaṃ paryaṅkamābadhvā ṛjukena kāyena; tathārūpamahamāsphānakaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyāyeyaṃ, āśvāsapraśvāsā vyupaśameyaṃ; ekavāraṃ divasena dhyānādvyuttiṣṭheyaṃ,
vyutthāya cāhamardhatilakaphalamāhāramāhareyaṃ, ardhaṃ pratigrāhakasyānuprayaccheyaṃ / tāvacciraṃ cāhamevaṃrūpāṃ duṣkaracārikāṃ careyaṃ, yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaparyantena sarve devā ye sahe buddhakṣetre paryāpannāsta upasaṃkrāmeyurmama ca pūjāṃ kurvāṇāḥ, sarve me sākṣiṇaḥ syurduṣkaracaryāyāṃ / yaiśca tatra śrāvakayāne bījamavaruptaṃ syātteṣāṃ bhadanta bhagavan kleśavyupaśamāya santāne bhaveyaṃ, caramabhavikāśca mama vaineyā bhaveyuḥ; ye pratyekabuddhayānikā (
children.translated_text: ) by that <s>samādhi</s>, may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that those beings would zealously strive through the three vehicles with intense aspiration. And may those beings there who are of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle all attain the <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) called <s>Vairocanakusumā</s> (Vairocana Flower); and those in whom the <s>Mahāyāna</s> seed has been planted may all attain the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vajradharasamudrasaṃkopita</s> (Shaken by the Ocean of the Vajra-Holder), and by that <s>samādhi</s> may they transcend three stages. And may I myself take a seat of grass, prepare it at the foot of the <s>bodhi</s>-tree on the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne), and sit down with legs crossed and body upright. May I practice such a <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) of extraordinary power, and may my inhalations and exhalations cease. Once a day may I rise from <s>dhyāna</s>, and upon rising, may I take as food half a grain of sesame, and give the other half to the one who offers it. And may I practice such austere conduct for as long as it takes until all gods, up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (Highest) heaven, who are comprised within the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, approach me and make offerings, and may they all be my witnesses in this austere practice. And for those in whom the seed of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle has been planted, O venerable Blessed One, may I be the [final] link in their continuum for the pacification of afflictions, and may those in their last existence become my trainees; and those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 243.

children.text: ) yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / evaṃ nāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragapretapiśācakumbhāṇḍāḥ pañcābhijñā ṛṣaya upasaṃkrāmeyurmama pūjākarmaṇe, sarve ca me sākṣiṇo bhaveyurduṣkaracaryāyāṃ; ye ca śrāvakayānikā yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / ye ca tatra cāturdvīpikāyāmanyatīrthikā lūhatapo vrataduṣkaracārikāṃ caranti, teṣāṃ cāmānuṣā ārocayeyuḥ / "na yūyaṃ duṣkarakārakā, yathāsmin pradeśe caramabhaviko bodhisattvo duṣkaracārikāṃ carati, tathārūpaṃ dhyāyati hṛdaye manaskāraṃ badhnāti praśrabdhakāyasaṃskāraḥ praśrabdhavāksaṃskāraḥ praśāntāścāsya praśvāsāśvāsāḥ; dinedine caikāṃ velāṃ dhyānādvyutthitvārdhatilakaphalamāhāramāharati / sā duṣkaracaryā maharddhikā sā mahāphalā mahāvistārā, na cireṇāsau anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / sacenna śraddhadhvaṃ gacchata svayaṃ paśyata" / te ca tāṃ duṣkaracaryāmutsṛjya mama duṣkaracaryāṃ dṛṣṭvā yeṣāṃ śrāvakayānasantānabījāṅkuraṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ syāt, yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ / ye manuṣyarājā (
children.translated_text: ) as previously stated. Likewise may <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), and <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, as well as sages of the five <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), approach me for the purpose of worship, and may they all be my witnesses in the austere practice; and those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle — as previously stated. And whatever non-Buddhist ascetics in that four-continent world-system practice vows and austerities of severe asceticism, may non-human beings declare to them: 'You are not performers of austerities, for in this place a <s>bodhisattva</s> in his final existence practices austere conduct, meditating in such a manner, fixing attention in his heart, with body-formations calmed, speech-formations calmed, and inhalations and exhalations stilled; and day by day, rising once from <s>dhyāna</s>, he takes as food half a grain of sesame. That austere practice is of great supernatural power, of great fruit, of vast scope — before long he will attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. If you do not believe it, go and see for yourselves.' And may they, abandoning their own austere practices and having seen my austere practice — those in whom the seed and sprout of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle continuum is established — as previously stated. And whatever human kings (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 244.

children.text: ) vā bhaṭṭā vā naigamajānapadā gṛhasthapravrajitā gṛhāgārasaṃpannāste 'pi mama duṣkaracaryāmupasaṃkrāmeyuryāvacchrāvakayānikā yathā pūrvoktaṃ / yaśca mātṛgrāmo mama darśanayopasaṃkramet, sa tasya paścimako mātṛgrāmapratilābho bhaved iti, ye śrāvakayānikā yathā pūrvoktaṃ / ye mṛgapakṣiṇo duṣkaraṃ caramāṇaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ paśyeyussa teṣāṃ paścimakastiryagyonipratilābho bhaved iti; yaiśca mṛgapakṣibhiḥ śrāvakayāne bījānyavaropitāni tenaikajātipratibaddhā mama caiva vaineyā bhaveyurye pratyekabuddhayānā yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ / evaṃvidhāḥ kṣudrakāstiryagyonikā vaktavyā, evaṃ pretā vaktavyāstāvacciraṃ cāhamevaṃrūpāṃ duṣkaracaryāṃ careyaṃ ekaparyaṅkena yāvad bahusattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi duṣkaracaryāyāṃ sākṣibhūtā bhaveyuḥ āścaryaprāptāśca, teṣāṃ ca santāne 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ mokṣabījāṃ praropayeyaṃ / tathārūpāmahaṃ duṣkaracaryāṃ careyaṃ yathā na pūrvaṃ kenacit sattvasaṃkhyātena anyatīrthikena vā śrāvakayānikena vā pratyekabuddhayānikena vā anuttaramahāyānikena vā evaṃ duṣkaracaryācīrṇapūrvaḥ syāt; na ca punaḥ paścāt kaścit sattvasaṃkhyātaścaret anyatīrthikā vā evaṃrūpāṃ duṣkaracārikāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) or officials, townsfolk and country people, householders and renunciants, and those established in the household life — may they too approach my austere practice, and those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle as previously stated. And whatever women come to see me, may that be their last obtaining of a female form; those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle as previously stated. Whatever deer and birds see me seated practicing austerities, may that be their last obtaining of an animal birth; and whatever deer and birds have seeds of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle planted in them, may they be bound to one more birth and become my very trainees; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle as previously stated. Likewise for small creatures of animal birth, likewise for <s>pretas</s>. And may I practice such austere conduct in a single cross-legged posture for as long as it takes until many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings have become witnesses of the austere practice and have been filled with wonder, and may I plant seeds of liberation in the continuum of those immeasurable and incalculable beings. May I practice such austere conduct as has never before been practiced by any being reckoned among non-Buddhist ascetics, those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, or those of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>; nor shall anyone afterward, any being reckoned among non-Buddhist ascetics, be able to practice such austere conduct (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 245.

children.text:
) śaktāṃścarantu yathāhaṃ careyaṃ / aprāptāyāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tadāhaṃ puruṣakāraṃ kuryāṃ sabalakāyaṃ māraṃ parājayeyaṃ, sāvaśeṣakarmaphalaṃ cādhiṣṭhiheyaṃ, kleśamāraṃ jineyaṃ, anuttarāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / tadahamekasattvasya santāne 'rhatvaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, tathā dvitīyasya tathā tṛtīyasya tathā caturthasya dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, santāne cārhatvaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ / ekaikasya sattvasyārthamahaṃ śatasahasraśaḥ prātihāryāṇi
darśayeyaṃ, tasya ca santāne samyagdṛṣṭiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, bahuni ca dharmārthavyañjanasahasrāṇi bhāṣayeyaṃ, yathā śaktyā ca phale pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ / vajramayāṃśca sattvānāṃ santāne kleśaparvatāṃ jñānavajreṇa bhindyāṃ triyānena vyavasthānena dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / ekasattvasyārthāyāhaṃ bahuyojanaśatāni padbhyāṃ gaccheyaṃ dharmadeśanārthamabhayapade pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ / apratiṣedhaśca me śāsane bhavet pravrajyāyāḥ, durbalasya muṣṭasmṛteḥ vibhrāntacittasya mukharapragalbhacittasya praduṣṭacittasya duḥprajñacittasya bahukleśākulacittasya mātṛgrāmasya mama śāsane pravrajyopasaṃpadbhavet / (
children.translated_text: ) as I shall practice. Before attaining <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), may I exert my manly effort, vanquish <s>Māra</s> together with his host, master the residual fruits of <s>karma</s>, conquer the <s>Māra</s> of afflictions, and attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Then may I establish one being's continuum in <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship), likewise a second, likewise a third, likewise may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to a fourth and establish arhatship in their continuum. For each and every being, may I display hundreds of thousands of miracles, establish right view in their continuum, and speak many thousands of words concerning the meaning and letter of the <s>Dharma</s>, and establish them in the fruit according to their capacity. And may I split the diamond-like mountains of afflictions in beings' mind-streams with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) of wisdom, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> through the arrangement of the three vehicles. For the sake of a single being, may I walk many hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> on foot for the purpose of teaching the <s>Dharma</s> and establishing them in the state of fearlessness. And in my teaching, may there be no prohibition against ordination — even for the weak, the forgetful, the confused in mind, the garrulous and bold-minded, the corrupt-minded, the dull-witted, the mind overwhelmed by many afflictions, and for women — may ordination and full admission in my teaching be available. (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 246.

children.text: ) catasraśca me parṣāḥ syurbhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopasikāḥ / bahujanaprabhūtaṃ me śāsanaṃ bhavet devānāṃ satyadarśanaṃ yakṣāṇāṃ nāgānāmasurāṇāmāryāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgata upoṣadhavāsaḥ, yāvattiryagyonigatānāmapi brahmacaryāvāso bhavet /
children.translated_text: ) And may I have four assemblies: <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers). May my teaching abound with many people. May there be vision of truth for the gods, and for <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> the observance of the <s>upoṣadha</s> (sabbath) endowed with the noble eightfold [path]; and even for those gone to animal births may there be the dwelling in the holy life.

body.translated_text: At that time, I would descend from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, enter the womb of the chief queen of a distinguished <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) lineage, a sovereign royal family, for the purpose of ripening the wholesome roots of beings to be trained. At that time, I would suffuse this entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with magnificent radiance — upward to the limit of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> abode, downward to the limit of the golden wheel — I would suffuse it with magnificent radiance. And whatever beings at that time are reborn in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — in the hells, the animal realm, <s>Yama</s>'s world, or among gods and humans (

body.text: bodhiprāptasya ca me bhadanta bhagavan ye sattvā mama praduṣṭacittā vadhakacittāḥ śastreṇa vāgninā vā śaktyā va vividhena vā praharaṇenopasaṃkrāmeyuḥ, rukṣaiḥ paruṣairvacanairākrośeyuḥ paribhāṣeyurdigvidikṣu vāyaśaḥśabdaṃ cāreyuḥ, viṣasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ vāhārapānamupanāmayeyuḥ; evaṃrūpāṃ karmaphalānaparikṣīṇānadhiṣṭhihitvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / yathā bodhiprāptasya me sattvāḥ pūrvaṃ vaireṇa vadhakopakaraṇaprayogena paruṣavacanavividhapraharaṇaviṣānnapānasaṃsṛṣṭenopasaṃkrāmeyuḥ rudhiraṃ ca me utpādayeyuḥ, teṣāṃ sattvānāmahaṃ śīlaśrutasamādhimahākaruṇābhāvitena brahmasvaraghoṣadundubhinarditena svareṇa tathārūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, yatteṣāṃ cittāni prasādayeyaṃ kuśale ca niyojayeyaṃ; yathā te sattvāḥ karmāvaraṇaṃ deśayeyuḥ, āpatyāṃ saṃvaramāpadyeyuḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 247.

children.text: ) na ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ svarge mokṣaphale vairāgye āśravakṣaye vā āvaraṇakarma bhaved iti, mama cātrāparikṣīṇakarmaphalakṣīṇavyantīkṛtaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: ) and that their obstructive <s>karma</s> may not be a hindrance to heaven, the fruit of liberation, dispassion, or the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements); and for me, those unexhausted fruits of <s>karma</s> shall be exhausted and extinguished.

body.translated_text: And when I have attained awakening, O venerable Blessed One, whatever beings approach me with hostile intent, with murderous intent, with weapons or fire or spears or various instruments of attack, who revile me and abuse me with harsh and rough words, who spread the sound of ill-repute in all directions, who offer me food and drink mixed with poison — may I, having mastered such unexhausted fruits of <s>karma</s>, attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And when I have attained awakening, whatever beings approach me out of former enmity, with instruments of murder, with harsh words, with various weapons, with food and drink mixed with poison, and draw my blood — to those beings may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in such a voice, cultivated through moral conduct, learning, <s>samādhi</s>, and great compassion, with the sound of the <s>Brahma</s>-voice, like a great drum, that I should inspire faith in their minds and engage them in the wholesome; so that those beings may confess their obstructive <s>karma</s> and undertake the restraint of their transgressions, (

body.text: bodhiprāptasya ca me bhadanta bhagavan yāvanto mama romakūpā bhaveyustāvanto divasaṃ buddhavigrahānnirmiṇuyāṃ dvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtānaśītibhiranuvyañjanaistāṃścāhaṃ buddhavigrahān śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu preṣayeyaṃ, aśūnyeṣu ca preṣayeyaṃ, pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu preṣayeyaṃ / ye cāpi teṣu buddhakṣetreṣvānantaryakārakāḥ sattvā bhaveyuḥ saddharmapratikṣepakāḥ āryāpavādakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānakāḥ, ye 'pi tatra sattvāḥ śrāvakayānasaṃprasthitāḥ pratyekabuddhayānasaṃprasthitā mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ śikṣāyāṃ kalmāṣakāriṇaḥ chidracāriṇaḥ mūlāpattimāpannāḥ dagdhasantānāḥ śubhamārgapraṇaṣṭāḥ saṃsārāṭavīsaṃprasthitāḥ kumārgavihanyamānā mahāsaṅkaṭaprāptāḥ, tathārūpāḥ sattvāḥ sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrādeko buddhavigraha ekadivase (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 248.

children.text: ) sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayet / ye sattvā maheśvarabhaktikāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ maheśvararūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / sahe ca buddhakṣetre mama varṇaṃ bhāṣayeyustatra ca sattvānāṃ praṇidhānamudyojayeyaṃ / te ca sattvā mama varṇaṃ śrutvā mamaiva buddhakṣetre praṇidhānaṃ kurvīran, upapattiṃ cākāṅkṣeyuḥ / yādyahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ maraṇakālasamaye purataḥ na tiṣṭheyaṃ dharmaṃ na deśayeyaṃ cittaṃ na saṃprasādayeyaṃ, mā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / yadi me sattvāḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā durgatīṣūpapadyeyurna ca mama buddhakṣetre manuṣyapratilābhaṃ labheyuḥ, sarve mama dharmā saṃmoṣaṃ gaccheyurmā ca me pratibhāyeyurmā cāhaṃ śakyaṃ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ niṣpādayituṃ / ye sattvā nārāyaṇabhaktikā yāvatte sattvāḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā durgatiṃ prapateyustanmā cāhaṃ śakyaṃ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ niṣpādayituṃ /
children.translated_text: ) teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. To whatever beings are devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord Śiva), may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>. And may they proclaim my qualities in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, and there may I inspire beings to make aspirations. And having heard my qualities, may those beings make their aspirations toward my very <s>Buddha</s>-field and desire rebirth there. And if, O venerable Blessed One, I do not stand before those beings at the time of their death, do not teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and do not inspire faith in their minds — then may I not attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. If my beings, having died, are reborn in the lower realms and do not obtain human rebirth in my <s>Buddha</s>-field, may all my <s>dharmas</s> be forgotten and may they not arise for me, and may I not be able to accomplish the complete <s>Buddha</s>'s work. Whatever beings are devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (Viṣṇu) — likewise, if those beings having died fall into the lower realms, then may I not be able to accomplish the complete <s>Buddha</s>'s work.

body.translated_text: And when I have attained awakening, O venerable Blessed One, may I each day emanate as many <s>Buddha</s>-forms as there are pores in my body, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being and the eighty minor marks, and may I send those <s>Buddha</s>-forms to empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields, to non-empty [<s>Buddha</s>-fields], and to <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the five defilements. And whatever beings in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, reject the <s>Saddharma</s>, slander the Noble Ones, and up to those who accumulate unwholesome roots — and whatever beings there who have set forth in the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, or the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who act with impurity in the training, who act with breaches, who have committed root transgressions, whose continuum is burnt, who have lost the wholesome path, who have set forth into the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who are obstructed by wrong paths and have fallen into great straits — for such beings, may a single <s>Buddha</s>-form in one day, out of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings (

body.text: bodhiprāptasya ca me sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu sattvā ānantaryakārakā yāvat kumārge vihanyamānā mahāsaṅkaṭaprāptāḥ sattvāḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeran, idaṃ teṣāṃ nimittaṃ pāṃśuvarṇāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 249.

children.text: ) piśācamukhī muṣṭasmṛtayo durgandhā duḥśīlā alpāyuṣkā vividharogopahatā vividhapariṣkāraparihīṇāśca te sattvā bhaviṣyanti; teṣām sattvānāmarthe 'haṃ yāvattasmin samaye sahe lokadhātau cāturdvīpikā bhaveyuḥ, sarvatra ca cāturdvīpikāyāṃ saṃtuṣitabhavanāvataraṇaṃ māturgarbhe cāhaṃ jātumupadarśayeyaṃ, vistareṇa kumārakrīḍāśilpakarmasthānaduṣkaracaryāmāradharṣaṇabodhyabhisaṃbudhyanadharmacakrapravartanaṃ, sarvatra ca cāturdvīpikāsu sakalaṃ buddhakāryamupadarśayeyaṃ, parinirvāṇaṃ yāvaccharīravibhāgamupadarśayeyaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) with <s>piśāca</s>-like (demonic) faces, forgetful, foul-smelling, immoral, short-lived, afflicted by various diseases, and bereft of various provisions — such shall those beings be. For the sake of those beings, at whatever time in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm there are four-continent world-systems, in every four-continent world-system may I display my descent from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, my entry into the mother's womb, and in full — the youthful sports, the training in crafts and occupations, the austere practice, the subjugation of <s>Māra</s>, the attainment of awakening, the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma) — in every four-continent world-system may I display the complete <s>Buddha</s>'s work, and up to the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the distribution of relics.

body.translated_text: And when I have attained awakening, may beings in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields who commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, and up to those obstructed by wrong paths who have fallen into great straits — having died, may they be reborn in my <s>Buddha</s>-field. This shall be the sign for them: those beings shall be of dust-colored complexion, (

body.text: bodhiprāptaścāhaṃ ekapadavyāhareṇa dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / ye sattvāḥ śrāvakayānikāste śrāvakayānakathāpiṭakaṃ dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye sattvāḥ pratyekabuddhavaineyāste pratyekabuddhayānakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyurye sattvā anuttaramahāyānikāste 'nuttaramahāyānakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ / ye sattvāḥ saṃbhāravirahitāste dānakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyurye sattvāḥ puṇyavirahitāḥ sukhasvargābhilāṣināste śīlakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye parasparabhītakaluṣacittāḥ praduṣṭacittāste (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 250.

children.text: ) maitryāvyāhārakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; prāṇātipātikāḥ karuṇādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ya īrṣyāmātsaryābhibhūtāste muditāvyāhārakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye rūpārūpyamadamattacittāste upekṣāvyāhārakathādharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ / ye kāmarāgamadamattacittā aśubhavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye ca sattvā mahāyānikauddhatyavyākulacittopagatāste ānāpānasmṛtivyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye duḥprajñā vā pradīpapratītyasamutpādavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; ye 'lpaśrutavādinaste 'saṃpramoṣaśrutadhāraṇīvipraṇāśavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; kudṛṣṭisaṅkaṭaprāptāḥ śūnyatāvyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; vitarkasamudācāropahatā animittavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitāmājānīyurapraṇihitāpariśuddhopahatā apraṇihitavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; āśayāpariśūddhāḥ pariśuddhāśayavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; vyavakīrṇasamudācāropahatā bodhicittāsaṃpramoṣavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; kṣamaprayogoṣmopahatā (
children.translated_text: ) would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); those who kill living beings would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion); those overcome by envy and miserliness would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy); those whose minds are intoxicated by the pride of form and formless [realms] would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). Those whose minds are intoxicated by the pride of sensual desire would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the impure; and those beings whose minds are agitated and confused by the restlessness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing); those of poor wisdom would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the lamp of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination); those who are of little learning would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the unfailing retention of what has been heard through <s>dhāraṇī</s>; those who have fallen into the straits of wrong views would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); those afflicted by the arising of discursive thought would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the signless; those afflicted by the impure [state of] wishlessness would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the wishless; those of impure disposition would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of purified disposition; those afflicted by the arising of scattered conduct would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of non-forgetfulness of <s>bodhicitta</s>; those afflicted by the patient practice of warmth (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 251.

children.text: ) akṛtrimavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; adhyāśayapraśrabdhopahatā aniśritavyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuḥ; kliṣṭacittāḥ peyālaṃ kalpacittavyāhāreṇa; kuśalasaṃpramoṣacittā vairocanavyāhāreṇa; mārakarmodyuktāḥ śūnyatāvyāhāreṇa; paravadhe saṃpratipannā abhyudgatavyāhāreṇa; vividhakleśopahatacittā vigatavyāhāreṇa; viṣamamārgasaṃpratipannā āvartavyāhāreṇa; mahāyānakautuhalacittā vivartavyāhāreṇa; saṃsārodvignānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ rativyāhāreṇa; kuśalabhūmijñānavagatā amūḍhavyāhāreṇa; parasparāsaṃtuṣṭakuśalamūlānāṃ śrutavyāhāreṇa; parasparāsamacittānāmapratihataraśmivyāhāreṇa; viṣamakarmasaṃpratipannānāṃ kriyāvatāraṇavyāhāreṇa; parṣadbhayopagatānāṃ siṃhaketuvyāhāreṇa; caturmārābhibhūtacittānāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of the unartificial; those afflicted by the relaxation of superior disposition would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the discourse of non-reliance; those of afflicted mind — abbreviated — through the discourse of purified mind; those whose wholesome minds are lost, through the discourse of <s>Vairocana</s> (radiance); those engaged in the deeds of <s>Māra</s>, through the discourse of <s>śūnyatā</s>; those engaged in the killing of others, through the discourse of the exalted; those whose minds are afflicted by various defilements, through the discourse of the departed; those who have entered the uneven path, through the discourse of turning; those whose minds are curious about the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through the discourse of evolution; for <s>bodhisattvas</s> wearied of <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the discourse of delight; those who have entered the knowledge of the wholesome stages, through the discourse of the undeluded; for those whose wholesome roots are mutually unsatisfying, through the discourse of learning; for those of mutually unequal mind, through the discourse of unobstructed radiance; for those engaged in uneven deeds, through the discourse of entering into action; for those overcome by fear of the assembly, through the discourse of the lion-banner; for those whose minds are overcome by the four <s>Māras</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 252.

children.text:
) śūravyāhāreṇa; buddhakṣetrānavabhāsagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ prabhāvyūhavyāhāreṇa; anunayapratighānāṃ śailoccayavyāhāreṇa;
buddhadharmālokanābhibhūtānāṃ dhvajāgrakeyūravyāhāreṇa; mahāprajñāvirahitānāmulkāpātavyāhāreṇa; mohāndhakāragatānāṃ bhāskarapradīpavyāhāreṇa; kṣayāniruktiprayuktānāṃ guṇākaravyāhāreṇa; phenapiṇḍopamātmābhikāṅkṣiṇāṃ nārāyaṇavyāhāreṇa; calācalabuddhīnāṃ sārānugatavyāhāreṇa; avalokitamūrdhānāṃ merudhvajavyāhāreṇa; pūrvapratijñotsṛṣṭānāṃ sāravativyāhāreṇa; cyutābhijñānāṃ vajrapadavyāhāreṇa; bodhimaṇḍābhikāṅkṣiṇāṃ vajramaṇḍavyāhāreṇa; sarvadharmajugupsitānāṃ vajropamavyāhāreṇa; sattvacaritamaprajānatāṃ cāritravativyāhāreṇa; indriyaparāparānabhijñānāṃ prajñāpradīpavyāhāreṇa; paraspararutamaprajānatāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) through the discourse of the hero; for beings who have not attained the radiance of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, through the discourse of the array of radiance; for those of attraction and aversion, through the discourse of the mountain-heap; for those overcome by the illumination of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, through the discourse of the banner-crest armlet; for those lacking great wisdom, through the discourse of the meteor; for those gone into the darkness of delusion, through the discourse of the sun-lamp; for those engaged in the expression of decay, through the discourse of the mine of virtues; for those who desire a self like a mass of foam, through the discourse of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; for those of wavering and unwavering intelligence, through the discourse of following the essence; for those who look upward, through the discourse of the <s>Meru</s>-banner; for those who have abandoned their former vows, through the discourse of the substantive; for those who have lost their <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), through the discourse of the <s>vajra</s>-stage
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 253.

children.text: ) rutapraveśavyāhāreṇa; dharmakāyamapratilabdhānāṃ saddharmakāyavibhāvanavyāhāreṇa; tathāgatadarśanavirahitānāmanimiṣavyāhāreṇa; sarvālaṃbanavigopitānāmaraṇyavyāhāreṇa; dharmacakrapravartanābhikāṅkṣiṇāṃ cakravimalavyāhāreṇa; ahetuvidyāsaṃprasthitānāṃ vidyāpratītyānulomavyāhāreṇa; ekabuddhakṣetraśāśvatadṛṣṭīnāṃ sukṛtavicayavyāhāreṇa; lakṣaṇānuvyañjanānavaruptabījānāmalaṅkāravativyāhāreṇa; vācārutaprabhedāsamarthānāṃ nirhāravativyāhāreṇa; sarvajñajñānābhikāṅkṣiṇāṃ dharmadhātvavikopanavyāhāreṇa; pratyutpannāvartanadharmāṇāṃ dṛḍhavyāhāreṇa; dharmadhātumaprajānatāṃ abhijñāvyāhāreṇa; prajñotsṛṣṭānāmacyutavyāhāreṇa; mārgavigopitānāmavikāravyāhāreṇa; ākāśasamajñānābhikāṅkṣiṇāṃ niṣkiñcanavyāhāreṇa; (
children.translated_text: ) through the discourse of entering into speech; for those who have not attained the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), through the discourse of the manifestation of the true <s>dharmakāya</s>; for those deprived of beholding the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the discourse of the unblinking; for those who conceal all supports, through the discourse of the forest; for those who desire the turning of the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of <s>Dharma</s>), through the discourse of the pure wheel; for those who have set out in knowledge without cause, through the discourse of the conformity to dependent knowledge; for those of the eternalist view regarding a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, through the discourse of the investigation of well-done deeds; for those whose seeds of marks and minor marks are not yet planted, through the discourse of the ornamental; for those incapable of the analysis of vocal speech, through the discourse of the leading forth; for those who desire the knowledge of omniscience, through the discourse of the non-disruption of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>); for those
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 254.

children.text: ) pāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ pariśuddhapratiṣṭhāvyāhāreṇa; aparipūrṇāsaṃgrahavastūnāṃ susaṃgṛhītavyāhāreṇa; brahmavihāravimārgitānāṃ samaprayogavyāhāreṇa; bodhipakṣaratnāparipūrṇānāmavyavasthitaniryāṇavyāhāreṇa; subhāṣitajñānāṃ pramuṣṭacittānāṃ sāgaramudravyāhāreṇa; anutpattikadharmakṣāntikautūhalacittānāṃ niścitavyāhāreṇa; yathāśrutadharmapramuṣṭacittānāmasaṃpramoṣavyāhāreṇa; parasparasubhāṣitāsaṃtuṣṭānāṃ vitimiravyāhāreṇa; triratnāpratilabdhaprasādānāṃ puṇyotsadavyāhāreṇa; dharmamukhapravarṣaṇāsaṃtuṣṭānāṃ dharmameghavyāhāreṇa; triratnocchedadṛṣṭīnāṃ ratnavyūhavyāhāreṇa; jñānārditakarmābhiyuktānāmanupamavyāhāreṇa; sarvasaṃyojanabandhanagatānāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) whose <s>pāramitās</s> are fulfilled, through the discourse of the purified establishment; for those whose bases of attraction are unfulfilled, through the discourse of the well-gathered; for those who have not sought the <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), through the discourse of equal practice; for those whose jewels of the factors of awakening are unfulfilled, through the discourse of the unsettled emergence; for those whose minds have lost the well-spoken knowledge, through the discourse of the ocean-seal; for those whose minds are curious about the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (forbearance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>), through the discourse of the definite; for those whose minds have lost the <s>Dharma</s> as heard, through the discourse of the unforgetting; for those mutually unsatisfied with what is well-spoken, through the discourse of the dispersal of darkness; for those who have not attained faith in the Three Jewels, through the discourse of the heap of merit; for those unsatisfied with the raining of the <s>Dharma</s>-gateways
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 255.

children.text:
) gaganamukhavyāhāreṇa; sarvadharmānanyacittānāṃ
jñānamudravyāhāreṇa; tathāgataguṇāparipūrṇānāṃ lokavidyāsaṃmukhībhāvavyāhāreṇa; pūrvabuddhāsukṛtādhikāriṇāṃ viniścitaprātihāryavyāhāreṇa; ekadharmamukhāparāntakakalpānirdiṣṭānāṃ sarvadharmanayavyāhāreṇa; sarvasutrāntāviniścitānāṃ dharmasvabhāvasamatāviniścitavyāhāreṇa; ṣaṭpārāyaṇīyadharmaparivarjitānāṃ sarvadharmanayavyāhāreṇa; vimokṣacittāśayānabhiyuktānāṃ vikriḍitābhijñāvyāhāreṇa; tathāgataguhyānupraveśavimarśitānāṃ aparapraṇeyavyāhāreṇa; bodhisattvacaryānabhiyuktānāṃ jñānāgamavyāhāreṇa; jñātikāmasaṃdarśikānāṃ sarvatrānugatavyāhāreṇa; sāvaśeṣabodhisattvacārikānāmabhiṣekavyāhāreṇa; daśatathāgatabalāparipūrṇānāmanavamardavyāhāreṇa; (
children.translated_text: ) through the discourse of the sky-gateway; for those whose minds are not distracted from all <s>dharmas</s>, through the discourse of the knowledge-seal; for those whose <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities are unfulfilled, through the discourse of the manifestation of world-knowledge; for those who have not performed well-done deeds under former <s>Buddhas</s>, through the discourse of the definite miraculous display; for those for whom a single <s>Dharma</s>-gateway has not been expounded to the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, through the discourse of the method of all <s>dharmas</s>; for those who are undecided about all <s>sūtras</s>, through the discourse of the investigation of the equality of the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>; for those who have abandoned the six objects of devotion, through the discourse of the method of all <s>dharmas</s>; for those whose mind-intention is not engaged in liberation, through the discourse of the <s>abhijñā</s> of play; for those who examine the entrance into the secrets of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the discourse of not being led by others; for those <s>bodhisattvas</s>
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 256.

children.text: ) caturvaiśāradyāpratilabdhānāmaparyādīnavavyāhāreṇa; āveṇikabuddhadharmāpratilabdhānāmasaṃhāryavyāhāreṇa; amoghaśravaṇadarśanānāṃ praṇidhānavyāhāreṇa; sarvabuddhadharmasaṃmukhānubodhāya śrotāvilānāṃ vimalasamudravyāhāreṇa; sāvaśeṣasarvajñajñānānāṃ suvibuddhavyāhāreṇa; aprāptasarvatathāgatakāryābhiprāyānāmaparyantaniṣṭhāvyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyuriti / ye bodhisattvā aśaṭhā amāyāvino ṛjukā ṛjuka jātīyāśca teṣāṃ caturaśītidharmamukhasahasrāṇi caturaśītisamādhimukhasahasrāṇi pañcasaptatidhāraṇīmukhasahasrāṇi aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ ekapadavyāhāreṇa ime guṇāḥ santāne pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; (
children.translated_text: ) who have not attained the four fearlessnesses, through the discourse of the unfaltering; for those who have not attained the exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, through the discourse of the unshakeable; for those of unfailing hearing and seeing, through the discourse of the vow; for those whose hearing is turbid regarding the face-to-face realization of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, through the discourse of the stainless ocean; for those whose knowledge of omniscience has a remainder, through the discourse of the well-awakened; for those who have not attained the purpose of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>' deeds, through the discourse of the boundless culmination — would understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are without deceit, without guile, straight, and born of a straight nature — for them, eighty-four thousand <s>Dharma</s>-gateways, eighty-four thousand <s>samādhi</s>-gateways, seventy-five <s>dhāraṇī</s>-
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 257.

children.text:
) yena bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhā bhaveyuḥ; acintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣābhyudgatā bhaveyuracintyajñānadarśanabodhisadguṇālaṅkṛtā bhaveyuḥ, tadyathā kāyālaṅkṛtā lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaiḥ, vāgalaṅkṛtā bhaveyuryathābhiprāyāḥ, sattvāḥ subhāṣitena saṃtoṣayeyuḥ, śrutālaṅkṛtāḥ samādhyavacanatayā, smṛtyālaṅkṛtā dhāraṇyasaṃpramoṣatayā, mano 'laṅkṛtā nirvṛtyālaṅkṛtāḥ kugatyavabudhyanatayā, āśayālaṅkṛtā dṛḍhapratijñātayā, prayogālaṅkṛtāḥ pratijñottāraṇatayā, adhyāśayālaṅkṛtā bhūmyā bhūmisaṃkramaṇatayā, dānālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvavastuparityāgatayā, śīlālaṅkṛtāḥ suśrutāvitavimalatayā, kṣāntyalaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasattvāpratihatacittatayā, vīryālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasaṃbhāropacitatayā, dhyānālaṅkṛtāḥ
sarvasamāpattivikrīḍitābhijñā bhaveyuḥ, prajñālaṅkṛtāḥ (
children.translated_text: ) by which <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> would be armored with the great armor: they would be exalted through inconceivable extraordinary vows, adorned with inconceivable knowledge-and-vision and the good qualities of awakening — namely, adorned in body with the marks and minor marks; adorned in speech so as to be in accord with the intentions of beings, satisfying them with well-spoken words; adorned with learning through the non-verbal [understanding of] <s>samādhi</s>; adorned with mindfulness through the non-forgetfulness of <s>dhāraṇī</s>; adorned in mind, adorned with <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) through the awakening from the lower realms; adorned in disposition through firm vows; adorned in application through the fulfillment of vows; adorned in superior disposition through the transition from stage to stage
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 258.

children.text: ) kleśavāsanaparijñāvino, maitryālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasattvasya trāyānugatāḥ, karuṇālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasattvāparityāgasthitā, muditālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvadharmākathaṃkathāprāptā, upekṣālaṅkṛtā unnāmāvanāmadvayavigatāḥ, abhijñālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvavikrīḍitābhijñāḥ, puṇyālaṅkṛtā akṣayabhogaratnapāṇitāpratilabdhā, jñānālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasattvacittacaritābhijñā, buddhyālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvasattvakauśalyadharmavibodhayitāraḥ, ālokālaṅkṛtāḥ prajñācakṣurālokaṃ pratilabheyuḥ, pratisaṃvidalaṅkṛtā arthadharmaniruktipratibhānapratisaṃvitpratilabdhā bhaveyurvaiśāradyālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvamāraparapravādinabhibhūtā, guṇālaṅkṛtā buddhānāṃ guṇānuprāptā, dharmālaṅkṛtāḥ satatasamitamasaṅgapratibhānena sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyuḥ, ālokālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvabuddhadharmāvabhāsagatāḥ, prabhālaṅkṛtāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrāvabhāsagatā, ādarśanaprātihāryālaṅkṛtā akṣuṇavyākaraṇā, (
children.translated_text: ) thoroughly knowing the traces of afflictions; adorned with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), following all beings in protection; adorned with <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), standing firm in not abandoning any being; adorned with <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), having attained freedom from doubt regarding all <s>dharmas</s>; adorned with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), free from the duality of rising and falling; adorned with <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), possessed of all playful higher knowledges; adorned with merit, having attained inexhaustible enjoyment and jewel-hands; adorned with knowledge, knowing the mental activities and conduct of all beings; adorned with understanding, awakening all beings to the <s>dharmas</s> of skillful means; adorned with illumination, they would attain the illumination of the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); adorned with <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge), having attained the analytical knowledges of meaning, <s>dharma</s>, etymology, and eloquence
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 259.

children.text: ) anuśāsanīprātihāryālaṅkṛtā yathāvadanuśāsanīpradāyakā, ṛddhiprātihāryālaṅkṛtāścaturṛddhipādaparamapāramitāprāptāḥ, sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānālaṅkṛtāstathāgataguhyānupraviṣṭā, dharmaiśvaryālaṅkṛtā aparādhīnajñānapratilabdhāḥ, sarvakuśaladharmapratipattisārālaṅkṛtā yathāvāditathākārisarvato 'navamarditā bhaveyuriti / apramāṇāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ sattvānāmekapadavyāhāreṇāhaṃ mahatā kuśalaviśodhanasaṃnicayena saṃtarpayeyaṃ / tataste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmeṣvaparapratyayajñānaṃ pratilabheyuḥ, mahatā ca dharmāvabhāsena samanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyuriti /
children.translated_text: ) adorned with the miraculous display of instruction, bestowing instruction as it truly is; adorned with the miraculous display of supernatural power, having attained the supreme perfection of the four bases of supernatural power; adorned with the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having entered into the secrets of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; adorned with sovereignty over the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained knowledge independent of others; adorned with the essence of the practice of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, they would be undefeated in all respects, being ones who act as they speak. With a single utterance of discourse, through the great accumulation of purification of the wholesome, I would satisfy immeasurable and incalculable beings who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, having attained knowledge independent of others regarding all <s>dharmas</s>

body.translated_text: And when I have attained awakening, may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in a single utterance. Whatever beings are of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, may they understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught as the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle discourse collection; whatever beings are to be trained by the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> [vehicle], may they understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught as the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle discourse; whatever beings are of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>, may they understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught as the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourse. Whatever beings lack the requisites [of merit], may they understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught as a discourse on generosity; whatever beings lack merit and desire happiness and heaven, may they understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught as a discourse on moral conduct; whatever beings have fearful, turbid minds toward each other, with hostile minds, those (

body.text: ye 'pi te bhadanta bhagavan sattvā bhaveyuranyeṣu lokadhātuṣvānantaryakārakā yāvanmūlāpattisāparādhikā dagdhasantānāḥ śrāvakayānikā vā pratyekabuddhayānikā vā anuttaramahāyānikā vā praṇidhānavaśena mama buddhakṣetre pratyājāyeyuḥ / akuśalamūlasamavadhānā rukṣāḥ pāpecchāḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 260.

children.text: ) krūrakhaṭuṅkasantānā viparītabuddhaya āgṛhītasantānāḥ teṣāṃ cāhaṃ caturaśītiścittarutasahasrāṃ deśayeyuḥ, yāvat kuśīdacittānāṃ sattvānāmahaṃ caturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi vistareṇa deśayeyaṃ / ye ca tatra sattvā anuttaramahāyānikā bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ cāhaṃ vistareṇa ṣaṭpāramitādharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, dānapāramitāṃ vistareṇa deśayeyaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāṃ vistareṇa deśayeyaṃ / ye ca punastatra sattvāḥ śrāvakayānikā vā pratyekabuddhayānikā vā bhaveyuḥ, anavaruptakuśalamūlā bhaveyuḥ, śāstārābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ, tāṃścāhaṃ triśaraṇagamanena vyavasthāpayeyaṃ, paścāt pāramitāsu niyojayeyaṃ; vihiṃsāratānāṃ prānātipātavairamaṇyāṃ vyavasthāpayeyaṃ; viṣamalobhābhibhūtānāmadattādānavairamaṇyāṃ vyavasthāpayeyaṃ; adharmarāgaraktāṃ kāmamithyācāravairamaṇyāṃ vyavasthāpayeyaṃ; parasparaparuṣavacanabhāṣiṇo mṛṣāvādavairamaṇyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) of cruel and harsh mind-streams, of perverted understanding, of grasping mind-streams — to them I would teach eighty-four thousand vocal discourses, and so on, to beings of lazy mind I would teach in detail eighty-four thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s>. And to those beings there who would be followers of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>, I would teach in detail the <s>Dharma</s> of the six <s>pāramitās</s> — I would teach in detail <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) and so on up to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). And furthermore, to those beings there who would be followers of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle or the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, who have not yet planted wholesome roots, who desire a teacher
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 261.

children.text: ) vyavasthāpayeyaṃ; unmattābhiratān surāmaireyamadyapramādavairamaṇyāṃ vyavasthāpayeyaṃ / yeṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ sarvapañcadoṣā bhaveyustāṃ pañcadoṣavairamaṇyopāsakasaṃvare vyavasthāpayeyaṃ / ye sattvā anabhiratāḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu tāṃścāhaṃ rātriṃdivasamaṣṭāṅge śīle pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ / ye sattvāḥ parīttakuśalamūlābhiratacittāstāṃścāpyahaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye upaśleṣayeyaṃ, pravrajyāsaṃvare daśaśikṣāpade brahmacarye sthāpayeyaṃ / ye sattvāḥ kuśalān dharmān paryeṣṭukāmāstānapyahaṃ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu samādāpya sakale brahmacaryavāse pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ / evaṃrūpānāmānantaryakārakānāṃ yāvad āgṛhītasantānānāṃ sattvānāmarthe cāhaṃ bahuvividhanānārthapadavyañjanaprātihāryairdharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, anityaduḥkhānātmaśūnyaskandhadhātvāyatanāni darśayeyaṃ, kuśale kṣeme śive śānte 'bhayapure nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ / evamahaṃ caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ; ye ca vādārthino bhaveyusteṣāṃ ahaṃ dharmavādaśāstraṃ prakāśayeyaṃ; ye ca nābhiratāḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu teṣāṃ cāhaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) I would establish [them]; those intoxicated and addicted, I would establish in abstinence from the negligence of liquor, spirits, and intoxicants. And those beings who have all five faults, I would establish in the lay precepts (<s>upāsakasaṃvara</s>) of abstaining from the five faults. Those beings who have no delight in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, I would establish day and night in the eightfold morality (<s>aṣṭāṅga śīla</s>). Those beings who delight in meager roots of merit, I would draw near to the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and establish them in the going-forth precepts (<s>pravrajyāsaṃvara</s>), in the ten training rules (<s>daśaśikṣāpada</s>), and in the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). Those beings who wish to seek wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, them too I would [establish] in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 262.

children.text:
) vaiyāvṛtyakarmāṇi nirdiśeyam, svādhyāyābhiratānāmekāṃśena śūnyatāṃ dhyānavimuktigāmināṃ nirdeśayeyaṃ / ekaikasya sattvasyārthāyāhaṃ bahuyojanaśatasahasrāṇi pradbhyāṃ gaccheyaṃ, bahuvividhanānāprakārārthapadavyañjanopāyaprātihāryairakhedamutsaheyaṃ, yāvannirvāṇe sthāpayeyaṃ; yāvat samādhānabalenāhaṃ pañcamabhāgamāyuḥsaṃskārāṇāmavasṛjeyaṃ, parinirvāṇakālasamaye cāhaṃ svayameva svaśarīrasarṣapaphalapramāṇamātraṃ bhindeyaṃ, sattvānāṃ kāruṇyārthe cāhaṃ paścāt parinirvāpayeyaṃ; parinirvṛtasya ca me varṣasahasraṃ saddharmastiṣṭhet,
pañcapunarvarṣaśatāni saddharmapratirūpakastiṣṭhet /
children.translated_text: ) I would assign the tasks of service; for those delighting in study, I would teach emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) in one aspect, leading to <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). For the sake of each and every being, I would travel on foot hundreds of thousands of <s>yojanas</s>; through many and varied kinds of meanings, words, syllables, skillful means, and miracles, I would bear the tirelessness [of teaching] until I establish them in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And by the power of concentration (<s>samādhāna</s>), I would release one-fifth of my lifespan; and at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I myself would divide my own body into portions the size of mustard seeds, for the sake of compassion toward beings, and afterward I would pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; and after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—

body.translated_text: And, O Venerable Blessed One, whatever beings in other world-realms have committed the <s>ānantarya</s> (acts of immediate retribution), and so on up to those who have committed root transgressions and whose mind-streams are burned, whether they are followers of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s> — by the power of their vows, they would be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. Those of unwholesome root-tendencies, rough, of evil desires (

body.text: ye ca sattvā mama parinirvṛtasya śarīreṣu pūjautsukyamāpadyeyū ratnairyāvadvādyairantaśa ekabuddhanāmaikavandanā ekapradakṣinīkaraṇena ekāñjalikarmaṇā ekapuṣpeṇa pūjāṃ kurvīran, sarve te 'vaivartikā bhaveyuryathābhiprāyāstribhiryānaiḥ / ye ca sattvā mama parinirvṛtasya śāsane 'ntaśa ekaśikṣāpadamapi gṛhṇīyuryathoktaṃ samādāya varteyuryāvaccatuṣpadagāthāṃ paryavāpnuyurvācayeyuḥ, pareṣāṃ ca deśayeyuḥ, ye 'pi śṛṇuyuścittaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 263.

children.text: ) vā prasādayeyurdharmabhāṇakasya vā pūjāṃ kuryurantaśa ekapuṣpeṇāpi ekavandanenāpi, sarve te 'vaivartikā bhaveyustribhiryānairyathābhiprāyā; yāvat saddharme 'ntarhite saddharmolkāyāṃ nirvāpitāyāṃ dharmadhvaje patite te ca mama janmaśarīramavatareyuryāvat kāñcanacakre tiṣṭheyuryasmin kāle sahe buddhakṣetre ratnadurbhikṣaṃ bhavet tasmin samaye ketumatirnāma maṇivaiḍuryamayaṃ agninirbhāsaṃ tiṣṭhet / tacca tato 'bhyudgamyorddhvaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavane sthitvā vividhāṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ pravarṣet, māndāravamahāmāndāravapārijātakamañjuṣakamahāmañjuṣakarocamahārocamānapūrṇācandravimalāśatapatrasahasrapatraśatasahasrapatrasamantaprabhāsamantagandhāsurucirasadāphalāhṛdayanayanābhiramyājyotiprabhājyotirasānantavarṇānantagandhānantaprabhānāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) or would generate faith, or would make offerings to a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher even with a single flower or a single salutation—they would all become irreversible through the three vehicles according to their aspiration. And when the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared, when the torch of the true <s>Dharma</s> is extinguished and the <s>Dharma</s>-banner has fallen, those [relics] would descend into my birth-body and remain down to the golden wheel [at the base of the earth]. And when there is a dearth of jewels in this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, at that time a [pillar] called <s>Ketumati</s>, made of maṇi-gems and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, blazing like fire, would stand there. And rising upward from there to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, it would rain down various flower-showers—<s>māndārava</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 264.

children.text: ) evaṃrūpānāṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ abhipravarṣet / tataśca puṣpavarṣādvividhā śabdā niścareyustadyathā buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabda upāsakasaṃvaraśabda āryāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatopoṣadhopavāsaśabdo daśapravrajyāśikṣāpadasaṃvaraśabdo dānaśabdaḥ śīlaśabdaḥ sakalabrahmacaryaparipūrṇopasaṃpadāśabdo vaiyāvṛttiśabdo 'dhyayanaśabdaḥ pratisaṃlayanaśabdaḥ yoniśomanasikāraśabdo 'śubhaśabdo ānāpānasmṛtiśabdo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaśabda ākiñcanyāyatanaśabdo vijñānānantyāyatanaśabda ākāśānantyāyatanaśabdo 'bhibhavāyatanaśabdaḥ kṛtsnāyatanaśabdaḥ śamathavipaśyanāśabdaḥ śūnyatāpraṇihitaśabdo 'nimittaśabdaḥ pratītyasamutpādaśabdaḥ sakalaśrāvakapiṭakaśabdaśca niścaret, sakalapratyekabuddhayānapiṭakaśabdo niścaret, sakalamahāyānakathāṣaṭpāramitāśabdaḥ te puṣpā avakireyuḥ / sarve ca rūpāvacarā devāḥ śṛṇuyuḥ (
children.translated_text: ) it would rain down flowers of such a kind. And from that flower-rain, various sounds would issue forth, namely: the sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, the sound of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the sound of the lay precepts (<s>upāsakasaṃvara</s>), the sound of the observance-fast endowed with the noble eightfold [path] (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga-upoṣadha-upavāsa</s>), the sound of the ten training rules of the going-forth precepts, the sound of giving (<s>dāna</s>), the sound of morality (<s>śīla</s>), the sound of complete ordination fulfilling the entire holy life, the sound of service, the sound of study, the sound of solitary retreat, the sound of proper mental attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>), the sound of impurity [contemplation] (<s>aśubha</s>), the sound of mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>), the sound of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the sound of the sphere of nothingness, the sound of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sound of the sphere of infinite space, the sound of the overcoming [bases] (<s>abhibhv</s>)—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 265.

children.text:
) svakasvakāni pūrvakṛtāni kuśalamūlānyanusmareyuḥ, sarvakuśaleṣu dharmeṣu mahāsattvā ajugupsanīyāste tato 'vatareyuḥ sarve sahe lokadhātau manuṣyāṃ daśakuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu niyojayeyuḥ pratiṣṭhāpayeyuḥ / evameva sarve kāmāvacarā devāḥ śṛṇuyusteṣāṃ ca tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanaratikrīḍāsaumanasyābhiratāṃścittacaitasikāṃ sarvān praśrambhayeyuḥ, te sarve svakāni pūrvakṛtāni kuśalamūlānyanusmareyuḥ, te ca devalokādavatīrya sarve sahe lokadhātau manuṣyāṃ daśakuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayeyuḥ pratiṣṭhāpayeyuḥ / te ca puṣpā ākāśe vividhā ratnāḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ, tadyathā bhadanta bhagavan rūpyahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍarajatajātarūpāśmagarbhadakṣiṇāvartāḥ,
sarve sahe buddhakṣetre evaṃrūpāṃ ratnavṛṣṭiṃ abhipravarṣeyuḥ / sarve ca sahe buddhakṣetre kalikalahavivādadurbhikṣarogaparacakraparuṣavāgrukṣaviṣaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ praśameyuḥ, kṣemārogyā akalahābandhanavigrahāḥ subhikṣāḥ sarve sahe buddhakṣetre saṃsthiheyuḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) they would recall their own respective previously performed roots of merit; those great beings without loathing in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> would descend from there, and all would engage and establish human beings in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśakuśala karmapatha</s>). Likewise, all the gods of the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) would hear, and their mental and psychological [states] of craving, fetters, delight, play, and satisfaction would all be calmed. They would all recall their own previously performed roots of merit, and descending from the heavenly realms, they would all inspire and establish human beings in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm in the ten wholesome courses of action—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 266.

children.text: ) yāni ca sattvāni tāni ratnāni paśyeyuḥ spṛśyeyuḥ upabhogakarma vā kurvīran te sarve tribhiryānairavaivartyā bhaveyuste ca punaradho yāvat kāñcanacakre sthiheyurevameva bhadanta bhagavan śastrāntarakalpakāle samaye punasta indranīlamaṇiratnāḥ saṃsthiheyurūrdhvaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaparyante, sthitvā vividhāṃ puṣpavṛṣṭimabhipravarṣeyuḥ, tadyathā māndāravamahāmāndāravapāriyātrā yāvadevānantaprabhāstasmācca puṣpavarṣādvividhā manojñāḥ śabdā niścareyustadyathā buddhaśabdo dharmaśabdaḥ saṅghaśabdo yāvatpūrvoktaṃ / te punaḥ śarīrā adho yāvat kāñcanacakre sthiheyuḥ / evaṃ tasmiṃ samaye durbhikṣāntarakalpakāle punaste śarīrā ūrdhvamudgaccheyuryāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaparyantaṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiryāvat pūrvoktaṃ / yāvad rogāntarakalpaṃ yathā pūrvoktaṃ / yathā bhadrake mahākalpe mama parinirvṛtasya śarīrāstṛkāryaṃ kuryuḥ, gaṇanātikrāntānvaineyāṃ tribhiryānairavaivartikān sthāpayeyaṃ / evaṃ pañcabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairmahākalpe vartamānairmama śarīrāḥ sattvān vineyustribhiryānairavaivartikāṃ sthāpayeyuḥ; yadā (
children.translated_text: ) and those beings who would see, touch, or make use of those jewels—they would all become irreversible through the three vehicles. And they would again remain below down to the golden wheel. Likewise, O venerable Blessed One, at the time of the intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of weapons, those jewels of <s>indranīla</s> maṇi (sapphire gems) would stand, reaching upward to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, and would rain down various flower-showers, namely <s>māndārava</s>, <s>mahāmāndārava</s>, <s>pāriyātra</s>, and even <s>anantaprabhā</s> (infinite-light [flowers]). And from that flower-rain, various delightful sounds would issue forth, namely: the sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, the sound of the <s>Saṅgha</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 267.

children.text: ) paścāt sahasragaṅgānadīvālikāsamairasaṃkhyeyairatikrāntairdaśasu dikṣvaprameyairasaṃkhyeyairanyonyebhyo lokadhātubhyaste buddhā bhagavanta utpadyeyurye mayā bodhisattvabhūtenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau caryāṃ caratā prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāḥ syuḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā, mayā ca ṣaṭpāramitāsu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: ) afterwards, after incalculable [aeons] equal to the sands of a thousand <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers have passed, in the ten directions, from immeasurable and countless world-realms different from one another, those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, shall arise who were first inspired and established by me in supreme perfect enlightenment while I was practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, and who were inspired, established, and settled by me in the six <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.translated_text: And those beings who would eagerly wish to make offerings to the relics (<s>śarīra</s>) of me after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—with jewels, or instruments of music, even with a single utterance of a <s>Buddha's</s> name, a single salutation, a single circumambulation, a single gesture of joined palms, or worship with a single flower—they would all become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) through the three vehicles (<s>yāna</s>) according to their aspiration. And those beings who, in my teaching after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, would take up even a single training rule, practice as taught, or would master and recite even a verse of four lines, and teach it to others—and even those who hear it and generate faith—

body.text: bodhiprāptaścāhamapi sattvānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayeyaṃ niveśayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, ye ca punaḥ parinirvṛtasya śarīravikurvaṇenāpi sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayeyuste 'pi paścāt sahasragaṅgānadīvālikāsamairasaṃkhyeyairvartamānairasaṃkhyeyairatikrāntairdaśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā mama varṇaṃ bhāṣyayeyuḥ śrāvayeyurghoṣaṃ codīrayeyu"ryacciraṃ bhadrako nāma kalpo babhūva, tasmiṃśca bhadrake mahākalpe 'nupraviṣṭe caturthe jinabhāskara evaṃnāmā tathāgato babhūva, yena vayaṃ prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 268.

children.text: ) niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, dagdhasantānā akuśalasamavadhānagatā ānantaryakārakā yāvanmithyādṛṣṭikāstena vayaṃ ṣaṭpāramitāsu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / yena vayametarhi sarvajñāḥ sarvākāradhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayāmaḥ, nirvarte tu gaticakre bahusattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrān svarge mokṣaphale ca pratiṣṭhāpayāmaḥ syuḥ" / ye ca sattvā bodhyarthikāsteṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sakāśe mama varṇakīrtiyaśaśca śṛṇuyuste taṃ tathāgataṃ pṛccheyuḥ, "kamarthavaśaṃ sampaśyamānaḥ sa bhagavāṃstathāgata evaṃ pañcakaṣāye kaliyuge vartamāne 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ?" te ca tathāgatāsteṣāṃ bodhyarthikānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā imaṃ mama mahākaruṇāsamanvāgataṃ prathamacittotpādaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ praṇidhānapūrvayogaṃ ca bhāṣeyuste ca bodhyarthikāḥ kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaro vā āścaryaprāptā bhaveyuste 'pyudārādhimuktikā bhaveyuste 'pyevaṃrūpāṃ mahākaruṇāṃ sattveṣūtpādayeyurevaṃrūpaṃ ca praṇidhānaṃ kurvīran, evaṃrūpe tīvrapañcakaṣāye kleśakaṣāye kaliyuge buddhakṣetre ānantaryakārakāṃ yāvadakuśalasamavadhānāṃ vaineyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) were established and settled—those with burned [karmic] continuums, those fallen into unwholesome states, committers of heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>), and even those of wrong views—by him we were inspired, established, and settled in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. By him we are now omniscient, turning the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel that is righteous in all aspects (<s>sarvākāradhārmika dharmacakra</s>); we turn [beings] away from the wheel of destinies and establish many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings in heaven and in the fruit of liberation." And those beings who aspire to enlightenment, hearing my praise, glory, and renown in the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, would ask that <s>Tathāgata</s>: "Seeing what purpose did that Blessed One, that <s>Tathāgata</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 269.

children.text: ) pratigṛhṇīyuste ca buddhā bhagavantastān mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatāṃ bodhyarthikāṃ kulaputrān vā kuladuhitṝn vā evaṃrūpeṇa vyākareṇana vyākuryuryathābhiprāyāṃ taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhirvā tīvrapañcakaṣāye kleśe kaliyuge praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / apare buddhā bhagavanto mama śarīravivartanebhiḥ pūrvayogaiḥ sattvānāṃ bodhyarthikānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā vistareṇa bhāṣayeyuḥ, "evaṃ ciramevaṃnāmā jinasūryo babhūva; parinirvṛtasya śarīrebhirevaṃ ciramevaṃrūpaṇāṃ duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya evaṃrūpāṇi vividhāni prātihāryāṇi vividhā ca nānāprakārā vikurvaṇākṛtāstasya śarīravikurvaṇābhirvayaṃ prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃcoditāḥ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vayaṃ kuśalamūlasamavadhānān prathamacittotpādādidaṃ pāramitāsu codyogaḥ kṛtaḥ, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ vistareṇa" /
children.translated_text: ) accept?" And those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, would give prophecy to those sons or daughters of good family who aspire to enlightenment and are endowed with great compassion, with a prophecy of such a kind, according to their aspiration—those sons or daughters of good family who made aspirations in a time of fierce five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>), afflictions, and the degenerate age (<s>kaliyuga</s>). Other <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, through the miraculous transformations of my relics and through former connections, would speak in detail to those sons or daughters of good family who aspire to enlightenment: "Thus long ago there was a <s>Jina</s>-sun of such-and-such a name; from his relics after <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, thus long, for the benefit of such suffering beings, thus—"

body.translated_text: And when I too have attained enlightenment, I shall inspire, establish, and settle beings in supreme perfect enlightenment. And those who, even through the miraculous transformations of the relics (<s>śarīravivartana</s>) after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment—they too, afterwards, after incalculable [aeons] equal to the sands of a thousand <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, both past and present, in immeasurable and countless world-realms in the ten directions, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who have attained supreme perfect enlightenment shall speak my praise, proclaim, and extol the renown: "Long ago there was a fortunate aeon called <s>Bhadraka</s>, and in that <s>Bhadra</s>—

body.text: atha khalu samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohito ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purataḥ sadevagandharvamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ imāṃ mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatāṃ pañcaśatāni praṇidhānāni (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 270.

children.text: ) kṛtavān, sa evamāha - "yadi me bhadanta bhagavannevaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta tathā cāhamanāgate 'dhvani bhadarake kalpe tīvrakleṣe raṇakaṣāye kaliyuge vartamāṇe 'ndhaloke 'nāyake 'pariṇāyake dṛṣṭivyasanāndhakāraprakṣipte loke ānantaryakārakānāṃ yāvat pūrvoktaṃ; yadi cāhaṃ śaktaḥ sakalamevaṃ buddhakāryaṃ niṣpādayituṃ yathā ca me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, na ca visarāmi bodhau praṇidhānaṃ, na cānyakṣetre kuśalamūlaṃ pariṇāmayāmi; evameva bhadanta bhagavan vyavasāyaṃ / na ca punarahaṃ anena kuśalamulena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ prārthayāmi, na ca śrāvakayānaṃ prārthayāmi, na devamanuṣyaloke rājatvaṃ prārthayāmi, na devamanuṣyaloke aiśvaryaṃ prārthayāmi, na pañcakāmaguṇaparibhogārthaṃ, na devopapattiṃ prārthayāmi, na gandharvāsurayakṣarākṣasanāgagarūḍopapattiṃ prāthayāmi, na cātra kuśalamūlaṃ pariṇāmayāmi / yacca bhagavān evamāha - "dānaṃ mahābhogatāyai saṃvartate, śīlaṃ svargopapattaye śrutaṃ mahāprajñatāyai bhāvanā visaṃyogāya" / uktaṃ caitatpunarbhagavatā, (
children.translated_text: ) he spoke thus: "If, Venerable Blessed One, such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, and thus in the future time, in the <s>Bhadra</s> <s>kalpa</s>, when intense affliction prevails, when the defilement of strife and the degenerate age are present, in a blind world without a leader, without a guide, a world cast into the darkness of the calamity of wrong views, for those who commit acts of immediate retribution — as previously stated — and if I am able to accomplish the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s> as my aspiration was made, and I do not abandon my aspiration for awakening, and I do not dedicate my roots of merit to another <s>Buddha</s>-field — this is my determination, Venerable Blessed One. And further, by this root of merit, I do not seek the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, nor do I seek the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle; I do not seek sovereignty in the world of gods and humans; I do not seek lordship in the world of gods and humans; not for the enjoyment of the five strands of sensual pleasure; I do not seek rebirth among gods; I do not seek rebirth among <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, or <s>garuḍas</s>; nor do I dedicate roots of merit for that. And the Blessed One has said: 'Giving leads to great wealth; morality leads to heavenly rebirth; learning leads to great wisdom; meditation leads to liberation.' And furthermore this was said by the Blessed One: (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 271.

children.text: ) "ṛdhyati āśayo 'bhiprāyaḥ kuśalamūlapariṇāmanā puṇyavataḥ sattvasya" / yacca mayā bhadanta bhagavan dānamayaṃ vā śīlamayaṃ vā śrutamayaṃ vā bhāvanāmayaṃ vā puṇyamārjitaṃ syāt / yadi naivaṃrūpā āśā paripūryeta yathā me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tadahaṃ tatsarvaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ nairayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ pariṇāmayāmi; ye sattvāḥ pracaṇḍamaṇḍaghore 'vīcau narake duḥkhānyanubhavanti te cānena kuśalamūlena tato vyuttiṣṭhantu, iha ca buddhakṣetre manuṣyapratilābhaṃ pratilabhantu, tathāgatapraveditaṃ ca dharmavinayamārāgayeyuḥ, agratve ca parinirvāyeyuḥ / yacca teṣāṃ sattvānāmaparikṣīṇakarmaphalaṃ syāttadahametarhi kālaṃ kṛtvāvicau mahānarake upapadyeyaṃ; buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamādhyagamaṇīyāśca me kāyāḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ / ekaikaśca me kāyaḥ sumeruparvatarājapramāṇo mahān saṃbhavet; ekaikaśca me kāya (
children.translated_text: ) 'The intention and purpose of a meritorious being prospers through the dedication of roots of merit.' And, Venerable Blessed One, whatever merit I may have accumulated through giving, morality, learning, or meditation — if such a hope of mine should not be fulfilled as my aspiration was made, then I would dedicate all those roots of merit to the beings in the hells.
