Those beings who experience sufferings in the fierce, terrible <s>Avīci</s> great hell — may they, by this root of merit, arise from there and obtain human rebirth in this <s>Buddha</s>-field, and may they delight in the <s>Dharma</s> and discipline taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the highest. And whatever unexpired karmic fruit those beings may have — may I, having died at this time, be reborn in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell; and may bodies arise for me, as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, impossible to traverse. May each of my bodies become as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains; and may each of my bodies (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 272.

children.text:
) evaṃrūpāḥ suduḥkhā vedanā jānīyādyathaitarhi eṣa ekaḥ śarīraḥ suduḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ saṃjānāti; ekaikaśca me ātmabhāvo buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃ tīvrāṃ caṇḍāṃ kharāṃ nairayikāṃ kāraṇāṃ anubhaveyurye caitarhi buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvā ānantaryakārakā yāvadavīciparāyaṇāni karmāṇi samudānītāni syuryacca yāvadbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu mahākalpeṣvatikrānteṣu daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatvānantaryakarmāṇi kṣipeyuḥ samutthāpayeyurvā,
sarveṣāṃ arthāyāhaṃ tatkarmāvīcau mahānarake sthito 'nubhaveyaṃ, mā ca me sattvā narakeṣūpapadyeyuḥ, sarve ca te sattvā buddhā bhagavanta ārāgayeyuḥ, saṃsārāccottārayeyuḥ, nirvāṇanagaraṃ praveśayeyuḥ; tadāhametaccireṇa narakāt parimucyeyaṃ / yāvaddaśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvaistathārūpaṃ karmasamutthāpitaṃ ākṣiptaṃ niyatavedanīyaṃ pratāpane narake upapadyitavyaṃ, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / evaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) experience such extremely painful feelings as this single body now perceives extremely painful feelings; and may each of my individual existences experience torments of the hells — intense, fierce, sharp — as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And those beings in other world-realms in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, who have committed acts of immediate retribution, up to deeds destined for <s>Avīci</s>, and who, over the course of great <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, have gone to other <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and have cast or generated acts of immediate retribution — for the sake of all of them, standing in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell, I shall experience that karma. May those beings of mine not be reborn in the hells; may all those beings delight in the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, may they be rescued from <s>saṃsāra</s>, may they be led into the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Then, after a long time, may I be freed from hell. And in other <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, whatever karma has been generated and cast by beings with inevitable retribution, leading to rebirth in the <s>Pratāpana</s> hell — and likewise as previously stated. Thus (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 273.

children.text: ) santāpane mahāraurave saṅghāte kālasūtre saṃjīvane, evaṃ nānāvidhā tiryagyonirvācyāḥ, evaṃ yamaloke vaktavyaḥ, evaṃ yakṣadāridre vaktavyaṃ, evaṃ kumbhāṇḍapiśācāsuragaruḍā vācyāḥ / yadā buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvairevaṃrūpaṃ karmākṣiptaṃ syāt, ye ca manuṣyāndhabadhirā ajihvākā ahastakā apādakāḥ smṛtipramuṣṭacittairutpādyitavyaṃ aśucibhakṣayitavyaṃ, peyālaṃ yathā pūrvoktaṃ / punarevamahamavīcau mahānarake upapadyeyaṃ; yāvacciraṃ saṃsāre dhātvāyatanaskandhaṃ pratigṛhṇīyustāvacciramahaṃ evaṃrūpāṃ vividhe narakatiryakpreteṣu yakṣāsurarākṣaseṣu yāvan manuṣyaduḥkhopapattibhirevaṃ duḥkhamanubhaveyaṃ, yathā pūrvoktaṃ; yadi me evaṃrūpā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āśā na paripūryeta /
children.translated_text: ) in <s>Saṃtāpana</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Saṅghāta</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃjīva</s> — likewise the various kinds of animal realms are to be stated; likewise the world of <s>Yama</s> is to be stated; likewise the poverty of <s>yakṣas</s> is to be stated; likewise <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>garuḍas</s> are to be stated. When beings in other world-realms in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, have cast such karma [as leads to rebirth as] humans who are blind, deaf, tongueless, handless, footless, with deranged minds, who must eat impure things — abbreviated as previously stated. Furthermore, may I be reborn in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell; and for as long as they continue to take up elements, sense-bases, and aggregates in <s>saṃsāra</s>, for that long shall I experience such sufferings in the various hells, animal realms, <s>preta</s> realms, among <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and up to human rebirths of suffering — as previously stated — should my hope for unsurpassed perfect awakening not be fulfilled.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest, in the presence of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, before an assembly including gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and humans, [recited] these five hundred aspirations endowed with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)—

body.text: atha khalu ca punarme evaṃrūpānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āśā paripūryeta yāvat pūrvoktaṃ, sākṣībhūtā me buddhā bhagavanto bhavantu / ye daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti te mama buddhā bhagavantaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 274.

children.text: ) sākṣībhūtā bhaviṣyanti, jñānabhūtā bhaviṣyanti / vyākarotu me bhadanta bhagavannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, bhadrake kalpe bhaveyamahaṃ viṃśottaravarṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampanno yāvadbuddho bhagavān; śakto 'hamevaṃrūpaṃ buddhakāryamabhiniṣpādayituṃ yā me pratijñā kṛtāḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) shall be my witnesses, shall be my knowers. May the Blessed One prophesy me in unsurpassed perfect awakening: may I, in the <s>Bhadra</s> <s>kalpa</s>, when the generation has a lifespan of one hundred and twenty years, become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. I am able to accomplish such a work of a <s>Buddha</s> as the vows I have made."

body.translated_text: But if such a hope of mine for unsurpassed perfect awakening should be fulfilled — as previously stated — may the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones be my witnesses. Those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who dwell, abide, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> in other world-realms in the ten directions, immeasurable and incalculable — those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones (

body.text: atha tāvadeva sarvāvatī parṣā sadevagandharvamānuṣāsuraśca lokaḥ kṣitigaganasthitāḥ, sthāpayitvā tathāgataṃ te sarve 'śrūṇi pravartayamānāḥ pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vanditvāhuḥ / "sādhu sādhu mahākāruṇika, gaṃbhīrā te smṛtirgaṃbhīreṣu sattveṣu mahākaruṇotpannā, gaṃbhīraṃ ca mahāpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / tadādhyāśayena sarvasattvā mahākaruṇayā saṃcchāditāya bhūyasānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā vaineyāḥ pratigṛhītā; etena praṇidhānena jñāyate yathā tvaṃ prathamacittotpādenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sattvānāṃ bhaiṣajyabhūtastrāṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ; sattvānāṃ duḥkhapramocanārthaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā te āśā paripūryatu vyākarotu ca bhagavānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" /
body.translated_text: Then at that very moment, the entire assembly, together with the gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s> of the world, standing on the earth and in the sky — all except the <s>Tathāgata</s> — shedding tears, bowing at his feet with the five-point prostration, spoke: "Excellent, excellent, O greatly compassionate one! Profound is your mindfulness; great compassion has arisen toward beings in profound [suffering]; and a profound great aspiration has been made. Through your superior intention, all beings have been sheltered by your great compassion; moreover, you have accepted as disciples those who commit acts of immediate retribution, up to those who have reached the accumulation of unwholesome roots. By this aspiration it is known that you, from the first generation of the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, are a medicine for beings, a refuge, a resort. You have made your aspiration for the liberation of beings from suffering; may your hope thus be fulfilled, and may the Blessed One prophesy you in unsurpassed perfect awakening."

body.text: svayaṃ ca rājā amṛtaśuddhaḥ prarudamāno brāhmaṇasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vanditvāha /
body.translated_text: And King <s>Amṛtaśuddha</s> himself, weeping, bowed at the brahmin's feet with the five-point prostration and said:

children.translated_text: "O supremely profound one, you are unattached to pleasures;

children.text: sattveṣu tvaṃ dayāpannaḥ asmākaṃ tvaṃ nidarśakaḥ" //
children.translated_text: You are compassionate toward beings; you are an example for us."

body.text: peyālaṃ, avalokiteśvara āha -
body.translated_text: Abbreviated — <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said:

children.translated_text: "Among beings who are attached, you are unattached; in matters beyond the senses, you are beyond the senses;
You create mastery of the senses here; you shall speak the treasure-house of knowledge, the <s>dhāraṇī</s>."

body.text: peyālaṃ, mahāsthāmaprāptastvāha -

children.translated_text: "For the welfare of many thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of beings, they have assembled;
They weep at your compassion — supremely and extremely difficult [is your deed]."

body.translated_text: Abbreviated — <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> said:

body.text: mañjuśrīrbodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said:

children.translated_text: "O one of firm vigor and resolve, of excellent, discerning wisdom,
You are worthy of our worship with garlands, fragrances, and ointments."

body.text: gaganamudro bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> said:

children.text: "evaṃ dattaṃ tvayā dānaṃ sattvebhyo mahatī kṛpā /
children.translated_text: "Such giving you have given, and great compassion toward beings;
In this time of depletion, you, O Protector, shall become one endowed with excellent marks."

body.text: vajracchedaprajñāvabhāso bodhisattvo 'pyevamāha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "As space is vast and wide, so are you the abode of compassion;
By you, this path of the course of awakening has been shown to beings."

body.text: vegavairocano bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vegavairocana</s> said:

children.translated_text: "No other has such compassion toward beings, save for the <s>Tathāgata</s>;
You who are endowed with all virtues, of excellent, discerning wisdom."

body.text: siṃhagandhastvāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Siṃhagandha</s> said:

children.translated_text: "In the future age, in the <s>Bhadra</s> [<s>kalpa</s>] that destroys afflictions,

children.text: yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ tvamāpnoṣi sattva mocayi duḥkhitān" //
children.translated_text: You shall attain fame and renown — liberate suffering beings!"

body.text: samantabhadro bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> said:

children.translated_text: "Striving in the wilderness of births, dependent on the wrong [refuge], fallen into peril,
You have accepted those of burnt continuity, [beings] who feed on flesh and blood."

body.text: akṣobhya āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Akṣobhya</s> said:

body.text:
"avidyāṇḍakaprakṣiptā kleśapaṅke samutthitāḥ /
gṛhītā dagdhasantānā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 279.
) those who commit acts of immediate retribution — you have accepted them."

body.translated_text: "Cast into the eggshell of ignorance, risen from the mire of afflictions,

body.text: gandhahasto 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Gandhahasta</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "You, having seen the future danger as if in a mirror-disc,
Have accepted those of burnt continuity, those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: ratnaketurapyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnaketu</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "Established in knowledge, morality, and concentration, adorned with kindness and compassion,
You have accepted those of burnt continuity, those who revile the noble ones."

body.text: vigatabhayasaṃtāpa āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Vigatabhayasaṃtāpa</s> said:

children.translated_text: "You, having seen the suffering of beings on the path to the three lower realms,
Have accepted those of burnt continuity, those like an empty fist, who have taken refuge in you."

body.text: utpalahasto 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Utpalahasta</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "By compassion, knowledge, and vigor, the assembly is subdued by you;
You have accepted those of burnt continuity, those afflicted by birth and death."

body.text:
jñānakīrtirāha -
"bahurogopahatā kleśavāyusamīritāḥ /
śamesi jñānatoyena (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 281.
) and you crush the forces of <s>Māra</s>."

body.translated_text: <s>Jñānakīrti</s> said: "Those afflicted by many diseases, stirred by the wind of afflictions — you pacify them with the water of knowledge, (

body.text: dharaṇīmudro 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Dharaṇīmudra</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "We do not have such firm vigor in liberating from afflictions at their end,
As you, like a heroic sun, crush the net of afflictions."

body.text: utpalacandro 'pyāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Utpalacandra</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "O one of firm vigor and enthusiasm, endowed with virtues and the abode of compassion,

children.text: mocesi tvaṃ trayaṃ lokyaṃ prabaddhaṃ bhavabandhanaiḥ" //
children.translated_text: You liberate the triple world bound by the bonds of existence."

body.text: vimalendra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalendra</s> said:

children.translated_text: "O greatly compassionate one, you have declared the domain of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>;
We bow to you, who have arisen from the cause of compassion."

body.text: balavegadhāryapyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Balavegadhārya</s> also said:

children.translated_text: "In the degenerate age yoked to afflictions, the awakening you have undertaken —
Cut the afflictions with their roots; may your firm aspiration succeed!"

body.text: jyotipālo 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Jyotipāla</s> also said:

body.text: "jñānakośasamaṃ tulyaṃ kṛtā praṇidhi nirmalā /

children.translated_text: You set forth on the course of awakening — you are the medicine for beings, their refuge."

body.translated_text: "Equal to a treasure-house of knowledge, you have made a stainless aspiration;

body.text: balasandarśano bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prarudamāno brāhmaṇasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vanditvāñjaliṃ pragṛhītavānāha -
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Balasandarśana</s>, weeping, bowed at the brahmin's feet with the five-point prostration, joined his palms together, and said:

children.translated_text: "O torch of knowledge, dispelling the disease of afflictions for beings,

children.text: kṛpālu prajvālitā te sattvān mocesi duḥkhitān" //
children.translated_text: O compassionate one, you are kindled — you liberate suffering beings!"

body.text: sarvāvatī ca kulaputra sā parṣā sadevagandharvamāṇuṣā brāhmaṇasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau vanditvā kṛtāñjaliḥ sthitvā vicitrābhiranvayapadayuktābhirgāthābhisabhistavitvā tasthau //
body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, that entire assembly, together with gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and humans, bowed at the brahmin's feet with the five-point prostration, stood with palms joined, and praised him with various verses accompanied by connected lines, and remained standing.

body.text: yadā ca kulaputra samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyāgrato dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati / atha tāvadeva mahāpṛthivicālaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ samantācca daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pṛthivī calati pracalati saṃpracalati kṣubhati prakṣubhati saṃprakṣubhati vedhati pravedhati saṃpravedhati raṇati praraṇati saṃpraraṇati / punarapi mahān avabhāsaḥ prādurbhūtā, vividhā ca puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitāstadyathā māndāravamahāmāndāravaṃ yāvadanantaprabhā evaṃrūpā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitavatī / yaddaśasu diśāsu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti pariśuddheṣu buddhakṣetreṣu apariśuddheṣu vā sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti / ye ca tatra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāsteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantike niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstaṃ pṛthivīcālaṃ dṛṣṭvā punaste bodhisattvāstāṃ buddhāṃ bhagavataḥ paripṛcchanti / "ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 285.
) and for a great flower-rain to shower down?"

body.translated_text: When, O son of good family, <s>Samudrareṇu</s> the brahmin placed his right knee on the ground before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, at that very moment a great earthquake arose, and in all ten directions, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the earth trembled, shook, and shook greatly; quaked, quaked mightily, and quaked tremendously; rumbled, rumbled greatly, and rumbled tremendously; resounded, resounded greatly, and resounded tremendously. Furthermore, a great radiance arose, and various flower-rains fell — namely <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers, up to flowers of infinite radiance — such a flower-rain fell. In the ten directions, in world-realms as numerous as the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who dwell, sustain, and abide, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in pure and impure <s>Buddha</s>-fields — and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who were seated in the presence of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones for hearing the <s>Dharma</s> — those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, having seen that earthquake, asked those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones: "What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, for the arising in the world of a great earthquake (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena pūrvasyāṃ diśi ito buddhakṣetrādekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya ratnavicayā nāma lokadhātustatra ratnavicaye buddhakṣetre ratnacandro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhagavāṃstiṣṭhati yāpayati aprameyebhyo 'saṃkhyeyebhyo bodhisattvebhyaḥ puraskṛtaḥ parivṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma yaduta buddhakṣetre mahāyānakathā / tatra buddhakṣetre ratnaketurnāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvāścandraketuśca; tau dvau bodhisattvau yena ratnacandrastathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ratnacandraṃ tathāgatametadavocatāṃ - "ko bhadanta bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya, mahatyāśca puṣpavṛṣṭeḥ pravarṣaṇatāyai?" / ratnacandrastathāgata āha - "asti kulaputra paścimāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrādekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamān buddhakṣetrānatikramya tatra santīraṇo nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra santīraṇe buddhakṣetre (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 286.

children.text: ) ratnagarbhastathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavāṃstiṣṭhati yāpayati bahubodhisattvakoṭirvyākarotyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bodhisattvaviṣayasaṃdarśanapraṇidhānavyūhasamādhiviṣayadhāraṇīmukhavyūhaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣamāṇa; ekaścātra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvastenaivaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ mahākaruṇāparibhāvitā vāgbhāṣitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākaraṇanirdeśaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tathārūpā praṇidhānā udbhāṣitā yadbahubhiḥ prāṇakoṭibhirbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāśca parigṛhītā vaineyasattvāśca parigṛhītāḥ, sarvataśca sa eko mahākaruṇāsamanvāgato mahābodhisattvo yaḥ sarvāvatīṃ tāṃ parṣadamabhibhūya kliṣṭaṃ pañcakaṣāyaṃ kleśaraṇikaliyugaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarva ānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dagdhasantānā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ; sarvāvatī ca sā parṣat sadevagandharvamāṇuṣāsuraśca lokastaṃ ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamapahāya tasya mahākāruṇikasya paścimakasya pūjāyodyuktāḥ pañcamaṇḍalena ca vanditvā prāñjalībhūtāḥ sthitāstasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate / sa ca (
children.translated_text: ) the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, abides and teaches — he is prophesying many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> for supreme perfect awakening while expounding the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) of the Display of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s Domain through the Aspiration and Array of the <s>Samādhi</s>-Domain Gateway of <s>Dhāraṇī</s>. And there, one <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> of great compassion has made such an aspiration — words pervaded by great compassion have been uttered, and in the prophecy-teaching for supreme perfect awakening, such aspirations by <s>bodhisattvas</s> have been declared that many <s>koṭīs</s> of beings have made aspirations for awakening, and arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities have been undertaken, and beings to be trained have been accepted. And from among all of them, that one great <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with great compassion, having surpassed that entire assembly, has accepted a defiled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the five degeneracies, the affliction-battlefield of the dark age — committers of <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds, even those fallen into the accumulation of unwholesome roots with scorched mental continua — he has accepted them as his disciples. And that entire assembly, together with <s>devas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, setting aside even the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, is devoted to worshipping that last one, the one of great compassion, and having bowed with the five-point prostration, they stand with joined palms, praising him. And that (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 287.

children.text: ) mahāsattvastasya bhagavato ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purato niṣaṇṇo vyākaraṇaṃ śṛṇvānaḥ / yadā ca sa mahāsattvastasya bhagavataḥ purato dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nikṣiptavāṃstadā sa bhagavāṃstathārūpaṃ smitaṃ prādurakārṣidyathā daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā lokadhātavaścalitāḥ puṣpavarṣaṃ cābhipravarṣitaṃ / sarvatra ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prabodhanārthaṃ mahākaruṇābodhisattvapraṇidhānacaryānidarśanārthaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamebhyo digbhyo buddhakṣetrebhyaḥ sannipatanārthaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ samādhānamukhanirdeśacaryāvaiśāradyadharmaparyāyāṃ bhāṣaṇārthaṃ tena tathāgatena evaṃrūpāṇi prātihāryāṇi darśitāni" /
children.translated_text: ) <s>mahāsattva</s>, seated before that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, listens to the prophecy. And when that <s>mahāsattva</s> placed his right knee upon the ground before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, that <s>Bhagavān</s> produced such a smile that world-realms equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions trembled, and a rain of flowers showered down. And in all those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> — for the purpose of awakening them, for the purpose of displaying the aspiration-conduct of the great-compassion <s>bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of assembling <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> from <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the directions equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, and for the purpose of expounding to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> of the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway teaching, the conduct-confidence — for these purposes that <s>Tathāgata</s> displayed such miraculous manifestations."

body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the eastern direction, passing beyond <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to the sands of one Gaṅgā river from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there was a world-realm called <s>Ratnavicayā</s> (Jewel-Array). In that <s>Ratnavicaya</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnacandra</s> (Jewel-Moon), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, a <s>Bhagavān</s>, abided and taught the <s>Dharma</s> to immeasurable and incalculable <s>bodhisattvas</s> who surrounded and attended him — namely, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) discourse in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there was a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnaketu</s> and one named <s>Candraketu</s>. Those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having bowed with joined palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s>, said to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s>: "What, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great earthquake in the world, and for the showering of a great rain of flowers?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s> said: "There is, O sons of good family, in the western direction, passing beyond <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to the sands of one Gaṅgā river from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, a world-realm called <s>Santīraṇa</s>. In that <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (

body.text: tau ca kulaputra dvau bodhisattvau taṃ ratnacandraṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchate sma / kiyaccirotpāditaṃ bhadanta bhagavāṃstena mahākāruṇikena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bodhicittaṃ?; kiyacciraṃ bodhicārikāṃ cīrṇavān, yena pañcakaṣāye loke tīvrakleśaraṇe kaliyuge vartamāne kālaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 288.

children.text: ) parigṛhīta ānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dagdhasantānāḥ sattvā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ?" / ratnacandrastathāgata āha - "sāṃprataṃ kulaputra tena mahākāruṇikena prathamacittamutpāditaṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / gacchata kulaputra yūyaṃ tat santīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ tasya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / taṃ ca samādhānamukhanirdeśaṃ caryāvaiśāradyadharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyatha / taṃ ca mahākāruṇikaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ madvacanān pṛcchatha; evaṃ ca vadatha, "ratnacandrastathāgatastvāṃ satpuruṣaṃ pṛcchati / idaṃ ca candrarocavimalaṃ puṣpaṃ preṣitavān, sādhukāraścānupradatta / evaṃ ca prathamacittotpādena tvaṃ satpuruṣa mahākāruṇikavyāhāreṇa daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāsu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetrāṇi śabdenāpūritāni, tena tvayā sarvatra mahākāruṇika nāma pratilabdhaṃ / tena tvaṃ satpuruṣa sādhu bhūyaḥ paścimakānāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāvyāhāreṇa praṇidhānanetrīdhvajamucchrayaṇaṃ / tena tvaṃ satpuruṣa (
children.translated_text: ) he has accepted the time — committers of <s>ānantarya</s> deeds, even those fallen into the accumulation of unwholesome roots with scorched mental continua — he has accepted them as beings to be trained?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s> said: "Just now, O sons of good family, that one of great compassion has generated the first mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Go, O sons of good family, to that <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for seeing, venerating, and attending upon him. And you shall hear that <s>dharmaparyāya</s> of the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway teaching and the conduct-confidence. And ask that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> of great compassion, speaking my words; and say thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s> asks you, O good man. He has sent this <s>Candrarocavimala</s> (Moon-Glow Immaculate) flower, and has given his approval. Thus, O good man, by your very first generation of the mind, through your utterance of great compassion, <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in world-realms have been filled with that sound, and thereby you have everywhere obtained the name Great Compassionate One. Therefore, O good man, well done! You shall further raise the banner of aspiration led by the great-compassion utterance, for the sake of the last ones — the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> of great compassion. Therefore, O good man (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 289.

children.text: ) bhūyo buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān anāgatānasaṃkhyeyān kalpān buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān daśadiśi lokadhātuṣu yaśaḥkīrtiśabdenāpūraya / yena tvayā bahvasaṃkhyeyasattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāni niveśitāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni bhagavataḥ sakāśamupanītāni, avaivartikāni sthāpitānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / bhaviṣyanti kecittatra praṇidhānena buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāṃ parigṛhīṣyanti, ye paścād vyākaraṇaṃ lapsyante, ye tvayā bodhau samādāpitāḥ sarve te paścād yāvad buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāsaṃkhyeyakalpairdaśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhatvaṃ prāpya dharmacakraṃ pravartayitvā tvāṃ ārabhya varṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyante / anena tṛtīyena kāraṇena te sādhu satpuruṣa" /
children.translated_text: ) furthermore fill world-realms in the ten directions, for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in incalculable future times, with the sound of your fame and renown. For by you many incalculable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of beings have been inspired toward supreme perfect awakening, settled therein, established therein, and brought near to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and established in non-retrogression from supreme perfect awakening. Some among them will, by their aspirations, accept arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities — those who will later receive the prophecy. All those whom you have inspired toward awakening, they, for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, in other world-realms equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, having attained Buddhahood and turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, will speak your praise. This is the third reason: well done, O good man!'"

body.translated_text: And those two sons of good family, those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, asked that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s>: "How long ago, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, did that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> of great compassion first generate the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening)? How long has he practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, that in the world of the five degeneracies, with fierce afflictions, in the battle-time of the dark age (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena dvānavatibodhisattvakoṭya ekakaṇṭhena vadanti / "vayamapi bhadanta bhagavan santīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gacchemaḥ tasya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya, taṃ ca satpuruṣaṃ darśanāya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 290.

children.text: ) vandanāya, yasya tathāgatena tribhiraṅgaiḥ sādhukāraḥ preṣita, imaṃ ca candrarocavimalaṃ puṣpaṃ preṣitaṃ" / sa ca kulaputra ratnacandrastathāgata āha - "gacchata kulaputrā yasyaitarhi kālaṃ manyadhve, tatra ca ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya sakāśāt samādhānamukhanirdeśaṃ caryāvaiśāradyadharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyadhve" /
children.translated_text: ) and venerate him, to whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> has sent his approval with three reasons, and has sent this <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flower." And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s>, O son of good family, said: "Go, O sons of good family, if you deem now to be the right time. There from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> you shall hear the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> of the <s>samādhi</s>-gateway teaching and the conduct-confidence."

body.translated_text: At that time, ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> spoke with one voice: "We too, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, wish to go to the <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, to the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for seeing, venerating, and attending upon him, and to see that good man (

body.text: atha tau dvau kulaputrau ratnaketuścandraketuśca ratnacandrasya tathāgatasya sakāśāccandrarocavimalaṃ puṣpaṃ gṛhītvā sārdhaṃ dvānavatibhirbodhisattvakoṭībhī ratnavicayāyāṃ lokadhātau saṃprasthitau / tadyathāpi nāma vidyutā evameva tato bodhisattvaparṣād ratnavicaye buddhakṣetre 'ntarhitau, iha saṃtīraṇe buddhakṣetre jambūvanodyāne ca sthitau / yena ratnagarbhastathāgatastenopasaṃkrāme taṃ upetya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā vividhābhirbodhisattvavikurvaṇābhiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyāgrato brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvāvatīṃ ca bodhisattvaparṣāṃ prāñjalībhūtāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣamāṇāṃ tayorbodhisattvayoretadabhavad / "ayaṃ sa mahākaruṇāsamanvāgato yasya ratnacandreṇa tathāgateneme (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 291.

children.text: ) candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpāḥ preṣitāḥ" / atha tau dvau bodhisattvau bhagavataḥ sakāśāt parivartitvā brāhmaṇasya puṣpaṃ upanāmayitvā etadavocatāṃ - "imaṃ te satpuruṣa ratnacandreṇa tathāgatena candrarocavimalaṃ puṣpaṃ preṣitaṃ, sādhukāraśca te satpuruṣaḥ preṣitaḥ; yāvadyathoktaṃ pūrvaṃ / peyālaṃ, aprameyāsaṃkhyeyebhyaḥ pūrvāyāṃ diśāyāṃ buddhakṣetrebhyo bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ santīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ saṃprāptāḥ, candrarocavimalapuṣpāṃ gṛhītvā brāhmaṇasya puṣpāḥ preṣitāḥ, tribhiścāṅgaiḥ sādhukāraḥ preṣito; yathā pūrvoktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers." Then those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having turned away from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, presented the flower to the brahmin and said: "This <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flower has been sent to you, O good man, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s>, and his approval has been sent to you, O good man" — all in full as previously stated. Abbreviated: from immeasurable and incalculable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the eastern direction, <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> arrived at the <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, bearing <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers, sending them to the brahmin, and the approval with three reasons was sent, as previously stated.

body.translated_text: Then those two sons of good family, <s>Ratnaketu</s> and <s>Candraketu</s>, having received from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s> the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flower, together with ninety-two <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, set out from the world-realm <s>Ratnavicayā</s>. Just as if by a flash of lightning, they vanished from the <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly there in the <s>Ratnavicaya</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and appeared here in the <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, in the <s>Jambūvana</s> garden. They approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and having approached, they bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with their heads, and having performed worship through various miraculous transformations of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, they saw the brahmin before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and the entire <s>bodhisattva</s>-assembly standing with joined palms, speaking his praise. Then those two <s>bodhisattvas</s> thought: "This is that one endowed with great compassion, to whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacandra</s> has sent these (

body.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśāyāmito buddhakṣetrāt saptanavatibuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrānatikramitvā tatra niryūhavijṛṃbhito nāma lokadhātustatra niryūhavijṛṃbhite buddhakṣetre siṃhavijṛṃbhiteśvararājā nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastiṣṭhati yāpayati śuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ śuddhāṃ mahāyānakathāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma / tasmiṃśca parṣadi dvau bodhisattvau mahāsattvau, eko jñānavajraketurnāma dvitīyaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 292.

children.text:
) siṃhavajraketustau dvau bodhisattvau siṃhavijṛṃbhiteśvararājaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchataḥ sma - "ko bhadanta bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya mahataśca puṣpavarṣasya?"; yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ / peyālaṃ, yāvad aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyanyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyā bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāḥ saṃtīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetramanuprāptāḥ, yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ /
tena khalu punaḥ samayena paścimāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrādekonanavatibuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrabuddhakṣetrānatikramitvā tatra jayāvatirnāma buddhakṣetraṃ, tatra jitendriyaviśālanetro nāma tathāgatastiṣṭhati yāpayati, caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ tribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayati sma / tatra bhadravairocano nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ siṃhavijṛṃbhitakāyaśca nāma dvitīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastau dvau satpuruṣau jitendriyaviśālanetraṃ (
children.translated_text:
) named <s>Siṃhavajraketu</s>. Those two <s>bodhisattvas</s> asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃhavijṛṃbhiteśvararāja</s>: "What, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great earthquake in the world and for the great rain of flowers?" And so forth, as previously stated. Abbreviated: immeasurable and incalculable <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands from other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the southern direction arrived at the <s>Santīraṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — all as previously stated.
Now at that time, in the western direction, passing beyond eighty-nine <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there was a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> called <s>Jayāvatī</s> (Victorious). There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jitendriyaviśālanetra</s> (Conqueror of Senses, Wide-Eyed) abided and taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies through the three vehicles. There a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Bhadravairocana</s> and a second <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Siṃhavijṛṃbhitakāya</s> — those two good men asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jitendriyaviśālanetra</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 293.

children.text: ) tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripṛcchataḥ - "kuto 'yaṃ mahāpṛthivīcālaprādurbhāvo, mahātaśca puṣpavṛṣṭipravarṣaṇasya?"; yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) about this matter: "What is the origin of this great earthquake, and of the showering of the great rain of flowers?" And so forth, as previously stated.

body.translated_text: Likewise in the southern direction, passing beyond ninety-seven <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there was a world-realm called <s>Niryūhavijṛṃbhita</s> (Extended Display). In that <s>Niryūhavijṛṃbhita</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Siṃhavijṛṃbhiteśvararāja</s> (King Lord of the Lion's Display), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, abided and taught pure <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourse as the <s>Dharma</s> to pure <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. In that assembly were two <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> — one named <s>Jñānavajraketu</s> and the second (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenottarasyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrādbuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya tatra jamburnāma lokadhātustatra lokeśvararāja nāma tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavān śuddhānāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śuddhāṃ mahāyānakathāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma / tatra dvau bodhisattvau, eko 'calasthāvaro nāma dvitīyaḥ prajñādharo nāma, tau lokeśvararājaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchataḥ sma - "ko bhadanta bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvasya, mahatyāśca puspavṛṣṭer[?"];yāvad yathā pūrvoktaṃ /
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the northern direction, passing beyond <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there was a world-realm called <s>Jambu</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Lokeśvararāja</s> (Lord King of the World), and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, taught pure <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourse as the <s>Dharma</s> to pure <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had set out on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. There were two <s>bodhisattvas</s> — one named <s>Acalasthāvara</s> and the second named <s>Prajñādhara</s>. They asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>: "What, O Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great earthquake in the world, and for the great rain of flowers?" And so forth, as previously stated.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenādho diśīto buddhakṣetrādaṣṭānavatibuddhakṣetranayutānatikramya tatra vigatatamo 'ndhakārā nāma lokadhātustatra vigatabhayaparyutthānaghoṣo nāma tathāgatastiṣṭhati yāpayati, caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 294.

children.text: ) tribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayati sma / tatra buddhakṣetre dvau bodhisattvau mahāsattvāveko 'rajavairocano nāma dvitīyaḥ svargavairocano nāma, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) taught the <s>Dharma</s> through the three vehicles. In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> were two <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> — one named <s>Arajavairocana</s> (Dustless Radiance) and the second named <s>Svargavairocana</s> (Heavenly Radiance) — and so forth, as previously stated.

body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the downward direction, passing beyond ninety-eight <s>nayutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, there was a world-realm called <s>Vigatatamoandhakārā</s> (Free from Darkness and Obscurity). There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vigatabhayaparyutthānaghoṣa</s> (Sound of Freedom from Fear and Agitation) abided, and to the four assemblies (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenopariṣṭhāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrāddve śatasahasre buddhakṣetrāṇāmatikramitvā tatra saṃkusumitā nāma lokadhātustatra saṃkusumite buddhakṣetre prasphulitakusumavairocano nāma tathāgata yāvad buddho bhagavāṃstiṣṭhati yāpayati, caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ tribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayati sma / tatra buddhakṣetre dvau bodhisattvau mahāsattvau prativasata, ekaḥ svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣayo nāma dvitīyo dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopito nāma bodhisattvastau dvau satpuruṣau prasphulitakusumavairocanaṃ tathāgataṃ pṛṣṭavantau / "ko bhadanta bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 295.

children.text: ) mahatyāśca puṣpavṛṣṭeḥ?" / prasphulitakusumavairocanastathāgata āha - "asti kulaputrādho diśīto buddhakṣetrāt dve śatasahasre buddhakṣetrāṇāmatikramya tatra saṃtīraṇo nāma lokadhātustatra ratnagarbho nāma tathāgato yāvadbuddho bhagavāṃstiṣṭhati dharmaṃ ca deśayati sma / bahusattvakoṭyo vyākarotyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bodhisattvaviṣayakṣetrasandarśanapraṇidhānaviṣayavyūhasamādhiviṣayadhāraṇīmukhaniryūhaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣamāṇa ; ekaśca tatra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sa evaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān, mahākaruṇāparibhāvitā vācā bhāṣitā, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākaraṇanirdeśaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ, yathārūpā praṇidhānanetryudbhāvitā yathā bahubodhisattvakoṭībhirbuddhakṣetrapraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā vaineyasattvāśca parigṛhītāḥ; sa caiko mahākaruṇāsamanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ sarvāvatiṃ parṣadamabhibhūya kliṣṭaṃ pañcakaṣāyaṃ kleśāraṇikaliyugaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ (
children.translated_text: ) and a great shower of flowers?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s> said: "There is, O sons of good family, passing beyond two hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields from this <s>Buddha</s>-field in the downward direction, a world-realm called <s>Saṃtīraṇa</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnagarbha</s> (Jewel Womb), up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, is abiding and teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. He is prophesying many <s>koṭis</s> of beings for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and is expounding a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) that reveals the entrances of <s>samādhi</s>, the display of <s>bodhisattva</s> domains and <s>Buddha</s>-field visions, the realm of aspirations and arrays, and the exposition of the gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. And there one greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has made such an aspiration — words infused with great compassion have been spoken — a revelation of the prophecy for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, such as the guiding aspirations that have been brought forth, such as the <s>Buddha</s>-field aspirations made by many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, and the beings to be trained who have been accepted. And that one greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s>, surpassing the entire assembly, has accepted a defiled <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five defilements, in the age of strife, a wilderness of afflictions — (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 296.

children.text:
) parigṛhītaṃ, sarve cānantaryakārakā yāvad akuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dagdhasaṃtānā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / sarvāvatīrca sā parṣā sadevagandharvāsuramānuṣaśca loko ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pūjāmapahāya tasya mahākāruṇikasya pūjākarmaṇe udyuktāḥ pañcamaṇḍalena vanditvā prāñjalibhūtāḥ sthitvā varṇaṃ bhāṣante sma / sa ca mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purato niṣaṇṇo vyākaraṇaṃ śṛṇvānaḥ / yadā ca tena mahāsattvena tasya bhagavataḥ purato dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nikṣiptaṃ tadā tena bhagavatā tathārūpaṃ smitaṃ prāviṣkṛtaṃ, yadā daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ calitā pracalitā saṃpracalitā kaṃpitā yāvat puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitā / sarvebhyaśca tebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prabodhanārthaṃ, mahākāruṇyā bodhisattvapraṇidhānacaryā nidarśanārthaṃ, bodhisattvā mahāsattvā buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamebhyo lokadhātubhyo daśabhyo digbhyastatra buddhakṣetre sannipatanārthaṃ, bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ samādhānamukhanirdeśacaryāvaiśāradyaṃ
dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣaṇārthaṃ tena tathāgatenaivaṃrūpāṇi (
children.translated_text: ) and has accepted as beings to be trained all those who commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, up to those who have accumulated unwholesome roots and whose continuum is burnt. And the entire assembly, including the world with its gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and humans, setting aside the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, became devoted to making offerings to that greatly compassionate one, bowing with the five-point [prostration], standing with palms joined, proclaiming his qualities. And that <s>mahāsattva</s>, seated before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, is hearing his prophecy. And when that <s>mahāsattva</s> set his right knee upon the ground before the Blessed One, then the Blessed One displayed such a smile that in world-realms in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the great earth trembled, shook, quaked, shuddered — and a shower of flowers rained down. And from all those <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> [have come] for the purpose of awakening, for the purpose of demonstrating the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of aspirations impelled by great compassion, for the purpose of gathering <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> from world-realms equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions to that <s>Buddha</s>-field, and for the purpose of expounding to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the mastery of the exposition of the entrances of <s>samādhi</s> and the conduct — by that <s>Tathāgata</s>, such (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 297.
) miracles were displayed."

body.translated_text: At that time, passing beyond two hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields from this <s>Buddha</s>-field in the upward direction, there was a world-realm called <s>Saṃkusumitā</s> (Fully Blossoming). In that <s>Saṃkusumitā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s> (Brilliance of Blossoming Flowers), up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, was abiding and sustaining, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies by means of the three vehicles. In that <s>Buddha</s>-field dwelt two <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>: one named <s>Svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣaya</s> (He Whose Domain Agitates [Other] Domains), and the second a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopita</s> (Agitated by the Joy of <s>Dhāraṇī</s>). Those two good men asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s>: "What, O venerable Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation in the world of a great earthquake (

body.text: tau ca kulaputra dvau bodhisattvau mahāsattvau svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣayaśca dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopitaśca taṃ prasphulitakusumavairocanaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchataḥ sma / "kiyaccirotpāditaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃstena mahākāruṇikena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bodhāya cittaṃ?; kiyacciraṃ vā sa mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhicārikāṃ cīrṇaṃ, yena pañcakaṣāye loke tīvrakleśaraṇike kaliyuge vartamāne kālaḥ parigṛhīta ānantaryakārakā yāvad akuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dagdhasaṃtānā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ?" / prasphulitakusumavairocanastathāgata āha - "saṃprati kulaputra tena mahākāruṇikena prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ / gacchata kulaputrā yūyaṃ santīraṇaṃ lokadhātuṃ tasya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya taṃ ca samādhānamukhanirdeśaṃ caryāvaiśāradyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śravaṇāya / taṃ ca mahākāruṇikaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ mama vacanena pṛcchatha evaṃ ca vaktavyaḥ; prasphulitakusumavairocanastathāgatastvāṃ (
