children.text: ) satpuruṣa pṛcchate candrarocavimalaṃ puṣpaṃ preṣitaṃ sādhukāraścānupradattaḥ / evaṃ ca tvayā satpuruṣa prathamacittotpādena mahākaruṇāvyāhāreṇa daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā lokadhātavaḥ śabdenāpūritāḥ, mahākaruṇāśabdaśca pratilabdhastena tvaṃ satpuruṣa sādhu bhūyaḥ, paścimakānāṃ mahākaruṇāmahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāvyāhāreṇa praṇidhānanetrīdhvajāmucchrepayasi; tena tvaṃ satpuruṣa sādhu bhūyastvaṃ satpuruṣa buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāgatā asaṃkhyeyakalpabuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā daśadiśa lokadhātavo yaśaḥkīrtiśabdenāpūritāstena tvaṃ satpuruṣa bahvasaṃkhyeyasattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā, bhagavataḥ sakāśamupanītā, avaivartikāśca sthāpitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / kaiścittatraiva bhagavataḥ sakāśe praṇidhānena buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ parigṛhītā vaineyāḥ sattvāḥ svakaruṇāraśmibhirācchāditā; (
children.translated_text: ) asks after you, O good man, and has sent the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> (Moonlight Stainless) flowers, and has given his approval. Thus by your first generation of the mind, O good man, and by the utterance of your great compassion, world-realms in the ten directions equal in number to the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields have been filled with the sound, and the renown of great compassion has been won — therefore, O good man, well done! Furthermore, for the sake of future <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> who have set forth in the great compassionate <s>Mahāyāna</s>, you raise the banner of guiding aspirations through the utterance of great compassion — therefore, O good man, well done! Furthermore, O good man, from <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to atoms, through incalculable <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, world-realms in the ten directions have been filled with the sound of your fame, glory, and renown — and thereby, O good man, you have inspired, established, and grounded many incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), led them to the presence of the Blessed One, and placed them in irreversibility toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And some of them, right there in the presence of the Blessed One, through their aspirations have accepted the arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, and have sheltered beings to be trained under the rays of their own compassion; (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 299.

children.text: ) ye tvayānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā na ca vyākaraṇapratilabdhaṃ, te 'pi paścādvyākaraṇaṃ pratilapsyante, sarve te paścādyāvadbuddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairdaśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhatvaṃ prāpya dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayitvā tvāmevārabhya varṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyanti / etena tṛtīyena kāraṇena tvaṃ satpuruṣa sādhu" /
children.translated_text: ) those whom you have inspired toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> but who have not yet received their prophecy — they too shall later receive their prophecy; all of them, in the future, over <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in other world-realms equal in number to atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, having attained <s>Buddhahood</s> and turned the righteous <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma), shall proclaim your qualities. By this third reason, O good man, well done!'"

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, those two <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣaya</s> and <s>Dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopita</s>, asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s>: "How long ago, O venerable Blessed One, did that greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> first generate the mind of awakening? And how long has that greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, that he has accepted a time when the world is of the five defilements, in the wilderness of intense afflictions, in the prevailing age of strife, and has accepted as beings to be trained all those who commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, up to those who have accumulated unwholesome roots and whose continuum is burnt?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s> said: "Just now, O sons of good family, that greatly compassionate one has for the first time generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Go, O sons of good family, to the world-realm <s>Saṃtīraṇa</s>, for the sight of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for veneration and attendance, and for hearing the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the mastery of the exposition of the entrances of <s>samādhi</s> and the conduct. And ask that greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> in my name, and tell him thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s> (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bahubodhisattvakoṭya evamūcur["]vayamapi bhadanta bhagavaṃstatra saṃtīraṇe buddhakṣetre gacchema, tasya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya, taṃ ca satpuruṣaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya, yasya tathāgatena tribhiraṅgaiḥ sādhukāro 'nupreṣita, ime ca candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpāḥ preṣitāḥ" / sa ca kulaputra prasphulitakusumavairocanastathāgatastānāha - "gacchata yūyaṃ kulaputrā yasyaitarhi kālaṃ manyadhve / tatra yūyaṃ kulaputrā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya sakāśāt samavadhānamukhanirdeśacaryāvaiśāradyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 300.

body.translated_text: At that time, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> spoke thus: "We too, O venerable Blessed One, wish to go to that <s>Saṃtīraṇa</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, for the sight of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for veneration and attendance, and for the sight, veneration, and attendance of that good man to whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> has sent his approval with three praises, and these <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers." And the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s>, O son of good family, said to them: "Go, O sons of good family, at whatever time you deem fit. There, O sons of good family, from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, you shall hear the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the mastery of the exposition of the entrances of <s>samādhi</s> and the conduct (

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra tau dvau bodhisattvau svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣayaśca dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopitaśca tasya prasphulitakusumavairocanasya tathāgatasya sakāśāccandrarocavimalāṃ puṣpāṃ gṛhītvā bahubodhisattvakoṭībhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃkusumitādbuddhakṣetrāt prasthāpitā iha buddhakṣetra ekakṣaṇena saṃprāptā jambūvanodyāne tasthuryena ca ratnagarbhastathāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / tena khalu punaḥsamayena sarvāvantaṃ saṃtīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ evaṃrūpaṃ paripūrṇaṃ mahāyānikairbodhisattvaiḥ pratyekabuddhayānikaiḥ śrāvakayānikaiḥ kulaputrairdevairyāvan mahoragaistadyathāpi nāma ikṣuvanaṃ vā naḍavanaṃ vā tilavanaṃ vā śālivanaṃ vā saṃpannaṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavet / evameva tasmin samaye saṃtīraṇaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paripūrṇaṃ sphuṭaṃ mahāyānikaiḥ kulaputrairyāvan mahoragaiste ca bodhisattvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā vividhasamādhānabalena bodhisattvavikurvaṇena pūjāṃ kṛtvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purataḥ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvāvatyaśca tāḥ parṣāḥ prāñjalibhūtāḥ sthitvā varṇaṃ bhāṣamāṇāḥ / teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmetadabhavat - (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 301.

children.text: ) "ayaṃ mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yasya prasphulitakusumavairocanena tathāgatena ime candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpā visarjitās[" / ]te ca bodhisattvā bhagavataḥ sakāśāt parāvṛtya tasya brāhmaṇasya te candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpā upanāmayitvāhuḥ / "ime te satpuruṣa prasphulitakusumavairocanena tathāgatena candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpāḥ preṣitāḥ, sādhukāraśca te satpuruṣānupradattaḥ" / yāvatpūrvoktaṃ tribhiraṅgaiḥ sādhukāraṃ niveditamiti / yāni ca tāni puṣpāṇi śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pravarṣitāni, vividhaśca kuśalaśabdaistāvadbuddhakṣetrāṇyāpūritāni; tadyathā buddhaśabdena dharmaśabdena saṅghaśabdenāvabhāsaśabdena pāramitāśabdena balaśabdena vaiśāradyaśabdena abhijñāśabdenānabhisaṃskāraśabdenānutpādaśabdenānirodhaśabdena śāntaśabdenopaśāntaśabdena praśāntaśabdena mahāmaitrīśabdena mahākaruṇāśabdena / yaddaśasu diśāsu teṣu śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tenāvabhāsenāvabhāsitāstatra (
children.translated_text: ) "This is the greatly compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> to whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s> has sent these <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers." Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, turning away from the Blessed One, presented those <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers to the brahmin and said: "These, O good man, are the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers sent to you by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s>, and an approval has been given to you, O good man." They conveyed the threefold approval as previously stated. And those flowers rained down upon the empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and those <s>Buddha</s>-fields were filled with various wholesome sounds: namely, the sound of '<s>Buddha</s>,' the sound of '<s>Dharma</s>,' the sound of '<s>Saṅgha</s>,' the sound of 'radiance,' the sound of 'the <s>pāramitās</s>,' the sound of 'the powers,' the sound of 'the [four] fearlessnesses,' the sound of 'the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges),' the sound of 'non-fabrication,' the sound of 'non-arising,' the sound of 'non-cessation,' the sound of 'peace,' the sound of 'calm,' the sound of 'complete peace,' the sound of 'great loving-kindness,' the sound of 'great compassion.' And in the ten directions, in those empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields illuminated by that radiance, there (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 302.

children.text:
) ye kecit sattvā manuṣyā vāmanuṣyāste sarve ye kecit sattvā yamasadṛśāḥ kecidudakasadṛśāḥ kecicchikharasadṛśāḥ kecidbrahmasadṛśāḥ kecicchakrasadṛśāḥ kecit puṣpasadṛśāḥ kecidgaruḍasadṛśāḥ kecit siṃhasadṛśāḥ kecit sūryasadṛśāḥ keciccandrasadṛśāḥ kecit tārakasadṛśāḥ kecidgṛdhrasadṛśāḥ śṛgālakāyāḥ saṃdṛśyante; yathārūpeṇa kuśalapakṣamanaskāreṇa te sattvāḥ sanniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya, tathārūpeṇa kāyena saṃdṛśyante / tathārūpāśca kulaputra tatra sattvāḥ svakaṃ kāyaṃ paśyanti; tathārūpāśca te sattvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya kāyaṃ samanupaśyanti / sa ca kulaputra
samudrareṇurbrāhmaṇo 'grapurohito ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ purataḥ sahasrapatre saptaratnamayapadmakeśare niṣaṇṇaṃ samanupaśyati / sarve cātra kulaputra sattvā niṣaṇṇā vā sthitvā vā kṣitau vā ambare vā ekaikaḥ sattvo ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgatamevaṃ paśyanti; "agrato ratnagarbhastathāgato niṣaṇṇo 'haṃ" sarvacetasā samanvāharanti, "māmekamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati" /
children.translated_text: ) whatever beings there were, whether human or non-human — some appeared like <s>Yama</s>, some like water, some like mountain peaks, some like <s>Brahmā</s>, some like <s>Śakra</s>, some like flowers, some like <s>garuḍas</s>, some like lions, some like the sun, some like the moon, some like stars, some like vultures, and some with bodies like jackals — according to the kind of wholesome mental attention with which those beings sat down to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, in such a form did they appear. And, O son of good family, those beings there perceived their own bodies in such forms; and those beings perceived the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> in such forms. And, O son of good family, the brahmin <s>Samudrareṇu</s>, the chief priest, perceived the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> seated before him on the pistil of a thousand-petalled lotus made of the seven jewels. And all beings here, O son of good family, whether seated or standing, on the ground or in the sky, each being perceived the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> is seated before me' — all thought with their entire mind — 'He teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for me alone.'

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Svaviṣayasaṃkopitaviṣaya</s> and <s>Dhāraṇīsaṃpraharṣaṇavikopita</s>, taking the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers from the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prasphulitakusumavairocana</s>, departed from the <s>Saṃkusumitā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field together with many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and arrived in this <s>Buddha</s>-field in a single instant, standing in the <s>Jambūvana</s> garden. They then approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>. At that time, the entire <s>Saṃtīraṇa</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field was completely filled with <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle followers, <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle followers, sons of good family, gods, and up to <s>mahoragas</s> — just as a field of sugarcane, or a thicket of reeds, or a field of sesame, or a rice paddy might be full and dense, even so at that time the <s>Saṃtīraṇa</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field was filled and packed with <s>Mahāyāna</s> sons of good family and up to <s>mahoragas</s>. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with their heads, having made offerings through the power of various <s>samādhis</s> and <s>bodhisattva</s> miraculous displays, and having seen the brahmin before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, all those assemblies stood with palms joined, proclaiming his qualities. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> had this thought: (

body.text: sa ca kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samudrareṇorbrāhmaṇasya sādhukāramanupradattaḥ / "sādhu sādhu mahākāruṇika mahābrāhmaṇa, gaṇanātikrāntānāṃ sattvānāṃ tvaṃ asi kāruṇikahitakaraḥ prabhāsakaro loke saṃdṛśyase / tadyathāpi nāma brāhmaṇa saṃpannaṃ puṣpakṣetraṃ nānāvarṇaṃ nānāgandhaṃ nānāsparśaṃ nānāpatraṃ nānādaṇḍaṃ nānāmūlaṃ nānābhaiṣajyopakaraṇasthānaṃ / kecidatra puṣpā yojanaśataṃ pramāṇena varṇena gandhena tapanti virocanti, keciddviyojanaśataṃ kecittriyojanaśataṃ, peyālaṃ, kecidatra puṣpā yāvat sarvacāturdvīpikāṃ lokadhātuṃ varṇena gandhena tapanti virocanti / ye ca tatra sattvāścakṣurhīnāste puṣpagandhaṃ ghrātvā cakṣuṃsi pratilabhante, badhirāḥ śrotrāṇi pratilabhante, yāvat sarvāṅgavihīnāḥ sarvāṅgāni pratilabhante / ye ca tatra sattvāścaturuttararogaśatopadrutāste taṃ gandhaṃ ghrātvā sarvarogebhyaḥ parimucyeyuḥ / ye ca tatra sattvā mattonmattaparamattāḥ suptacittā vikṣiptacittāḥ smṛtipraṇaṣṭāsteṣāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ gandhamāghrātvā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 304.

children.text: ) sarve smṛtiṃ pratilabheyuḥ / evaṃ ca tatra madhye puṣpakṣetre puṇḍarīkamutpannaṃ, dṛḍhasāraṃ vajramayaṃ vaidūryadaṇḍaṃ śatakomalaṃ kanakapatramaśmagarbhakiṃśukaṃ lohitamuktikeśaraṃ, caturaśītiryojanasahasrāṇyuccatvena yojanaśatasahasraṃ vistāreṇa / tacca puṇḍarīkaṃ daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamāllokadhātuṃ varṇena gandhena sphuritvā virocate / ye ca brāhmaṇa teṣu daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvā dhātuviruddhāḥ kāyā vyādhyupahatā aṅgavihīnā vā mattapramattonmattāḥ suptasmṛtipraṇaṣṭā vikṣiptacittāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasya puṇḍarīkasyāvabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā gandhaṃ ghrātvā sarvavyādhayaḥ praśamaṃ gaccheyuḥ smṛtiṃ ca pratilabheyuḥ / ye ca tatra buddhakṣetreṣu sattvā mṛtā acirakālagatā avikṣiptaśarīrāsteṣāṃ kuṇapebhyaḥ tasya puṇḍarīkasya raśmayo nipatitvā gandhena vā spṛṣṭvā punaste kuṇapā jīvitendriyaṃ pratilabheyuḥ, punaścottiṣṭheyurmitrasālohitāṃśca dṛṣṭvā te sarve udyānaṃ praviśya pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samaṅgībhūtā vihareyusye ca punastataścyaveyusteṣu dve brahmavihāra upapadyeyuḥ, ye ca tatra cirasthāyino bhaveyuraparīttāyuṣkā, na ca tatra cyūtvā anyatropapadyeyuḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) all would regain their mindfulness. And in the midst of that flower-field, a <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) arose — of firm essence, made of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), with a stalk of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), with a hundred soft petals of gold, with pistils of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald) and <s>kiṃśuka</s> (scarlet), with stamens of red pearls, eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth. And that <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, having pervaded world-realms in the ten directions equal in number to the atoms of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with its color and fragrance, shone brilliantly. And, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, whatever beings in those world-realms in the ten directions equal in number to the atoms of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> have obstructed bodily elements, are afflicted by disease, are deprived of limbs, or are intoxicated
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 305.

children.text:
) yathā brāhmaṇāstaṃ puṣpakṣetramevamayaṃ mahāyānasannipāto draṣṭavyaḥ / yathā sūryodgamanakāle pratyupasthite te puṣpā visaritā prasphulitā bhavanti tapanti virocanti kecidyojanaśatamuccatvena kecid yāvad yojanasahasramuccatvena, bahunāṃ sattvānāṃ vividharogāḥ praśamanti, evameva satpuruṣāḥ tathāgato buddhasūryo loka udapādi / yathā te puṣpāḥ sūryoditasya asya raśmibhirvikasitā bhāsanti
tapanti virocanti, vividharogopahatānāṃ sattvānāṃ rogopaśamo bhavati / evamevāhaṃ satpuruṣa loka utpannaḥ sattvāṃ kāruṇyaraśmibhiḥ chādayitvā vikasitvā bhūyaḥ sattvāṃstriṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu niyojayāmi, tvayāpyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveṣitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā mama ca sakāśamupanītāstaiśca sattvairmama sakāśe svakasvakāni praṇidhānāni kṛtāni buddhakṣetrāṇi ca parigṛhītāni, kecit pariśuddhā buddhakṣetrāḥ parigṛhītāḥ kecidapariśuddhāḥ, tathā caivaṃ mayā vyākṛtāḥ / yaiḥ satpuruṣairmama sakāśāt pariśuddhā buddhakṣetrāḥ parigṛhītāstaiḥ śuddhāśayāḥ suvineyā avaruptakuśalamūlā vaineyāḥ sattvāḥ parigṛhītā, (
children.translated_text: ) just as, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, that flower-field — so should this <s>Mahāyāna</s> assembly be viewed. Just as when the time of sunrise arrives, those flowers open and bloom, they shine and blaze, some a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height, some up to a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, and the various diseases of many beings are pacified — even so, O good men, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-sun, has arisen in the world. Just as those flowers, expanded by the rays of the risen sun, illuminate, shine, and blaze, and the pacification of diseases occurs for beings afflicted by various diseases — even so, O good man, I have arisen in the world as one who
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 306.

children.text: ) na te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ucyante, na ca teṣāṃ mahāpuruṣakāryaṃ, na ca teṣāṃ mahākaruṇācittacaitasikeṣu pravartate, na ca te bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ karuṇārthāyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ paryeṣante / ye 'pi te pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇanti, utsṛṣṭakṛpāste bodhisattvā; ye śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikaiḥ parivarjitaṃ buddhakṣetramākāṅkṣanti, na ca te bodhisattvāḥ kuśalajñānāśayabhūtā / yeṣāmevaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ yathā vayaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhavarjitā akuśalamūlasamavadhānagatairmātṛgrāmairvivarjite narakatiryagyoniyamalokavivarjite buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyurmahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhaparivarjitāṃ śuddhāṃ mahāyānakathāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ, bodhiprāptaścāhaṃ dīrghāyuṣko bhaveyaṃ cirasthāyī, bahūni kalpāni śūddhāśayānāṃ suvinītānāṃ kuśalamūlasamavadhānagatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ / tena te bodhisattvā na kuśalajñānāśayasaṃbhūtā, na mahāsattvā ityucyate /
children.translated_text: ) those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> are not so called, nor is the great task of a great being theirs, nor does great compassion operate in their mental factors, nor do those <s>bodhisattvas</s> seek supreme perfect awakening for the sake of compassion for all beings. And those who take up a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> are <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have abandoned active concern; those who desire a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> free of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — those <s>bodhisattvas</s> are not truly endowed with the disposition of wholesome wisdom. Those whose vow has been made thus: 'We, rejecting <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, with beings who have fallen into the tendency of unwholesome roots'

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, gave his approval to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Samudrareṇu</s>: "Well done, well done, O greatly compassionate one, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>! You are a compassionate benefactor of beings beyond calculation, and you appear in the world as a light-maker. Just as, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, there is a flourishing flower-field, of various colors, various fragrances, various textures, various leaves, various stems, various roots, and a place for various medicinal preparations — some flowers there shine and blaze with a measure of a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in their color and fragrance, some two hundred <s>yojanas</s>, some three hundred <s>yojanas</s> — abbreviated — some flowers shine and blaze with their color and fragrance throughout the entire four-continent world-realm. And whatever beings there are blind — upon smelling the fragrance of those flowers, they obtain eyesight; the deaf obtain hearing; and so on, up to those deprived of all limbs who obtain all their limbs. And whatever beings there are afflicted by four hundred and more diseases — upon smelling that fragrance, they would be freed from all diseases. And whatever beings there are intoxicated, insane, supremely intoxicated, of dormant mind, of distracted mind, who have lost their mindfulness — upon smelling the fragrance of those flowers (

body.text: sa ca kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato bāhuṃ prasārayitvā pañcabhiraṅgulībhirnānāvarṇā anekavarṇā anekaśatasahasravarṇā raśmayaḥ prāmuñcan, te gatvā raśmayo 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyā purimāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrān avabhāsayitvā, tatrāṅguṣṭhā nāma lokadhātuḥ, tatrāṅguṣṭhāyāṃ lokadhātau daśavarṣāyuṣkā manuṣyā durvarṇā drohoḍimakā akuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā aṅguṣṭhamātramuccatvena / tatra jyotīraso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / sa ca kaliyugapramāṇānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ hastapramāṇena hastamekaṃ tathāgata ūrdhvatvena hastaśca; aṅguṣṭhapramāṇānāṃ puruṣānāṃ pramāṇena saptāṅguṣṭhāni / sa ca tathāgatastiṣṭhati dhriyati yāpayati caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ tribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayati /
body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> extended his arm, and from his five fingers emitted rays of various colors, of many colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors. Those immeasurable and incalculable rays, having gone and illuminated <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the eastern direction, [revealed] a world-realm there named <s>Aṅguṣṭhā</s> ('Thumb'). In that <s>Aṅguṣṭhā</s> world-realm, humans had a lifespan of ten years, were of ugly appearance, malicious and hostile, had fallen into the tendency of unwholesome roots, and were the size of a thumb in height. There, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One [dwelt]. He, among those thumb-sized beings, was the size of a hand by the hand-measure of those thumb-sized beings — that <s>Tathāgata</s>, among a populace with a ten-year lifespan, turned the righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: atha khalu kulaputra tacca buddhakṣetraṃ tāṃśca manuṣyāṃstaṃ ca tathāgataṃ sarvāvatī ca sā parṣādrākṣīt / ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha āha - "anena jyotīrasena tathāgatenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairatikrāntaiḥ prathamacittamutpāditamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 308.

children.text: ) ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsasya tathāgatasyāgrato, bahuprāṇakoṭīnayutānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitāni niveśitāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni; yathābhiprāyāṃ sattvaistasya tathāgatasya purataḥ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, kecidbuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāḥ parigṛhītāḥ pariśuddhāḥ kecidapariśuddhāḥ pañcakaṣāyāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / tatra ca tena mahāsattvenāhaṃ samādāpito niveśitaścānuttarāyāṃ samyaksabodhau / tatra ca mayā ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsasya tathāgatasya purato 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhapraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / sa ca me tathāgataḥ sādhukāramadāsīt vyākṛtaścāhamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / yo 'sāvasmākaṃ bodhāya samādāyakaḥ kalyāṇamitro 'tīva satpuruṣastīvrapañcakaṣāye kaliyuge vartamāne kāle pratikliṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ, ānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā dagdhasantānāḥ saṃsārāṭavīkāntārasaṅkaṭaprāptā vaineyasattva praṇidhānaḥ parigṛhītastasya satpuruṣasya daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyebhyo 'nyonyalokadhātubhyastiṣṭhanto (
children.translated_text: ) in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsa</s>. Many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of beings were encouraged, established, and confirmed in supreme perfect awakening. According to their aspirations, beings made their vows before that <s>Tathāgata</s>; some took up the qualities of purified <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, and some took up impurified [fields], the five degenerations. And there, that <s>mahāsattva</s> encouraged and established me in supreme perfect awakening. And there, I, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsa</s>, regarding supreme perfect awakening in a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the five degenerations
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 309.

children.text: ) yāpayanto buddhā bhagavantaḥ sādhukāraṃ pradattavantaḥ preṣitavanto, mahākaruṇāvairocanasaumyo nāma kṛtaṃ / sa ca mahākaruṇāvairocanasaumyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'smākaṃ kalyāṇamitro hitakara etarhyacirābhisaṃbuddho 'ṅguṣṭhavatyāṃ lokadhātau aṅguṣṭhapramāṇānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye, teṣāṃ evāṅguṣṭhapramāṇānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ hastapramāṇena hastapramāṇakaḥ sa tathāgato daśavarṣāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitavān; tasyāpi bodhiprāptasya daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyebhyo lokadhātubhyastiṣṭhadbhiryāpayadbhistaistairbuddhairbhagavadbhirdūtāḥ preṣitāḥ pūjanārthāya, ye tena prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / ye tena prathamaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāstairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ pūrvakṛtajñatāmanusmaraṇamāṇaistasya tathāgatasya puṣpāḥ preṣitāḥ / paśya brāhmaṇa yathā te buddhā bhagavataḥ sarveṣu buddhakṣetreṣu dīrgheṇāyuṣā pariśuddhāśayānāṃ sukhavihāriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakāryaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, standing and sustaining, gave their approval and named him <s>Mahākaruṇāvairocanasaumya</s> ('Gentle Radiance of Great Compassion'). And that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākaruṇāvairocanasaumya</s> is our spiritual friend and benefactor who has now recently awakened in the <s>Aṅguṣṭhavatī</s> world-realm, in the midst of thumb-sized beings. That <s>Tathāgata</s>, being of hand-size by the hand-measure of those thumb-sized beings, among a populace with a ten-year lifespan, has turned the righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. And after his attainment of awakening, from immeasurable and incalculable world-realms in the ten directions
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 310.

children.text:
) kurvanti; sa ca jyotīrasastathāgata evaṃ pratikruṣṭe pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre buddhatvaṃ prāptavān, ānantaryakārakānāṃ yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatānāṃ sattvānāmevālpakenāyuṣā bahvatirekaṃ buddhakāryaṃ karoti, anujjhitvā śrāvakāṃ pratyekabuddhāṃśca dharmaṃ deśayari / evameva tvayā satpuruṣa sarvāmimāṃ bodhisattvaparṣāmabhibhūya viśiṣṭataraṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, pratikruṣṭe buddhakṣetre pañcakaṣāye vartamāne ānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā vaineyāḥ sattvāḥ parigṛhītāḥ / ye ca te mahāsattvā yaiḥ pariśuddhā buddhakṣetrāḥ parigṛhītā narakatiryagyoniparivarjitāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhaparivarjitāḥ
śuddhāśayāḥ suvinītā avaruptakuśalamūlāḥ sattvā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītā ime sattvāḥ puṣpopamā ucyante, na te mahāsattvāḥ puṇḍarīkopamā ye suvinītānāmavaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ madhye buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyanti /
children.translated_text: ) perform [Buddha-work]. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotīrasa</s> attained Buddhahood in such a reviled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the five degenerations, and for beings who have committed the <s>ānantarya</s> (acts of immediate retribution) and so on down to those who have fallen into the tendency of unwholesome roots — even with such a short lifespan, he performs abundant and surpassing <s>Buddha</s>-work, without abandoning <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Even so, O good man, you have surpassed this entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> with a more distinguished vow, having taken up a reviled <s>buddhakṣetra</s> where the five degenerations prevail, with beings to be trained who have committed the <s>ānantarya</s> and so on down to those who have fallen into the tendency of unwholesome roots. And those

body.translated_text: Then, O son of good family, the entire assembly beheld that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, those humans, and that <s>Tathāgata</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, said: "This <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, having passed beyond immeasurable and incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, first generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (

body.text: catvāri brāhmaṇa bodhiattvānāṃ kuśīdavastūni / katamāni catvāri? pariśuddhabuddhakṣetrapraṇidhānaṃ, pariśuddhāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakāryapraṇidhānaṃ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 311.

children.text: ) śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānakathā bodhiprāptasya deśanāpraṇidhānaṃ, bodhiprāptasya dīrghāyuṣkatāpraṇidhānaṃ / imāni catvāri bodhisattvānāṃ kuśīdavastūni / yena bodhisattvāḥ puṣpopamā ityucyante, na puṇḍarīkopamā na mahāsattvā ityucyante / tadyathāpi nāma brāhmaṇa imān mahābodhisattvaparṣāṃ sthāpayitvā vāyuviṣṇunā yenāpariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ kleśākulāḥ sattvā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītā ekatyo bhadrakalpikāḥ kulaputrāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) the vow to teach the discourse of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles after attaining awakening; and the vow for a long lifespan after attaining awakening. These are the four bases of laziness for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Because of them, <s>bodhisattvas</s> are called 'flower-like' and not 'white-lotus-like,' and not called <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings). Just as, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, setting aside this assembly of great <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Vāyuviṣṇu</s> took up an impurified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and accepted as his charges beings turbulent with afflictions — those are the particular sons of good family of the <s>Bhadra</s> <s>kalpa</s>.

body.translated_text: There are four bases of laziness for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. What four? The vow for a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; the vow for <s>Buddha</s>-work among beings of purified dispositions; (

body.text: catvārīmāni bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmārabdhavīryavastūni / katamāni catvāri? apariśuddhabuddhakṣetrapraṇidhānaṃ, apariśuddhāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakāryapraṇidhānaṃ, bodhiprāptasya śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānakathādeśanapraṇidhānaṃ, madhyamāyā pratipadā bodhiprāptasya nātidīrghatānālpāyuṣkatāpraṇidhānaṃ / imāni catvāri bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmārabdhavīryavastūni / yena te bodhisattvāḥ puṇḍarīkopamā ityucyante, na puṣpopamāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ityucyante / tadyathāpi (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 312.

children.text: ) tvaṃ brāhmaṇaitarhi aprameyānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ madhye kuśalavyākaraṇakṣetraṃ tathāgatasyāgrataḥ karuṇāpuṇḍarīkamutpannaṃ praṇidhānaviśeṣeṇa / yadā tvayā ānantaryakārakā yāvadakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā vaineyāḥ parigṛhītāstīvraṃ pañcakaṣāyaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhītaṃ / mahākaruṇāvyāhāreṇa tvaṃ satpuruṣa daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ sādhukāro datto, dūtāśca preṣitā, mahākāruṇikaśca te nāma kṛtaṃ, sarvā ceyaṃ parṣattavaiva pūjākarmaṇe udyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) You, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, now, in the midst of immeasurable and countless <s>bodhisattvas</s>, a lotus of compassion (<s>karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s>) has arisen before the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the field of skillful prophecy, through the distinction of your aspiration. Since you have accepted as your disciples those who have committed heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>) and even those fallen into unwholesome states, and have accepted a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of fierce five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>)—through the utterance of great compassion, O good man, you have been given approval by <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, and messengers have been sent, and you have been given the name <s>Mahākāruṇika</s> (the Great Compassionate One), and this entire assembly is devoted to making offerings to you.

body.translated_text: There are four bases of exerted vigor for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. What four? The vow for an impurified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; the vow for <s>Buddha</s>-work among beings of impurified dispositions; the vow to teach the discourse of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles after attaining awakening; and the vow for a middle way — neither an excessively long nor a short lifespan after attaining awakening. These are the four bases of exerted vigor for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. Because of them, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> are called 'white-lotus-like' and not 'flower-like' — they are called <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>. Just as (

body.text: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ mahākāruṇikānāgate 'dhvanyatikrāntānāmekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ kalpānāṃ parīttāvaśiṣṭe dvitīye gaṅgānadīvālikāsame 'saṃkhyeye, tasmineva sahe buddhakṣetre bhadrake kalpe viṃśottaravarṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ, jarāmaraṇādyadhike buddhakṣetre 'ndhaloke 'nāyake 'kuśalamūlasamavadhānagate kumārge vihanyamānānāṃ mahāsaṅkaṭaprāptānāṃ sattvānāmānantaryakārakānāmāryāpavādakānāṃ saddharmapratikṣepakānāṃ mūlāpattisamāpannānāṃ yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ, ākīrṇe (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 313.

children.text: ) loke tathāgato bhaviṣyasi vidyācaraṇasaṃpanno yāvadbuddho bhagavān; vivartitagaticakraḥ pravartitadharmacakraḥ vivartitavaśavartimārakleśamāraśca anantāparyantāni daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrāṇi śabdenāpūrayitvā, mahāśrāvakasannipātaśca te bhaviṣyanti yadutārdhatrayodaśairbhikṣuśataiḥ; anupūrveṇa pañcacatvāriṃśatibhirvarṣairevaṃrūpaṃ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ paripūrayiṣyasi, yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / yathā tasmin samaye 'yaṃ rājāmṛtaśuddho 'mitāyurnāmāprameyaiḥ kalpaiḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyati, evameva tvaṃ mahākāruṇika tatra sahe buddhakṣetre bhadrake mahākalpe viṃśottaravarṣaśatāyāṃ prajāyāṃ pañcacatvāriṃśatibhirvarṣairevaṃrūpaṃ sakalaṃ mahābuddhakāryaṃ kariṣyasi, śākyamunirnāma tathāgato bhaviṣyasi / parinirvṛtasya ca te satpuruṣānuttaraparinirvāṇenādhikaṃ varṣasahasraṃ saddharmaḥ sthāsyate / saddharme cāntarhite tava satpuruṣa te 'pi dhātavaḥ janmaśarīre evaṃrūpaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyanti, yathā svayaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, evaṃ ciraṃ sattvān vinayiṣyasi, (
children.translated_text: ) you shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s> endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), and so forth up to <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. Having reversed the wheel of destinies, having turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, having reversed the dominion of <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One) and the <s>Māra</s> of the afflictions, and having filled immeasurable and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions with sound—you shall have a great assembly of chief disciples (<s>mahāśrāvaka</s>), namely twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>. And gradually, in forty-five years, you shall fulfill such complete work of a <s>Buddha</s>, just as the aspiration was made. Just as at that time King <s>Amṛtaśuddha</s>, [named] <s>Amitāyus</s>, will perform the complete work of a <s>Buddha</s> for immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 314.
) as previously described."

body.translated_text: You, <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, in the future age, having passed beyond incalculable <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of one river <s>Gaṅgā</s> with little remaining in the second incalculable [aeon] equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in this very <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, in the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, among a people whose lifespan is one hundred and twenty years, in a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> beset by old age, death, and the rest, in a blind world without a guide, fallen into unwholesome states, straying on wrong paths, among beings greatly afflicted, committers of heinous acts, slanderers of the noble ones (<s>āryāpavādaka</s>), rejecters of the true <s>Dharma</s>, those who have fallen into root transgressions, and so forth as previously described, in a world teeming—

body.text: tatkāle kaitapure brāhmaṇa āsīt, sa evamāha - "teṣu teṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu tava satpuruṣa bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇasyāhaṃ nityopasthāyaka upakaraṇamaitryānukūlaḥ sahāyako bhūtvā tvāmupasthiheyaṃ; caramabhavikasyāhaṃ tava pitā bhaveyaṃ / bodhiprāptasya ca te satpuruṣa agradānapatirbhaveyaṃ; tvaṃ ca māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / aparā ca tatra vinītabuddhirnāma samudradevatā, sāpyāha - "teṣu teṣu yāvaccaramabhavikasyāhaṃ janetrī mātā bhaveyaṃ / bodhiprāptaśca tvaṃ mahākāruṇika māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / varuṇacāritranakṣatrā devatā, sāpyāha - "teṣu teṣu yāvaccaramabhavikasyāhaṃ kṣīradhātrī mātā bhaveyaṃ / bodhiprāptaśca māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / sanemo nāma śakraḥ, aparastu pāracintī nāma śakraḥ, te ubhaye 'pyāhatuḥ / "vayamapi bho mahākāruṇika teṣu teṣu yāvad; bodhiprāptasya ca te vayaṃ śrāvakayugaprajñāvanto (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 315.

children.text: ) ṛddhimantaśca bhavemaḥ" / aparaścāritracaraṇasudarśayūthiko nāma śakraḥ, sa evamāha - "ahaṃ te mahākāruṇika teṣu teṣu yāvaccaramabhavikasya putro bhaveyaṃ" / aparā śikharadevatā saurabhyākiṃśukā nāma, sāpyāha - "ahaṃ te mahākāruṇika tāsu tāsu jātiṣu bhāryā bhaveyaṃ / bodhiprāptaśca tvaṃ satpuruṣa māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / kaduścaro nāmāsurendraḥ, so 'pyāha - "ahaṃ te mahākāruṇikā teṣu teṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu satpuruṣa bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇasyāhamupakaraṇamaitryānukulaḥ sahāyo dāsatvenopasthiheyaṃ, caramabhavikasyāhaṃ te upasthāyako bhaveyaṃ / bodhiprāptasya ca te satpuruṣa dhārmikaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartane 'dhyayeyaṃ, ahaṃ ca te dharmadeśanāṃ prathamāṃ saphalāṃ kuryāṃ, dharmarasaṃ ca piveyaṃ, amṛtaṃ cauṣadhiṃ gaccheyaṃ, yāvat sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhatvaṃ prāpnuyāṃ" / peyālaṃ, gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāśca tatra devanāgāsurā mahākāruṇikasyānupravṛtticaryāya (
children.translated_text: ) and may we be endowed with supernatural powers." And there was also a <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) named <s>Āritracaraṇasudarśayūthika</s>, who spoke thus: "I, O <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, in all those [births] and even in your final existence, would be your son." And there was a mountain-goddess named <s>Saurabhyākiṃśukā</s>, who also said: "I, O <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, in all those births, would be your wife. And when you, O good man, have attained enlightenment, you should give me prophecy for supreme perfect enlightenment." And there was a lord of <s>asuras</s> named <s>Kaduścara</s>, who also said: "I, O <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, throughout those immeasurable and countless <s>kalpas</s>, while you, O good man, are practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, I would be a companion favorable with material kindness—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 316.

children.text: ) praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavanto vaineyamupanyastā / ekaśca tatra saṃjñāvikaraṇabhīṣmo nāmājīvikaḥ, sa āha - "ahaṃ te bho mahābrāhmaṇa bahūpakaraṇasahāyako bhaviṣyāmi / nityamahaṃ te 'prameyeṣu kalpeṣu saphalacārikopajīvījñātiko bhaveyaṃ; nityaṃ ca tvatsakāśamupasaṃkrameyaṃ vastuyācanārthaṃ śayyāsanavāhanahastyaśvarathagrāmanigamanagarakulaputraduhitṛmāṃsarudhiracarmāsthihastapādajihvākarṇanāsanayanaśīrṣāṇi ca yāceyaṃ / evaṃrūpo 'haṃ tava mahābrāhmaṇa dānapāramitāsahāyako bhaveyaṃ, yāvatprajñāpāramitāsahāyako bhaveyaṃ / evaṃrūpo 'haṃ mahābrāhmaṇa bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇasya tava ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu sahāyako bhaveyaṃ; yāvattvaṃ bodhiṃ prāpnuyā ahaṃ ca te śrāvakasthānamāsādayeyaṃ, aśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇyudgṛhṇīyāṃ pṛṣṭhaśca dharmadeśako bhaveyaṃ / tvaṃ ca māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / śrutvā ca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko brāhmaṇo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā vanditvā, taṃ saṃjñāvikaraṇabhīṣmājīvikaṃ śabdāpayitvāha - (
children.translated_text: ) made their aspirations and entrusted [themselves as] disciples. And there was one <s>ājīvika</s> (naked ascetic) named <s>Saṃjñāvikaraṇabhīṣma</s>, who said: "I, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, shall be your companion of many provisions. Throughout immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, I shall always be a dependant kinsman, living off the fruits of your practice. And I shall always approach you for the purpose of asking for things—bed, seat, vehicle, elephant, horse, chariot, village, town, city, sons, daughters, flesh, blood, skin, bones, hands, feet, tongue, ears, nose, eyes, and head. Such shall I be as your companion in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), and even the companion in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>)—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 317.

children.text: ) "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa yastvaṃ mama sahāyako bhaviṣyasi anuttaracaryāya, yāvacca tvaṃ mamāprameyāsaṃkhyeyajanmāntaranayutasahasreṣūpasaṃkramervastuyācanārthāya / tadāhaṃ prasannacitto dadyāṃ, mā ca tvamapuṇyabhāgī bhaveḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) "Excellent! Excellent, O good man! You shall be my companion for the supreme conduct, and throughout immeasurable and countless tens of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of births, you shall approach me for the purpose of asking for things. And I, with a clear and faithful mind, shall give. And may you not become one whose share is demerit."

body.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Kaitapura</s>, there was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. He spoke thus: "Throughout those immeasurable and countless <s>kalpas</s>, while you, O good man, are practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, I would be your constant attendant, a companion favorable with material kindness, serving you. And in your final existence, I would be your father. And when you, O good man, have attained enlightenment, I would be your chief patron of giving (<s>agradānapati</s>); and you should give me prophecy for supreme perfect enlightenment." And there was also a sea-goddess (<s>samudradevatā</s>) named <s>Vinītabuddhi</s>, and she too said: "In all those [births] and even in your final existence, I would be your mother who gave you birth. And when you, O <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, have attained enlightenment—

body.text: bhūyaśca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purata āha - "sacenme bhadanta bhagavaṃsteṣu teṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣvanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caramāṇasya ye mama purato yācanakāḥ sthitvānnaṃ yācanti mṛduvacanena vā puruṣavacanena vā ullaṅghanavacanena vā spaṣṭavacanena vā yāceyuḥ; sacedahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan yācanakasyāntike ekacittakṣaṇamapi roṣaṃ utpādayeyaṃ / aprasādaṃ votpādayeyaṃ dānasya vā phalavipākaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇo dānaṃ dadyāṃ, visaṃvāditā me bhaveyuḥ ye 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, mā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / sacedahaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 318.

children.text: ) bhadanta bhagavan yācanakasya prasannacitto dānaṃ dadyāṃ, tadapi dānapratigrāhakasya śraddhādeyavinipātanaṃ, mākuśalairdharmairantarāyakaraṃ bhavet; antaśo vālāgrakoṭīpramāṇamātramapi visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuḥ / yadīdaṃ pratigrāhakasya vālāgrakoṭīpramāṇamātramapi kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvantarāyaṃ kuryuḥ, ahamapyavīciparāyaṇo bhaveyaṃ / yathānnasya tathā vastrasya / yāvad ye mama yācanakāḥ śīrṣaṃ yāceyuḥ, mṛduvacanena vā paruṣavacanena vā ullaṅghyavacanena vā spaṣṭavacanena vā śīrṣaṃ yācayeran; sacedahaṃ bhadanta bhagavan yācanakasyāntike ekacittakṣaṇamapi roṣamutpādayeyaṃ, aprasādacittamutpādayeyaṃ, dānaphalavipākamākāṅkṣaṃ śīrṣaṃ parityajeyaṃ, visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuḥ; yāvadahamapyavīciparāyaṇo bhaveyaṃ / yathā dānamevaṃ śīlaṃ yāvatprajñā parityāgo vācyaḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) O venerable Blessed One, I should give to the petitioner with a clear mind. And if even that gift should cause the downfall of the recipient's faith-offering, or cause an obstruction to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—even to the extent of the tip of a hair—then the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, would have been deceived by me. If it should cause an obstruction to wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for the recipient, even to the extent of the tip of a hair, then I should be destined for <s>Avīci</s> [hell]. As with food, so with clothing. And even those petitioners who ask for my head—whether with gentle words, harsh words, mocking words, or blunt words—even those who ask for my head—

body.translated_text: And furthermore, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, in the presence of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, said: "If, O venerable Blessed One, throughout those immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, while I am practicing the conduct of supreme perfect enlightenment, those who stand before me as petitioners ask for food—whether with gentle words, harsh words, mocking words, or blunt words—if I, O venerable Blessed One, even for a single moment of thought, should generate anger toward a petitioner, or should generate displeasure, or should desire the fruit and result of giving—

body.text: sa ca kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato mahākāruṇikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sādhukāramadāsīt / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, mahākaruṇāpratiṣṭhitena manasā tvayā satpuruṣemaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ" / sā ca kulaputra sarvāvatī parṣā sadevagandharvamānuṣāsuraśca lokaḥ prāñjalībhūtaḥ sthitvā sādhukāraṃ prādāsīt / "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, mahākaruṇāpratiṣṭhitena manasā tvayā satpuruṣa praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam / tvamapi sattvāṃ ṣaṭparāyaṇīyadharmaiḥ saṃtarpayiṣyasi" / sa ca kulaputra yathā saṃjñāvikārabhīṣmājīviko bodhisattvo dānapratigrāhikayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān, evameva caturaśītibhiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / sa ca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvastānyevaṃrūpāṇi praṇidhānāni caturaśītīnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ sakāśācchrutvā saṃjñāvikārabhīṣmeṇa praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / atha mahākāruṇikaḥ paramaprītisaumanasyajātaḥ prāñjalībhūtaḥ sthitvā sarvāvatīṃ parṣāṃ vyavalokya paramaprītamanā āha / "aho āścaryaṃ, bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ dharmadurbhikṣakṣīṇakāle mahākleśaraṇe kaliyuge pañcakaṣāye vartamāne loke 'nāyake sārthavāho 'vabhāsakaraḥ pradīpakaraḥ atrāṇānāmandhānāṃ mārganidarśakaḥ / yatra (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 320.

children.text: ) hi nāmāhaṃ prathamacittotpādenaivamevaṃrūpāmanuttarāyāṃ bodhicaryāyāṃ sahāyakāḥ pratilabdhā ye mama janmāntareṣu śīrṣapratigrāhakā bhaviṣyanti nayanakarṇanāsājihvāhastapādacarmāsthirudhiraṃ yāvadannasya pratigrāhakā bhaviṣyanti" /
children.translated_text: ) "Indeed, from the very first generation of the mind [of enlightenment], I have obtained such companions for the supreme conduct of enlightenment—those who in my future births will be the recipients of my head, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands, feet, skin, bones, blood, and even recipients of food."

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> gave his approval to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>: "Excellent! Excellent, O good man! With a mind established in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) you, O good man, have made this aspiration." And, O son of good family, that entire assembly, together with the world including gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, stood with palms joined and gave their approval: "Excellent! Excellent, O good man! With a mind established in great compassion you, O good man, have made the aspiration. You too shall satisfy beings with the six <s>dharmas</s> of going-beyond (<s>pārāyaṇīya</s>)." And, O son of good family, just as the <s>ājīvika</s> <s>Saṃjñāvikārabhīṣma</s>—

body.text: punarapi kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purato niṣaṇṇa āha - "ye ca mama bhadanta bhagavan teṣu teṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu janmāntareṣu yācanakā upasaṃkrāmeyuryadi vānnaṃ yadi vā pānaṃ yāvacchiraḥ pratigṛhṇīyurantaśo vālāgrakoṭīpramānamātramapi mama hastadānaṃ pratigṛhṇīyuryāvadbodhiparyantena / sacedahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya na tāṃ sattvāṃ saṃsārāt parimocayeyaṃ, na ca punarvyākuryāṃ chrāvakayānena vā pratyekabuddhayānena vā mahāyānena vā, visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuḥ ya etarhi daśasu dikṣu, yāvan, mā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ" /
body.translated_text: And again, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, seated in the presence of <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, said: "And, O venerable Blessed One, those who in those immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, in my future births, come as petitioners—whether they receive food or drink, and even [those who receive] my head—even those who accept from my hand a mere fraction the size of a hair-tip—until the attainment of enlightenment. If, having attained supreme perfect enlightenment, I should not liberate those beings from <s>saṃsāra</s>, and should not give them prophecy through the vehicle of <s>śrāvakas</s> or through the vehicle of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>—

body.text: punarapi kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato mahākāruṇikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sādhukāraṃ prādāsīt / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 321.

children.text: ) "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, evaṃrūpaṃ te satpuruṣa bodhicārikāpraṇidhānaṃ, yathā meruśikhariṃdhareṇa tathāgatena pūrvaṃ prathamacittotpādena lokeśvarajyotiṣastathāgatasya purataḥ evaṃrūpayā bodhisattvacaryayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ evaṃrūpā bodhisattvacārikā cīrṇā yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā mahākalpā atikrāntā yathā tena satpuruṣeṇa purimāyāṃ diśīto koṭīśatasahasrabuddhakṣetre jvālapratisaṃkhyāyāṃ lokadhātau varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho, jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvaro nāma babhūva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhagavān, pañcacatvāriṃśadvarṣāṇi buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau praviṣṭaḥ / tasya khalu mahākāruṇika jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvarasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya varṣasahasraṃ saddharmanetrī asthāsīt; saddharmasyāntarhitasya varṣasahasraṃ punaḥ saddharmapratirūpakamasthāsīt / ye khalu mahākāruṇika jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvarasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmanetryavasthitāyāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) "Excellent, excellent, O worthy one! Such is your aspiration for the course of awakening, O worthy one. Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Meruśikhariṃdhara</s> formerly, with the first generation of the mind, made such an aspiration for the <s>bodhisattva</s> course before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvarajyotiṣa</s>, and practiced such a <s>bodhisattva</s> course as his aspiration was made — great <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> elapsed — and that worthy one, in the eastern direction, in a world-realm called <s>Jvālapratisaṃkhyā</s>, a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields [away], when the generation had a lifespan of a hundred years, attained unsurpassed perfect awakening. He became the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, Blessed One named <s>Jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvara</s>. Having performed the work of a <s>Buddha</s> for forty-five years, he entered the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder. After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvara</s>, O greatly compassionate one, the guiding [lamp] of the true <s>Dharma</s> endured for a thousand years; and after the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the counterfeit of the true <s>Dharma</s> endured for a thousand years. Those who, during the endurance of the guiding [lamp] of the true <s>Dharma</s> after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvara</s>, O greatly compassionate one, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 322.

children.text: ) saddharmapratirūpakā vā bhikṣurbhikṣuṇī vā duḥśīlapāpadharmā viṣamasamudācārāḥ staupikavastugrāhakālajjikā vā dharmapūjācchedālajjasaṃsṛṣṭā vā caturdiśasaṅghasya vā saṃmukhībhūtasaṅghasya vā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraṃ vā chinnaṃ paudgalikaparigrahe yāvadātmanā paribhuktaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ vā dattaṃ; tena khalu mahākāruṇika jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvareṇa tathāgatena sarve 'nupūrveṇa vyākṛtastribhiryānaiḥ / ye kecin mahākāruṇika tasya bhagavataḥ śāsane raktakāṣāyaprāvṛtāḥ sarve te avaivartikā vyākṛtāstribhiryānaiḥ; ye 'pi kecin mūlāpattisamāpannā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā vā pūrvameva te tena tathāgatena śāstṛsaṃjñākuśalamūlavipākena tribhiryānairavaivartikā vyākṛtāḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) or during the counterfeit [<s>Dharma</s>] — monks or nuns who were of bad morality and evil qualities, of uneven conduct, who were shameless seizers of <s>stūpa</s> property and materials, or who were shameless in disrupting <s>Dharma</s>-worship, or who cut off the robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick belonging to the <s>Saṅgha</s> of the four directions or the <s>Saṅgha</s> present in person, taking them for personal use or giving them to householders — all of these, O greatly compassionate one, were gradually prophesied by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānakusumavirajasamucchrayabodhīśvara</s> through the three vehicles. Whoever, O greatly compassionate one, were clothed in the red <s>kāṣāya</s> robe in the teaching of that Blessed One — all of them were prophesied as non-retrogressing through the three vehicles. Even those monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who had committed root transgressions — they too were previously prophesied as non-retrogressing through the three vehicles by that <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the karmic fruit of their root of merit of having generated the perception of the Teacher."

body.translated_text: And again, O son of good family, <s>Ratnagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> gave his approval to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra sa mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purata āha - "eṣaiva me bhadanta bhagavan praṇidhiryāvadevāhamanuttarāyāṃ bodhicaryāyāṃ caramāṇo yān sattvānahaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ niyojayeyaṃ samādāpayeyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ yāvat (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 323.

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitāyāmantaśo vālāgrakoṭīpramāṇamātramapi kuśalamūle niyojayeyaṃ; yāvadbodhiparyantena caryāṃ caramāṇo na tān sattvāṃstribhiryānairavaivartikabhūmau sthāpayeyamantaśa ekasattvamapi, visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuḥ ye daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, mā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / anuttarajñānapratilabdhaścāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavan ye me sattvāḥ śāsane raktakāṣāyaprāvṛtā bhaveyuḥ; yadi vā mūlāpattimāpannāḥ syuryadi vā dṛṣṭivyasanaṃ saṃpratipannāḥ syuryadi vā triṣu ratneṣu skhalitāḥ sāparādhā bhaveyurbhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā ya ekakṣaṇamapi mama sakāśe śāstṛsaṃjñāṃ vā gauravacittaṃ votpādayeyurdharme vā saṅghe vā gauravacittamutpādayeyuḥ; sacedahaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃstān sattvāṃstribhiryānairavaivartikāṃ na vyākuryāmantaśa ekasattvamapi riṃceyurvisaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuryāvan mā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / bodhiprāptasya (
children.translated_text: ) even to the extent of a hair-tip's worth of wholesome roots I would establish them in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom); if, while practicing the course up to the point of awakening, I should not establish those beings through the three vehicles on the stage of non-retrogression — even a single being — then may I have deceived the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who dwell, sustain, and abide in immeasurable, incalculable world-realms in the ten directions, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>; and may I not attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. And, Venerable Blessed One, when I have attained unsurpassed knowledge — those beings who would be clothed in the red <s>kāṣāya</s> robe in my teaching — even if they have committed root transgressions, even if they have fallen into the calamity of wrong views, even if they have stumbled regarding the Three Jewels, even if they are monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who are guilty — if they would generate even for a single moment the perception of the Teacher toward me, or a mind of respect, or would generate a mind of respect toward the <s>Dharma</s> or the <s>Saṅgha</s> — if, Venerable Blessed One, I should not prophesy those beings as non-retrogressing through the three vehicles, if even a single being should be left out, then may I have deceived the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in the ten directions, and may I not attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. When I have attained awakening, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 324.

children.text: ) ca me bhadanta bhagavan devamanuṣyasatkṛtaṃ gurukṛtaṃ mānitaṃ pūjitaṃ raktakāṣāyacīvaraṃ bhavet / sahadarśanena sattvāḥ kāṣāyakaṇṭhāstribhiryānairavaivartikā bhaveyurye sattvāḥ kṣuttarṣapīḍitā annapānavirahitā yakṣadāridrā vāntaśaḥ yāmalaukikāḥ sattvā ye kāṣāyamabhilaṣeyurantaśaścaturaṅgulamapi, sarve te 'nnapānasaṃpannā bhaveyuḥ paripūrṇābhiprāyāḥ / ye sattvāḥ parasparaviruddhavairabahulāḥ parasparayuddhasaṃgrāmagatā vā devā vā yakṣā vā rākṣasā vā nāgā vā asurā vā garuḍā vā kinnarā vā mahoragā vā kuṃbhāṇḍā vā piśācā vā manuṣyā vā saṃgrāmagatāḥ kāṣāyamanusmareyuḥ, te sattvāḥ karuṇācittā mṛducittā avairacittāḥ karmaṇyacittā bhaveyurye sattvāḥ saṃgrāme vā vivāde vā yuddhe vā kalahe vā kāṣāyakhaṇḍakaṃ rakṣārthaṃ pūjanārthaṃ gauravārthaṃ hareyuste sattvāḥ sadā aparājitā bhaveyuraskhalitā aviheṭhitā bhaveyuḥ, svastinā tataḥ saṃgrāmādvā yuddhādvā kalahādvā vivādādvā parimucyeyuḥ / yadi me bhadanta bhagavannebhiḥ pañcabhirāryaguṇai raktaṃ kāṣāyaṃ na samanvāgataṃ bhavet, visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyurye daśasu dikṣu, (
children.translated_text: ) Venerable Blessed One, the red <s>kāṣāya</s> robe shall be honored, esteemed, respected, and worshipped by gods and humans. Beings who merely see it, who wear the <s>kāṣāya</s> at their neck, shall become non-retrogressing through the three vehicles. Those beings afflicted by hunger and thirst, deprived of food and drink, even <s>yakṣas</s> suffering poverty, or even beings of <s>Yama</s>'s world — whoever would desire even four finger-widths of the <s>kāṣāya</s>, all of them shall become endowed with food and drink, with their wishes fulfilled. Those beings who are filled with mutual hostility and enmity, who have gone to mutual battle and war — whether gods, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, or humans — whoever in battle would recall the <s>kāṣāya</s>, those beings shall become compassionate-minded, gentle-minded, free from enmity, with pliant minds. Those beings who in battle, conflict, war, or quarrel would carry even a piece of the <s>kāṣāya</s> for protection, worship, or reverence — those beings shall always be undefeated, unobstructed, unharassed, and shall safely be freed from that battle, war, quarrel, or conflict. If, Venerable Blessed One, the red <s>kāṣāya</s> should not be endowed with these five noble qualities, then may I have deceived the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in the ten directions, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 325.

children.text:
) yāvan, mā cāhaṃ śaktaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ pariniṣpādayituṃ, dharmā me saṃmoṣaṃ gaccheyurmā cāhaṃ śaktaḥ anyatīrthikāṃ parigṛhītuṃ / ye ca bhadanta bhagavan mamābhisaṃbuddhasya yāvat parinirvṛtasya
vā namaskāraṃ kariṣyanti, "namaḥ śākyamunaye tathāgatāye"ti vācaṃ bhāṣiṣyante, teṣāṃ sarvakarmāvaraṇakṣayo bhaviṣyati, ante cānuttareṇa buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvāsyanti"ti /
children.translated_text: ) and may I not be able to accomplish the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>; may my <s>dharmas</s> fall into oblivion; and may I not be able to convert those of other paths. And, Venerable Blessed One, those who after my full awakening, or even after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will make salutation, who will utter the words 'Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>' — for all of them there will be the exhaustion of all karmic obscurations, and in the end they will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the unsurpassed <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of a <s>Buddha</s>."

body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the Greatly Compassionate One, said before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>: "This indeed is my aspiration, Venerable Blessed One — that as long as I am practicing the course of unsurpassed awakening, those beings whom I shall establish, inspire, and ground in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), up to (

body.text: sa ca punaḥ kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayitvā karatalena mahākāruṇikasya bodhisattvasya śiraḥ parimārjayitvāha - "sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa, kalyāṇaṃ te praṇidhānaṃ bhadrakaprativimarśa; evameva te satpuruṣa pañcabhirāryaguṇai raktakāṣāyaṃ sattvānāmupajīvyaṃ bhaviṣyati" /
body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> extended his right arm, stroked the head of the <s>bodhisattva</s> the Greatly Compassionate One with his palm, and said: "Excellent, excellent, O worthy one! Beautiful is your aspiration, O one of <s>Bhadra</s>-like discernment. Just so, O worthy one, the red <s>kāṣāya</s> endowed with the five noble qualities shall be a source of livelihood for beings."

body.text: sa bho punaḥ kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvastena vyākareṇena sādhukāraprāmodya prasādena tathāgatapuṇyadīrghāṅguliparicchāditena dakṣiṇena mṛdutaruṇakaratalasaṃsparśeṇa kumārabhūtaḥ saṃvṛto viṃśadvarṣasadṛśo jātipramāṇena /
body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the Greatly Compassionate One, through that prophecy, commendation, delight, and serenity, and by the touch of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s right palm — soft, tender, with merit-lengthened fingers — covering [his head], became like a youth, appearing as though twenty years of age in his bodily measure.

body.text: punarapi kulaputra sarvāvatī sā parṣā sadevagandharvamānuṣā prāñjalibhūtā tasthau, mahākāruṇikasya pūjākarmaṇe udyuktāḥ puṣpairvādyairmahākāruṇikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā vicitravarṇaiḥ ślokaistuṣṭāva //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, the entire assembly, together with gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and humans, stood with palms joined, devoted to the worship of the Greatly Compassionate One. Having made worship to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the Greatly Compassionate One, with flowers and music, they praised him with verses of various colors.

body.text: iti śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīke mahāyānasūtre bodhisattvavyākaraṇaparivartaścaturthaḥ //4//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Prophecy of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in the holy <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra. // 4 //

body.text: V dānaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ
body.translated_text: V. The Fifth Chapter, named the Chapter on Giving.

body.text: sa ca punaḥ kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya pañcamaṇḍalena pādau śirasā vanditvā ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya purato niṣasāda ratnagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchat - "samādhānamukhanirdeśasaṃbhāraviśuddhimukho dharmaparyāyo bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo bhagavatā nirdiṣṭaḥ; kiyatā bhadanta bhagavan samādhānamukhanirdeśasaṃbhāraviśuddhimukho dharmaparyāyo bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo bhagavatā nirdiṣṭaḥ?; kiyatā bhadanta bhagavan samādhānamukhanirdeśasaṃbhāraviśuddhimukho dharmaparyāyaḥ paripūrṇo bhavati?; kiyadrūpeṇa vā bhadanta bhagavan saṃbhāreṇa samanvāgataḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛḍhapratiṣṭhito bhavati?; kiyadrūpeṇa samādhānamukhanirdeśanālaṅkṛto bhavati?" sa bhoḥ punaḥ kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho mahākāruṇikaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - "sādhu (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 328.

children.text: ) sādhu mahākāruṇika bhadrakaḥ praśnaḥ kalyāṇaṃ te pratibhānaṃ / bhūyasyā mātrayā tvaṃ mahākāruṇikāprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ hitakaro bahukaraścotpanno, yatra hi nāma tvaṃ mahākāruṇika tathāgatamidamevaṃrūpaṃ praśnaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / tena hi mahākāruṇika śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru ca /
children.translated_text: ) excellent, O Greatly Compassionate One! Beautiful is your question; beautiful is your eloquence. To an even greater degree, you have arisen as a benefactor and great helper for immeasurable, incalculable <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, O Greatly Compassionate One, inasmuch as you think to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> such a question. Therefore, O Greatly Compassionate One, listen well and carefully, and attend with your mind.

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the Greatly Compassionate One, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> with the five-point prostration, sat down before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>: "The Blessed One has taught the <s>Dharma</s> discourse called 'The Purification Gateway of the Accumulation through the Exposition of <s>Samādhi</s> Gateways' as the path for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. To what extent, Venerable Blessed One, has the Blessed One taught this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, the path for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, 'The Purification Gateway of the Accumulation through the Exposition of <s>Samādhi</s> Gateways'? To what extent, Venerable Blessed One, is this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, 'The Purification Gateway of the Accumulation through the Exposition of <s>Samādhi</s> Gateways,' complete? With what kind of accumulation, Venerable Blessed One, is a son or daughter of good family firmly established? With what kind of 'Exposition of <s>Samādhi</s> Gateways' is one adorned?" Then, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, said this to the <s>bodhisattva</s> the Greatly Compassionate One: "Excellent (

children.text: ) dharmasthitiṃ samanupaśyati / gaganakalpena samādhinā sarvasamādhīn gaganasvabhāvāsāratvāya samanupaśyati / niścittena samādhinā sarvasamādhiṣu cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ prahīyante / rūpāparyantena samādhinā rūpamavabhāsayati / vimalapradīpena samādhinā sarvasamādhīnāṃ pradīpaṃ karoti / sarvadharmāparyantena samādhinā sarvasamādhiṣvaparyantajñānaṃ darśayati / vidyudunmiṣeṇa samādhinā sarvasamādhiṣvaparyantaṃ jñānaṃ darśayati / sarvaprabhaṃkareṇa samādhinā sarvasamādhiṣu prabhaṃkaramukhamupadarśayati / dhātuparyantena samādhinā sarvasamādhīnaparyantavijñāpanāyopadarśayati / samādhiśuddhasāreṇa samādhinā śūnyatāṃ samādhidharmeṣvanuprāpnoti / merucitreṇa samādhinā sarvadharmeṣu ṛktatāṃ saṃdarśayati / vimalaprabhena samādhinā sarvasamādhīnāṃ malamapakarṣayati / sarvadharmāsaṃprabhedena samādhinā sarvasamādhīnāṃ vyupakṛṣṭatāṃ saṃdarśayati / (

Through the <s>Candravimala</s> (Moon-Immaculate) <s>samādhi</s>, he produces light in all <s>samādhis</s> (

children.translated_text: ). Through the <s>Śuddhapratibhāsa</s> (Pure Reflection) <s>samādhi</s>, he attains the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) in all <s>samādhis</s>. Through the <s>Kārākāra</s> (Prison-Maker) <s>samādhi</s>, he performs the activity of prison-dwelling and perceives the banner of knowledge. Through the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> (Jewel-Peak) <s>samādhi</s>, he appears like a jewel peak in all <s>samādhis</s>. Through the <s>Varadharmamudra</s> (Excellent Dharma-Seal) <s>samādhi</s>, all <s>samādhis</s> become sealed; through the equality of <s>dharmas</s>, he does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> released from equality. Through the <s>Ākāranirhāravat</s> (Possessed of Aspect-Extraction) <s>samādhi</s>, he perceives the aspectless extraction of all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Saṅketarutapraveśa</s> (Entering Conventional Sounds) <s>samādhi</s>, he enters all conventional sounds. Through the <s>Ghoṣavāgbhirakṣaravimukta</s> (Freed from Syllables of Sound and Speech) <s>samādhi</s>, he perceives the liberation from syllables in all <s>dharmas</s> (

children.translated_text: ). Through the <s>Vimalaprabhāsa</s> (Stainless Splendor) <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive stainlessness of the conditioned in all <s>samādhis</s>. Through the <s>Sārānugata</s> (Following the Essence) <s>samādhi</s>, he does not apprehend inessentiality in all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Pūrṇacandravimala</s> (Full Moon Immaculate) <s>samādhi</s>, he becomes replete with qualities in all <s>samādhis</s>. Through the <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array) <s>samādhi</s>, he becomes endowed with the great array in all <s>samādhis</s>. Through the <s>Sarvalokaprabheda</s> (Penetrating All Worlds) <s>samādhi</s>, he illuminates all <s>dharmas</s> with knowledge. Through the <s>Araṇa</s> (Conflict-Free) <s>samādhi</s>, he does not engage in conflict with all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Anilaniketa</s> (Wind-Abode) <s>samādhi</s>, he does not cling to any dwelling in all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Tathāsthitanīścitta</s> (Established in Suchness-Mindlessness) <s>samādhi</s>, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) does not turn back in all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Kāyakalisaṃpramathana</s> (Crushing Bodily Strife) <s>samādhi</s>, he does not apprehend the body-view in all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the <s>Vākkaliviḍhvaṃsanagaganapratiladbha</s> (Obtained like Sky, Destroying Verbal Strife) <s>samādhi</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 338.

children.text: ) bodhisattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣu vākkarma nopalabhate / ākāśasaṃgagativimuktinirupalepasamādhisthito bodhisattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣvākāśasaṃgatāmanuprāpnoti / ayaṃ samādhimukho mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ nirveśaḥ /

body.translated_text: For sons of good family who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), there is, O Greatly Compassionate One, a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Śūraṃgama</s> (Heroic March) — a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in that <s>samādhi</s> enters into all <s>samādhis</s>. There is a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ratnamudra</s> (Jewel Seal) — by it all <s>samādhis</s> are sealed. There is a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s> (Lion's Sport) — established in it, one sports with all <s>samādhis</s>. The <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sucandra</s> (Beautiful Moon) illuminates all <s>samādhis</s>. The <s>samādhi</s> <s>Candradhvajaketu</s> (Moon-Banner-Crest) holds the banner of all <s>samādhis</s>. The <s>samādhi</s> <s>Sarvadharmodgata</s> (Arising from All Dharmas) — all <s>samādhis</s> enter into it. The <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vilokitamudra</s> (Gaze Seal) surveys the summit of all <s>samādhis</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the <s>samādhi</s> <s>Dharmadhātuvigata</s> (Freed from the Dharma-Realm) (

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ saṃbhāraviśuddhimukhasaṃgraho dharmaparyāyaḥ? dānasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sattvaparipācanatayā saṃvartate / śīlasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ praṇidhānapūryā saṃvartate / kṣāntisaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaparipūryā saṃvartate / vīryasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakāryaparipūryā saṃvartate / dhyānasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmājāneyacittatayā saṃvartate / prajñāsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakleśaparijñayā saṃvartate / śrutasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmasaṅgapratibhānatayā saṃvartate / puṇyasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasattvopajīvyatayā saṃvartate / jñānasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmasaṅgajñānatayā saṃvartate / (

children.text: ) śamathasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ karmaṇyacittatayā saṃvartate / vipaśyanāsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ vigatakathaṃkathayā saṃvartate / maitrīsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmapratihatacittatayā saṃvartate / karuṇāsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ paripākākhedatāyai saṃvartate / muditāsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ dharmārāmaratiramaṇatāyai saṃvartate / upekṣāsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmanunayapratighaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / dharmaśravaṇasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ vivaraṇaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / niṣkramaṇasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaparigrahotsargāya saṃvartate / araṇyavāsasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ kṛtakarmāvipraṇāśatayā saṃvartate / smṛtisaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ dhāraṇīpratilābhatayā saṃvartate / matisaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ buddhiprabhedanatayā saṃvartate / gatisaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmarthagatyanubudhyanatayā saṃvartate / smṛtyupasthānasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ kāyavedanācittadharmānubudhyanatayā saṃvartate / samyakprahāṇasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇatāyai saṃvartate, sarvakuśaladharmabhāvanāya ca (
children.translated_text: ) The accumulation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' workable-mindedness. The accumulation of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' freedom from doubt. The accumulation of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' unobstructed mind. The accumulation of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' unwearied ripening [of beings]. The accumulation of <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' delight and enjoyment in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>. The accumulation of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' abandonment of attraction and aversion. The accumulation of hearing the <s>Dharma</s> conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' abandonment of hindrances. The accumulation of renunciation conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' relinquishment of all possessions. The accumulation of forest-dwelling conduces to the non-destruction of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' performed wholesome deeds. The accumulation of mindfulness conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. The accumulation of intelligence conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' discernment of wisdom. The accumulation of progress conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' awakening to the meaning and its application. The accumulation of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' awakening to body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. The accumulation of the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and to the cultivation of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 340.

children.text: ) / ṛddhipādasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ kāyacittalaghutvatayā saṃvartate / indriyasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasattvendriyaparipūryā saṃvartate / balasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakleśānavamardanatayā saṃvartate / bodhyaṅgasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ dharmasvabhāvānubudhyanatayā saṃvartate / mārgasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakumārgasamatikramatāya saṃvartate / satyasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmakuśaladharmāpasaraṇasvargopapattipratilābhāya saṃvartate / pratisaṃvitsaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasattvasaṃśayacchedanatayā saṃvartate / pratisaraṇasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāmaparādhīnajñānatayā saṃvartate / kalyāṇamitrasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaguṇāya dvāratayā saṃvartate / āśayasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvalokāvisaṃvādanatayā saṃvartate / prayogasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasaṃbhārottaraṇatayā saṃvartate / adhyāśayasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ viśeṣagāmitayā saṃvartate / pratisaṃlānasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ yathāśrutadharmapratipatyā saṃvartate / saṅgrahavastusaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sattvaparipācanatayā (
children.translated_text: ). The accumulation of the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' lightness of body and mind. The accumulation of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) conduces to the fulfillment of the faculties of all beings for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The accumulation of the <s>balas</s> (powers) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' crushing of all afflictions. The accumulation of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' awakening to the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>. The accumulation of the <s>mārga</s> (path) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' transcending of all wrong paths. The accumulation of the <s>satyas</s> (truths) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' abandonment of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and attainment of rebirth in heaven. The accumulation of the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' cutting through the doubts of all beings. The accumulation of the <s>pratisaraṇas</s> (reliances) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' independent knowledge. The accumulation of virtuous friends conduces to being the gateway to all the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' qualities. The accumulation of [pure] intention conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' not deceiving any world. The accumulation of application conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' surpassing all [other] accumulations. The accumulation of superior intention conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' progress to distinction. The accumulation of seclusion conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> as heard. The accumulation of the means of gathering [disciples] conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' ripening of beings (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 341.

children.text: ) saṃvartate / saddharmaparigrahasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ triratnavaṃśānupacchedanatayā saṃvartate / pariṇāmanāvidhijñakauśalyasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhyā saṃvartate / upāyakauśalyasaṃbhāro bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajñajñānaparipūryā saṃvartate / ayaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvānāṃ saṃbhāraviśuddhimukhasaṅgraho dharmaparyāyaḥ" /
