The accumulation of skill in the method of dedication conduces to the purification of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. The accumulation of skill in means conduces to the fulfillment of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' omniscient knowledge. This, O son of good family, is the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) of the Compendium of the Gateway of Purification of Accumulations for <s>bodhisattvas</s>."

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) of the Compendium of the Gateway of Purification of Accumulations for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>? The accumulation of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' ripening of beings. The accumulation of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) conduces to the fulfillment of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' aspirations. The accumulation of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) conduces to the fulfillment of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' marks and minor marks. The accumulation of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) conduces to the accomplishment of all the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' tasks. The accumulation of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' thoroughbred-mindedness. The accumulation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' full comprehension of all afflictions. The accumulation of learning conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' unobstructed eloquence. The accumulation of merit conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' being a support for all beings. The accumulation of knowledge conduces to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' unobstructed knowledge. (

body.text: punarapi kulaputra ratnagarbhastathāgato mahābodhisattvaparṣadaṃ vyavalokya mahākāruṇikaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayitvāha - "tatra mahākāruṇikā kiyadrūpeṇa vaiśāradyālaṅkāreṇālaṅkṛto bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣāntiṃ paripūrayati? paramārthadarśino bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāmoghavyāyāmaparigrahacittaḥ sarvatraidhātuke yo 'parigrahacittaḥ sarvasattvebhyaḥ sa ucyate mahāvaiśāradyaśramaṇadharmo yasyākāśapāṇisamacittaṃ sarvadharmeṣu / ayaṃ mahākāruṇika bodhisattvasya vaiśāradyālaṅkāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, surveying the great <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Mahākāruṇika (the Great Compassionate One) and said: "Therein, O Great Compassionate One, adorned with what kind of ornament of confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> fulfill patience? For the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who sees the ultimate truth, who has a mind that grasps non-futile exertion, who has a mind of non-grasping toward the entire triple world and toward all beings — he is called one possessed of the <s>śramaṇa</s>-<s>dharma</s> (ascetic quality) of great confidence, whose mind in all <s>dharmas</s> is equal to an open hand and space. This, O Great Compassionate One, is the ornament of confidence of the <s>bodhisattva</s>."

body.translated_text: While this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse was being spoken, sixty-four hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the ten directions to <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> ('Vulture Peak') Mountain, to the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, to hear the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Saṃbhāraviśuddhimukha</s> ('Gateway of Purification of Accumulations'), the exposition of the gateway of former practice and <s>samādhi</s> — they obtained forbearance regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> said: "When this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse was being spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, forty-eight times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> obtained the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (forbearance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>)

body.text: sa ca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nupūrveṇa caturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya sakāśācchrāvakayānakathāṃ paṭhitavān paryavāptavāṃśca; navatidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi pratyekabuddhayānakathāmuddiṣṭavāṃ paṭhitavān paryavāptavān; tataḥ śatasahasramanuttaramahāyānakathāyāṃ tathā kāyasmṛtyupasthānakathāyāmuddiṣṭavān paṭhitavān paryavāptavāṃśca, śatasahasraṃ vedanāsmṛtyupasthānakathāyāṃ, śatasahasraṃ cittasmṛtyupasthānakathāyāṃ, śatasahasraṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānakathāyāmuddiṣṭā paṭhitā paryavāptāśca; śatasahasraṃ dhātuskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasramāyatanaskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasraṃ rāgasaṃyojanaprahāṇaskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasraṃ dveṣasaṃyojanaprahāṇaskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasraṃ mohaprahāṇapratītyasamutpādaskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasraṃ samādhivimokṣaskandhakathāṃ, śatasahasraṃ (

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s>, in due order, studied, recited, and mastered eighty-four thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s> — the discourse of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle; he expounded, studied, and mastered ninety thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s> — the discourse of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle. Then he expounded, studied, and mastered a hundred thousand [collections] of the discourse of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and likewise a hundred thousand of the discourse on the <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of the body), a hundred thousand of the discourse on the <s>vedanāsmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of feelings), a hundred thousand of the discourse on the <s>cittasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of mind), a hundred thousand of the discourse on the <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>)

body.text: yāvadapareṇa kālasamayena ratnagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ / sa ca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko bodhisattvaḥ nānāvidhāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā vādyapuṣpacūrṇāmālyagandhavilepanacchatradhvajapatākāratnaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtavān, nānāgandhaiśca snāpanaṃ kṛtavān, śarīrapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ ca saptaratnamayaṃ stūpaṃ kṛtavān pañcayojanamuccatvenārdhayojanaṃ vistāreṇa / tataḥ saptadivasānyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā vādyapuṣpamālyagandhavilepanacchatradhvajapatākāratnaiśca pūjāṃ kṛtvā, punarapi tatrāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāstriṣu yāneṣu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / sa teṣāṃ saptānāṃ divasānāmatyayena caturaśītibhiḥ prāṇasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ niṣkramya keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāni vastrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayāgārādanāgarikāṃ pravrajya ratnagarbhasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya śāsanaṃ jvālitavān; daśavarṣasahasrāṇi (

children.text: ) saddharmadhārako babhūva / tatra cāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāṃ sattvāṃstribhiryānaiḥ samādāpayāmāsa niveśayāmāsa pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa, triśaraṇagamane ca pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa, upāsakasaṃvare ca śrāmaṇerasaṃvare upasaṃpadāyāṃ bhikṣubhāve brahmacaryavāsasaṃvare niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / sa bahūni prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi abhijñarddhikauśalye ca niyojayitvā sauratyabrahmacaryavāse niyojayitvā śatrubhūteṣu ca skandhesu parijñāyāṃ niyojayitvā śūnyagrāmāyatanaparijñāyāṃ niyojayitvā pratītyasamutpannāḥ sarvadharmāḥ saṃskṛtajñānaparijñāyāṃ niyojayitvā pratibhāsopamān marīcyupamān dakacandropamān sarvadharmān darśayitvānutpādānirodhāpratisaṃdhinirodhaśāntapraśāntopaśāntaparamapraṇītanirodhanirvāṇaparijñānaṃ darśayitvā āryāṣṭāṅge mārge pratiṣṭhāpayitvā kālaṃ kṛtavān / evameva ca te sattvāstasya mahākāruṇikasya mahāśramaṇasya śarīreṣu śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtavanto, yathā rājñaścakravartinaḥ śarīreṣu śarīrapūjā kriyate / evameva tasmin samaye te sattvā mahākāruṇikasya mahāśramaṇasya śarīreṣu śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtavanto / yasmiṃśca divase mahākāruṇiko (

And there, he encouraged, established, and confirmed immeasurable and incalculable beings in the three vehicles, and established them in the threefold refuge, and established and confirmed them in the <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee) precepts, the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice) precepts, the full ordination of <s>bhikṣu</s>-hood, and the <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate) life. He engaged many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of beings in the skillfulness of the higher knowledges and supernatural powers, engaged them in the gentle celibate life, engaged them in the comprehension of the aggregates as enemies, engaged them in the comprehension of the empty village of the sense-bases, and [taught that] all <s>dharmas</s> are dependently arisen

body.translated_text: Then, at a later time, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder. And, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahākāruṇika</s> made offerings of immeasurable and incalculable varieties — musical instruments, flowers, powdered incense, garlands, fragrances, unguents, parasols, banners, flags, and jewels — and bathed [the relics] with various fragrances, and enshrined the relics in a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven precious substances, five <s>yojanas</s> in height and half a <s>yojana</s> in breadth. Then, for seven days, having worshipped with immeasurable and incalculable musical instruments, flowers, garlands, fragrances, unguents, parasols, banners, flags, and jewels, furthermore

body.text: kālagataśca kulaputra mahākāruṇiko mahāśramaṇaḥ praṇidhānavaśena dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśāyāmito buddhakṣetrāddaśabuddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya tatra saṃkarṣaṇo nāma lokadhāturaśītivarṣāyuṣkāśca tatra manuṣyā akuśalamūlasamavadhānā raudrā lohitapāṇayaḥ pāpaniviṣṭā adayāpannaḥ sarvasattveṣu amātṛjñā apitṛjñā aparalokabhayādarśinaḥ / praṇidhānavaśena mahākāruṇiko mahāśramaṇastatra saṃkarṣaṇe buddhakṣetre caṇḍālakula upapanno 'bhūt / sa cātīvadīrghaśarīro 'bhūdatīvabalavān atīvavegavān atīvasmṛtimān atīvapratibhānavān atīvajavasamanvāgato 'bhūt / sa dṛḍhena balavegena sattvān saṃgṛhītvāha - "yadi yūyaṃ bho sattvā adattādānāt prativiramata, kāmamithyācārādyāvan (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 349.

children.text: ) mithyādṛṣṭyāḥ prativiramata, tadahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ jīvitaṃ prayacchāmi jīvitopakaraṇāni ca dāsyāmi / atha ca punarna prativiramata, ahaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayitvā prakramiṣyāmi" / tataste sattvā añjaliṃ pragṛhyāhuḥ / "vayamidānīn tava nāthasya vacanenādyāgreṇa yāvajjīvamadattādānādyāvan mithyādṛṣṭyāḥ prativiramāmaḥ" / sa balacaṇḍālo gatvā rājño vā rājabhaṭṭānāṃ vā nivedayati / "jīvitopakaraṇena me prayojanamannena vā pānena vā khādyena vā bhojyena vā peyavastraśayyāgandhahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktavaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍarajatajātarūpeṇa vā prabhūtāni jīvitopakaraṇāni dadata mama" / sa balacaṇḍālaḥ sattvān yāvajjīvaṃ daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / tataste manuṣyāḥ pañcavarṣaśatāyuṣkā babhūvuḥ / yaśca tatra rājā sa kālagataḥ tatastai rājāmātyaiḥ sa balacaṇḍālo rājābhiṣekenābhiṣicya rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ puṇyabalo nāma saṃskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) 'Desist from wrong views, and I shall grant you your lives and give you the provisions for life. But if you do not desist, I shall depart after having deprived you of your lives.' Then those beings, having joined their palms, said: 'We now, by the word of you, our protector, from this day forth until the end of our lives, desist from taking what is not given, and so on up to wrong views.' The strong <s>caṇḍāla</s>, having gone, informed the king or the king's officers: 'I have need of provisions for life — food, drink, edibles, meals, beverages, clothing, bedding, fragrances, gold, silver, <s>maṇi</s> (jewels), pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl)

body.translated_text: And, O son of good family, when the great ascetic <s>Mahākāruṇika</s> passed away, by the power of his vow, in the southern direction from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, having passed beyond ten <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, there was a world-realm named <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>. Humans there had a lifespan of eighty years, and those humans had fallen into the tendency of unwholesome roots — they were fierce, blood-handed, steeped in evil, merciless toward all beings, ungrateful toward their mothers, ungrateful toward their fathers, and unable to see the danger of the next world. By the power of his vow, the great ascetic <s>Mahākāruṇika</s> was reborn there in the <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) family. He was extremely tall in body, extremely strong, extremely swift, extremely mindful, extremely eloquent

children.translated_text: ) The <s>ājīvika</s> <s>Pāṃśughoṣa</s> said: "I, O great king, desire the status of a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder) and wish to accomplish a spell for crushing the great <s>asura</s> battle. For that purpose I stand before you and inform you: I have need of the skin and the eyes of a living man." Then, O son of good family, King <s>Puṇyabala</s> thought thus: "I have obtained the sovereignty of a powerful <s>cakravartin</s>. Beings beyond counting have been established in the ten wholesome courses of action and yoked to the three vehicles, and immeasurable generosity has been given by me. And this is my virtuous friend — from this worthless body I shall extract what is essential." The king said: "Be pleased — I give you these ordinary, fleshly eyes, and by that may I obtain the supreme eye of the <s>Dharma</s>! I give you my own skin with a serene mind, and by that may I attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)!" Then, O son of good family, King <s>Puṇyabala</s>, with his right hand, extracted both eyes and gave them to the <s>ājīvika</s>, and with his blood-smeared face said: "Let the gods, <s>yakṣas</s>, and powerful beings here hear me, whatever humans, <s>asuras</s>, and spirits have come here, sky-farers and those standing on the ground — for the sake of awakening I have directed this gift; may I attain the peaceful state, may I ferry beings across, from the terrible ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and establish them on the far shore, in the supreme, auspicious <s>nirvāṇa</s>." He further said: (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 352.

children.text: ) "yadyahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāpnuyāṃ, tāvacciraṃ mama jīvitendriyaṃ mā nirudhyeta mā ca me smṛtirnaśyeta mā ca me vipratisāro bhaved, yāvacciramasyājīvikasya sā vidyā na siddhā bhavet" / āha - "gṛhṇāhi carma" / sa ca kulaputra pāṃśughoṣājīvikastīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā rājño dhriyataḥ kāyaccarmamapanetvā carma gṛhītvā vidyāṃ sādhayitvā, tathā saptadivasāni rājñaḥ puṇyabalasya jīvitendriyaṃ na niruddhaṃ, na ca smṛtiḥ pramuṣṭā, na ca tāṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati, na cāsyaikakṣaṇaṃ api vipratisāro jātaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) "If I shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, then may my life-faculty not cease, may my mindfulness not perish, and may I have no regret, for as long as that <s>ājīvika</s>'s spell is not accomplished." He said: "Take the skin." And, O son of good family, the <s>ājīvika</s> <s>Pāṃśughoṣa</s>, taking a sharp blade, while the king remained steadfast, removed the skin from his body, took the skin, and accomplished the spell. And for seven days, King <s>Puṇyabala</s>'s life-faculty did not cease, nor was his mindfulness lost, nor did he experience that painful sensation, nor did even a single moment of regret arise in him.

If you, O great king, will fulfill my wish, you, O great king, shall become a light of the world, a <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One)." The king said: "By what (

children.text: ) sthitvā sattvāṃ kuśale niyojya svabalaparākrameṇa yāvadbalacakravartitvaṃ prāptaṃ, sarvajaṃbūdvīpe ca kalikaluṣakalahāḥ praśamitā, āyuśca vardhāpitāḥ / ayaṃ ca me prathama ātmaparityāgaḥ, yadā ca me svanetrāḥ parityaktāḥ svacarmaparityāgaśca / so 'haṃ tataścyutastatraiva saṃkarṣaṇe kṣetre dvitīye dvīpe praṇidhānavaśena caṇḍālakula upapannaḥ / peyālaṃ, tatra ca mayaivaṃrūpeṇa dṛḍhavīryaparākrameṇa sattvānniyojayitvā kuśaleṣu karmeṣu, yāvadbalacakravartitvaṃ me prāptaṃ / tatra ca kalikaluṣakalahavairavigrahāḥ praśamitā, āyuśca vardhāpitaṃ / tatra ca svaśarīrāt jihvā karṇau ca parityaktau, yāvat sarvan tatsaṃkarṣaṇaṃ mahāsāhasraṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarvadvīpeṣvevaṃ puruṣakāraṃ kṛtaṃ / praṇidhānadṛḍhavīryaparākrameṇānuprabandhena praṇidhānavaśena gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu evaṃrūpaṃ mahāpuruṣakāraṃ kṛtaṃ, sattvāśca kuśaleṣu niyojitāḥ, triṣu ca yāneṣu samādāpitāḥ, kalikaluṣakalaharaṇavigrahāḥ śamitāḥ / ityarthaṃ kulaputrānyeṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhaṃ / yadā te buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrve 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhicaryāṃ caramāṇā na parāmāpattyā (
children.translated_text: ) having engaged beings in the wholesome by my own strength and valor, I attained the sovereignty of a powerful <s>cakravartin</s>, and throughout the entire <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> I pacified the strife, corruption, and quarrels of the age of <s>Kali</s>, and increased their lifespans. And this was my first self-sacrifice — when my own eyes were given up and my own skin was sacrificed. Then, having passed away from there, in that very <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> field, on the second continent, by the power of my aspiration, I was reborn in a <s>caṇḍāla</s> family — abbreviated. And there, by such firm effort and valor, having engaged beings in wholesome actions, I attained the sovereignty of a powerful <s>cakravartin</s>. And there the strife, corruption, quarrels, enmity, and conflict of the <s>Kali</s> age were pacified, and lifespans were increased. And there my tongue and ears from my own body were sacrificed, until throughout the entire <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> great-thousandfold <s>Buddha</s>-field, in all continents, such manly effort was made. By the continuity of firm effort and valor in aspiration, by the power of aspiration, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the five defilements equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, such great manly effort was made, and beings were engaged in the wholesome and inspired toward the three vehicles, and the strife, corruption, quarrels, enmity, and conflict of the <s>Kali</s> age were pacified. For this reason, O sons of good family, the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of those other <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones are purified. When those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, formerly, while practicing the conduct of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, did not incite through transgression, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 354.

children.text: ) codayanti, na ca parasya bhayaṃ darśayanti, na śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne sattvāṃ samādāpayanti / ityarthaṃ teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ paripūrṇābhiprāyāṇāṃ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhavati / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre āpattināma, na śikṣāgrahaṇasya, na ca paruṣavacanaṃ śrūyate, na cākuśalaśabdaḥ; anyatra dharmaśabdena tadbuddhakṣetramapagatāmanāpaśabdena sphuṭaṃ bhavati / tatra ca sattvā yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavanti, na ca tatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānasya nāma prajñaptiprādurbhāvo 'sti / yadā ca mayā gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu mahākalpeṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu paruṣavacanabhayena sattvāḥ prāṇātipātavairamaṇye samādāpitā yāvattriṣu yāneṣu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) nor did they show fear to others, nor did they inspire beings toward the <s>śrāvaka</s> or <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. For this reason, the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones of fulfilled intent are purified. In those <s>Buddha</s>-fields there is no name of transgression, no taking up of training rules, no harsh speech is heard, no sound of unwholesomeness; apart from the sound of <s>Dharma</s>, that <s>Buddha</s>-field is filled, devoid of the sound of the unpleasant. And there beings do as they please, and there is no arising even of the designation of the <s>śrāvaka</s> or <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. But when I, through great <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the five defilements equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, inspired beings to abstain from taking life through the fear of harsh speech, and up to inspiring, establishing, and grounding them in the three vehicles — (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 355.

children.translated_text: ) by that residual <s>karma</s>, my <s>Buddha</s>-field is now so defiled, filled with the sound of unwholesomeness, filled with beings who have accumulated unwholesome roots, and I teach the <s>Dharma</s> by means of the three vehicles. As was my former aspiration, so is the <s>Buddha</s>-field I have accepted. According to what kind of beings I accepted as those to be trained, with precisely that kind of powerful energy and vigor did I practice the conduct of awakening; and according to what kind of seed was planted, such is the <s>Buddha</s>-field I have obtained — in accordance with the aspiration I made.

body.translated_text: What do you think, O sons of good family? He who at that time, in that era, was called the Great Compassionate One — he is none other than myself. I was he who at that time, in that era, was called the Great Compassionate One, the father of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnagarbha</s>. This was my first generation of the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And by my first generation of the mind, beings beyond counting were inspired toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. This was my first act of heroism and heroic deed. Then I, by the power of my aspiration, having passed away from there, was reborn in the <s>Buddha</s>-field <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, in a family of <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) — this was my second heroic act and heroic deed. At that time, while dwelling in the <s>caṇḍāla</s> lineage, (

children.text: ) sarvaghoṣāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ saṃkaramardārcirnāma tathāgato varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / sa saptame divase parinirvāsyati / evaṃ vīryasaṃcodano nāma babhūva bodhisattvaḥ, yaḥ purimāyāṃ diśāyāmajayavatyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtavān gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā kalpātikrāntāḥ / yadā sa tathāgato 'nuttaraparinirvāṇena parinirvṛtaḥ, adyāpi tasya mahākāruṇikasya śarīrāṇi śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakāryaṃ kurvanti / evaṃ ca vadanti sārakusumito bodhisattvo dṛḍhavīryasamādhāno balavegaparityāgena bodhisattvacārikāṃ carati / daśagaṅgānadīvālikāsamairmahākalpairatikrāntaiḥ paścāt sa tatrottarāyāṃ diśāyāṃ sahetusaṃkarṣaṇo nāma bhaviṣyati pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre tatrāsau satpuruṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyati, sahetukṛṣṇavidhvaṃsanarājo nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yāvad buddho bhagavān / prajñārciḥsaṃkopitadaṣṭo (
children.translated_text: ) in the world-realm <s>Sarvaghoṣā</s>, he attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and as the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Saṃkaramardārci</s> (Flame that Crushes Defilements) teaches the <s>Dharma</s> among people of hundred-year lifespans. He will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> on the seventh day. Likewise there was a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vīryasaṃcodana</s> (Inciter of Vigor), who in the eastern direction, in the world-realm <s>Ajayavatī</s>, attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and performed the <s>Buddha</s>'s work among people of hundred-year lifespans — <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> have passed since then. When that <s>Tathāgata</s> passed into supreme <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, even now his relics of that greatly compassionate one continue performing the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the five defilements. Likewise, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sārakusumita</s> (Blossoming with Essence) practices the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct with firm effort, <s>samādhi</s>, and powerful, energetic renunciation. After ten great <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> have passed, in the northern direction, in a <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five defilements that shall be called <s>Sahetusaṃkarṣaṇa</s>, that good man shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sahetukṛṣṇavidhvaṃsanarāja</s> (King Who Destroys Darkness with Cause), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñārciḥsaṃkopitadaṣṭa</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 357.

children.text: ) nāma bodhisattvaḥ satpuruṣa ekasya mahākalpasyātyayena paścimāyāṃ diśi bhairavatī nāma lokadhāturbhaviṣyati pañcakaṣāye varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, sūryagarbhārcivimalendro nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhagavān / ayaṃ punaḥ saṃrocano gaṇanātikrāntaiḥ kalpairnirdiṣṭitairuparimasyāṃ diśi kṣāravarcanikuñjitāyāṃ lokadhātau pañcakaṣāye tīvrakaluṣasaṃkṣobhaṇe kalpe 'sau saṃrocanaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānena pañcāśadvarṣāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ tatra kṣāravarcanikuñjite buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) O good man, after the passage of one great <s>kalpa</s>, in the western direction, in a world-realm called <s>Bhairavatī</s> (Terrifying), of the five defilements, among people of hundred-year lifespans, shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sūryagarbhārcivimalendra</s> (Lord of Stainless Solar Womb Radiance), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, a Blessed One. And this <s>Saṃrocana</s>, after incalculable designated <s>kalpas</s>, in the upward direction, in a world-realm called <s>Kṣāravarcanikuñjitā</s>, of the five defilements, in a <s>kalpa</s> of intense turbulence and agitation, that <s>Saṃrocana</s>, by his former aspiration, among people of fifty-year lifespans, in that <s>Kṣāravarcanikuñjita</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, shall attain <s>anuttarā</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 358.

/ tatraiva divase tasya tathāgatasya saddharmo 'ntardhāsyati, daśavarṣāṇi punastaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ śūnyaṃ bhaviṣyati / tataḥ paścādasau prahasitabāhurbodhisattvastatra ca kṣāravarcanikuñjite buddhakṣetre 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, vairocanadharmo nāma bhaviṣyati tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho / so 'pi daśavarṣāṇi sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyati / tasya ca parinirvṛtasya pūrvapraṇidhānena saptavarṣāṇi saddharmaḥ sthāsyati / atra dvau satpuruṣau labdhapūrvavyākaraṇau labdhāsvādāvanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bhagavataḥ purataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā prītisaumanasyaprāmodyena saptatālamātrapramāṇamuparyantarīkṣe 'bhyudgamya prāñjalībhūtau sthitvā bhagavantamekasvareṇa gāthābhiradhyabhāṣatāṃ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Acintyarocana</s> (Inconceivable Brilliance), up to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He, by his former aspiration, having performed the complete <s>Buddha</s>'s work for ten years, shall pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. On that very day his <s>Saddharma</s> shall disappear, and for ten years that <s>Buddha</s>-field shall be empty. Thereafter, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Prahasitabāhu</s> (Laughing Arms) shall attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in that <s>Kṣāravarcanikuñjita</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field and shall become the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vairocanadharma</s> (Dharma of Vairocana), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. He too, having performed the complete <s>Buddha</s>'s work for ten years, shall pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder. And after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, by his former aspiration, the <s>Saddharma</s> shall endure for seven years. Here, two good men who had received former prophecies and tasted the bliss of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, having bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, rose up into the sky to the height of seven palm trees with joy, delight, and gladness, stood with palms joined, and praised the Blessed One with these verses in a single voice:

body.translated_text: In brief, O son of good family, I shall tell you of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity): the generosity and renunciation practiced by me while performing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct has not been practiced by any <s>bodhisattva</s> before, nor shall any <s>bodhisattva</s> in the future practice such generosity and renunciation while performing the conduct of awakening, as I have given while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — except for the eight good men. There was a good man named <s>Dharaṇidatta</s>. In the southern direction, (

children.text: "virocase buddha yathaiva sūrya abhyudgato merurimasmiṃ loke /
children.translated_text: "You shine forth, O <s>Buddha</s>, like the sun risen upon <s>Meru</s> in this world,

children.text: viśuddhacakṣurvirajā vināyakā ālokabhūtā sugatā namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: With purified eye, stainless guide, become a light — homage to you, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)!

body.text: bahūni kalpāna ti vīryabhāvitā paryeṣamāṇena ti agrabodhi /

children.text: bahujinā pūjitā pūrve ye tvayā na caiva te vyākarṣīmatitanāyakāḥ //
children.translated_text: Many <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) were worshipped by you in the past, yet they did not prophesy you — those surpassing guides!

body.translated_text: Through many <s>kalpas</s>, cultivated in vigor, seeking the supreme awakening,

children.text: prahīṇarāgā parimuktacittā kṛtaṃ ti kāryamiha sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: With attachment abandoned, with mind fully liberated, your work here in all the world is done,

children.text: praṇaṣṭamārgāṇa deśesi dharmaṃ sattvāṃśca uttārayase bhavārṇavāt //
children.translated_text: To those who have lost the path you teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and you ferry beings across the ocean of existence!

children.text: vayaṃ pi pravrajya svayaṃbhūśāsane yā prātimokṣa jina śikṣa deśitā /
children.translated_text: We too, having gone forth in the teaching of the Self-Born One, the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> training taught by the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: vayaṃ pi śikṣitva samāhitendriyā tavaiva āsanna sadā bhavemaḥ //
children.translated_text: We too, having trained with faculties concentrated, may we ever be near to you!
Unattached to life, <s>karma</s>, and desires, knowing the Teacher and hearing the <s>Dharma</s>,
We shall attain the bliss of the stage of consecration — the <s>Jina</s> has prophesied for precisely this purpose!"

body.text: bhagavānāha - "tau ca kulaputra dvau anutpāditabodhicittau; imau ca saṃrocanaḥ prahasitabāhuḥ, te catvāro dharaṇidatto vīryasaṃcodanaḥ sārakusumitaḥ prajñārciḥsaṃkopitadaṣṭaḥ, ime ṣaṭsatpuruṣā mayā prathamaṃ bodhāya samādāpitāstāṃ śṛṇu /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Those two, O son of good family, have not yet generated the mind of awakening; and these are <s>Saṃrocana</s> and <s>Prahasitabāhu</s>. Those four — <s>Dharaṇidatta</s>, <s>Vīryasaṃcodana</s>, <s>Sārakusumita</s>, and <s>Prajñārciḥsaṃkopitadaṣṭa</s> — these six good men were first inspired by me toward awakening. Now hear:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputrātīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyairapramāṇaiḥ kalpairatikrāntaiḥ, yadāsīttena kālena tena samayenedaṃ buddhakṣetramarajamerujugupsitaṃ nāmābhut, tadāhaṃ mahākalpe vartamāne varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ gandhapadmasya tathāgatasya śāsane saddharmapratirūpake (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 361.

children.text: ) vartamāne 'haṃ ca kulaputra tena kālena durdhano nāma babhūva balacakravartī jambūdvīpavijayī sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ babhūva / tānapyahamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitavān / te 'pyapareṇa samayena niṣkramya gandhapadmasya tathāgatasya śāsane pravrajitāste ca bhūyasyā mātrayā gandhapadmasya tathāgatasya śāsanaṃ jvālitavantaḥ, sthāpayitvā ṣaṭputrāṃ ye na pravrajitā na cecchanti bodhicittamutpādayituṃ / ahaṃ ca punaḥ punarvijñāpayāmi / "ko yuṣmākamabhiprāyo yadyūyaṃ bodhicittaṃ notpādayatha, na ca pravrajatha?" / te āhuḥ / "na vayaṃ pravrajāmaḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ?, yaḥ kṣayāntakāle saddharmapratirūpake vartamāne pravrajito 'śaktaḥ sakalaṃ śīlaskandhamārādhayituṃ, sa ca saptadhanavirahito bhavati, magnaḥ saṃsārapaṅke, punaśca sa devamanuṣyaśrīḥ kadācillabhati, nityaṃ triṣvapāyeṣu paribhramati, buddhaśikṣāyāṃ na samādāya vartate / ityarthaṃ vayaṃ na parivrajāmaḥ" / tānahaṃ punaḥ pṛṣṭavān / "kiṃ punaryūyaṃ bodhau cittaṃ notpādayatha?" / ta āhur["]yadyasmākaṃ sarvaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ dadyādevaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) at that time, O son of good family, I was a powerful wheel-turning king (<s>balacakravartin</s>) named <s>Durdhana</s>, conqueror of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and I had a thousand sons. I inspired them too in supreme perfect enlightenment. They also, at a later time, left home and went forth in the teaching of <s>Gandhapadma</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. And they greatly caused the teaching of <s>Gandhapadma</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> to blaze forth—except for six sons who did not go forth and did not wish to generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of enlightenment). And I again and again admonished them: "What is your intention, that you do not generate <s>bodhicitta</s>, and do not—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 362.
) we shall generate the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment."

body.translated_text: In the distant past, O son of good family, in a past time, after incalculable and immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> had passed, when at that time, in that era, this <s>Buddha</s>-field was called <s>Arajamerujugupsita</s> (Shunned by Dustless Meru), at that time, during a prevailing great <s>kalpa</s>, among people of hundred-year lifespans, in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhapadma</s> (Fragrant Lotus), during the counterfeit of the <s>Saddharma</s> (

body.text: tadahaṃ kulaputra śrutvā paramaprītamanā evaṃ cintayāmi / "mayā sarvaṃ jambudvīpakā manuṣyastriśaraṇagamane pratiṣṭhāpitā, āryāṣṭāṅge upoṣadhavāse samādāpitāstriṣu ca yāneṣu samādāpitā / yannūnamahamimaṃ jambudvīpaṃ ṣaḍbhāgaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṇṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ dadyāṃ; datvā cānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpayeyaṃ / ahaṃ ca niṣkramya pravrajeyaṃ" / evaṃ sarvaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ ṣaḍbhāgaṃ kṛtvā putrāṇāṃ dattaṃ / ahaṃ ca niṣkramya pravrajitaste ca ṣajjambūdvīparājānaḥ parasparaviruddhāḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigraharogaparacakrasaṃkṣobhavividamāpannāḥ / yataḥ sarvajambūdvīpe durbhikṣaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ, śaṣpāni na saṃpadyante, varṣaṃ na pravarṣati, vṛkṣebhyaśca patrapuṣpaphalāni na niṣpadyante, oṣadhitṛṇāni ca na saṃpadyante, mṛgapakṣiṇo 'pi kṣuttṛṣṇāprajvālitagātrā vihanyante / tadāhamevaṃ cintayāmi / "mayā caitarhi ātmaparityāgaḥ kartavyaḥ, sattvāḥ svamānsarudhireṇa saṃtarpayitavyās[ / "]tato 'ham āśramaṃ parityajya madhyameṣu janapadeṣu gatvā dagapālaṃ parvatamabhiruhya praṇidhānamakarot /
body.translated_text: Then I, O son of good family, hearing this, with a mind of supreme joy, thought thus: "By me, all the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> have been established in taking the three refuges (<s>triśaraṇagamana</s>), inspired in the observance-fast of the noble eightfold [path], and inspired in the three vehicles. Why should I not divide this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> into six parts and give them to my six sons? And having given, I should inspire them in supreme perfect enlightenment. And I should leave home and go forth." Thus I divided all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> into six parts and gave them to my sons. And I left home and went forth. But those six kings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, at odds with one another, [fell into] quarrel, dispute, conflict, strife—

body.text:
"yathā tyajāmi svaśarīrajīvitaṃ kāruṇyahetorna ca svargahetorarthāya
lokasya sadevakasya bhaved ihāparvatamātramucchrayaṃ //
body.translated_text: "Just as I give up my own body and life for the sake of compassion and not for the sake of heaven, for the benefit of the world including the gods—may it rise here to the height of a mountain.

children.text: yathā tyajāmi priyarūpasaṃpadaṃ na śakrabrahmāṇa na mārakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Just as I give up my dear and beautiful possessions, not for the sake of <s>Śakra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s>, not because of <s>Māra</s>,

children.text: arthaṃ karo bheṣyasi devaloke bhaveyaṃ mahyaṃ bahumānsaśoṇitaṃ //
children.translated_text: acting for the benefit [of all]—you shall be in the world of the gods—may there be for me an abundance of flesh and blood.

children.text: śṛṇvantu nāgā naradevayakṣā ye devatā śailagirau nivāsiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Nāgas</s>, human-gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and deities dwelling on rocky mountains hear!

children.text: kṛpā mamotpannaya sattvahetoḥ tarpaṣya sattvāṃ svakamāṃsaśoṇitaiḥ" //
children.translated_text: Compassion has arisen in me for the sake of beings—I shall satisfy beings with my own flesh and blood."

body.text: yadā ca mayā kṛtaṃ praṇidhānaṃ, kṣubhitāstrayo lokāḥ, kaṃpitā dharaṇī, calito meruḥ, rudanti devagaṇāstato 'hamātmānaṃ dagapālātparvatātpātayāmāsa / praṇidhānavaśena mama parvatapramāṇamātmabhāvaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, yojanaśataṃ vistāreṇa yojanamuccatvena; yāvan manuṣyamṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ārabdhā mānsarudhiraṃ bhakṣayituṃ / mama ca kulaputra sa kāyaḥ sattvaiḥ paribhujyamānaḥ pratidinaṃ vardhate, yojanaśatasahasraṃ vistāreṇa saṃvṛttaḥ yojanasahasramuccatvena / sarvatra mānuṣaśirāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ sakeśakarṇanayanānāsauṣṭhadāntāḥ sajihvā anekamukhaśatasahasrāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ / te ca mukhā manuṣyaśabdena ghoṣayanti / "bhoḥ sattvā bho gṛhṇatha yenārthaṃ, mānsaṃ paribhuñjatha, rudhiraṃ pivatha, nayanāṃ gṛhṇatha, karṇanāsāṃ keśauṣṭhadantajihvāṃ gṛhṇatha / yasyārthaṃ yenārthaṃ yāvadarthaṃ saṃtarpitaśarīrāḥ paripurṇābhiprāyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayatha, śrāvakayānena vā pratyekabuddhayānena vā / ayaṃ yuṣmākamupabhogaparibhogo na kṣīyate, na ca yuṣmākaṃ śraddhādeyaṃ bhaviṣyati, mā vaḥ kṣiprameva jīvitakṣayo bhavatu" / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 365.

children.text: ) ye ca tatra vijñāḥ sattvāste kecicchrāvakayāne cittamutpādayanti, kecit pratyekabuddhayāne, kecidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayanti, kecit punardevamanuṣyopapattau cittānyutpādayanti; mānsaṃ bhakṣayanti, rudhiraṃ pivanti, kecinnayanāni gṛhṇanti, kecit karṇau, kecinnāsāṃ, kecidoṣṭhau, keciddāntāṃ gṛhṇanti; gṛhitvā prakramanti; praṇidhānavaśena cānyonyaṃ prādurbhavati, mānsaṃ na cāpacayaṃ bhavati, na parikṣayaṃ gacchati / yāvaddaśavarṣasahasrāṇi sarvajambūdvīpakā manuṣyā yakṣamṛgapakṣiṇo 'pi svaśarīreṇa saṃtarpayāmāsa / taiśca daśabhirvarṣasahasrairgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni mayā netrāṇi parityaktāni, catuḥsamudrodakapramāṇaṃ mayā rudhiraṃ parityaktaṃ, sumerusahasrapramāṇaṃ mayā mānsaṃ parityaktaṃ, cakravāḍaparvatapramāṇā mayā jihvā parityaktā, yugandharamerupramāṇā mayā karṇāḥ parityaktāḥ, vipulāsumerupramāṇā mayā nāsāḥ parityaktāḥ, imaṃ gṛdhrakūṭaparvatapramāṇā mayā dāntāḥ parityaktāḥ, kṛtsnaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ prajñāpanapramāṇaṃ me tatra svacarma parityaktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) and those beings there who were wise—some generated the mind for the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, some for the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, some generated the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment, and some generated the mind for rebirth among gods and humans. They ate the flesh, they drank the blood; some took the eyes, some the ears, some the nose, some the lips, some the teeth, and having taken them, departed. And by the power of the aspiration, each [part] appeared again; the flesh did not diminish, nor was it exhausted. For ten thousand years, all the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, animals, and birds—

body.translated_text: And when I had made the aspiration, the three worlds trembled, the earth quaked, <s>Meru</s> shook, and the hosts of gods wept. Then I threw myself down from the <s>Dagapālā</s> mountain. By the power of the aspiration, my body became the size of a mountain—a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in breadth and a <s>yojana</s> in height. Then humans, animals, and birds began to eat the flesh and blood. And, O son of good family, that body of mine, being consumed by beings, grew day by day, and became a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth and a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height. Everywhere, human heads appeared, complete with hair, ears, and eyes—

body.text: paśya kulaputra daśavarṣasahasrāṇi evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāparimāṇāḥ svaśarīraparityāgāḥ parityaktā ekajīvitena; evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāparimāṇāḥ sattvāḥ saṃtarpitāḥ; ekacittakṣaṇamapi me vipratisāro notpannaḥ / evaṃ ca me tatra praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / yadyahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, iyaṃ me āśā paripūryatu, yathā mayaikadvīpe svaśarīreṇa sarvasattvāḥ saṃtarpitāḥ, evameva gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā varṣasahasrā asminnarajamerujugupsite buddhakṣetre sarvadvīpeṣvevaṃrūpo mamātmabhāvaḥ prādurabhavat, yathaikadvīpe daśavarṣasahasrāṇi evaṃ sarvadvīpeṣu sattvāṃ svamānsarudhiracarmanayanakarṇanāsauṣṭhajihvākeśaiḥ saṃtarpayitvā triṣu yāneṣu samādāpayeyaṃ, manuṣyāṃ yakṣarākṣasāṃ sarvatiryagyonikān ye kecin mānsarudhirabhojanāhārāḥ pṛthagyakṣā yāvadantaśaḥ yāmalaukikāḥ tāṃścāhaṃ saṃtarpayeyaṃ / yathā cāhamekasmin buddhakṣetre svaśarīreṇa sarvasattvāṃ saṃtarpayeyaṃ / evameva samantaddaśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 367.

children.text: ) buddhakṣetreṣu svamānsarudhiracarmanayanāṃ yāvajjihvābhirevaṃrūpeṇātmabhāvena gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān mahākalpān teṣu teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu svakāyajīvitena sattvāṃ saṃtarpayeyaṃ, evaṃrūpamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhya / visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyurye daśasu dikṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pravartitadharmacakrāḥ tiṣṭhanti yāpayanti dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, māhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, mā cāhaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaramāṇo buddhaśabdaṃ śṛṇuyāṃ mā ca dharmaśabdaṃ mā saṅghaśabdaṃ mā pāramitāśabdaṃ mā mārabalaparāśayaśabdaṃ mā vaiśāradyaśabdaṃ yāvat kuśalaśabdamapi saṃsāre mā śṛṇuyāṃ, nityaṃ cāvīcau narake saṃbhaveyaṃ; yadi me evaṃrūpaḥ svaśarīraparityāgaḥ sattvasaṃtarpaṇārthe na saṃpadyata, naivaṃrūpaṃ ca me praṇidhānaṃ paripūri syādyathā me āśā cintitā / ye 'pi cemasmiṃ buddhakṣetre sarvatra dvīpeṣvekaikasmiṃ dvīpa evaṃrūpā ātmabhāvāḥ parityaktāḥ sattvāṃśca mānsarudhireṇa saṃtarpitā, evaṃ daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvā evaṃrūpeṇātmabhāvena svamānsarudhireṇa santarpitāḥ / paśya (
children.translated_text: ) in [all] <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, with my own flesh, blood, skin, eyes, and even tongues—with such a body, for <s>mahākalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in those respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, I would satisfy beings with my own body and life, having attained such a form. May the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, be deceived by me—those who in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions have turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, who preside, dwell, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>—[if I fail, then] may I not attain supreme perfect enlightenment, may I not, while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, hear the sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, nor the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, nor the sound of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, nor the sound of the <s>pāramitās</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 368.

children.text: ) kulaputra tathāgatasya dānapāramitā ātmabhāvaparityāgaṃ ya mayānuprabandhena tatkālaṃ netrāḥ parityaktāḥ teṣāṃ punarayaṃ jambūdvīpe yāvattrāyastriṃśaddevaparyantapramāṇe rāśirbhavet / ayaṃ kulaputra tathāgatasya saṃkṣiptena ātmaparityāgadānapāramitā /
children.translated_text: ) O son of good family, this is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) through the renunciation of his own body. The eyes that I gave away in continuous succession during that time—their heap in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> would measure up to the boundary of the <s>Trāyastriṃśat</s> heaven. This, O son of good family, is in brief the <s>Tathāgata's</s> perfection of giving through self-sacrifice.

body.translated_text: Behold, O son of good family! For ten thousand years, thus immeasurable, countless, and boundless acts of giving up my own body were performed with a single life. Thus immeasurable, countless, and boundless beings were satisfied. Not even for a single moment of thought did regret arise in me. And thus was my aspiration made: "If I should attain supreme perfect enlightenment, may this hope of mine be fulfilled—just as with a single continent I have satisfied all beings with my own body, so may my body appear in this manner throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, for thousands of years, in this despicable <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of <s>Naraka</s> and <s>Meru</s>, in all continents—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra tataḥ paścādaprameyānāṃ kalpānāmatyayena ayaṃ buddhakṣetraścandravidyuto nāma babhūva; tamapi pañcakaṣāyaṃ babhūva / ahaṃ cāsmiṃ jambudvīpe rājā babhūva pradīpapradyoto nāma balavāṃścakravartī / evaṃ ca mayā sarvajaṃbūdvīpakāḥ sattvāḥ kuśaleṣu niyojitā, yathā pūrvoktaṃ / paścādahamudyānabhūmiṃ niryātaḥ svabhūmidarśanāya; tatra cāhaṃ puruṣamadrākṣaṃ, paścādbāhuṃ gāḍhabandhanaṃ badhyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayāmātyāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ / "kim anena puruṣeṇa kṛtaṃ?" / amātyā māṃ pratyūcur[ / "]ayaṃ puruṣo devasya sāparādhiko; yadetasya puruṣasya saṃvatsare śaṣpaṃ dhānyaṃ cotpadyate tato devasya ṣaṭkāṃśo deyaḥ, yathānye kuṭumbino dadantyāyadvāraṃ ye devasya nagaragrāmajanapadakarvaṭeṣu prativasanti (

children.translated_text: ) earn their livelihood through craft; and this man does not give [his share]." I said to them: "Release this man! Let no one seize wealth and grain by force from anyone." They said: "Your Majesty, no one gives with a clear and willing mind. The daily food, drink, and provisions enjoyed by Your Majesty, the queens, the royal household, the princes, and the princesses—all that is taken from others by force. And no one gives willingly." And I, extremely distressed, thought: "To whom should I give this entire kingdom and sovereignty of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?" And my five—

body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, after the passage of immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> thereafter, this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> was called <s>Candravidyut</s> (Moon-Lightning); and it too was afflicted with the five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>). And I was a king in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> named <s>Pradīpapradyota</s> (Lamp-Illuminator), a powerful wheel-turning king. And thus all the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were engaged in wholesome [deeds] by me, as previously described. Afterwards, I went out to the garden-grounds to see my domain. And there I saw a man being bound tightly with his arms behind his back, and I asked my ministers: "What has this man done?" The ministers replied to me: "This—

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena pañcaśatā jambūdvīpakānāṃ vāṇijānāṃ mahāsamudramavatīrṇāstaistataḥ prabhūto ratnaskandha āsāditaḥ / tatra ca candro nāma sārthavāhaḥ (

children.text: ) tena bhāgyavatā vijñapuruṣeṇa cintāmaṇiḥ samāsāditaḥ / sa tato ratnadvīpādvipulaṃ ratnadhanaskandhaṃ taṃ ca cintāmaṇiṃ gṛhītvā saṃprasthitaḥ, tataḥ kṣubhitaḥ samudro nāgā ākulā rudanti devatā yāstatra nivāsinyastatra cāśvasto nāma riṣirbodhisattvaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānena tatropapannaḥ; tena mahāsattvena sa sārthaḥ svastinā kṣemeṇa ca mahāsamudrāduttāritastasya ca sārthavāhasyānyataro duṣṭarākṣasaḥ pratyarthiko 'vatāraprekṣī vivaragaveṣī pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ / tena saptadivasāni paramakaluṣā vātavṛṣṭiravasṛtā; yataste vaṇijaḥ praṇaṣṭamārgā paramabhītāduccasvareṇa krandanti rudanti paridevanti, devatāmāyācanti śivavaruṇāṃ yāvan mātāpitaramākrandanti priyaputrāṃ / yāvadaśroṣīdahaṃ divyena śrotreṇa yāvattatrāgatvā vaṇijaḥ samāśvāsitāḥ, "samāgato 'haṃ; mā bhāyatha; ahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ mārgāmupadarśayiṣyāmi, yāvajjambūdvīpaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) that fortunate, wise man obtained the wish-fulfilling gem. Having taken a vast mass of jewel-wealth from that jewel-island, along with the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), he set forth. Then the ocean became turbulent; the <s>nāgas</s> were agitated and weeping. The deities who dwelt there — and there was a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Aśvasta</s>, who had been reborn there through a former aspiration — by that <s>mahāsattva</s>, the caravan was safely and securely brought across the great ocean. But a certain malicious <s>rākṣasa</s>, an adversary of that caravan-leader, watching for an opportunity, seeking a gap, followed closely behind. For seven days, he released an extremely turbid wind and rain-storm. Those merchants, having lost their way, cried out in a loud voice, supremely frightened — they wailed, lamented, and mourned; they called upon deities, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, called upon their mothers and fathers, their dear sons. Then I heard with divine hearing, went there, and comforted the merchants: 'I have arrived; do not be afraid! I will show you the way, and you will reach <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 371.

children.text: ) svastinā kṣemeṇa ca prāpsyatha" / tadāhaṃ paṭṭaṃ tailena mrakṣayitvā svahastaṃ veṣṭya agninā prajvālya satyavacanamakarot - "yadi mayā ṣaṭtriṃśadvarṣā caturbhirbrāhmairvihārairvanakhaṇḍanivāsināṃ sattvānāmarthāya hitāya navamūlaphalāhāreṇa caturaśītīnāṃ nāgayakṣasahasrāṇāṃ cittasantatiḥ paripācitā avaivartikāśca sthāpitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tena satyena satyavacanena kuśalamūlaparipākena jvalatu me hastaṃ; labhantu mārgaṃ vaṇijaḥ svastinā kṣemeṇa jambūdvīpaṃ prāpayantu" / yāvat saptarātridivasāḥ svahastaṃ jvālitavān, te vaṇijo jambūdvīpe sthāpitāstatra mayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ : yadā jambūdvīpaṃ ratnaparihīṇaṃ bhavet, tad yadāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, tadā iyaṃ me āśā paripūryatu, sārthavāho bhaveyaṃ jambudvīpe saptavārāṃ cintāmaṇimānayitvā vividhaṃ ratnavarṣaṃ abhipravarṣayeyaṃ; yāvat sarvadvīpeṣvasmin buddhakṣetre evameva daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu śūnyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu ratnaṃ pravarṣayeyaṃ, yāvatpūrvoktaṃ / (
children.translated_text: ) safely and securely.' Then I smeared a cloth with oil, wound it around my own hand, set it ablaze with fire, and made a truthful declaration: 'If for thirty-six years, dwelling in forest groves by means of the four <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes (divine dwellings), eating only roots and fruits for the benefit and welfare of beings, I have ripened the mental continuity of eighty-four thousand <s>nāgas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s> and established them as non-retrogressing in unsurpassed perfect awakening — by that truth, by that truthful declaration, by the ripening of those roots of merit, may my hand blaze! May the merchants find their way and safely, securely reach <s>Jambudvīpa</s>!' For seven nights and days I kept my own hand blazing, and those merchants were established in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. And there I made this aspiration: 'When <s>Jambudvīpa</s> becomes devoid of jewels — when I attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, may this wish of mine be fulfilled: may I become a caravan-leader in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and having brought the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> seven times, may I shower down various rains of jewels; and likewise in all the continents of this <s>Buddha</s>-field, and similarly in the ten directions, in empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, may I shower down jewels' — as previously stated. (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 372.

) evaṃ ca me āśā paripūrṇā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ mahākalpānāmantareṇa sārthavāho 'bhūvan, gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ratnāni pravarṣitāni; ekaikadvīpe saptavārāṃ vividhaṃ ratnavarṣaṃ pravarṣitaṃ / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā ratnaiḥ paripurṇābhiprāyāḥ kṛtāstriṣu ca yāneṣu niyojitāḥ / paśya kulaputra
tathāgatasya ratnaparityāgalakṣaṇaṃ vipākakuśalamūlaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) And thus my aspiration was fulfilled — during the interval of great <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, I became a caravan-leader; in empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, jewels were showered; on each continent, seven times a various rain of jewels was showered. Thus immeasurable, incalculable beings were satisfied with jewels and fulfilled in their wishes, and were established in the three vehicles. Behold, O son of good family, the karmic fruit of the root of merit — the mark of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relinquishment of jewels.

body.translated_text: Now at that time, five hundred merchants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> had descended into the great ocean, and from there they obtained an abundant mass of jewels. And among them was a caravan-leader (<s>sārthavāha</s>) named <s>Candra</s>—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputrāprameyāṇāṃ kalpānāmatyayenāntareṇāyaṃ buddhakṣetrastimiraṃ nāmābhūt; saṃtoṣaṇe kalpe vartamāne pañcakaṣāye pañcavarṣasahasrikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ praṇidhānenāhamasmin jambūdvīpe sūryamālagandho nāma brāhmaṇo 'bhūvan vedapāṭhakaḥ / tatkālaṃ ca sattvā bhūyasā śāśvatadṛṣṭayo 'bhūvan savairaparākramāḥ sakalahādhiṣṭhānāḥ / teṣāṃ cāhaṃ mahābalavegaparākrameṇa sattvānāṃ śatrubhūtaṃ skandhaprayogena dharmaṃ deśayāmi, śūnyagrāmāyatanapratyavekṣaṇāpratyayasamanubaddhaṃ sotpādavyayaṃ ānāpānasmṛtimanaskāraṃ darśayāmi / te 'nuttarāyāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 373.

children.text:
) samyaksaṃbodhau cittotpādanakuśalamūlapariṇāmanābhiyojitāḥ, svayameva cāhaṃ pañcābhijñaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; tena ca samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā mamāvavādānuśāsanena pañcābhijñāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāḥ kalahavigrahavairānavasṛjya vanakhaṇḍamāśṛtya vanakhaṇḍe mūlaphalāhārā dhyāyantaścaturbhirbrāhmairvihārai rātridivasamatināmitavantaḥ / tataḥ kṣīyamāṇe kalpe yadā tairdakṣiṇīyaiḥ kṛtsnaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ sphuṭamabhūt / te ca kalikalaharaṇavairavigrahavivādāḥ praśāntāḥ, akālavātavarṣāḥ praśamitāḥ, praṇītā ojavatīpṛthivīsaṃniśritāḥ śaṣpā babhūvuḥ / kevalaṃ vividharogopahatā babhūvuḥ kalpadoṣeṇa /
tadāhamevaṃ cintayāmi, "yadyahaṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhiṃ na śaktaḥ śamayituṃ" / tasya mamaitadabhavad, "yannūnamahaṃ śakraṃ mahābrāhmaṇaṃ lokapālānanye ca devarṣayo vā (
children.translated_text: ) engaged in the dedication of roots of merit through the generation of the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, and I myself attained the five <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges). At that time, immeasurable, incalculable beings, through my instruction and guidance, attained the five <s>abhijñās</s>. Thus immeasurable, incalculable beings, having abandoned quarrel, strife, and enmity, took refuge in forest groves, and dwelling in the forest groves, eating roots and fruits, meditating, they passed day and night by means of the four <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes (divine dwellings). Then, when the <s>kalpa</s> was declining, when the worthy ones had spread throughout the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — the strife, quarrel, conflict, enmity, and dispute of the degenerate age were pacified; untimely winds and rains were calmed; fine, nourishing grasses dependent on the vitality of the earth arose. However, they became afflicted by various diseases due to the fault of the <s>kalpa</s>. Then I thought thus: 'If I am not able to pacify the diseases of beings' — and this occurred to me: 'Let me assemble <s>Śakra</s>, great <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, and other divine <s>ṛṣis</s>, or (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 374.

children.text: ) nāgarṣayo vā śakrarṣayo vā manuṣyarṣayaśca sannipātayeyaṃ, bhaiṣajyopakaraṇaśāstraṃ sattvānāṃ hitārthamupadarśayeyaṃ / tadāhamṛddhyā gatvā śakrabrahmāṇalokapāladevarṣīṇāṃ nāgarṣīṇāṃ śakrarṣīṇāṃ manuṣyarṣīṇāṃ ārocayeyaṃ / ekaviḍapatirnāma parvataḥ, tatra saṃnipātayitvā viḍacarakamūrdhani nāma sthānaṃ bhūtasaṃnivāraṇapratiśaraṇaṃ rakṣāvātapittaśleṣmasaṃprasādanaśāstraṃ nirdeśayeyaṃ" / peyālaṃ, aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhipraśamanaṃ kṛtaṃ / tatra mahāpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ yathā mayaikadivase 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ prajñāvabhāsaḥ kṛtaḥ, triṣu ca yāneṣu niyojitā, apāyapathāḥ pithitāḥ, svargapathapratiṣṭhāpitā, vividhāśca vyādhayaḥ praśamitāḥ parimocittāśca / evamaprameyānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ prajñāloko dattaḥ, saukhye 'vasthāpitāḥ / tadanena kulaputra (
children.translated_text: ) <s>nāga</s> sages, or <s>Śakra</s> sages, or human sages, and reveal to beings the treatise on medicinal remedies for their benefit.' Then, going by supernatural power, I announced to <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, divine sages, <s>nāga</s> sages, <s>Śakra</s> sages, and human sages. There is a mountain named <s>Ekaviḍapati</s>; having assembled them there, at a place called <s>Viḍacarakamūrdhani</s>, I revealed the treatise on warding off demons, providing protection, and purifying wind, bile, and phlegm.' Abbreviated — the pacification of diseases of immeasurable, incalculable beings was accomplished. There a great aspiration was made: 'Just as by me in a single day the illumination of wisdom was given to immeasurable, incalculable beings, and they were established in the three vehicles, the paths to the lower realms were blocked, they were established on the path to heaven, various diseases were pacified, and they were liberated — thus the light of wisdom was given to immeasurable, incalculable beings, and they were established in well-being.' By this, O son of good family, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 375.

children.text: ) kuśalamūlavipākena iyaṃ me praṇidhānāśā paripūrṇāḥ / yadā ca mayaikadivase 'prameyānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmapāyapathā nirodhitāḥ, svargapathe ca pratiṣṭhāpitā, glānapratyayopakaraṇārthaṃ devarṣiyakṣasaṅghāḥ sannipātitāḥ sattvānāmarthāya viḍacarakamūrdhani devaloke prakāśite sattvānāmārogyakauśalyamevameva timire buddhakṣetre sarvadvīpeṣu caivaṃrūpaḥ puruṣakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, sattvāśca svargapathe pratiṣṭhāpitā, devanāgayakṣamanuṣyā ṛṣayaḥ sannipātitā yaissattvānāmarthāya vividhā vidyāsthānāḥ prakāśitāḥ / yathena timire buddhakṣetre evameva daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣvevaṃrūpaḥ puruṣakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, sattvāśca triṣu yāneṣu niyojitāḥ, svargapathe ca pratiṣṭhāpitā, vividhāśca vidyāsthānā loke prakāśitāḥ, sattvā vyādhitaḥ parimocitā, anuttarā ca me kulaputraivaṃrūpā āśā paripūrṇāḥ / api tatra timire buddhakṣetre sarvadvīpeṣvevaṃrūpaḥ puruṣakāraḥ kṛto yathā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / apyanuttareṇa (
children.translated_text: ) through the karmic fruit of this root of merit, this aspiration-wish of mine was fulfilled. And when by me in a single day the paths to the lower realms of immeasurable, incalculable beings were blocked and they were established on the path to heaven, and assemblies of divine sages, <s>yakṣas</s>, and others were convened for the purpose of providing remedial medicines for the sick, for the benefit of beings, and the skill of healing for beings was revealed in the heaven at <s>Viḍacarakamūrdhani</s> — just so, in the <s>Timira</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, in all the continents, such manly effort was made, and beings were established on the path to heaven; divine, <s>nāga</s>, <s>yakṣa</s>, and human sages were assembled, and by them various fields of knowledge were revealed for the benefit of beings. Just as in this <s>Timira</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, so too in the ten directions, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, such manly effort was made; beings were established in the three vehicles, established on the path to heaven; various fields of knowledge were revealed in the world; beings were liberated from disease; and, O son of good family, my unsurpassed aspiration of this kind was fulfilled. Moreover, in the <s>Timira</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, in all the continents, such manly effort was made as my aspiration was made. And with unsurpassed (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 376.

) jñānena daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣvaikaikasmin buddhakṣetre sarvadvīpeṣvevaṃrūpaḥ puruṣakāraḥ kṛto, yathā me pūrvapraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / paśya kulaputra prajñāviśeṣaṃ bodhicaryāyāṃ, ayaṃ ca tathāgatasya trayāṇāṃ sucaritānāṃ kuśalamūlabījaṃ

children.translated_text: ) knowledge, in the ten directions, in empty <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in each <s>Buddha</s>-field, in all the continents, such manly effort was made, as my former aspiration was made. Behold, O son of good family, the distinction of wisdom in the course of awakening — this is the seed of the root of merit of the three good conducts of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, after the passage of immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> in the interim, this <s>Buddha</s>-field was called <s>Timira</s> (Darkness); during the <s>Saṃtoṣaṇa</s> <s>kalpa</s>, afflicted by the five degenerations, when the generation had a lifespan of five thousand years, by aspiration, I was born as a brahmin named <s>Sūryamālagandha</s> in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a reciter of the <s>Vedas</s>. At that time, beings were mostly of eternalist views, of hostile aggression, established in quarrel. And with great, forceful, vigorous exertion, I taught the <s>Dharma</s> through the method of the aggregates to those beings who were like enemies — demonstrating the contemplation of emptiness of the village of sense-bases, connected with conditions, with arising and passing away, the mindfulness of in-and-out breathing and mental attention.
