body.text: tathā pratyavarakālasamaye 'saṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairadhikatarairantareṇedaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ vicitadoṣaṃ nāmābhūt, saṃśrayase mahākalpe vartamāne tadapi pañcakaṣāyaṃ / purimāyāṃ diśyanupañcāśāyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ vaḍaṃ nāma jambūdvīpamabhūt / tatrāpyahaṃ sattvaparipācanārthamupapannaḥ, caturdvīpeśvaraḥ cakravartī rājā ambaro nāma babhūva / tatra ca mayā sattvā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāstriṣu yāneṣu samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / sarvaṃdadaśca babhūva sarvatradāyī / tatra ca me yācanakā āgatvā vividhāni ratnāni yācanti, tadyathā hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 377.

children.text: ) yāvaccendranīlamahānīlajyotīrasadakaprasādakāni yācanakānāṃ tāvatprabhūtāni ratnāni labhyante / tadāhamamātyāṃ pṛṣṭavān / "kuta eṣāṃ ratnānāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ?" / ta āhuḥ / "nāgarājāno nidhīrnidarśayanti, nidhīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvādratnānāṃ prādurbhāvo bhavati / na kevalaṃ tāttakā nirdeśayanti yāttakā devasya yācanakāḥ" / tadāhaṃ praṇidhānamakarot / "yadyahaṃ pañcakaṣāye loke vartamāne tīvrakleśāraṇe kaliyuge vartamāne varṣaśatāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyeyaṃ / tadiyaṃ me āśā paripūryatu, yadahamasmin buddhakṣetre nidhidarśako nāma nāgarājā bhaveyaṃ / sarvatra cāsmiṃ vijitaghoṣe buddhakṣetre sarvadvīpeṣu ca ekaikasmin dvīpe saptajanmāni parigṛhṇīyāṃ / ekaikasmiṃśca janmani nidhikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi darśayeyaṃ prayaccheyaṃ ca nānāratnaparipūrṇāni: tadyathā hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ yāvadindranīlamahānīlajyotīrasadakaprasādāśca / ekaikaśca nidhiyojanasahasrāṇi gatvā vistareṇa paripūrṇamapi ratnaṃ sattvānāṃ nidarśayeyaṃ prayacchayeyaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) up to <s>indranīla</s>, <s>mahānīla</s>, <s>jyotīrasa</s>, and <s>dakaprasāda</s> [gems] — and the supplicants obtained jewels in such abundance. Then I asked my ministers: 'Whence is the appearance of these jewels?' They said: '<s>Nāga</s> kings reveal treasures; from the appearance of treasures in the world comes the appearance of jewels. But they do not reveal as much as there are supplicants of the king.' Then I made this aspiration: 'If, when the world is afflicted by the five degenerations, when the degenerate age of intense affliction and strife prevails, when the generation has a lifespan of a hundred years, I should attain unsurpassed perfect awakening — may this wish of mine be fulfilled: may I become in this <s>Buddha</s>-field a <s>nāga</s> king named <s>Nidhidarśaka</s> (Revealer of Treasures). In all the continents of this <s>Vijitaghoṣa</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, may I accept seven births on each continent. In each birth, may I reveal and bestow hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of treasure-troves, filled with various jewels — namely silver and gold, up to <s>indranīla</s>, <s>mahānīla</s>, <s>jyotīrasa</s>, and <s>dakaprasāda</s> [gems]. And each treasure-trove, extending for a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, filled to its full extent with jewels, I shall reveal and bestow upon beings, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 378.

children.text: ) ca, yadasmiṃ buddhakṣetre evaṃrūpaṃ śūrabhāvaṃ kuryāṃ / evameva daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu lokadhātuṣu ekaikasmin kṣetre sarvatra dvīpe saptajanmāni pratigṛhṇīyāṃ", yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) performing such heroic deeds in this <s>Buddha</s>-field. Just so, in the ten directions, in <s>Buddha</s>-fields afflicted by the five degenerations as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in each world-realm, on every continent, I shall accept seven births' — as previously stated.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, at yet another later time, after the passage of incalculable additional <s>kalpas</s>, this <s>Buddha</s>-field was called <s>Vicitadoṣa</s> (Various Faults); during the <s>Saṃśrayase</s> great <s>kalpa</s>, afflicted by the five degenerations. In the eastern direction, in the fifty-first <s>cāturdvīpikā</s> (four-continent world-system), in a <s>Jambudvīpa</s> called <s>Vaḍa</s>, there too I was born for the sake of ripening beings — I became a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning) king, lord of the four continents, named <s>Ambara</s>. There I inspired, established, and grounded beings in the ten wholesome courses of action, and inspired, established, and grounded them in the three vehicles. And I became an all-giver, giving everywhere. And there, supplicants came to me asking for various jewels — such as silver and gold, (

body.text: yadā ca me kulaputraivaṃrūpaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tadā gaganatale devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairantarīkṣāt puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ pravarṣitā sādhukāraścānupradattaḥ / "sādhu sādhu sarvaṃdada, ṛdhiṣyati te evaṃrūpā āśā yathā te praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ" / aśroṣīn mahājanakāyaḥ rājño 'mbarasya devairgaganatalagataiḥ sarvaṃdada iti nāma kṛtaṃ, śrutvā caiṣametadabhavat / "yannūnaṃ vayaṃ duṣkaraparityāgaṃ dānaṃ yācemaḥ / yadi parityakṣyati tadā sarvaṃdada iti nāma bhaviṣyati" / tataste sarvā ārabdhā rājño 'mbarasyāntaḥpurikāṃ yācituṃ, devīmagramahiṣīṃ putraduhitṝṇāṃ yācituṃ; tadā rājāmbaraḥ prayacchati prasannacittasteṣāṃ etadabhavat / "na cedaṃ duṣkaraṃ yo bhāryāṃ parityajati / yannūnaṃ vayaṃ rājño 'mbarasyāṅgapratyaṅgāni yācamaḥ / tadyadi dāsyati sarvaṃdado bhaviṣyati, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 379.

children.text: ) atha na dāsyati na sarvaṃdado bhaviṣyati" /
children.translated_text: ) but if he does not give, he will not be the All-Giver.'

body.translated_text: And when, O son of good family, I made such an aspiration, at that time from the sky, by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of gods, a flower-rain was showered from the atmosphere, and a cry of approval was given: 'Excellent, excellent, O All-Giver! Such a hope of yours will succeed, as your aspiration was made.' A great multitude of people heard that the gods in the sky had given the name <s>Sarvaṃdada</s> (All-Giver) to King <s>Ambara</s>, and having heard, they thought: 'Let us ask for a difficult relinquishment as a gift. If he gives it up, then the name All-Giver will be true.' Then they all began to ask King <s>Ambara</s> for his queen, the chief consort of his inner palace, and to ask for his sons and daughters. Then King <s>Ambara</s> gave them away with a serene mind. They thought: 'This is not difficult — giving up one's wife. Let us now ask King <s>Ambara</s> for his limbs and members. If he gives them, he will truly be the All-Giver; (

body.text: tatastasyāgrataḥ tatra jyotīraso nāma māṇavako rājño 'mbarasyāgrataḥ sthitvā, "sarvaṃdada rājyaṃ dadasve"ti prārthitavān / śrutvā ca rājñāmbareṇa paramaprītimanasā svayameva brāhmaṇaṃ snāpayitvā paṭṭaṃ badhvā rājābhiṣekenābhiṣicya rājatve pratiṣṭhāpayitvā sarvaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ niryātayitvā, praṇidhānamakarod / "ahaṃ sarvajambūdvīpaparityāgenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ / yadīyaṃ me āśā paripūryati, yo 'yaṃ mamaitarhi sarvajambūdvīpe rājā pratiṣṭhāpito vartatvasya jambūdvīpe ājñā, dīrghāyuṣca bhavatu, rājā cakravartī cirasthāyī / yadā cāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ, yadā yuvarājatvena vyākuryāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" / roco nāma brāhmaṇastena me ubhau pādau yācitau, tasya mayā svayameva prasannacittena tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā svapādau chitvā pradattau, praṇidhānaṃ cākarot / "labheyāhamanuttarāṃ śīlapādāṃ" / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 380.

children.text: ) tatra drāṣṭāvo nāma brāhmaṇastena me ubhe netre yācite, tasya ca mayā ubhe netre utpādya datte, peyālaṃ, anuttaraṃ pañcacakṣuḥ pratilabhāya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān / na cireṇa saracchighoṣo nāma brāhmaṇastena me ubhau karṇau yācitau, svayameva tasya mayā karṇau chitvā dattau, anuttaraśrotāpratilābhāya ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / saṃjīvanaśca nāmājīviko 'bhūt, tena me puruṣanimittaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ yācitaṃ, svayameva ca mayā chitvā dattaḥ, anuttaravastiguhyatālakṣaṇapratilābhāya ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / apareṇa ca me māṃsarudhiraṃ yācitaṃ, svayameva ca mayā dattaṃ, suvarṇavarṇatālakṣaṇapratilābhāya ca me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / aparaśca kṣīraso nāma parivrājakastena ca me ubhau hastau yācitau, svayameva ca mayā dakṣiṇena hastena vāmaṃ hastaṃ chitvā dakṣiṇaṃ chedāpayitvā datto, anuttaraśraddhāhastapratilābhāya ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / yadā cāṅgapratyaṅgāni chinnāni tadā ca mayā rudhiramrakṣitena kāyena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / "yadi (
children.translated_text: ) There, a brahmin named <s>Drāṣṭāva</s> requested both my eyes from me; to him I plucked out and gave both my eyes — abbreviated — and made the aspiration to attain the supreme five eyes. Before long, a brahmin named <s>Saracchighoṣa</s> requested both my ears from me; I myself cut off and gave him my ears, and made the aspiration to attain the supreme hearing. And there was a naked ascetic named <s>Saṃjīvana</s>; by him the male organ was requested from me; I myself cut it off and gave it, and made the aspiration to attain the supreme mark of the sheathed private parts. By another, my flesh and blood were requested; I myself gave them, and made the aspiration to attain the mark of a golden-colored body. And another wandering ascetic named <s>Kṣīrasa</s> requested both my hands from me; I myself, with my right hand, cut off my left hand, then had the right one cut off and gave it, and made the aspiration to attain the supreme hand of faith. And when my limbs and members had been severed, with my body smeared in blood, I made this aspiration: "If (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 381.

children.text: ) me 'nena parityāgenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āśā paripūryeta, avaśyamahamasya kāyasya pratigrāhakaṃ pratilabheyaṃ" /
children.translated_text: ) through this relinquishment, my wish for supreme perfect awakening is to be fulfilled, I shall surely obtain a restorer of this body."

body.translated_text: Then, in his presence, a young man named <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, standing before King <s>Ambara</s>, requested: "O <s>Sarvaṃdada</s> (All-Giving One), give up the kingdom!" And hearing this, King <s>Ambara</s>, with a supremely joyful mind, himself bathed the brahmin, tied the turban upon him, consecrated him with the royal consecration, established him in kingship, handed over all of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, and made this aspiration: "Through the relinquishment of all <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, may I attain supreme perfect awakening. If this wish of mine is fulfilled, may the one now established by me as king in all of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> exercise sovereignty over <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, may he be long-lived, and may he be a long-enduring <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). And when I attain supreme perfect awakening, may he be prophesied for the position of crown prince in supreme perfect awakening." A brahmin named <s>Roca</s> requested both my feet from me; to him, I myself, with a serene mind, took a sharp blade, cut off my own feet, and gave them, and made this aspiration: "May I attain the supreme feet of moral conduct." (

body.text: te 'pyakṛpakā anāryā akṛtajñāḥ sattvāḥ koṭṭarājāno 'mātyāścāhuḥ / "ayaṃ durbuddhiralpamedhāḥ sarvāṅgavikartitaḥ sarvarājyaiśvaryaparibhraṣṭaḥ / kiṃ bhūyo 'nena mānsapeśinā prayojanaṃ?" / te māṃ gṛhītvā bahirnagaraśmaśānabhūmau choritvā prakāntāḥ / tatra daṃśamaśakā āgatvā rudhiraṃ pibanti, kurkuraśṛgālagṛdhrā āgatvā mānsaṃ bhakṣayanti / tatra cāhaṃ prasannacittaḥ praṇidhānamakarot / "yadā ca mayā sarvarājyaiśvaryaṃ parityaktaṃ, sarvaśarīraṃ caivāṅgapratyaṅgāni parityajatā, ekakṣaṇamapi na vipratisārikṛtaṃ cittaṃ, na ca me roṣa utpāditastena me āśā paripūryatu, ayaṃ me kāyo mānsaparvataḥ saṃtiṣṭhatāṃ, ye kecit sattvā mānsāhārā rudhirapānāste māṃsaṃ bhakṣayantu rudhiraṃ pibeyantu / yāvacca (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 382.

children.text: ) me sattvā māṃsaṃ bhakṣayeyū rudhiraṃ ca pibeyustāvan me praṇidhānavaśena śarīraṃ vardhatu, anupūrveṇa yāvadyojanaśatasahasramuccatvena kāyaḥ saṃvardhatu pañcayojanasahasraṃ vistāreṇa / tatra mayā varṣasahasraṃ svamānsarudhireṇa sattvāḥ saṃtarpitā; yāvabhyaśca mayā jihvāḥ parityaktā yā mṛgapakṣibhiḥ paribhaktāḥ praṇidhānavaśena cānyonyāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ teṣāṃ ayaṃ gṛdhrakūṭaparvatapramāṇo rāśiḥ syānnityaṃ cānuttarāprabhūtājihvatālakṣaṇapratilābhāya me praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) beings eat my flesh and drink my blood, for that long, by the power of my aspiration, may my body grow, gradually increasing until my body reaches a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and five thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth." There, for a thousand years, beings were satisfied by my own flesh and blood. And as many tongues as I relinquished, which were consumed by beasts and birds, by the power of my aspiration new ones appeared — the heap of those would equal the measure of <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain. And I made the constant aspiration to attain the supreme mark of the inexhaustible, far-reaching tongue.

body.translated_text: Those merciless, ignoble, ungrateful beings — the vassal kings and ministers — said: "This fool of little intelligence has had all his limbs cut off and has lost all royal sovereignty. What further use is there for this lump of flesh?" They seized me, cast me outside the city in the charnel ground, and departed. There biting flies and mosquitoes came and drank my blood; dogs, jackals, and vultures came and ate my flesh. And there, with a serene mind, I made this aspiration: "Since I have relinquished all royal sovereignty and am also relinquishing my entire body with its limbs and members, not for even a single moment have I felt regret in my mind, nor have I generated anger — may this wish of mine be fulfilled. May this body of mine, this mountain of flesh, remain; whatever beings feed on flesh and drink blood, let them eat my flesh and drink my blood. And for as long as (

body.text: tatrāhaṃ cyutvā rūḍhavaḍe jambūdvīpe pūrvapraṇidhānena nāgeṣūpapanno nidhisaṃdarśano nāma nāgarājā babhūva / yāmeva rātriṃ nāgeṣūpapannastāmeva rātriṃ nidhikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi nidhānānāṃ saṃdarśitāni svayameva ghoṣaṃ cārayāmi / "bhoḥ sattvā asmin pradeśe nidhiḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, nānāratnaparipūrṇastadyathā hiraṇyasuvarṇaḥ yāvaddakaprasādakaṃ / yūyaṃ gṛhṇadhvaṃ / gṛhītvā bhoḥ sattvā daśakuśalān karmapathān samādāya vartadhvaṃ, anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayata, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 383.

children.text: ) śrāvakayānena vā pratyekabuddhayānena vā cittamutpādayatha / gacchatha gṛhṇatha ratnāni yāvadarthaṃ" / tatra ca rūḍhavaḍe jambūdvīpe saptanāgajanmaparivartena saptasaptavarṣakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā nidhayo nirdarśitāśca pradattāśca / evaṃ ca tatrāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāstribhiryānairniveśitā, daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapathesu niveśitā, nānāvidhaiśca ratnaiḥ saṃtarpitā, anuttaradvātriṃśallakṣaṇapratilābhāya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / evaṃ dvitīye dvīpe saptabhirnāgajanmaparivartairevaṃrūpaṃ puruṣakāraṃ kṛtavān / evaṃ tritīye yāvatsarvatra vijitadoṣāyāṃ lokadhātau sarveṣu dvīpeṣu evaṃrūpaḥ puruṣakāraḥ kṛtaḥ / evameva daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamesu śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu, ekaikasmin dvīpe evaṃrūpāḥ saptanāgajanmaparivarteṣu mayā yāvat saptasaptavarṣakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairevamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā nidhayaḥ sattvānāṃ pradattā, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / paśya kulaputra tathāgatasya bodhicārikāṃ, yathā tathāgatastīvreṇa balavīryeṇa dvātriṃśallakṣaṇaparyeṣaṇabodhicaryāṃ cīrṇavān, yathātra pūrve na (
children.translated_text: ) or generate the mind for the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle or the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle. Go, take the jewels as much as you need." And there, in the <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> of <s>Rūḍhavaḍa</s>, through seven <s>nāga</s> birth-cycles, for seven times seven <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of years, immeasurable and incalculable treasures were revealed and given. And thus, there, immeasurable and incalculable beings were established in the three vehicles, established in the ten wholesome courses of action, and satisfied with various jewels; and the aspiration was made to attain the supreme thirty-two marks. Likewise in the second continent, through seven <s>nāga</s> birth-cycles, such heroic endeavor was performed. Likewise in the third, and so on everywhere in the world-realm <s>Vijitadoṣā</s>, in all continents, such heroic endeavor was performed. Likewise in the ten directions, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid [of Buddhas] equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā river, in the five degeneracies — in each and every continent, through seven <s>nāga</s> birth-cycles, for as many as seven times seven <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of years, such immeasurable and incalculable treasures were given to beings, all as previously stated. Behold, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, how the <s>Tathāgata</s> practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct of seeking the thirty-two marks with intense powerful vigor — such that in the past no (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 384.

children.text: ) ye bodhisattvā evaṃrūpāṃ tīvrabalavīryeṇa bodhicārikāṃ cīrṇavantaḥ, na kaścidetarhi, na ca punaḥ kaścit paścādbhaviṣyati bodhisattvo ya evaṃ tīvreṇodyogabalavegenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cārikāṃ caret, sthāpayitvā tānaṣṭau yathā pūrvoktaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) <s>bodhisattvas</s> have practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct with such intense powerful vigor, none do so at present, nor will any <s>bodhisattva</s> in the future practice the conduct toward supreme perfect awakening with such intense force and vigor — except those eight, as previously stated.

body.translated_text: There, having passed away, in the <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> of <s>Rūḍhavaḍa</s>, through my former aspiration I was reborn among the <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) and became a <s>nāga</s> king named <s>Nidhisaṃdarśana</s> (Treasure-Revealer). On the very night I was reborn among the <s>nāgas</s>, that very night <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of treasure hoards were revealed. I myself proclaimed: "O beings! In this place a treasure has appeared, filled with various jewels — namely gold, silver, and so forth up to water-purifying gems. Take them! And, O beings, having taken them, undertake and abide by the ten wholesome courses of action, and generate the mind for supreme perfect awakening (

body.text: tadā cāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ kalpānāmatyayena pratyavarakālasamayenedaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pravāḍodupānirnāma babhūva / śūnye pañcakaṣāye utpale mahākalpe vartamāne 'syāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāmahaṃ śakro 'bhūvan savirocano nāma / apaśyamahamasmin jambūdvīpe sattvānāmakuśalaparyeṣṭicaryāṃ; dṛṣṭvā cāhaṃ paramabhīṣaṇakaṃ yakṣarūpamātmānamabhinirmāyāsmiṃ jambūdvīpe 'vatīrya manuṣyāṇāṃ purataḥ pratyasthāṃ / te ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītā māṃ pṛcchanti / "kena te prayojanaṃ?, vayaṃ te taddāsyāmaḥ" / mayoktaṃ / "āhāreṇa me prayojanaṃ" ta āhuḥ / "kīdṛśasta āhāraḥ?" / mayoktaṃ / "manuṣyān mārayitvā bhakṣayāmi / tāṃścāhaṃ na khādayāmi ye manuṣyā yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātādviratā, yāvan mithyādṛṣṭyāḥ prativiratā, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayanti pratyekabuddhayānena vā śrāvakayānena (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 385.

children.text: ) vā cittānyutpādayanti tānapyahaṃ na khādayāmi" / tatra ca me sattvā nirmitakāḥ paribhūktāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā te sattvā bhayena yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātātprativiratā adattādānādyāvan mithyādṛṣṭeḥ prativiratāḥ / kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ, kaiścit pratyekabuddhayāne kaiścicchrāvakayāne cittamutpāditaṃ / sarve cāturdvīpikāḥ sattvā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu triṣu ca yāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāstatra mayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / "yadi me 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āśā paripūryeta, tadidaṃ me praṇidhānaparipūrṇaṃ bhavet, yathā ca me cāturdvīpikāḥ sattvāḥ kuśale mārge niyojitā / evameva sarvatrāsmiṃ buddhakṣetre sarvacāturdvīpikeṣu sattvāḥ evaṃrūpeṇa bhayena māṃ paśyeyuḥ, daśasu caiva kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, triṣu ca yāneṣu niyojayeyaṃ / evameva samantāddaśasu dikṣu śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvāṃ daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ, triṣu ca yāneṣu niyojayeyaṃ" / evameva me kulaputra āśā praṇidhiśca paripūrṇaḥ sarvatra pravāḍodupānāyāṃ lokadhātau manuṣyā yakṣarūpeṇa vinītāḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / evameva daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu (
children.translated_text: ) — those too I do not eat." There, when the beings saw my emanated forms being consumed, out of fear they abstained for their entire lives from killing, from stealing, and so forth up to from wrong views. Some generated the mind for supreme perfect awakening, some for the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, some for the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle. All the beings of the four-continent world were established in the ten wholesome courses of action and in the three vehicles. There I made this aspiration: "If my wish for supreme perfect awakening is to be fulfilled, then may this aspiration of mine be accomplished — that just as the beings of this four-continent world have been engaged by me on the wholesome path, even so, throughout this entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, in all four-continent [worlds], may beings see me in such a terrifying form, and may I establish them in the ten wholesome courses of action and engage them in the three vehicles. Likewise, in all directions everywhere, in the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid [of Buddhas], in the five degeneracies in the ten directions, may I establish beings in the ten wholesome courses of action and engage them in the three vehicles." And indeed, O son of good family, my wish and aspiration were fulfilled — throughout the world-realm <s>Pravāḍodupānī</s>, humans were tamed by the <s>yakṣa</s> form and [established] in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> devoid [of Buddhas] equal in number to the sands of the Gaṅgā in the ten directions (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 386.

children.text:
) śūnyeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu yakṣarūpeṇa mayā manuṣyāḥ kuśalamārgacaryāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / yathā ca mayā bahavaḥ sattvā bhayāt kuśalacaryāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ; tena karmāvaśeṣeṇa mamaitarhi bodhivṛkṣamūle vajrāsane niṣaṇṇasya bodhimabhisaṃbodhukāmasya māraḥ pāpīyāṃ mahāsainyenopasaṃkrānto bodhau vyākṣepakaraṇārthaṃ / ayaṃ me kulaputra saṃkṣiptena dānapāramitā; bodhicaryāṃ caramāṇasya labdhā cāhaṃ gaṃbhīrāṃ kṣāntiṃ gaṃbhīrāṃ dhāraṇīṃ gaṃbhīrāṃ samādhiṃ pañcalaukikābhijñāḥ pratilabdhāḥ; evaṃrūpaṃ mahāpuruṣakāraṃ kṛtavān / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāḥ pratyekabuddhayāne, evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāḥ śrāvakayāne samādāpitā niveśitāḥ
pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / sthāpayitvā yāvanto mayā bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caramāṇena, buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamā me buddhā (
children.translated_text: ) in the five degeneracies, by me in the form of a <s>yakṣa</s>, humans were established in the conduct of the wholesome path. And because I established many beings in wholesome conduct out of fear, by the residual <s>karma</s> of that deed, now as I sit at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree on the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne) wishing to attain awakening, <s>Māra</s> the evil one approached with his great army for the purpose of causing obstruction to awakening. This, O son of good family, is in brief my <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity). While practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, I attained profound forbearance, profound <s>dhāraṇī</s>, profound <s>samādhi</s>, and the five mundane <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges); such great heroic endeavor I performed. Thus immeasurable and incalculable beings were inspired toward supreme perfect awakening, settled therein, and established therein. Thus immeasurable and incalculable beings were inspired toward the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle; thus immeasurable and incalculable beings were inspired toward the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, settled therein, and established therein. Setting aside those whom I [helped] while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 387.

children.text: ) bhagavantaḥ paryupāsitāḥ, ekaikasya buddhasyāntike sāgarodakabindupramāṇā mayā guṇāḥ parigṛhītāḥ, gaṇanātikrāntānāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ mayā pūja kṛtā, gaṇanātikrāntānāṃ tathāgataśrāvakānāṃ pūjā kṛtā, evaṃ mātāpitṝṇāṃ pañcābhijñānāmṛṣīṇāṃ pūjā kṛtā / mayā ca kṛpayā pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇena svamāṃsarudhireṇa sattvāḥ saṃtarpitā, idānīmapi dharmeṇa saṃtarpitāḥ //
children.translated_text: ) attended upon by me. From each and every <s>Buddha</s>, I acquired qualities as numerous as the drops of water in the ocean. I performed worship of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> beyond reckoning, performed worship of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>śrāvakas</s> beyond reckoning, and likewise worship of mothers and fathers and of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) possessing the five <s>abhijñās</s>. And formerly, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, out of compassion, beings were satisfied by my own flesh and blood; now too they have been satisfied by the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Then, after the passage of incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, at a later time, this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> became known as <s>Pravāḍodupānī</s>. In the <s>Utpala</s> great <s>kalpa</s>, during the time of the five degeneracies when it was devoid [of Buddhas], in this four-continent world-system, I became <s>Śakra</s> (lord of the gods) named <s>Savirocana</s>. I saw the conduct of beings in this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, their pursuit of unwholesome ways. And having seen this, I manifested myself in a supremely terrifying <s>yakṣa</s> (demon) form, descended to this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, and stood before the humans. They, seeing me, were frightened and asked me: "What do you need? We shall give it to you." I said: "I need food." They said: "What kind of food do you eat?" I said: "I kill humans and devour them. But I do not eat those humans who for their entire lives abstain from killing, and so forth up to who abstain from wrong views, who generate the mind for supreme perfect awakening, or who generate minds for the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle or the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle (

body.text: iti śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīke mahāyānasūtre dānaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ // 5 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, entitled "The Chapter on Giving," in the noble <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>. // 5 //

body.text: VI (EPILOGUE) yathāhaṃ kulaputra buddhacakṣuṣā paśyāmi daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ parinirvṛtān, ye mayā prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, ye mayā dānapāramitāyāṃ prathamaṃ samādāpitā yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ samādāpitā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evamevaitarhi pūrvasyāṃ diśi aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāste buddhā bhagavantaḥ pravartitadhārmikadharmacakrāḥ tiṣṭhanto yāpayanto dharmaṃ deśayanto 'drakṣaṃ, ye mayā prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditā niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / evaṃ yāvatṣaṭsu pāramitāṣu vaktavyaṃ, evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottaraheṣṭimopariṣu dikṣu vaktavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: VI (Epilogue). "As I, O son of good family, behold with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, in the ten directions, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> who have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — they whom I first inspired toward supreme perfect awakening, settled therein, and established therein, whom I first inspired in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) and so forth up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), settled therein, and established therein. And likewise now, in the eastern direction, immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who have turned the righteous wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, who abide and teach the <s>Dharma</s> — I have seen them, they whom I first generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening, settled therein, and established therein. Likewise, it should be stated for the six <s>pāramitās</s>; likewise it should be stated for the southern, western, northern, downward, and upward directions.

body.text: paśyāmyahaṃ kulaputra purime digbhāge ito buddhakṣetrādekanavatibuddhakṣetraśatasahasrāṇyatikramya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 389.

children.text: ) saṃpuṣpite lokadhātau vimalatejaguṇarājo nāma tathāgatastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati / mayā sa bhagavān pūrvaṃ prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaḥ samādāpito niveśitaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ; mayā dānapāramitāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ prathamaṃ samādāpitāḥ, peyālaṃ / purimāyāṃ diśi abhiratye buddhakṣetre akṣobhyo nāma tathāgato, jambūnade buddhakṣetre sūryagarbho nāma tathāgataḥ, ratīśvare buddhakṣetre ratīśvaraghoṣajyotirnāma tathāgataḥ, sūryapratiṣṭhite buddhakṣetre jñānabhāskaro nāma tathāgataḥ, jayavaiśraye buddhakṣetre nāganinardito nāma tathāgataḥ, saṃjīvane buddhakṣetre vajrakīrtirnāma tathāgataḥ, svaraje buddhakṣetre vyāghraraśmirnāma tathāgataḥ, aratīye buddhakṣetre sūryagarbho nāma tathāgataḥ, vairaprabhe buddhakṣetre kīrtiśvararājo nāma tathāgataḥ, meruprabhe buddhakṣetre (
children.translated_text: ) in the <s>Saṃpuṣpita</s> ('Flowering') world-realm, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vimalatejaguṇarāja</s> stands, endures, sustains, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. That Blessed One was by me first caused to generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening, encouraged, established, and confirmed; by me he was first encouraged in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) — abbreviated. In the eastern direction, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Abhirati</s>, there is a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Akṣobhya</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Jambūnada</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sūryagarbha</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Ratīśvara</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratīśvaraghoṣajyotis</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Sūryapratiṣṭhita</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānabhāskara</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Jayavaiśraya</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nāganinardita</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Saṃjīvana</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vajrakīrti</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Svaraja</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vyāghraraśmi</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Aratīya</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sūryagarbha</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Vairaprabha</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kīrtiśvararāja</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Meruprabha</s> (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 390.

children.text: ) acintyarājo nāma tathāgataḥ, saṃvare buddhakṣetre jyotiśrīrnāma tathāgataḥ, kusumaprabhe buddhakṣetre prabhāketurnāma tathāgataḥ, kṣamottare buddhakṣetre merusvarasandarśanamerurnāma tathāgataḥ, dharaṇāvatyāṃ buddhakṣetre jñānabimbo nāma tathāgataḥ, kusumavicitre buddhakṣetre vimalanetro nāma tathāgataḥ / etāṃ pūrvaṃgamāṃ kṛtvā kulaputra purimāyāṃ diśyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyān buddhān bhagavatastiṣṭhato yāpayato dharmaṃ deśayato buddhacakṣuṣā paśyāmi / ye 'nutpāditabodhicittāḥ pūrve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitā mayā ca prathamaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ samādāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā, mayā ca prathamaṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ yāpayatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśamupanītā yatra taiḥ sarvaprathamaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabdhaṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau" //
children.translated_text: ) a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Acintyarāja</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Saṃvara</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jyotiśrī</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Kusumaprabha</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prabhāketu</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Kṣamottara</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Merusvarasandarśanameru</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Dharaṇāvatī</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jñānabimba</s>; in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Kusumavicitra</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vimalanetra</s>. Taking these as the first, O son of good family, in the eastern direction, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye I behold immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, standing, sustaining, and teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Those who had not yet generated the mind of awakening were first by me encouraged in supreme perfect awakening and first established by me in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; and by me they were first brought into the presence of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who stand and sustain, where they first obtained their prophecy of supreme perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: "I behold, O son of good family, in the eastern direction, passing beyond ninety-one hundred-thousand <s>buddhakṣetras</s> from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (

body.text: atha tasyāṃ velāyāṃ saṃpuṣpitāyāṃ lokadhātau tasya vimalaguṇatejarājasya tathāgatasyāsanaṃ prakaṃpitaṃ / ye tatra bodhisattvāste tasya vimalaguṇatejarājasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 391.

children.text: ) tathāgatasyāsanaṃ prakaṃpitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tameva tathāgataṃ pṛṣṭavantaḥ / "ko bhadanta bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadi idamadṛṣṭapūrvaṃ bhagavata āsanaṃ prakaṃpitam[?"]iti / sa tathāgatastānavocat - "asti kulaputrāḥ paścime digbhāge ito buddhakṣetrādekonanavatibuddhakṣetrānatikramya tatra sahā nāma lokadhātustatra śākyamunirnāma tathāgatastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati / sa etarhi caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ pūrvayogamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati / tena tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādapitāḥ, yena me prathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpannaṃ; tena tathāgatenāhaṃ prathamaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ samādāpito niveśitaḥ pratiṣṭhāpito yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ; tena tathāgatena pūrvabodhisattvacaryāṃ caratāhaṃ prathamaṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ yāpayatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśamupanīto, yatra me prathamaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabdhamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / sa ca me śākyamunistathāgataḥ kalyāṇamitraḥ sahe lokadhātau tiṣṭhati yāpayati, sa evaṃ caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ imaṃ pūrvayogamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati / tena tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena mamāsanaṃ kaṃpate / ko yuṣmākaṃ kulaputrotsahate (
children.translated_text: ) having seen the seat of that <s>Tathāgata</s> tremble, asked that very <s>Tathāgata</s>: "What, O Venerable Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that the Blessed One's seat, never before seen [to do so], has trembled?" That <s>Tathāgata</s> said to them: "There is, O sons of good family, in the western direction from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, having passed beyond eighty-nine <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, a world-realm there named <s>Sahā</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> stands, endures, and sustains. He is now, for the four assemblies, the former practice
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 392.

children.text: ) madvacanāt sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gantuṃ śākyamunestathāgatasyārogyakauśalyaṃ paripṛcchanāya?" / tataste bodhisattvā vimalaguṇatejarājānaṃ tathāgatamāhur[ / "]ya iha bhadanta bhagavan saṃpuṣpite buddhakṣetre ṛddhimantaḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇapāramitāprāptāste 'dya pūrvāhnasamaye mahāntamavabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvānyasmādbuddhakṣetrādvikurvyābhyāgatastenāyaṃ muhūrtaṃ pṛthivīcālaḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiśca" / te ca bodhisattvā āhuḥ / "vayamapi bhadanta bhagavan gamiṣyāmastaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ taṃ śākyamuniṃ vandanāya paryupasanāya taṃ ca sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śravaṇāya" /
children.translated_text: ) by my word, will go to the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> to inquire about the health and well-being of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>?" Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s>: "Those who here, O Venerable Blessed One, in the <s>Saṃpuṣpita</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> are possessed of supernatural power and have attained the perfection of all <s>bodhisattva</s>-qualities — they today, in the forenoon, having seen a great radiance, arrived from another <s>buddhakṣetra</s> by their supernatural transformation, and because of that there was this momentary earthquake and shower of flowers." Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>

body.translated_text: Then at that moment, in the <s>Saṃpuṣpita</s> world-realm, the seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> trembled. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> there, of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> (

body.text: te bahubodhisattvaśatasahasrāḥ svenarddhyanubhāvena tato buddhakṣetrātsaṃprasthitāḥ / te nāvagacchanti kva gantavyaṃ / te 'pyāhuḥ / "tāmapi vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan diśaṃ na jānīmo yatra sahā lokadhātuḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ" / tataḥ sa vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgato bāhuṃ prasārya pañcabhyo 'ṅgulibhyo vividhānyarciṃṣi pramumoca / tatastārciṣa ekonanavatibuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇyavabhāsitavān, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 393.

children.text: ) yāvaccemaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetramavabhāsitavān / yataste bodhisattvāḥ paśyanti sarvāvadimaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭaṃ bodhisattvairgaganatale ca devanāgayakṣāsuraiḥ sphuṭaṃ / dṛṣṭvā ca punaste bodhisattvāstaṃ vimalaguṇatejarājānaṃ tathāgatamevamāhuḥ / "paśyāmo vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarvāvantaṃ sphuṭaṃ, nāsti tatrāvakāśo 'ntaśo daṇḍanikṣepaṇamātramapi yanna sphuṭaṃ bodhisattvaiḥ / paśyāmaḥ śākyamunistathāgato 'smān nirīkṣate dharmaṃ ca deśayati" / sa ca vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgatasteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmevamāha - "samantacakṣuḥ kulaputrāḥ śākyamunistathāgato / ye kecit kulaputrāḥ sahe lokadhātau sattvā bhūmisthitā vā antarīkṣasthitā vā tataścaikaikaḥ sattva evaṃ saṃjānāti, "maṃ śākyamunistathāgataḥ sarvacetasā nirīkṣate mamaikamārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati" / sarvavarṇaṃśca sa kulaputra śākyamunistathāgato dharmaṃ deśayati ekavarṇasthānaṃ / (
children.translated_text: ) up to illuminating this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. Whereupon those <s>bodhisattvas</s> saw this entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and the surface of the sky filled with <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>asuras</s>. Having seen this, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s>: "We see, O Venerable Blessed One, the entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> completely filled — there is not even space there, not even so much as a staff-throw, that is not filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 394.

children.text: ) ye ca tatra kulaputra sattvā brāhmabhaktāste śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ brahmāṇaṃ samanupaśyanti, mahābrahmapativyāhāreṇa dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti; yāvad ye mārabhaktikā, ye sūryabhaktikā, ye candrabhaktikā, ye vaiśravaṇabhaktikā, ye virūḍhakabhaktikā, ye virūpākṣabhaktikā, ye dhṛtarāṣṭrabhaktikā, ye maheśvarabhaktikāste sattvā maheśvararūpavarṇasaṃsthānavacanavyāhāreṇa śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ paśyanti dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvanti / yāvaccaturaśītistatra sattvānāṃ varṇasaṃsthānabhaktirūpavyāhārasahasrāṇi te tathā caiva śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ paśyanti dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvanti" /
children.translated_text: ) And, O son of good family, whatever beings there are devoted to <s>Brahmā</s>, they see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> as <s>Brahmā</s> and hear the <s>Dharma</s> through the discourse of <s>Mahābrahmapati</s>; and so on — those devoted to <s>Māra</s>, those devoted to the Sun, those devoted to the Moon, those devoted to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, those devoted to <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, those devoted to <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, those devoted to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, those devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s> — those beings see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> in the form, appearance, shape, and speech of <s>Maheśvara</s>, and hear the <s>Dharma</s>

body.translated_text: Those many hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by their own supernatural power, set forth from that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. They did not know where to go. They too said: "We also, O Venerable Blessed One, do not know that direction where the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, is located." Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s>, extending his arm, from his five fingers released various rays. Those rays illuminated eighty-nine thousand <s>buddhakṣetras</s>

body.text: tasyāṃ ca parṣadi rahagarjito nāma bodhisattvo dvitīyaśca jyotiraśmirnāma bodhisattvaḥ / atha vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgatastān bodhisattvān āmantrayati sma / "gacchatha yūyaṃ kulaputrāḥ sahe lokadhātau śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ madvacanādārogyakauśalyaṃ sukhasparśavihāratāṃ paripṛcchatha" / te bodhisattvā āhuḥ / "sarvāvantaṃ bhadanta bhagavan sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sakṣitigaganaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 395.

children.text: ) bodhisattvaiḥ sphuṭaṃ samanupaśyāmaḥ / na cātraikasattvasyāpyavakāśo 'sti kṣitau gagane vā yatra vayaṃ pratitiṣṭhemaḥ" / sa ca vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgata āha - "mā kulaputrā evaṃ vadatha, "nāsti sahe buddhakṣetre 'vakāśaḥ" / vistīrṇāvakāśaḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato 'cintyairbuddhaguṇaiḥ, pūrvapraṇidhānena vistīrṇā tathāgatasya kṛpāśāsanāvatārapraveśā, triśaraṇagamanaṃ, triyānadharmadeśanāmārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati, trividhaṃ ca śikṣāsaṃvaraṃ deśayati, trīṇi ca vimokṣadvārāṇyupadarśayati, tribhyo 'pāyebhyaḥ sattvānuddharati, tisṛṣu ca śiveṣu patheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati /
children.translated_text: ) we see filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s>. There is not even space for a single being, on the ground or in the sky, where we might stand." The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> said: "Do not speak thus, O sons of good family: 'There is no space in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.' Spacious is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> with his inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-qualities; spacious, by his former vow, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s compassionate entry into teaching — from the threefold refuge, beginning with the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of the three vehicles

body.translated_text: In that assembly, there was a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Rahagarjita</s> and a second <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Jyotiraśmi</s>. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> addressed those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: "Go, O sons of good family, to the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm and inquire of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, with my words, about his health, well-being, and comfortable abiding." Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said: "O Venerable Blessed One, the entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, both earth and sky (

body.text: ekasmiṃ samaye kulaputra śākyamunistathāgato 'cirābhisaṃbuddho vaineyasattvāvekṣayā madhye śailaparvate indrākṣasya yakṣasya bhavane sālaguhāyāṃ viharati, saptāhamekaparyaṅkenātināmayati, vimuktiprītisukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayati / sarvāvatī ca sā sālaguhā tathāgatakāyena sphuṭā, nāsti tatrāvakāśo 'ntaśaścaturaṅgulapramāṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 396.

children.text: ) yattathāgatakāyena na sphuṭaṃ / tasya ca saptāhasyātyayena daśabhir diśābhirdvādaśanayutā bodhisattvānāṃ tatra sahe lokadhātau yastasya parvatasyābhimukhaṃ sthitvā śākyamunestathāgatasya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya / sa ca kulaputra śākyamunistathāgatastatra parśadi ridhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskṛtavān; sā ca sālaguhā evaṃ vistīrṇā caivaṃ vipulā ca prādurbhūtā, yadā te dvādaśanayutā bodhisattvānāṃ tatra sālaguhāyāṃ praviṣṭā vistīrṇāvakāśaṃ paśyanti sma / ekaikaśca bodhisattvastatra tathāgatasya vividhabodhisattvavikurvaṇena pūjāṃ kṛtvā, ekaiko bodhisattvastatra saptaratnamayāsanaṃ nirmitavān yatropaviṣṭā dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti sma / evaṃ vistīrṇāvakāśaḥ kulaputra sa śākyamunistathāgataḥ / te ca bodhisattvāstasya śākyamunestathāgatasya sakāśāddharmaṃ śrutvā śākyamunestathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu saṃprasthitāḥ / aciraprakāntānāṃ ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sālaguhā yathā paurvāṇāṃ saṃsthitā /
children.translated_text: ) that was not filled by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body. And after the passage of those seven days, from the ten directions twelve <s>nayutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm stood facing that mountain to worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, to attend upon him, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> performed a supernatural transformation in that assembly; and that <s>Sāla</s>-cave appeared so extensive and so vast that when those twelve <s>nayutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>

body.translated_text: At one time, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, recently awakened, surveying beings to be trained, dwelt in the <s>Sāla</s>-cave in the abode of the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Indrākṣa</s> on <s>Śailaparvata</s> ('Rock Mountain'), spending seven days sitting cross-legged without moving, experiencing the bliss of the joy of liberation. And that entire <s>Sāla</s>-cave was filled by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body; there was not even space, not even four finger-breadths (

body.text: tatra caturdvīpikāyāṃ kauśiko nāma śakra āyuḥparīkṣīṇastiryagyonyupapattibhayabhītaḥ, sa caturaśītibhistrayastriṃśaddevasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ yena sālaguhā yena ca bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmati / upasaṃkramya sāmantake indrākṣasya sālaguhābhavane sthitaḥ, tasya bhagavato 'nubhāvena etadabhavat / "yannūnaṃ vayaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ gandharvaputramadhyeṣemaḥ / sa ca pañcaśikho madhureṇa svareṇa bhagavantamabhimukhaṃ staviṣyati, tadā bhagavān dhyānasamādhibhyo vyutthāsyati" / tataḥ śakraḥ pañcaśikhaṃ gandharvaputramadhīṣṭhavān / atha pañcaśikho vīṇāṃ manojñena gītavāditena bhagavato 'nubhāvena pañcabhiḥ stavaśatairbhagavato varṇamabhāṣata / yadā ca kulaputra pañcaśikha ārabdho bhagavato 'bhistavanāya tataḥ sa śākyamunirbhagavān sughoṣavairocanaketuṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannastena samādhinā ye sahe lokadhātau maharddhikayakṣarākṣasā vāsurā vā garuḍā vā kinnarā vā mahoragā vā gandharvā vā sarve kāmāvacarā devā sarve rūpāvacarā devaputrāstatra sannipātā babhūvurye ca svarabhaktikāste svaraṃ śrutvā prasīdanti, ye varṇayaśobhaktikāste bhagavato varṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 398.

children.text: ) śrutvā tasya bhagavataḥ sakāśe tīvrapremaprasādagurugauravacitrīkārajātāḥ prasīdanti, ye veṇuvādyabhaktikāste veṇuvādyaṃ śrutvā prasīdanti / tataḥ śākyamunirbhagavāṃstataḥ samādhervyutthāya sālaguhāyā dvāraṃ darśāpayāmāsa / śakraścopasaṃkrānto bhagavantaṃ pṛṣṭavān / "bhagavaṃ kutropaviśāmaḥ?" / sa śākyamunistathāgata uvāca - "niṣīdadhvaṃ yakṣā yāvattasthuḥ samāgatāḥ" / tataḥ sālaguhā evaṃ vistīrṇā saṃsthitā yathā dvādaśagaṅgānadīvālikāsamā yakṣāstatra guhāyāṃ praviṣṭā, niṣaṇṇāyāśca tasyāḥ parṣadaḥ sa śākyamunistathāgatastathārūpāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavāṃ; yathā ye tasmin parṣadi śrāvakayānikā niṣaṇṇāste śrāvakayānakathāṃ śṛṇvanti, navanavatikoṭyastatra śrotāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ; ye ca tatra parṣadi anuttarasamyaksaṃbuddhayānikāste śuddhāṃ mahāyānakathāṃ śṛṇvanti; tatra ca pañcaśikhagandharvapūrvaṃgamā aṣṭādaśanayutā avaivartikāḥ saṃsthitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; yaiśca tatrānutpāditaṃ triṣu yāneṣu cittaṃ, tatra kaścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau (
children.translated_text: ) having heard, in the presence of that Blessed One, those filled with intense love, faith, respect, reverence, and wonder became serene; and those devoted to the playing of bamboo flutes, hearing the bamboo music, became serene. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, rising from that <s>samādhi</s>, revealed the door of the <s>Sāla</s> cave. And <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) approached and asked the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, where shall we sit?" The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> said: "Be seated, <s>Yakṣas</s>, as many as have come together." Then the <s>Sāla</s> cave became so vast that <s>yakṣas</s> as numerous as the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers entered that cave. And when that assembly was seated—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 399.

children.text: ) cittamutpāditaṃ, keścittatra pratyekabuddhayāne cittamutpāditaṃ, kaścicchrāvakayāne cittamutpāditaṃ; sa ca tatra kauśikaḥ śakro bhayātparimukto, varṣasahasraṃ cāyurvivṛddhaṃ, avaivartikaścānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau babhūva / tadevaṃ vistīrṇāvakāśaḥ kulaputra sa śākyamunistathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: ) some generated the mind for the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, some generated the mind for the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle; and <s>Śakra</s> <s>Kauśika</s> was freed from fear, and his lifespan was increased by a thousand years, and he became irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in supreme perfect enlightenment. Thus vast in scope, O son of good family, is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.translated_text: There, in the four-continent [world], <s>Śakra</s> named <s>Kauśika</s>, whose lifespan was exhausted, fearing rebirth in the animal realm, together with eighty-four thousand <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> <s>devas</s>, approached the <s>Sāla</s>-cave where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he stood nearby at the abode of <s>Indrākṣa</s>'s <s>Sāla</s>-cave. By the power of the Blessed One, he had this thought: "Let us request <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the son of the <s>gandharvas</s>. And <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, with a sweet voice, facing the Blessed One

body.text: evaṃ vistīrṇaṃ cāsya tathāgatasya svaramaṇḍalaṃ / na śakyaṃ kenacittasya tathāgatasya svaramaṇḍalasya paryantamudgṛhītuṃ vā gaṇāyituṃ vā / vistīrṇaṃ tasya tathāgatasyopāyakauśalyaṃ sattvaparipākaśca: na śakyaṃ tasya tathāgatasyopāyakauśalyaṃ paryantamudgṛhītuṃ / vistīrṇakāyaśca kulaputra tathāgato; na śākyaṃ kenacittasya mūrdhānamavalokayituṃ, kāyasya vā paryantamadhigantuṃ / yāvantaśca sattvā etarhi tatra sahe buddhakṣetre sannipatitā yadi te sattvāḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya kukṣau praviśeyuste sarve tatra vicareyuste ca sattvāstasya tathāgatasyaikaromamukhe praviśeyuḥ niṣkrameyuśca; te ekaromamukhāttasya tathāgatasya na śaktāḥ paryantamudgṛhītuṃ ūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vāntaśo (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 400.

children.text: ) divyenāpi cakṣuṣā / tadevaṃ vistīrṇakāyaḥ sa śākyamunistathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: ) even with the divine eye. Thus vast in body is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.translated_text: And thus vast is this <s>Tathāgata's</s> sphere of voice (<s>svaramaṇḍala</s>). No one is able to grasp or reckon the extent of this <s>Tathāgata's</s> sphere of voice. Vast is this <s>Tathāgata's</s> skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) and the ripening of beings (<s>sattvaparipāka</s>): no one is able to grasp the extent of this <s>Tathāgata's</s> skill in means. And vast in body, O son of good family, is this <s>Tathāgata</s>: no one is able to behold the crown of his head, or to reach the extent of his body. And all the beings presently gathered in this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>—if those beings were to enter the belly of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, they—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kulaputra vistīrṇabuddhakṣetraḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato / yāvantaśca daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikasamā buddhakṣetrā evaṃ paripūrṇā bhaveyuḥ sattvaistadyathāpi nāmaitarhi sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sarve te sattvā etarhi sahe buddhakṣetre viśeyuḥ sarve te tatra vicareyuḥ / tatkasmāddhetos[? / ] tathaiva tasya tathāgatasya pūrvaṃ prathamacittotpādenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ babhūva / tiṣṭhatu kulaputraikaṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavaḥ, sacetkulaputra yāvaddaśasu dikṣu sahasraṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhakṣetrā evaṃ vistīrṇāḥ tadyathaitarhi sahabuddhakṣetraṃ paripūrṇaṃ sattvaiḥ te sarve etarhi sahe lokadhātau praviśeyuste sarve tatra vicareyurevaṃrūpaṃ tasya tathāgatasya pūrvaṃ prathamacittotpāditānuttarajñānapratilābhāya praṇidhānaṃ babhūva / evaṃ vistīrṇabuddhakṣetraḥ sa kulaputra śākyamunistathāgataḥ / ebhiścaturdharmairviśiṣṭataraḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato yathāvadgṛhṇīta (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 401.

children.text: ) yūyaṃ kulaputrā imāṃ candrarocavimalāṃ puṣpāṃ, gacchatha paścimāṃ diśaṃ yathā svayaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ, mama vacanena taṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ ārogyakauśalyaṃ pṛcchata" /
children.translated_text: ) "You, O sons of good family, [take] these <s>Candrarocavimalā</s> flowers, go to the western direction, see the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> for yourselves, and on my behalf, inquire of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> about his health and well-being."

body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, vast in <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. If all the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were so filled with beings, just as this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is now, all those beings would enter into this present <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and all would move about freely there. Why is that? Because thus was that <s>Tathāgata's</s> aspiration from the very first generation of the mind for supreme perfect enlightenment. Let alone, O son of good family, world-realms as numerous as the sands of one <s>Gaṅgā</s> river—even if, O son of good family, in the ten directions a thousand—

body.text: sa ca vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgataścandrarocavimalāṃ puṣpāṃ gṛhītvā raharājasya bodhisattvasya jyotiraśmeśca bodhisattvasya datvāha - "gacchata kulaputrau mamarddhibalādhānena sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ" / tatra ca viṃśatiḥ prāṇisahasrāṇyāhur[ / "]vayamapi bhadanta bhagavan gacchemaḥ tathāgatānubhāvena sahaṃ lokadhātuṃ tasya śākyamunestathāgatasya darśanāye vandanāya paryupāsanāya" / vimalaguṇatejarājastathāgata āha - "gacchata kulaputrā yathābhiprāyāḥ" / tau ca dvau bodhisattvau raharājaśca jyotiraśmiśca sārdhaṃ viṃśatibhirbodhisattvasahasraistasya vimalaguṇatejarājasya tathāgatasya riddhibalena tataḥ saṃpuṣpitāyā lokadhātoḥ saṃprasthitā ekacittakṣaṇenedaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetramanuprāptā gṛdhrakūṭe parvate pratyasthātaḥ / te yena bhagavāṃ śākyamunistathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamyāhuḥ / "asti bhagavan (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 402.

children.text: ) purastime digbhāge ekonanavatibuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇyatikramya tatra saṃpuṣpito nāma lokadhātuḥ, tatra vimalaguṇatejarājo nāma tathāgataḥ / sa ca punastathāgato bodhisattvagaṇaparivārastathāgatasya guṇavarṇakīrtayamāna evamāha - "śākyamunirnāma tathāgataḥ sahe buddhakṣetre tiṣṭhati yāpayati / tena ca tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtena bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇenāhaṃ sarvaprathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpito niveśitaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitastasya ca vacanena mayānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ tena tathāgatenāhaṃ prathamaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ niveśito, yāvatpūrvoktaṃ / evamebhiścaturbhirdharmairviśiṣṭataraḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato / yathā teneme candrarocavimalā puṣpāḥ preṣitā ārogyakauśalyaṃ ca pṛcchati" /
children.translated_text: ) in the eastern direction, having passed beyond ninety-one thousand <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, there was a world-realm called <s>Saṃpuṣpita</s> (Fully Blossomed), where a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> [presided]. And that <s>Tathāgata</s>, surrounded by his assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, praising the qualities and virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [<s>Śākyamuni</s>], spoke thus: "A <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> presides and dwells in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. That <s>Tathāgata</s>, formerly as a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, was the very first to inspire, establish, and settle me in supreme perfect enlightenment, and by his word I made my aspiration for supreme perfect enlightenment—

body.translated_text: And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s>, taking the <s>Candrarocavimalā</s> flowers, gave them to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Raharāja</s> and the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Jyotiraśmi</s>, and said: "Go, O sons of good family, to the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm by the power of my supernatural ability." And there twenty thousand beings said: "We too, O venerable Blessed One, would go, by the <s>Tathāgata's</s> power, to the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, for the purpose of seeing, venerating, attending upon, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>." The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaguṇatejarāja</s> said: "Go, O sons of good family, as you wish." And those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Raharāja</s> and <s>Jyotiraśmi</s>—

body.text: evamabhiratyā buddhakṣetrādakṣobhyasya tathāgatasyāsanaṃ kaṃpati / ye ca tatra bodhisattvāḥ sannipattitaste cāpi dṛṣṭvākṣobhyasya tathāgatasyāsanaṃ kaṃpitaṃ paripṛcchanti sma / peyālaṃ yathā pūrvoktaṃ / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 403.

children.text: ) sarveṣāṃ evaṃ vaktavyaṃ / tena ca samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ purimāyāṃ diśi tathāgatadūtā bodhisattvā imaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sahacandrarocavimalaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃprāptāḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya paripṛcchanāya pūjanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca /
children.translated_text: ) All should be described in the same way. And at that time, immeasurable and countless <s>Tath��gata</s>-messengers, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, from the eastern direction, arrived at this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> together with <s>Candrarocavimalā</s> flowers, for the purpose of inquiring after, worshipping, venerating, attending upon, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.translated_text: Likewise, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Abhirati</s> of <s>Akṣobhya</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the seat trembled. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had gathered there, having seen the seat of <s>Akṣobhya</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> trembling, inquired. [The passage is abbreviated:] as previously described.

body.text: samanantaraparivāsito bhagavataḥ purimāyāṃ diśi buddhakṣetranāma parikīrtanaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ, dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ punarbhagavānārabdhaḥ parikīrtayituṃ / "paśyāmyahaṃ kulaputra dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrādekagaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya tatra sarvaśokāpagato nāma lokadhātustatrāśokaśrīrnāma tathāgatastiṣṭhati dhriyati yāpayati / mayā sa bhagavān sarvaprathamaṃ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpito, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / jaṃbūprabhe buddhakṣetre dharmeśvaravinardirnāma tathāgataḥ, merupratiṣṭhite buddhakṣetre gatīśvarasālendro (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 404.

children.text: ) nāma tathāgataḥ, guṇendraniryūhe buddhakṣetre siṃhavijṛmbhitarājā nāma tathāgataḥ, maṇimūlavyūhe buddhakṣetre nārāyaṇavijitagarbho nāma tathāgataḥ, muktāprabhasaṃcaye buddhakṣetre ratnaguṇavijṛmbhitasaṃcayo nāma tathāgataḥ, devasome buddhakṣetre jyotigarbho nāma tathāgataḥ, candanamūle buddhakṣetre nakṣatravidhānakīrtirnāma tathāgataḥ, viśiṣṭagandhe buddhakṣetre puṇyabalasālarājā nāma tathāgataḥ, suvidite buddhakṣetre manojñaghoṣasvaravinardito nāma tathāgataḥ, duraṇye buddhakṣetre sālajayabindurājā nāma tathāgataḥ, nardaścoce buddhakṣetre tejeśvaraprabhāso nāma tathāgataḥ, abhigarjite buddhakṣetre sumanojñasvaranirghoṣe nāma tathāgataḥ, ratnavisabhe buddhakṣetre ratnatalanāgendro nāma tathāgataḥ, palāmaratnavṛkṣaratne (
children.translated_text: ) a <s>Tathāgata</s> named [—], in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Guṇendraniryūha</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhitarāja</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Maṇimūlavyūha</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nārāyaṇavijitagarbha</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Muktāprabhasaṃcaya</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaguṇavijṛmbhitasaṃcaya</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Devasoma</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jyotigarbha</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Candanamūla</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nakṣatravidhānakīrti</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Viśiṣṭagandha</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Puṇyabalasālarāja</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Suvidita</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Manojñaghoṣasvaravinardita</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> <s>Duraṇya</s> a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sālajayabin</s>—
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 405.

children.text: ) buddhakṣetre dharmameghanirghoṣeśvarasaumyo nāma tathāgataḥ, peyālaṃ yathā pūrvoktaṃ / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyāsanāni kaṃpanti / sarve te buddhā bhagantaḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya varṇaṃ yaśaḥ kīrtimudīrayanti / yāvattena samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi tathāgatadūtā bodhisattvāḥ sahacandrarocavimalaiḥ puṣpairimaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetramanuprāptāḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya pṛcchanāya yāvaddharmaśravaṇāya" /
children.translated_text: ) in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> [—] a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmameghanirghoṣeśvarasaumya</s>. [The passage is abbreviated:] as previously described. Thus for immeasurable and countless <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in the southern direction, their seats tremble. All those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, extol the praise, renown, and glory of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And at that time, immeasurable and countless <s>Tathāgata</s>-messengers, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, from the southern direction, arrived at this <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s> together with <s>Candrarocavimalā</s> flowers, for the purpose of inquiring after [<s>Śākyamuni</s>] and hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Immediately after the Blessed One had finished proclaiming the names of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> and <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in the eastern direction, the Blessed One began to proclaim those in the southern direction: "I see, O son of good family, from a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in the southern direction, having passed beyond <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of one <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, there is a world-realm called <s>Sarvaśokāpagata</s> (Free from All Sorrow), where a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Aśokaśrī</s> (Glorious Sorrowless) presides, dwells, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. That Blessed One was the very first to be inspired by me, formerly as a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, in supreme perfect enlightenment—and so forth as previously described. In the <s>Jambūprabha</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>—

body.text: punaśca bhagavān āha - "paśyāmyahaṃ kulaputra paścimāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrāt saptānavatibuddhakṣetranayutaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya tatropaśāntamatirnāma buddhakṣetrastatra ratnagirirnāma tathāgataḥ tiṣṭhati dhriyati yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati / mayā sa bhagavān pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtena bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇena sarvaprathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpito, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 406.

children.text: ) yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / buddhakṣetrāṇāṃ peyālaṃ, vararaśmikośo nāma tathāgataḥ, svarajñakośo nāma tathāgataḥ, haritālakīrtiḥ, samantagarbhaḥ, brahmakusumaḥ, karadharavikramaḥ, dharmaveśapradīpaḥ, asamantaramerusvaravighuṣṭarājaḥ, brahmendraghoṣaḥ, yathā pūrvoktaṃ / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ paścimāyāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yeṣāṃ śākyamuninā tathāgatena nāmāni parikīrtitāni teṣāmāsanāni kaṃpanti / yāvattena samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ paścimāyāṃ diśi buddhadūtā bodhisattvāḥ sahacandrarocavimalaiḥ puṣpairimaṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetramanuprāptā yāvanniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya / peyālaṃ, evamuttarā digvaktavyā, evamuparimāyāmevamadhaḥ, evaṃ pūrvadakṣiṇā, evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimā, evaṃ paścimottarā, evamuttarapūrvā" /
children.translated_text: ) and so forth as previously described. The <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are abbreviated: <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vararaśmikośa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Svarajñakośa</s>, <s>Haritālakīrti</s>, <s>Samantagarbha</s>, <s>Brahmakusuma</s>, <s>Karadharavikrama</s>, <s>Dharmaveśapradīpa</s>, <s>Asamantaramerusvaravighuṣṭarāja</s>, <s>Brahmendraghoṣa</s>—as previously described. Thus for immeasurable and countless <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in the western direction, whose names were proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, their seats tremble. And at that time, immeasurable and countless <s>Buddha</s>-messengers, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, from the western direction, together with <s>Candrarocavimalā</s> flowers—

body.translated_text: And again the Blessed One said: "I see, O son of good family, from a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in the western direction, having passed beyond ninety-seven <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, there is a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> called <s>Upaśāntamati</s> (Pacified Mind), where a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnagiri</s> (Jewel Mountain) presides, dwells, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. That Blessed One was the very first to be inspired by me, formerly as a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, in supreme perfect enlightenment—

body.text: punaḥ śākyamunirbhagavānāha - "paśyāmyahaṃ kulaputrottarapūrvāyāṃ diśīto buddhakṣetrādaṣṭānavatibuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 407.

children.text: ) tatra vijayaṃ nāma buddhakṣetraṃ, vigatasaṃtāpobhavavaiśravaṇasālarājo nāma tathāgataḥ / mayā sa tathāgataḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtena bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇena sarvaprathamamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpito, yāvatṣaṭsu pāramitāsu; yāvanmayā sarvaprathamaṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ yāpayatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśamupanīto, yatra tena vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabdhamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; yadā nāma parikīrtitaṃ tadāsanaṃ kaṃpitāṃ; yāvaccaturaśītisattvānāṃ varṇabhaktisaṃsthānarūpavyāhārasahasrāṇi tathā śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ paśyanti dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvanti /
children.translated_text: ) there is a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> called <s>Vijaya</s> (Victory), where a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarāja</s> [presides]. That <s>Tathāgata</s> was the very first to be inspired by me, formerly as a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, in supreme perfect enlightenment, and [settled] in the six <s>pāramitās</s>; and I was the very first to bring him into the presence of the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who presided and dwelt [at that time], where he obtained the prophecy for supreme perfect enlightenment. When his name was proclaimed, his seat trembled. And eighty-four thousand varieties of beings' complexion, devotion, form, appearance, and utterance—likewise—

body.translated_text: And again the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> said: "I see, O son of good family, from a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in the northeastern direction, having passed beyond ninety-eight <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>—

body.text: tatra ca parṣadi dvau bodhisattvau, ekaḥ vigopaśikharo nāma dvitīyaḥ saṃrocanabuddho nāma; sa ca vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarājo nāma tathāgatastau dvau bodhisattvavāmantrayitvaivamāha - "gacchata yūyaṃ kulaputrau sahe buddhakṣetre, madvacanācchākyamunestathāgatasyārogyakaśalyaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 408.

children.text: ) sukhasparśavihāratāṃ paripṛcchata" / tāvāhatuḥ / "sarvāvantaṃ bhadanta bhagavannāvāṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sakṣitigaganaṃ samanupaśyāmaḥ / na ca tatraikasattvasyāpyavakāśo 'sti kṣitau vā gagane vā yatrāvāṃ pratiṣṭhevahi" / sa ca tathāgata āha - "mā kulaputraivaṃ vadata, "nāsti sahe buddhakṣetre 'vakāśaḥ" / tatkasmāddhetor[? / ]vistīrṇāvakāśaḥ kulaputrau sa śākyamunistathāgato 'cintyairbuddhaguṇaiḥ, pūrvapraṇidhānena vistīrṇā tasya tathāgatasya kṛpāśāsanāvatārapraveśā, triśaraṇagamanaṃ, tribhiryānairdharmaṃ deśayati, trividhaṃ śikṣāsaṃvaraṃ deśayati, trīṇi vimokṣadvārāṇi prakāśayati, tribhyaścāpāyebhyaḥ sattvānuddharati, triṣu ca śivapatheṣu sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayati /
children.translated_text: ) ask about the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s well-being and his abiding in pleasant contact." Those two said: "O venerable Blessed One, we see the entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field together with its ground and sky, and there is not even space for a single being, whether on the ground or in the sky, where we two might stand." That <s>Tathāgata</s> said: "Do not speak thus, O sons of good family, saying 'there is no space in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field.' Why not? The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, O sons of good family, is of vast scope through inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. By his former aspiration, vast is the entry into his teaching of compassion — the taking of the three refuges, the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> by means of the three vehicles, the teaching of the threefold training and discipline, the illumination of the three gates of liberation, the lifting of beings out of the three lower realms, and the establishing of beings on the three auspicious paths.

body.translated_text: And in that assembly were two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, one named <s>Vigopaśikhara</s> and the second named <s>Saṃrocanabuddha</s>. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarāja</s>, having addressed those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, spoke thus: "Go, O sons of good family, to the <s>Sahā</s> <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and on my behalf, inquire of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> about his health and well-being—

body.text: ekasmin samaye kulaputra sa śākyamunistathāgato 'cirābhisaṃbuddho vaineyasattvāvekṣayā viṣamaśailendraparvatamadhye indrākṣasya yakṣasya bhavane sālaguhāyāṃ viharati sma, saptāhamekaparyaṅkenātināmayati sma, vimuktiprītisukhasaṃvedī / sarvāvatī ca sā sālaguhā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 409.

children.text: ) sphuṭā tathāgatakāyena, nāsti tatrāvakāśo 'ntaśaścaturaṅgulapramāṇaṃ yanna tathāgatakāyena sphuṭaṃ / tasya ca saptāhasyātyayena daśabhyo digbhyaḥ dvādaśanayutā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sahe lokadhātau saṃprāptāstasya śākyamunestathāgatasya vandanāya / yāvadimaiścaturbhirdharmairviśiṣṭataraḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato yathānye tathāgatā /
children.translated_text: ) was filled with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body — there was no space there, not even the measure of four finger-breadths, that was not filled by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body. And after the passage of those seven days, twelve <s>nayutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> from the ten directions arrived in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm to venerate the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. By these four qualities is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> more distinguished than other <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.translated_text: At one time, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, having recently attained awakening, surveying the beings to be trained, was dwelling in the <s>Sāla</s> Cave in the abode of the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Indrākṣa</s> on the <s>Viṣama</s> (Rugged) <s>Śailendra</s> mountain, passing seven days in a single cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of the joy of liberation. And that entire <s>Sāla</s> Cave (

body.text: gṛhṇīdhvaṃ yūyaṃ kulaputrā imāṃ candrarocavimalāṃ puṣpāṃ; gṛhītvā gacchata dakṣiṇapaścimāṃ diśaṃ, yathā svayaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ; mama vacanāttasya śākyamunestathāgatasyārogyakauśalyaṃ pṛcchata" / sa ca vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarājastathāgataḥ candrarocavimalān puṣpāṃ gṛhītvā vigopaśikharasya bodhisattvasya dadāti saṃrocanabuddhasya ca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya, evaṃ cāha - "gacchata kulaputrau mamarddhibalādhānena sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ" / tatra viṃśatiprāṇasahasrāṇyāhuḥ / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 410.

children.text: ) "vayamapi bhagavan gamiṣyāmastathāgatasyānubhāvena sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya" / tathāgata āha - "gacchata kulaputrā yathābhiprāyāḥ" / tatastau dvau bodhisattvau sārdhaṃ viṃśatibhirbodhisattvasahasraistasya tathāgatasya riddhyanubhāvena tato virajādbuddhakṣetrātsaṃprasthitāḥ, ekakṣaṇeneha buddhakṣetre 'nuprāptā gṛdhrakūṭe parvate pratyasthuḥ / ekāntasthitāśca yena śākyamunistathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamyāhuḥ / "asti bhadanta bhagavannuttarapūrvāyāṃ diśi, yathā pūrvoktaṃ / tena tathāgateneme candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpāḥ preṣitā, bhagavataścārogyakauśalyaṃ pṛcchati" / evaṃ mārabhavanavidhvaṃsanasya tathāgatasyāsanaṃ kaṃpitaṃ / ye ca tatra bodhisattvāḥ sannipatitāste cāpi dṛṣṭvā taṃ mārabhavanavidhvaṃsanaṃ tathāgatasyāsanaṃ kaṃpitaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchanti, yāvadyathā pūrvoktaṃ / evaṃ sālendrarājā vikramaraśmiḥ padmottaraḥ (
children.translated_text: ) "We too, O Blessed One, shall go, by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power, to the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, for the sight, veneration, and attendance of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>." The <s>Tathāgata</s> said: "Go, O sons of good family, as you wish." Then those two <s>bodhisattvas</s>, together with twenty thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by the supernatural power of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, departed from that stainless <s>Buddha</s>-field and arrived in this <s>Buddha</s>-field in a single instant, standing on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain. Standing to one side, they bowed with joined palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> and said: "There is, O venerable Blessed One, in the north-eastern direction — as previously stated. That <s>Tathāgata</s> has sent these <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers and inquires about the Blessed One's health and well-being." Likewise, the seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mārabhavanavidhvaṃsana</s> (Destroyer of Māra's Abode) trembled. And whatever <s>bodhisattvas</s> had gathered there, they too, having seen the seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mārabhavanavidhvaṃsana</s> tremble, asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as previously stated. Likewise <s>Śālendrarāja</s>, <s>Vikramaraśmi</s>, <s>Padmottara</s>, (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 411.

children.text: ) candano merurājaḥ sāgaraḥ sārajyotirjñānavikramastathāgataḥ / yāvattena ca samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā uttarapurimāyāṃ diśi tathāgatāste bodhisattvāḥ sahacandrarocavimalapuṣpairiha sahe buddhakṣetre saṃprāptāḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya pṛcchanāya pūjanāya vandanāya dharmaśravaṇāya //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Candana</s>, <s>Merurāja</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Sārajyoti</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānavikrama</s> (Stride of Wisdom). At that time, immeasurable and incalculable <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the north-eastern direction — those <s>bodhisattvas</s> together with the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers arrived here in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, to inquire about, make offerings to, venerate, and hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.translated_text: Take these <s>Candrarocavimala</s> (Moonlight Stainless) flowers, O sons of good family. Having taken them, go to the south-western direction, so that you may see that <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field for yourselves. Ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> about his health and well-being in my name." The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarāja</s> (King of Śāla Trees, Vaiśravaṇa Arisen from the Departure of Anguish), taking the <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers, gave them to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vigopaśikhara</s> and to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Saṃrocanabuddha</s>, and said thus: "Go, O sons of good family, by the bestowal of my supernatural power, to the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field." At that point, twenty thousand beings said: (

body.text: tāvadeva śākyamunistathāgata ṛddhyanubhāvena sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ ye sahe buddhakṣetre sannipatitāsteṣāṃ ekaikasya sattvasya yojanapramāṇamātramātmabhāvaḥ saṃsthitaḥ; sarvāvantaṃ ca sahaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ evaṃrūpaiḥ sattvaiḥ sphuṭaṃ, na kaścidbuddhakṣetre kṣitau vā gagane vāvakāśo yaḥ sattvairasphuṭo 'ntaśo 'ñjanaśalākāpradeśamātramapi yaḥ sattvebhyo na sphuṭo 'bhūt / sarve ca te sattvāḥ śūnyamākāśaṃ paśyanti, na ca parasparaṃ paśyanti; na caiṣāṃ parvatasumerucakravāḍamahācakravāḍaparvatāścakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchanti, na lokāntarikā (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 412.

children.text: ) divyā vimānā ūrddhaṃ yāvadadho kāñcanacakraṃ tatorddhaṃ pṛthivī cakṣuṣo nābhāsamāgacchanti, sthāpayitvā tathāgataṃ śākyamuniṃ / te tathāgataṃ paśyanti / tatra ca bhagavān ākāśasphuraṇaṃ dharmāvacchedapraśrabdhisamādhiṃ samāpanno / yataste candrarocavimalāḥ puṣpāḥ sarvaromamukhesu bhagavataḥ praviśanti / sarve ca te sattvāḥ paśyanti sahe lokadhātāvantargatā vigatāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaitasikeṣu manasikārarūpasaṃdarśanatāḥ, te caiva bhagavato romamukhe nirīkṣante sma / tatra codyānamadrākṣuḥ, nānāratnavṛkṣaṃ nānāpatraṃ nānāpuṣpaṃ nānāphalākīrṇāṃ nānāvastraṃ nānācchatradhvajapatākākeyūramuktikāhārālaṅkṛtāṃstāṃ vṛkṣāṃ paśyanti, tadyathāpi nāma sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvudyānāṃ / sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ sattvānāmetadabhavat / "gacchāmo vayametadudyānaṃ darśanāya" / sarve ca te sattvā ye (
children.translated_text: ) nor the divine aerial palaces, nor upward [to the peak of existence], nor downward to the golden wheel, nor the earth above that — none of these came within the range of their sight, except for the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. They saw the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And there the Blessed One entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ākāśasphuraṇadharmāvacchedapraśrabdhi</s> (Tranquility of the Delimitation of <s>Dharmas</s>, Pervading Space). Thereupon those <s>Candrarocavimala</s> flowers entered through all the pores of the Blessed One's body. And all those beings saw that they had entered within the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, had passed beyond all beings' mental activities and perceptions of form in mind and mental factors, and they gazed into the very pores of the Blessed One's body. And there they saw a garden, with various jewel-trees, various leaves, various flowers, strewn with various fruits, and those trees adorned with various garments, various parasols, banners, pennants, diadems, pearl necklaces, and ornaments — just as the gardens in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). And all those beings thought: "Let us go to see this garden." And all those beings who (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 413.

children.text: ) sahe lokadhātāvantargatāḥ, sthāpayitvā nairayikāṃ yāmalaukikāṃ tairyagyonikāṃ ārūpyāvacarāṃ, sarve pariśiṣṭāḥ sattvāstasya tathāgatasya romamukhebhyastathāgataśarīre praviṣṭāḥ / atha bhagavāṃstāmṛddhiṃ pratiprasrambhayitvā vyutthitaḥ / tataste sattvā anyonyaṃ dṛṣṭvāhuḥ / "kutra śākyamunistathāgataḥ? / maitreyo bodhisattva āha - "saṃprajānaṃ tataḥ sattvāḥ samanvāharata sarve vayaṃ tathāgatasya kukṣau sannipatitāḥ" / tataste sattvāḥ sāntarabāhiraṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā svayaṃ pratyakṣībhūtā "yathā vayaṃ tathāgatasya kukṣāvantargatāḥ sannipatitāśca", teṣāmetadabhavat / "kuto vayaṃ tathāgatasya kukṣau praviṣṭāḥ, kenāsmin praveśitāḥ?" / tato maitreyaḥ sarvāvatī parṣadaṃ svareṇa vijñapayannuvāca - "śṛṇvantu bhavantastathāgatasyaivamṛddhivikurvaṇaprātihāryaṃ yadasmākaṃ hitakaraḥ śāstā dharmaṃ deśayati tadyuṣmābhiḥ sarvacetasā samanvāhartavyāḥ" / tataḥ sarvāvatī parṣatprāñjalībhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) had entered within the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm — except for hell-beings, beings of <s>Yama</s>'s world, animals, and those in the formless realm — all remaining beings entered through the pores of the <s>Tathāgata</s> into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body. Then the Blessed One, withdrawing that supernatural display, emerged [from <s>samādhi</s>]. Those beings, seeing each other, said: "Where is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>?" The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said: "Know this clearly, O beings — consider that we have all gathered within the belly of the <s>Tathāgata</s>." Then those beings, seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body from both inside and outside, and having themselves directly realized that "we have entered and gathered within the belly of the <s>Tathāgata</s>," they had this thought: "How did we enter the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s belly? Who caused us to enter?" Then <s>Maitreya</s>, informing the entire assembly with his voice, said: "Hear, noble ones, this miraculous display of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supernatural transformation — since our beneficent Teacher teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, you must attend to it with your entire minds." Then the entire assembly stood with palms joined.

body.translated_text: Thereupon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, by his supernatural power, caused the bodily form of each and every being who had gathered in the <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field to assume the measure of one <s>yojana</s> in size. And the entire <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field was filled with such beings — there was no space in the <s>Buddha</s>-field, whether on the ground or in the sky, that was not filled by beings, not even the space of the tip of an eyeliner-stick that was not filled with beings. And all those beings saw empty space and did not see each other; nor did mountains, <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, or <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> mountains come within the range of their sight, nor the inter-world darkness, (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 414.
