bhagavāṃśca sarvasukhacaryādharmaṃ deśayati sma / tatra katarā sarvasukhacaryā? / yaduta saṃsārapaṅkāduttāraṇaṃ āryāṣṭāṅgamārge 'vatāraṇaṃ sarvajñatā svayaṃbhūjñānaparipūrṇatā / tatra daśaprakārā dhyānaniveśacittotpādapariṇāmanatā, yaduta sarvasattvebhyo mahākaruṇācittādhiṣṭhānaṃ, hitavastusaṃjananatā, atīrṇasattvottāraṇatayā mahānāvasamudānanatā, amuktamocanatāsannāhaṃ asantaviparyāsaparimocanatayā, mahāsiṃhanādānutrāsanasannāha nairātmyadharmapratyavekṣaṇatayā, sarvalokadhātugamanasannāha māyāsvapnapratibhāsopamasarvadharmāvabudhyanatayā, sarvalokadhātvavabhāsanālaṅkaraṇasannāhaḥ śīlaskandhādhiṣṭhānapariśuddhyā, daśatathāgatabalapariniṣpādanasannāhaḥ sarvapāramitāparipūryā, caturvaiśāradyapratilābhasannāhaṃ yathāvāditathākāritayā, yāvadaṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmaniravaśeṣapratilābhasannāhaṃ, bodhisattvānāṃ yathāśrutadharmapratipattiraprapañcanatā ceyaṃ daśaprakārā niveśadharmamukhacaryā / alakṣaṇāmukhaparijñāgaticaryāyā sarvadharmanairātmyamanasikāracittānutpādānirodhāsamayam (
children.translated_text:
Chapter 4.
The Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> of the practice of all happiness. And what is the practice of all happiness? Namely: the lifting out of the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the entry into the noble eightfold path, omniscience, and the fulfillment of self-born wisdom. Therein are ten kinds of transformation of mind-generation directed toward the establishment in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation): namely, the empowerment of the mind of great compassion toward all beings; the generation of beneficial things; the preparation of the great vessel for the purpose of ferrying across beings not yet ferried; the armor of liberating those not yet liberated, for the purpose of freeing them from false inversions; the armor of fearlessness in the great lion's roar, through the contemplation of the <s>dharma</s> of non-self; the armor of going to all world-realms, through the understanding that all <s>dharmas</s> are like illusions, dreams, and reflections; the armor of illuminating and adorning all world-realms, through the purification of the aggregate of moral conduct; the armor of accomplishing the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, through the fulfillment of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); the armor of attaining the four fearlessnesses, through acting as one speaks; up to the armor of the complete attainment of the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; and the practice of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as heard <s>dharma</s>-practice without conceptual elaboration — this is the tenfold practice of the gate of the <s>dharma</s> of establishment. The practice of the course of the comprehension of the gate of signlessness is: the non-arising and non-cessation of the mind through attention to the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-conformity (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 415.

children.text: ) avaivartikabhūmiryatra saṃvartavivartānucchedamaśāśvatamavikṣiptaṃ / imasya khalu punardharmaparyāyasya bhāṣyamāṇasyāśītikoṭīgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāḥ sattvāstathāgatasya kukṣigatā avaivartikā abhūvannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; gaṇanātikrāntāśca tatra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ye nānāvidhadhāraṇīkṣāntipratilabdhā abhūn / sarve ca punastathāgataśarīrādromamukhebhyo niṣkrāntā āścaryaprāptā, bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā, daśadiśaḥ prakāntāḥ, svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gatāstathāgatasya svaramaṇḍalakāyapramāṇajñapanārthaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) of the irreversible stage, where there is no annihilation in the cycle of formation and destruction, neither eternalism, and the mind is undistracted. When this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) was being spoken, eighty <s>koṭis</s> of beings equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who were within the belly of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, became irreversible in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); and <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> beyond counting there attained various kinds of <s>dhāraṇī</s> and <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance). And then all [beings] emerged from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body through the pores, filled with wonder, bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, and departed in the ten directions, going each to their own <s>Buddha</s>-fields, to make known the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s voice-sphere and bodily extent.

body.text: tatra ye bodhisattvāḥ purimāṃ diśaṃ gacchanti aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ, purimāyāṃ diśi yadbuddhakṣetrānatikrāmanti na ca śākyamunestathāgatasya svaramaṇḍalaṃ pratihanyate, evaṃ ca tatra svaraṃ śṛṇvanti vicitrapadārthavyañjanāḥ, tadyathā śākyamunestathāgatasya purato niṣaṇṇairdharmaḥ śrutaḥ, evamevāsya dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 416.

children.text: ) api ca tatrāpi śākyamunestathāgatasya kāyasyonatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā na prajñāyate, śākyamunestathāgatasya kāyaḥ sphuṭo dṛśyate bodhisattvaiḥ śrāvakaiścāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā bodhisattvāḥ śrāvakāścaikaromamukhe śākyamunestathāgatasya praviśanto niṣkrāmantaśca saṃdṛśyante / evaṃ dvitīye romamukhe, yāvatsarvaromamukhebhyaḥ praviśanto niṣkrāmantaśca saṃdṛśyante, yāvaccaivaṃ daśasu dikṣu vaktavyaṃ /
children.translated_text: ) Moreover, there too, neither diminishment nor fullness of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s body was perceived. The body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> was seen filled by <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>; immeasurable and incalculable <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s> were seen entering and emerging from each pore of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Likewise from the second pore, and up to all the pores — they were seen entering and emerging. And likewise it should be stated for all ten directions.

body.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who went to the eastern direction were immeasurable and incalculable. In the eastern direction, as they passed through <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the voice-sphere of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> was not obstructed, and they heard the voice there with its varied meanings, words, and syllables — just as they heard the <s>Dharma</s> while seated before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, even so they heard his <s>Dharma</s>. (

body.text: sarvāvatī ca sā parṣā yāvadbhagavataḥ kāyāntargatāḥ sā bhagavataḥ kāyaromamukhebhyo niṣkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triṣpradakṣiṇī kṛtvā bhagavato 'bhimukhaṃ pratyavasthādbhagavantameva vicitrārthapadavyañjanarutavyāhāraiḥ stavamānāḥ / atha tāvaccaiva kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāśca devaputrā vicitrāṃ ca gandhamālyavilepanavṛṣṭiṃ pravarṣitā, divyāni ca tūryāṇi pravāditavanto, divyāni ca chatradhvajapatākāvastraduṣyābharaṇāni bhagavataḥ pūjāyodyuktāḥ //
body.translated_text: And the entire assembly, as long as they were within the Blessed One's body, having emerged from the pores of the Blessed One's body, bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, stood facing the Blessed One, and praised him with utterances of varied meanings, words, sounds, and syllables. Then at that very time, <s>devaputras</s> of the desire and form realms showered a rain of various fragrances, garlands, and ointments, played divine musical instruments, and devoted themselves to the worship of the Blessed One with divine parasols, banners, pennants, garments, fine cloths, and ornaments.

body.text: tatra vaiśāradyasamuddhāraṇirnāma bodhisattvo yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 417.

children.text: ) "kiṃ nāmāyaṃ bhadanta bhagavan mahāvyākaraṇaṃ sūtrāntaḥ?" / bhagavān āha - "sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśo nāma, bahubuddhakaṃ nāma, bahusannipātaṃ nāma, bodhisattvavyākaraṇaṃ nāma, vaiśāradyamārgottāraṇaṃ nāma, samādhānakalpāvataraṇo nāma, buddhakṣetrasandarśano nāma, sāgaropamo nāma, gaṇanātikrānto nāma, karuṇāpūṇḍarīko nāma" /
children.translated_text: ) "What is the name of this great prophecy-<s>sūtra</s>, O venerable Blessed One?" The Blessed One said: "It is called <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapravesa</s> (Entry into the Gate of <s>Dhāraṇī</s> of the Aspect of Omniscience); it is called <s>Bahubuddhaka</s> (Concerning Many <s>Buddhas</s>); it is called <s>Bahusannipāta</s> (The Great Assembly); it is called <s>Bodhisattvavyākaraṇa</s> (Prophecy of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>); it is called <s>Vaiśāradyamārgottāraṇa</s> (Crossing by the Path of Fearlessness); it is called <s>Samādhānakalpāvataraṇa</s> (Descent into the <s>Kalpa</s> of <s>Samādhi</s>); it is called <s>Buddhakṣetrasandarśana</s> (Vision of <s>Buddha</s>-Fields); it is called <s>Sāgaropama</s> (Like the Ocean); it is called <s>Gaṇanātikrānta</s> (Beyond Counting); it is called <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s> (The Lotus of Compassion)."

body.translated_text: Then a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vaiśāradyasamuddhāraṇi</s> (Rescuer through Fearlessness), bowing with joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: (

body.text: punarapyāha - "kiyantaṃ bhadanta bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati likhiṣyati likhāpayiṣyati antaśa ekagāthāmapi?" / āha - "pūrvaṃ ca mayoktamiha puṇyaskandhaṃ; saṃkṣepeṇedānīṃ kathayisyāmi / yaḥ kaścidimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati antaśa ekagāthāmapi, yaśca punaḥ paścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāmantaśo likhitvā dhārayiṣyati, sa bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati, na tvevaṃ ṣoḍaśamahākalpān ṣaṭpāramitācaramāṇasya bodhisattvasya puṇyaskandhaḥ / (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 418.

children.text: ) tatkasmāddhetoḥ? / sadevakasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśravaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sayakṣanāgagandharvakumbhāṇḍapretapiśācakinnarāsurāṇāṃ duṣṭacittānāṃ prasādanaḥ, sarvarogāṇāṃ praśamanaḥ, sarvakalikalahavigrahavivādavyupaśamanaḥ, sarvavātākālamaraṇarogapraśamanaḥ, sarvadurbhikṣapraśamanakaraḥ, kṣemakaraṇīyaḥ, subhikṣakaraḥ, ārogyasāmagrīkaraḥ, bhītānāmabhayasukhakaraḥ, kleśavyupaśamanakaraḥ, kuśalamūlavivṛddhikaraḥ, apāyaduḥkhapramocanakarastribhiryānairmārgasandarśanakaraḥ, samādhidhāraṇīkṣāntipratilābhakaraḥ, sarvasattvānāmupajīvakaro, vajrāsananiṣīdanakaraḥ, caturmāradharṣaṇakaro, bodhipakṣābhisaṃbudhyanakaro, dharmacakrapravartanakaraḥ, āryasaptadhanavirahitānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhipakṣasamṛddhikaraḥ, bahuparivāraḥ; abhayapuranagarapraveśakaraṇārthaṃ mayā dharmaparyāyo bhāṣitaḥ" /
children.translated_text: ) Why is that? Because [this discourse] generates faith in the world together with its gods, together with <s>Māra</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, in the generation including <s>śravaṇas</s> (ascetics) and brahmins, in <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>asuras</s> who are of hostile minds; it pacifies all diseases; it calms all strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute; it pacifies all untimely death from wind and disease; it allays all famine; it brings security; it brings abundance; it brings the fullness of health; it gives fearlessness and happiness to the frightened; it calms afflictions; it increases roots of merit; it liberates from the suffering of the lower realms and shows the path through the three vehicles; it brings the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience); it sustains all beings; it brings the sitting upon the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat); it brings the vanquishing of the four <s>Māras</s>; it brings the awakening to the factors of awakening; it brings the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>; it brings the flourishing of the factors of awakening for beings bereft of the seven noble treasures; it has a great retinue. For the purpose of leading into the city of fearlessness, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse was spoken by me."

body.translated_text: He further said: "How great a mass of merit, Venerable Blessed One, will a son or daughter of good family generate who will hear this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, take it up, retain it, recite it, and fully illuminate it to others in detail, write it or cause it to be written — even a single verse?" He said: "I have previously spoken of the mass of merit here; I shall now state it briefly. Whoever will hear this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, take it up, retain it, recite it, and fully illuminate it to others in detail — even a single verse — and moreover, whoever in the last fifty [years of the teaching] will copy it and retain it, shall generate a far greater mass of merit, not even equal to the mass of merit of a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) for sixteen great <s>kalpas</s>. (

body.text: "kasya haste imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ parindāmi? / ko mamemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ paścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāṃ rakṣiṣyati, adharmabhūmiṣṭhānāṃ sattvānāṃ bhinnaśīlānāṃ ca bhikṣūṇāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 419.

children.text: ) karṇapuṭe prakāśayiṣyati, adharmarāgaraktānāṃ viṣamalobhābhibhūtānāṃ mithyādharmaparicitānāṃ aparipakvacittāṃ saṃvejayiṣyati?" / sarvāvatī ca sā parṣā bhagavataścetasā cittamājñāya; tatra parṣadi merupuṇyo nāma yakṣariṣirniṣaṇṇaḥ / atha maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ merupuṇyaṃ yakṣariṣiṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ sakāśamupanītavān / bhagavān āha - "udgṛhṇa tvaṃ maharṣa imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ, yāvatpaścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāṃ deśāntaragatānāmavaivartikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ karṇapuṭeṣu prakāśasva / adya cāvaivartikacittaṃ saṃjanayasvā "hai"vaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścaturaśītimahākalpā atikrāmantā yanmayā bhadanta bhagavan pūrvaṃ praṇidhānena yakṣariṣitvālabdhyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bodhicārikāṃ caramāṇo gaṇanātikrāntāḥ sattvā mayā caturṣu brāhmavihāreṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, avaivartikabhūmau ca pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) and will arouse those whose minds are unripened, who are dyed with passion for unrighteousness, overcome by crooked greed, accustomed to wrong doctrines?" And that entire assembly, knowing the thought of the Blessed One's mind — in that assembly there sat a <s>yakṣa</s> sage named <s>Merupuṇya</s>. Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> took that <s>yakṣa</s> sage <s>Merupuṇya</s> and brought him before the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "Take up, O great sage, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse; and in the last fifty [years], proclaim it to the ears of non-retrogressing <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have gone to other lands. And today, generate the non-retrogressing mind." "Yes, Venerable Blessed One! Eighty-four great <s>kalpas</s> have elapsed since I, Venerable Blessed One, by my former aspiration, having obtained the state of a <s>yakṣa</s> sage, while practicing the course of awakening toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, established innumerable beings in the four <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes (divine dwellings) and established them on the stage of non-retrogression. (
<s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> 420.

children.text: ) ahaṃ ca sattvānāṃ svayameva paripācayāmi yāvatpaścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāṃ ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ udgṛhīṣyati, yāvadya itaścatuṣpadikāmapi gāthāṃ dhārayiṣyati" //
children.translated_text: ) I myself shall ripen beings, and in the last fifty [years], whoever will take up this <s>Dharma</s> discourse — and whoever will retain even a four-line verse from it."

body.translated_text: "Into whose hands do I entrust this <s>Dharma</s> discourse? Who will guard this <s>Dharma</s> discourse of mine in the last fifty [years of the teaching], and will proclaim it to the ears of beings established in unrighteousness and monks whose morality is broken, (

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān āttamanāḥ sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, the entire assembly — the world together with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> — rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: iti śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptaṃ //
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the holy <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of Compassion), a <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra.

body.text: śubham astu //
body.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness!

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetu teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from a cause — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: hevadatteṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādi mahāśramaṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation — thus has the Great Ascetic declared.

body.text: śubhamastu sarvadāt // śubhaṃ // śubhaṃ // śubhaṃ //
body.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness always! Auspiciousness! Auspiciousness! Auspiciousness!
